WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Combat Turn structure, actions, movement, attacks, damage, conditions, death, rests, and survival. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative Round and Turn Action Economy Attack Action Universal Actions Ready Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative, rounds, and combat-only resources are used only for genuine combat or another situation where structured turn order is necessary. Characters cannot manufacture artificial combat to farm cooldowns, resources, or timing triggers. Initiative Initiative = 1d20 + Dexterity modifier. Do not add PB unless an explicit feature says so. Alert adds +2 Initiative. There is no Surprise Round and Surprise does not grant Advantage on Initiative. When one side genuinely catches another side unaware, the GM may, at discretion, allow one appropriate pre-Initiative attack roll against the target's normal defense before Initiative is rolled. This is not an extra round, is not automatic, and does not create a general Surprise action economy. After that resolution, roll Initiative normally. Round and Turn One combat round represents approximately six seconds in the game world. Each participant normally takes one turn in Initiative order. All turns in the round abstract actions occurring within the same six-second span; do not add each turn as another six seconds. Action Economy Action. One per turn. Movement. Up to the creature’s available movement, subject to terrain and conditions. Bonus Action. Up to one, but only when a feature grants something that uses a Bonus Action. Reaction. Normally one per round, refreshing at the start of the creature’s turn unless an explicit class rule says otherwise. Object interaction. One free simple object interaction per turn. There is no universal Action-to-Bonus-Action or Bonus-Action-to-Action conversion. Unused movement or Actions are not stored for later turns. Attack Action The Attack Action makes one attack unless a feature such as Extra Attack says otherwise. Grapple and Shove are full Actions and do not replace one attack within Extra Attack. Player Weapon Requirement. A player character must be wielding an approved class weapon to take the normal Attack Action. Unarmed Attacks and Improvised Weapons are not player combat options unless a later explicit feature creates a specific exception. Opportunity Attacks. Opportunity Attacks remain part of the core combat rules. When a hostile creature you can perceive voluntarily leaves your melee reach, you may use your Reaction to make one melee attack against it, resolving the attack before it leaves that reach. Forced movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Universal Actions Dash. Gain additional movement equal to your current Speed for the turn. Difficult Terrain and other movement costs still apply. While flying, Dash adds horizontal movement but does not grant an additional altitude-layer change. Disengage. Until the end of your turn, your movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks. Dodge. Until the start of your next turn, attacks against you have Disadvantage if you can perceive the attacker, and you have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws. Dodge ends if you become Incapacitated or your Speed becomes 0. Hide. You must have meaningful concealment or another circumstance that allows hiding. Make Dexterity (Stealth) against Passive Perception or active Perception as appropriate. You cannot Hide while clearly seen. Hidden is not Invisible. Making an attack reveals your position after that attack resolves. Search. Deliberately search using a GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation). Use Object. Use this Action for substantial manipulation beyond the one free simple object interaction. A specific item’s activation rule controls when it states another cost. Ready A creature can prepare one Action for a perceivable trigger. When the trigger occurs, the creature may use its Reaction to perform the readied Action. Ready does not store ordinary movement, but Dash can be readied as the Action. Readied attacks retain all weapon properties. A readied spell must still meet implement and targeting requirements when released. Losing a mandatory implement before release prevents release. Concentration begins when the spell actually resolves. Ready never bypasses aerial restrictions, range, or other universal rules. Simultaneous Effects Effects resolve one at a time. The active creature orders its own simultaneous effects; the GM orders GM-controlled simultaneous effects. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Flight Exploration flight, Combat Flight Slots, airborne movement, gliding, falling, and Aether restrictions. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Flight & Aerial Combat Altitude Layers 3D Distance Melee Descending Attack Physical Ranged Attacks Flight Slots Aether State Interaction Flight & Aerial Combat Altitude Layers Layer Height Access Low 30 ft All functional Wings Mid 60 ft All functional Wings High 90 ft All functional Wings Legendary 120 ft Legendary Wings only Ground level is 0 feet and is not an altitude layer. There are four airborne altitude layers: Low (30 ft), Mid (60 ft), High (90 ft), and Legendary (120 ft). Voluntarily ascending or descending one altitude layer consumes all movement for that turn. A creature cannot both ascend and descend voluntarily in the same turn. Dash does not permit an additional altitude-layer change. A Daeva without Legendary Wings cannot voluntarily ascend above the High layer at 90 feet. 3D Distance For WoA aerial targeting, total distance = the greater of horizontal distance or vertical distance. Do not use Pythagorean distance and do not add horizontal and vertical distance together. Melee Airborne melee uses ordinary reach: usually 5 feet, or 10 feet for a Reach weapon. Being on the same altitude layer does not remove the need to physically move into reach. Descending Attack If a melee attacker begins its turn higher than the target, descends at least 25 feet, and then makes its first qualifying melee attack against that lower target, the attack has Advantage. Physical Ranged Attacks Universal Close-Range Rule. If the target of a physical ranged weapon attack is within 5 feet of the attacker, the attack roll has Disadvantage. This applies whether the attacker is grounded or airborne and does not change the weapon’s listed Normal Range or Maximum Range. A lower-altitude physical ranged attacker has Advantage against a higher-altitude winged airborne target because the wings are exposed. This Exposed Wings rule does not apply to wingless creatures flying through Saturated Aether. A higher-altitude ranged attacker gains no automatic Advantage merely for being above the target. When the physical ranged attacker is above the target, increase only the weapon’s Maximum Range by half the vertical distance, rounded up. The weapon’s Normal Range is unchanged. Magical attacks do not gain this extension. Flight Slots Level Base Max Slots 1–3 2 4–6 3 7–9 4 10–12 5 13–16 6 17–19 7 20 8 A stable airborne Daeva spends 1 Flight Slot at the end of each of its turns. A grounded Daeva recovers 1 Flight Slot at the end of each grounded turn. Short Rest restores half maximum, rounded down; Long Rest restores all. When a creature runs out of Flight Slots while airborne, it immediately falls. Aether State Interaction Depleted Aether. Flight is fully restricted. Stable Aether. Normal flight rules. Saturated Aether. Daevas spend no combat Flight Slots, though exploration Flight Time limits still apply. Wingless creatures capable of movement may gain flight equal to normal Speed while Saturated; they do not use Flight Slots and are not subject to Exposed Wings. Unstable Zone / Aether Instability. This is hazard-defined scene behavior rather than a universal Aether State. The three universal States are Stable, Depleted, and Saturated. Use the specific Aether Hazard rules for the area. Aether-State Changes and Boundaries Aether-State changes take effect immediately. Crossing into a new Aether State immediately applies the entered State. In Depleted Aether, Aether-supported flight is unavailable; an airborne Daeva entering a Depleted area loses flight and falls, using the normal DC 12 Dexterity Emergency Landing Reaction if eligible. Saturated → Stable: Daevas resume normal Flight Slot expenditure. A creature flying only because Saturated Aether granted it flight loses that flight and falls. Saturated → Depleted: affected airborne creatures immediately lose Aether-supported flight and fall. Stable → Saturated: Daevas stop spending Combat Flight Slots, and eligible wingless creatures gain access to Aether-supported flight equal to normal Speed, but no creature automatically takes off. Falling and Emergency Landing Falling damage is 1d6 per 10 feet fallen, maximum 20d6. A falling creature normally lands Prone unless an explicit effect says otherwise. When Flight Slot depletion causes a fall, the creature may use its Reaction for a DC 12 Dexterity save. Success halves fall damage; failure or no Reaction takes full damage. Controlled Descent changes a successful Emergency Landing to 0 fall damage according to that feat. Falling Onto Creatures The lower creature makes a DC 12 Dexterity save. On success it avoids the collision and the falling creature takes normal

WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Glossary & Core Terms A player-facing A–Z reference for the vocabulary used throughout Wings of Atreia, with direct links to the full rules and lore pages. How to use this page: definitions here are quick-reference summaries. Follow the “Read more” link whenever you need the complete rule, class text, or world context. A B C D E F G I K L M P R S U W 46 terms A Action Your main turn action. Many attacks, spells, class features, and other options specify that they use your Action. Read more: Combat → Advantage / Disadvantage Roll two d20s and use the higher result for Advantage or the lower result for Disadvantage. Read more: Core Resolution → Aether The supernatural power that underlies Daeva abilities, spellcasting, flight, and many extraordinary phenomena in Atreia. Read more: Aether & Spellcasting → Aether Enhancement The higher equipment-quality path beyond Profession +2. Aether upgrades are level-gated and handled separately from ordinary Profession work. Read more: Equipment → Ascension The transformation by which a mortal becomes a Daeva and receives Wings. WoA begins with this event in Session 0. Read more: Character Creation → At-Will A spell or ability frequency that may be used whenever its normal action and other requirements are met. Read more: Aether & Spellcasting → B Background A character-creation choice representing experience and identity before or around Ascension; it provides its defined skills and related benefits. Read more: Backgrounds → Bonus Action A secondary turn action available only when a feature, spell, or rule explicitly gives an option that uses it. Read more: Combat → C Character Manager The official WoA character-management method for creation records, advancement, current resources, equipment, spells, and other tracked character data. Read more: Character Creation → Class Your Daeva’s primary mechanical path. WoA uses eleven classes and does not use multiclassing. Read more: Classes → Class Resource A class-specific pool, charge, stance, meter, or other tracked mechanic defined by that class. Read more: Quick Reference → Class Save DC Normally 8 + Proficiency Bonus + the class ability identified by your class, unless a rule states otherwise. Read more: Core Resolution → Concentration A spell/effect limit: only one Concentration effect can be maintained at a time, and Incapacitated ends it. WoA does not use Concentration saving throws. Read more: Aether & Spellcasting → Condition A named rules state such as Poisoned or Incapacitated that changes what a creature can do or how rolls affect it. Read more: Combat → Cooldown A spell or ability frequency that becomes unavailable after use until its stated cooldown is satisfied; WoA also uses the universal out-of-combat cooldown rule where applicable. Read more: Aether & Spellcasting → D Daeva An Ascended immortal warrior of Atreia. Player characters in Wings of Atreia are Daevas. Read more: Character Creation → Daeva Points (DP) A resource unlocked at Level 10 and earned through participation in genuine combat victories. DP powers Ultimate Abilities and persists through rests. Read more: Daeva Points & Ultimates → E Empyrean Boon A powerful universal character option gained at Level 19 according to the advancement rules. Read more: Feats & Empyrean Boons → Empyrean Lord One of the great Daeva Lords whose authority and legacy shape Elyos and Asmodian civilization, together with the two historic Tower Guardians. Read more: World → F Faction Your character’s allegiance as Elyos or Asmodian. Faction affects culture, homeland, and campaign relationships rather than class statistics. Read more: Character Creation → Feat A universal character option chosen at designated advancement points instead of an Ability Score Improvement where the rules allow it. Read more: Feats & Empyrean Boons → Flight Slot A tracked unit of a Daeva’s flight capacity. The number of Flight Slots increases with character level. Read more: Flight → G Genuine Combat A real encounter using initiative and combat timing. Artificial encounters cannot be used to farm resources such as Daeva Points. Read more: Combat → I Implement A spellcasting equipment category that can follow the established quality and enhancement progression. Read more: Equipment → K Kinah The standard currency used for purchases, profession training, supplies, and other economic transactions. Read more: Professions & Economy → L Legendary Equipment Story-driven top-tier equipment above the Aether enhancement tiers. Legendary items are not ordinary Profession products. Read more: Equipment → Long Rest An 8-hour recovery period. What it restores depends on the specific class, spell, feature, or rule. Read more: Combat → Lord Action The dedicated off-turn action framework used by Empyrean Lords and Dragon Lords. Read more: Combat → M Milestone Advancement WoA’s advancement method. Choose Elyos or Asmodian. 2. Choose one of the 11 classes. 3. Assign 16, 14, 14, 12, 10, 8 among STR, DEX, CON, INT, WIS and CHA. 4. Choose one Background. 5. Enter class saving throws, armor, shield and weapon access in the Character Manager. 6. Choose exactly 2 Class Skills from the six Skill options listed for your Class and exactly 2 Background Skills from the six Skill options listed for your Background. text: Ability Checks. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Core Resolution The d20 test framework used for meaningful uncertain outcomes. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. d20 Tests & Core Resolution d20 Tests Ability Checks Saving Throws Save DCs Advantage and Disadvantage Help Passive Perception, Passive Investigation & Search d20 Tests & Core Resolution d20 Tests Ability Checks, attack rolls, and saving throws use a d20. Roll only when the outcome is uncertain and meaningful. If success is automatic, impossible, or consequence-free, no roll is needed. Ability Checks Choose the ability that best fits the approach, then add Proficiency Bonus if the character is proficient in the relevant skill. Expertise doubles the PB contribution for that proficiency. WoA retains six abilities and eighteen skills. A specialized Background can authorize a character to attempt obscure knowledge, but it does not automatically modify the roll. Saving Throws A saving throw uses the specified ability modifier and adds PB only if the creature is proficient in that saving throw. Ties are resolved according to the specific system; otherwise meeting a DC succeeds. Save DCs Default effect Save DC = 8 + Proficiency Bonus + the relevant ability modifier, unless an explicit class, spell, item, monster, or environmental rule gives a different DC. Advantage and Disadvantage When a rule grants Advantage, roll two d20s and use the higher. When it grants Disadvantage, roll two and use the lower. If both apply, they cancel unless a specific rule says otherwise. Resolve Advantage/Disadvantage before applying numeric modifiers. Help Help never grants Advantage. A meaningful helper grants +2 to one Ability Check. Normally only one helper can contribute. There is no Assist Attack and Help cannot modify Death Saves. Passive Perception, Passive Investigation & Search Passive Perception = 10 + your Wisdom (Perception) modifier. Passive Investigation = 10 + your Intelligence (Investigation) modifier. Advantage on the relevant check adds +5 to the passive score; Disadvantage subtracts 5. Multiple instances of the same source do not stack, and Advantage and Disadvantage cancel normally. Hide is opposed by Passive Perception; ties favor the observer. An active Search uses the GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation), against the relevant DC or opposing Stealth; ties favor the Searcher where opposed. Repeated checks require a meaningful change in circumstances. ← Back to Rules Wings of Atreia · Created & Designed by Clark Michael Zafra (“ArchQwynn”) · Non-commercial fan project.

text: WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Sorcerer Spell Absolute Zero Ice · Apex Control Source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 , Integrated Spell Compendium. Class Sorcerer Chain Ice Unlock Level 17 Prerequisite Ice Prison Spell Level 7 Casting Time Action Range 120 ft Frequency Long Rest 1 Duration Instantaneous Concentration No Role Apex Control Base Effect. Choose a point within 120 feet. Creatures in a 25-foot-radius sphere make a Constitution save. On a failure they take 5d8 Cold damage and are Restrained until the end of your next turn; on a success they take half damage and have Speed halved until then. Spell-Level Scaling. Damage increases by +1d8 at Spell Levels 3, 5, 7, and 9. Milestone Improvements Spell Level Milestone Improvement 3 Radius becomes 30 feet. 5 Failed-save creatures cannot take Reactions. 7 Failed-save creatures repeat the save at the end of their turns; on a failure the Restrained condition continues until the end of their next turn, to a maximum total duration of 3 rounds. 9 Successful saves also prevent Dash until the end of your next turn. ← Back to Spell Library View Sorcerer spells Wings of Atreia · Created & Designed by Clark Michael Zafra (“ArchQwynn”) · Non-commercial fan project.

title: Abyss Warfront System
desc: Abyss Warfront System — Wings of Atreia reference section.
text: Abyss Warfront System. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Legions & Complete Abyss Warfront System Player-created Legions plus the complete player-operable Warfront rules, unit catalogue, War Asset costs, Fortress procedures, and Open Abyss procedures. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Core Rulebook v4.2 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026 , synchronized with Player Handbook v3.10 . This page exposes the complete player-operable Warfront subsystem. Explicitly GM-facing enemy statblocks, hidden force composition, and closed GM-only resolution tables remain off the public player site. Legions Warfront Overview War Assets Unit Statistics Battle Exchange Unit Catalogue Unit Costs PC Participation Fortress Wars Open Abyss Reinforcements Quick Reference PLAYER-CREATED LEGIONS A player-created Legion is a lightweight organization for shared identity, missions, resources, and cross-faction cooperation when the campaign permits it. Legion membership does not create a new character progression track or grant automatic combat bonuses. When a Legion Can Be Founded Campaign Gate. The Campaign Director or controlling GM must explicitly declare Legion Founding available. Reaching Level 11 by itself does not unlock the system. Founding Player. One Founding Player must be Level 11 or higher. That character becomes the initial Legion Leader. Other members. Every other founding or joining member must be Level 3 or higher before joining and must already have reached their Specialization or Archetype choice where applicable. A Level 1-2 character cannot join early. Membership has no maximum size. There is no minimum number of additional founders; a qualifying Founding Player may establish the Legion alone if all other founding requirements are satisfied. Elyos and Asmodians may belong to the same Legion once the required campaign state is active. Every member retains their original faction identity and its normal consequences. Founding Fund and Treasury Founding requires 5,000 Kinah deposited into the new Legion Treasury. Eligible founding members may contribute toward the total. Before establishment, the Founding Fund cannot be withdrawn. If founding is abandoned, each contributor receives their contribution back. Once established, the 5,000 Kinah remains usable Treasury money. Any Legion member may deposit Kinah. Only the Legion Leader may withdraw Kinah or authorize spending. Legion missions may reward participating members, the Treasury, or both as determined by the GM. There is no passive Legion income, automatic salary, interest, business-profit engine, or mandatory recurring membership dues. Leadership and Membership The only default roles are Legion Leader and Legion Member. The Legion Leader admits and removes members, controls permissions for Legion assets, may transfer leadership, and may formally dissolve the Legion. Leadership may be transferred to any existing legal Legion member. The new Leader does not need to be Level 11; Level 11 is a founding requirement only. Member Benefits Members may display the Legion name, colors, crest, and insignia. Ordinary Legion identification occupies no Inventory Slot. Members may accept Legion missions and may use resources, facilities, contacts, and support the Legion actually possesses when the Legion Leader permits it. Where the campaign's cross-faction arrangements recognize the Legion, its insignia provides a legitimate reason for Elyos and Asmodian members to operate together. It does not grant diplomatic immunity or unrestricted access. Legion membership grants no automatic Hit, AC, damage, HP, saving throw, skill, Advantage, Spell DC, DP, class-resource, equipment-quality, or personal Inventory bonus. Legion Storage and Headquarters An established Legion has one secure shared Storage location with a capacity of 100 Inventory Slots. Normal Inventory Slot and stacking rules apply; Kinah remains in the Treasury and uses no Storage Slots. Any Legion member may deposit eligible items. Only the Legion Leader may withdraw items or authorize another member to retrieve them. Legion Storage is stationary and cannot be accessed remotely. It never increases a member's personal Inventory capacity in the field. A Legion may designate one legitimate location as its Headquarters. The Headquarters is simply its meeting place and Storage location; it grants no automatic bonuses and has no upgrade track. Lightweight Rule. There is no Legion XP, Legion Level, officer hierarchy, skill tree, research tree, reputation meter, headquarters progression, or other default Legion management subsystem. Abyss Warfront System Warfronts resolve formation-scale warfare separately from ordinary character-scale combat. They are used for Fortress Wars and Open Abyss Battles. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Backgrounds All nine player Backgrounds, their skill choices, roleplaying guidance, Languages, and Territorial Familiarity. Source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page is a player-facing reference extracted from the handbook rather than a replacement ruleset. Background Rules Soldier Scholar Acolyte Noble Outlander Underworld Artisan Merchant Entertainer Languages Background Rules Skill Selection: Choose exactly 2 Background Skills from the six options listed for your Background. Duplicate selections are prohibited. A Skill selected as a Class Skill cannot also be selected as a Background Skill. The four selected Class and Background Skill Proficiencies must therefore be four different Skills. Background Choose 2 Skills Soldier Athletics, Intimidation, Perception, Survival, Medicine, Religion Scholar Arcana, History, Investigation, Religion, Medicine, Perception Acolyte History, Insight, Medicine, Religion, Athletics, Survival Noble History, Insight, Persuasion, Performance, Investigation, Sleight of Hand Outlander Athletics, Nature, Perception, Survival, Persuasion, Stealth Underworld Deception, Insight, Sleight of Hand, Stealth, Investigation, Persuasion Artisan Investigation, Perception, Sleight of Hand, History, Arcana, Persuasion Merchant Insight, Investigation, Persuasion, History, Stealth, Athletics Entertainer Acrobatics, Deception, Performance, Persuasion, Nature, Animal Handling A relevant Background may establish that you have the experience necessary to attempt obscure or specialized knowledge. It does not automatically grant Advantage, Expertise, a numerical bonus, or guaranteed success. Understanding Your Background Your Class describes what your character has learned to do as an adventuring Daeva. Your Background describes the life, training, profession, upbringing, or experiences that helped shape who they were before the campaign began. Faction tells you where you belong, Background helps explain where you came from, and Class describes how you operate as an adventurer. A Background does not determine your morality, personality, beliefs, faction loyalty, or future choices. Two characters with the same Background may have completely different lives and goals. Mechanically, use the Background table above exactly as written: choose two skills from your Background’s listed skill pool. The entries below add roleplaying context and do not grant additional rules benefits. Soldier What Is a Soldier?. A Soldier has meaningful experience with organized military service: troops, guards, scouts, officers, fortress personnel, or other disciplined fighting forces. Life and Origins. Military life may have included patrols, garrison duty, campaigns, escort work, reconnaissance, fortification defense, or service under a commander. That service may have occurred before or after ascension. Motivations and Outlook. Duty, loyalty, comradeship, ambition, patriotism, protection, regret, or the memory of fallen companions may still shape the character. A Soldier may respect military order, resent it, or be deciding what is truly worth fighting for. Playing a Soldier. Decide what kind of service shaped you, who you served beside, and what relationship you now have with authority and your former comrades. Being a Soldier does not require obedience or a martial Class. Scholar What Is a Scholar?. A Scholar has devoted part of their life to seeking, preserving, interpreting, or teaching knowledge. Scholars include researchers, historians, scribes, teachers, philosophers, archivists, investigators, and field specialists. Life and Origins. Study may have taken place under a teacher, within an archive or institution, or independently. Subjects can include history, geography, creatures, Aether, ruins, cultures, warfare, or any other serious field of inquiry. Motivations and Outlook. A Scholar may adventure to recover lost knowledge, investigate mysteries, study ruins or creatures directly, protect important discoveries, or prevent dangerous knowledge from being misused. Playing a Scholar. Choose the subject that fascinates you and decide whether you are an academic, a practical field researcher, or something between. Being scholarly does not require being socially awkward or confined to books. Acolyte What Is an Acolyte?. An Acolyte has meaningful experience with religious or spiritual service, sacred traditions, temples, ceremonies, or communities of worship. Life and Origins. The character may have been raised around a temple, studied under a religious teacher, volunteered in a sacred institution, maintained holy places, assisted ceremonies, or found faith after a life-changing event. Motivations and Outlook. Faith, service, protection, reform, doubt, duty, spiritual curiosity, or concern for a community may lead an Acolyte into adventure. title: Action Economy

text: Action Economy. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Combat Turn structure, actions, movement, attacks, damage, conditions, death, rests, and survival. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative Round and Turn Action Economy Attack Action Universal Actions Ready Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative, rounds, and combat-only resources are used only for genuine combat or another situation where structured turn order is necessary. Characters cannot manufacture artificial combat to farm cooldowns, resources, or timing triggers. Initiative Initiative = 1d20 + Dexterity modifier. Do not add PB unless an explicit feature says so. Alert adds +2 Initiative. There is no Surprise Round and Surprise does not grant Advantage on Initiative. When one side genuinely catches another side unaware, the GM may, at discretion, allow one appropriate pre-Initiative attack roll against the target's normal defense before Initiative is rolled. This is not an extra round, is not automatic, and does not create a general Surprise action economy. After that resolution, roll Initiative normally. Round and Turn One combat round represents approximately six seconds in the game world. Each participant normally takes one turn in Initiative order. All turns in the round abstract actions occurring within the same six-second span; do not add each turn as another six seconds. Action Economy Action. One per turn. Movement. Up to the creature’s available movement, subject to terrain and conditions. Bonus Action. Up to one, but only when a feature grants something that uses a Bonus Action. Reaction. Normally one per round, refreshing at the start of the creature’s turn unless an explicit class rule says otherwise. Object interaction. One free simple object interaction per turn. There is no universal Action-to-Bonus-Action or Bonus-Action-to-Action conversion. Unused movement or Actions are not stored for later turns. Attack Action The Attack Action makes one attack unless a feature such as Extra Attack says otherwise. Grapple and Shove are full Actions and do not replace one attack within Extra Attack. Player Weapon Requirement. A player character must be wielding an approved class weapon to take the normal Attack Action. Unarmed Attacks and Improvised Weapons are not player combat options unless a later explicit feature creates a specific exception. Opportunity Attacks. Opportunity Attacks remain part of the core combat rules. When a hostile creature you can perceive voluntarily leaves your melee reach, you may use your Reaction to make one melee attack against it, resolving the attack before it leaves that reach. Forced movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Universal Actions Dash. Gain additional movement equal to your current Speed for the turn. Difficult Terrain and other movement costs still apply. While flying, Dash adds horizontal movement but does not grant an additional altitude-layer change. Disengage. Until the end of your turn, your movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks. Dodge. Until the start of your next turn, attacks against you have Disadvantage if you can perceive the attacker, and you have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws. Dodge ends if you become Incapacitated or your Speed becomes 0. Hide. You must have meaningful concealment or another circumstance that allows hiding. Make Dexterity (Stealth) against Passive Perception or active Perception as appropriate. You cannot Hide while clearly seen. Hidden is not Invisible. Making an attack reveals your position after that attack resolves. Search. Deliberately search using a GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation). Use Object. Use this Action for substantial manipulation beyond the one free simple object interaction. A specific item’s activation rule controls when it states another cost. Ready A creature can prepare one Action for a perceivable trigger. When the trigger occurs, the creature may use its Reaction to perform the readied Action. Ready does not store ordinary movement, but Dash can be readied as the Action. Readied attacks retain all weapon properties. A readied spell must still meet implement and targeting requirements when released. Losing a mandatory implement before release prevents release. Concentration begins when the spell actually resolves. Ready never bypasses aerial restrictions, range, or other universal rules. Simultaneous Effects Effects resolve one at a time. The active creature orders its own simultaneous effects; the GM orders GM-controlled simultaneous effects. For opposing same-time effects, resolve the active creature first, then use Initiative if needed. Damage resolves before state changes caused by that damage. Star

Either way, you'll only die tired.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Focus Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Ranger is a nonmagical ranged hunter that controls enemy movement with persistent battlefield traps, spends Focus on precision or evasive shots, and is rewarded for exploiting targets that walk into prepared terrain. Its sustained damage comes from two ranged attacks, not from spellcasting or a third standard attack. Class Identity Rangers are mobile ranged specialists who control distance through marksmanship, movement, traps, and battlefield awareness. They are most effective when they can read terrain before committing, choose favorable lines of attack, and punish enemies that approach carelessly. Focus represents the Ranger’s ability to convert patience and perception into precise action. Tradition & Outlook The Ranger tradition also descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines, but where Assassins close with a chosen target, Rangers cultivate distance, fieldcraft, and control of the approach. Rangers are common among scouts, hunters, pathfinders, border wardens, reconnaissance troops, and independent Daevas accustomed to surviving beyond secure settlements. They tend to value preparedness, observation, mobility, and freedom of movement. Appearance & Adventuring Rangers usually wear mobile armor and carry bows, ammunition, traps, and field equipment suited to extended movement. Their gear often reflects the terrain in which they learned their craft. Rangers adventure to explore dangerous regions, hunt monsters or enemy operatives, guide expeditions, secure routes, protect remote communities, or prove that no battlefield is truly open ground when preparation and range are on their side. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Ability Dexterity Secondary Ability Wisdom Hit Die d10 Saving Throws Dexterity, Strength Armor Leather Armor Weapons Longbows, Shortbows, Crossbows Skills Choose 2 from 6: Animal Handling, Athletics, Investigation, Nature, Perception, Survival Class Save DC 8 + PB + WIS modifier Signature Resource Focus Signature Mechanic Ranger Traps Extra Attack Level 5; two attacks only Spellcasting None Core Engine — Focus Maximum Focus equals your PB + WIS modifier, minimum 2. A Long Rest restores all expended Focus. A Short Rest restores Focus equal to PB, up to your maximum. Focus is a tactical reserve rather than ammunition or a tax on ordinary ranged attacks; Ranger Traps normally cost no Focus. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Starting State Focus is a rest-based reserve and does not reset merely because combat begins or ends. After a Long Rest it is normally full. Maximum PB + WIS modifier, minimum 2. Rest Recovery Long Rest restores all expended Focus. Short Rest restores Focus equal to PB, up to your maximum. Combat Recovery Hunter’s Rhythm and certain later Ranger/specialization features can regain Focus during genuine combat when their tactical conditions are actually satisfied. How You Spend It Precision Shot 1 Focus; Pinning Shot 1 Focus; Evasive Step 1 Focus; Deadeye Perfect Shot 1 Focus. Other Ranger features spend Focus only when their text states a cost. Refunds / Recovery A combat refund or recovery is not a new attack, trap trigger, or separate technique. It simply restores Focus up to your maximum. Persistence Unused Focus persists between encounters until spent or restored; there is no automatic combat-end reset. Does Not Generate Standing still and firing, harmless staged interactions, or ordinary trap placement do not create Focus unless an explicit recovery feature is actually triggered. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Focus Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Ranger is a nonmagical ranged hunter that controls enemy movement with persistent battlefield traps, spends Focus on precision or evasive shots, and is rewarded for exploiting targets that walk into prepared terrain. Its sustained damage comes from two ranged attacks, not from spellcasting or a third standard attack. Class Identity Rangers are mobile ranged specialists who control distance through marksmanship, movement, traps, and battlefield awareness. They are most effective when they can read terrain before committing, choose favorable lines of attack, and punish enemies that approach carelessly. Focus represents the Ranger’s ability to convert patience and perception into precise action. Tradition & Outlook The Ranger tradition also descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines, but where Assassins close with a chosen target, Rangers cultivate distance, fieldcraft, and control of the approach. Rangers are common among scouts, hunters, pathfinders, border wardens, reconnaissance troops, and independent Daevas accustomed to surviving beyond secure settlements. They tend to value preparedness, observation, mobility, and freedom of movement. Appearance & Adventuring Rangers usually wear mobile armor and carry bows, ammunition, traps, and field equipment suited to extended movement. Their gear often reflects the terrain in which they learned their craft. Rangers adventure to explore dangerous regions, hunt monsters or enemy operatives, guide expeditions, secure routes, protect remote communities, or prove that no battlefield is truly open ground when preparation and range are on their side. text: WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Advancement, Feats & Boons Universal Level 1–20 advancement, ASI/Feat choices, Universal Feats, and Empyrean Boons. Character-management workflow on this page is synchronized to Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.13 — CHARACTER_MANAGER_SYNC . The full current rules remain authoritative if any website summary differs. Universal Character Advancement What to Do Every Time You Level Up ASI / Feat Choices Universal Feats — Full Player Explanations Empyrean Boons Specialization Reassignment Universal Character Advancement Level PB Flight Slots Exploration Flight Inventory Universal Note 1 +2 2 1 min / 30 ft 15 Class progression 2 +2 2 1 min / 30 ft 15 Class progression 3 +2 2 3 min / 50 ft 15 Specialization begins for most classes 4 +2 3 3 min / 50 ft 15 ASI/Feat 5 +3 3 4 min / 70 ft 15 Class progression 6 +3 3 4 min / 70 ft 15 Class progression 7 +3 4 4 min / 70 ft 20 Class progression 8 +3 4 6 min / 100 ft 20 ASI/Feat 9 +4 4 6 min / 100 ft 20 Class progression 10 +4 5 8 min / 120 ft 20 Class progression; Daeva Points and Ultimate Ability 11 +4 5 8 min / 120 ft 20 Class progression 12 +4 5 8 min / 120 ft 20 ASI/Feat 13 +5 6 10 min / 140 ft 20 Class progression 14 +5 6 10 min / 140 ft 25 Class progression 15 +5 6 10 min / 140 ft 25 Class progression; Ultimate improvement 16 +5 6 12 min / 160 ft 25 ASI/Feat 17 +6 7 12 min / 160 ft 25 Class progression 18 +6 7 15 min / 180 ft 30 Class progression 19 +6 7 15 min / 180 ft 30 Empyrean Boon 20 +6 8 15 min / 180 ft 30 Class capstone; Apex Ultimate Leveling Rule. Advancement is milestone-only. Level 20 is the maximum normal level. There is no automatic post-Level-20 progression, recurring ASIs, additional class levels or recurring Boons. What to Do Every Time You Level Up • Read the full class-level entry and every specialization feature gained at that level. • Increase maximum HP using the class's fixed HP gain, CON modifier and class durability rules. • Update PB only if the universal table changes it. • Update class resource caps, dice, ranges, trap limits, spirit/Bastion chassis or other scaling. • Make an ASI/Feat choice if the level grants one. • Apply Spell Advancements if your class grants them, using the spell advancement rules. • Update Flight Slots, Exploration Flight and Inventory Slots. • Recalculate class Save DC, spell attack, AC, passive values and PB/ability-dependent features. • If you are changing your Active Profession, make that change now; Active Profession changes are allowed only when you gain a character level. Character Manager. Apply level-up choices and resulting character-state changes in the Wings of Atreia Character Manager after resolving the governing class and advancement rules. The rules determine what changes; the Character Manager records and tracks the resulting character state. ASI / Feat Choices Whenever your class grants a Feat / Ability Score Improvement, choose one: +2 to one Ability Score; +1 to two different Ability Scores; or one eligible Universal Feat. An Ability Score normally cannot exceed 20 through an ASI. Level Choice 4 ASI or Universal Feat 8 ASI or Universal Feat 12 ASI or Universal Feat 16 ASI or Universal Feat 19 Empyrean Boon; not a normal ASI Universal Feats — Full Player Explanations Feat Prerequisite Exact Benefit Player Use Alert None +2 Initiative. You cannot be Surprised while conscious. Acting early and staying ready. Skilled None Gain proficiency in two Skills. Duplicate proficiency must be replaced with another choice. Broader exploration/social competence. Expertise Proficient in chosen Skill Double PB contribution for one proficient Skill. Doubling effects do not stack. One signature highly reliable skill. Keen Senses None +2 passive Perception and passive Investigation. Active checks unchanged. Notice threats and clues passively. Mobile None Walking Speed +10 ft. Dash ignores extra cost of Difficult Terrain for that turn. Does not increase Flight. Ground repositioning. Sure-Footed None Advantage on checks/saves specifically to resist being knocked Prone by terrain, hazards or forced movement. Defensive stability. Weapon Specialist Access/proficiency with chosen weapon Choose one weapon. Once per turn before an attack roll with it, you may gain +2 to that attack roll. Reliability on one key weapon hit. Tough None HP maximum increases by 2 × character level when selected, then +2 each later level. Durability. Resilient Level 8 Choose a saving throw you lack proficiency in; gain proficiency. Patch a defensive weakness. Aerial Endurance Level 16 +2 maximum Flight Slot. Longer aerial combat. Controlled Descent None Successful DC 12 DEX Emergency Landing save causes 0 falling damage instead of half. Safer forced landing. Master Glider None Exploration Glide ratio improves 3:1 → 4:1. 1-hour cooldown remains. Exploration mobility. Aerial Conditioning None First grounded Flight Slot recovery after becoming airborne restores 2 instead of 1; reset by becoming airborne again. Faster combat recovery. Aether Adept None Choose Arcana or Sleight of Hand; gain proficiency if needed. 1/Long Rest reroll a failed Aether Interaction check using it. General Aether specialist. Aether Stabilizer None 1/Long Rest after failing a qualifying Arcana/Sleight of Hand stabilization/suppression/deactivation/repair check, add 1d6 to the failed check. Technical Aether specialist. Empyrean Boons Boon Frequency Benefit Transcendence Permanent Increase one Ability Score by 2; chosen score may reach 22. The Unbroken 1 / Long Rest When qualifying damage would reduce you to 0 HP without outright killing you, remain at 1 HP. The Relentless Once on each of your turns +2d8 damage from one attack or qualifying class feature; bonus dice do not double on Critical Hit. The Unbound Sky Permanent +1 maximum Flight Slot and grounded combat Flight Slot recovery becomes +2 per round; never bypasses Aether/flight restrictions. Aetheric Mastery Permanent Aether-focused Arcana/Sleight of Hand access, +2 on Aether Interaction checks, and basic awareness of current Aether State. Fate 1 / Short or Long Rest After failing a saving throw, reroll and use the new result. Cannot reroll a Death Saving Throw. Specialization Reassignment Initial choice — Level 3. Choose one Specialization available to your class. Reassignment checkpoints — Levels 6, 10, and 14. When gaining one of these levels, you may either continue your current Specialization or change to another Specialization available to your class. If you change Specialization, remove every feature granted by the previous Specialization and replace it with the complete feature package of the newly selected Specialization through your current checkpoint . Features from different Specializations cannot be mixed, retained, or combined. When newly entering a Specialization, make any choices required by the features you now gain. Continuing the same Specialization does not reset earlier internal choices unless an explicit feature says otherwise. If the removed Specialization granted extra known options, selections, capacities, or Specialization-dependent maxima, remove, reselect, or recalculate them as necessary to satisfy the new path. Reassignment itself does not restore HP or class resources, and current values cannot remain above any new maximum. Reassignment occurs only as part of gaining Level 6, Level 10, or Level 14 . It cannot be performed through a rest, downtime, training, ordinary retraining, or between adventures. The Level 14 decision is the final normal Specialization choice and remains locked through Level 20 unless a later explicit rule says otherwise. ← Back to Rules Wings of Atreia · Created & Designed by Clark Michael Zafra (“ArchQwynn”) · Non-commercial fan project.

title: Advantage and Disadvantage
desc: Advantage and Disadvantage — Wings of Atreia reference section.
text: Advantage and Disadvantage. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Core Resolution The d20 test framework used for meaningful uncertain outcomes. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. d20 Tests & Core Resolution d20 Tests Ability Checks Saving Throws Save DCs Advantage and Disadvantage Help Passive Perception, Passive Investigation & Search d20 Tests & Core Resolution d20 Tests Ability Checks, attack rolls, and saving throws use a d20. Roll only when the outcome is uncertain and meaningful. If success is automatic, impossible, or consequence-free, no roll is needed. Ability Checks Choose the ability that best fits the approach, then add Proficiency Bonus if the character is proficient in the relevant skill. Expertise doubles the PB contribution for that proficiency. WoA retains six abilities and eighteen skills. A specialized Background can authorize a character to attempt obscure knowledge, but it does not automatically modify the roll. Saving Throws A saving throw uses the specified ability modifier and adds PB only if the creature is proficient in that saving throw. Ties are resolved according to the specific system; otherwise meeting a DC succeeds. Save DCs Default effect Save DC = 8 + Proficiency Bonus + the relevant ability modifier, unless an explicit class, spell, item, monster, or environmental rule gives a different DC. Advantage and Disadvantage When a rule grants Advantage, roll two d20s and use the higher. When it grants Disadvantage, roll two and use the lower. If both apply, they cancel unless a specific rule says otherwise. Resolve Advantage/Disadvantage before applying numeric modifiers. Help Help never grants Advantage. A meaningful helper grants +2 to one Ability Check. Normally only one helper can contribute. There is no Assist Attack and Help cannot modify Death Saves. Passive Perception, Passive Investigation & Search Passive Perception = 10 + your Wisdom (Perception) modifier. Passive Investigation = 10 + your Intelligence (Investigation) modifier. Advantage on the relevant check adds +5 to the passive score; Disadvantage subtracts 5. Multiple instances of the same source do not stack, and Advantage and Disadvantage cancel normally. Hide is opposed by Passive Perception; ties favor the observer. An active Search uses the GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation), against the relevant DC or opposing Stealth; ties favor the Searcher where opposed. Repeated checks require a meaningful change in circumstances. ← Back to Rules Wings of Atreia · Created & Designed by Clark Michael Zafra (“ArchQwynn”) · Non-commercial fan project.

text: Aerial Rescue. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Flight Exploration flight, Combat Flight Slots, airborne movement, gliding, falling, and Aether restrictions. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Flight & Aerial Combat Altitude Layers 3D Distance Melee Descending Attack Physical Ranged Attacks Flight Slots Aether State Interaction Flight & Aerial Combat Altitude Layers Layer Height Access Low 30 ft All functional Wings Mid 60 ft All functional Wings High 90 ft All functional Wings Legendary 120 ft Legendary Wings only Ground level is 0 feet and is not an altitude layer. There are four airborne altitude layers: Low (30 ft), Mid (60 ft), High (90 ft), and Legendary (120 ft). Voluntarily ascending or descending one altitude layer consumes all movement for that turn. A creature cannot both ascend and descend voluntarily in the same turn. Dash does not permit an additional altitude-layer change. A Daeva without Legendary Wings cannot voluntarily ascend above the High layer at 90 feet. 3D Distance For WoA aerial targeting, total distance = the greater of horizontal distance or vertical distance. Do not use Pythagorean distance and do not add horizontal and vertical distance together. Melee Airborne melee uses ordinary reach: usually 5 feet, or 10 feet for a Reach weapon. Being on the same altitude layer does not remove the need to physically move into reach. Descending Attack If a melee attacker begins its turn higher than the target, descends at least 25 feet, and then makes its first qualifying melee attack against that lower target, the attack has Advantage. Physical Ranged Attacks Universal Close-Range Rule. If the target of a physical ranged weapon attack is within 5 feet of the attacker, the attack roll has Disadvantage. This applies whether the attacker is grounded or airborne and does not change the weapon’s listed Normal Range or Maximum Range. A lower-altitude physical ranged attacker has Advantage against a higher-altitude winged airborne target because the wings are exposed. This Exposed Wings rule does not apply to wingless creatures flying through Saturated Aether. A higher-altitude ranged attacker gains no automatic Advantage merely for being above the target. When the physical ranged attacker is above the target, increase only the weapon’s Maximum Range by half the vertical distance, rounded up. The weapon’s Normal Range is unchanged. Magical attacks do not gain this extension. Flight Slots Level Base Max Slots 1–3 2 4–6 3 7–9 4 10–12 5 13–16 6 17–19 7 20 8 A stable airborne Daeva spends 1 Flight Slot at the end of each of its turns. A grounded Daeva recovers 1 Flight Slot at the end of each grounded turn. Short Rest restores half maximum, rounded down; Long Rest restores all. When a creature runs out of Flight Slots while airborne, it immediately falls. Aether State Interaction Depleted Aether. Flight is fully restricted. Stable Aether. Normal flight rules. Saturated Aether. Daevas spend no combat Flight Slots, though exploration Flight Time limits still apply. Wingless creatures capable of movement may gain flight equal to normal Speed while Saturated; they do not use Flight Slots and are not subject to Exposed Wings. Unstable Zone / Aether Instability. This is hazard-defined scene behavior rather than a universal Aether State. The three universal States are Stable, Depleted, and Saturated. Use the specific Aether Hazard rules for the area. Aether-State Changes and Boundaries Aether-State changes take effect immediately. Crossing into a new Aether State immediately applies the entered State. In Depleted Aether, Aether-supported flight is unavailable; an airborne Daeva entering a Depleted area loses flight and falls, using the normal DC 12 Dexterity Emergency Landing Reaction if eligible. Saturated → Stable: Daevas resume normal Flight Slot expenditure. A creature flying only because Saturated Aether granted it flight loses that flight and falls. Saturated → Depleted: affected airborne creatures immediately lose Aether-supported flight and fall. Stable → Saturated: Daevas stop spending Combat Flight Slots, and eligible wingless creatures gain access to Aether-supported flight equal to normal Speed, but no creature automatically takes off. Falling and Emergency Landing Falling damage is 1d6 per 10 feet fallen, maximum 20d6. A falling creature normally lands Prone unless an explicit effect says otherwise. When Flight Slot depletion causes a fall, the creature may use its Reaction for a DC 12 Dexterity save. Success halves fall damage; failure or no Reaction takes full damage. Controlled Descent changes a successful Emergency Landing to 0 fall damage according to that feat. Falling Onto Creatures The lower creature makes a DC 12 Dexterity save. On success it avoids the collision and the falling creature takes norma

title: Aether & Spellcasting | Wings of Atreia
desc: Aether environment and interaction, universal spellcasting, and Spell Advancement.
text: WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Aether & Spellcasting Aether environment and interaction, universal spellcasting, and Spell Advancement. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Aether Environment, Interaction & Gathering Aether Interaction Aether Sources Refined Aether Gathering Aether Hazards Universal Spellcasting Universal Model Spell Acquisition Aether Environment, Interaction & Gathering Aether Interaction Aether Interaction uses Intelligence (Arcana) for intellectual analysis and Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) for physical manipulation. Typical DC guidance is 10, 12, 15, 18, or 20+ according to complexity and danger. Aether Sources Nodes, Currents, Fissures, and other environmental Aether phenomena can provide opportunities, hazards, travel effects, or Refined Aether. Their exact scene behavior is defined by the source. Refined Aether Gathering Gathering Refined Aether uses Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) against the source DC. Aether Level DC Yield Range Default Yield 1 8 2–6 4 2 10 6–12 9 3 12 12–24 18 4 15 24–40 32 5 18 40–60 50 The GM identifies a valid source and its Aether Level. Only the interacting character rolls. Apply normal modifiers and Help only if actually meaningful. On success, gain a yield within the listed range based on source richness; if no special richness is established, use the Default Yield. A successful gathering normally exhausts that source. Multiple deposits exist only when the GM explicitly establishes them. Failure gives no Refined Aether and does not automatically exhaust the source, but a new attempt requires a meaningful change in circumstances. Another party member does not automatically create a fresh attempt. Normal gathering is not performed during active combat unless gathering itself is an explicit encounter objective. Already-refined Aether recovered from caches or stores is ordinary loot and requires no gathering check. Aether Hazards Aether Hazards use the universal sequence Trigger → Save → DC → Effect → Duration. Standard severity bands are Minor DC 10–11, Moderate DC 12–14, Severe DC 15–17, and Extreme DC 18–20+. The four approved hazard families are Aether Storm, Aether Surge, Aether Eruption, and Unstable Zone. Each specific hazard defines its actual Trigger, Save, Effect, and Duration. Dangerous Aether changes are normally telegraphed in advance unless the hazard is specifically concealed. Strategic Refined Aether uses not defined in this handbook are deferred unless a future subsystem explicitly establishes them. Vehicle-related Refined Aether rules remain deferred with vehicle rules, and the current Abyss Warfront system uses no universal Refined Aether conversion for Fortress power. Universal Spellcasting Universal Model WoA has no spell slots and no cantrip category. Each spell is individually At-Will, Cooldown-based, Short-Rest limited, or Long-Rest limited. Class resources may modify spells but are not universal casting costs. Spell Acquisition Spells are class-granted abilities. They cannot be bought, sold, looted, copied from spellbooks or scrolls, learned from vendors, or acquired by commerce or exploration. A spell becomes available only when the character reaches its Unlock Level and, when applicable, satisfies the immediately preceding spell in its linear prerequisite chain. Unlocking a later spell never removes the earlier spell. Newly unlocked spells begin at Spell Level 1 unless explicitly stated otherwise. Spell Advancement — Final Rule. A class grants Spell Advancements according to its finalized progression. One Spell Advancement raises one eligible unlocked spell by 1 Spell Level, subject to that class’s Maximum Spell Level and listed prerequisites. Unspent Spell Advancements may be banked indefinitely, but banked or newly earned Spell Advancements may be spent only when the character gains a level; they cannot normally be spent during an adventure, between encounters, or during a rest. A character cannot spend more Spell Advancements than they have earned. Spell Retraining. There is no universal spell retraining. Once a Spell Advancement is spent, it is permanent unless a specific class feature, explicit story effect, or GM-approved exceptional circumstance directly permits reassignment. Casting Frequency and Action Economy At-Will spells may be cast whenever action economy permits. Cooldown X spells become available at the start of the caster’s Xth turn after the casting turn. Round-based cooldowns advance only during genuine combat; artificial Initiative cannot refresh, farm, or manipulate cooldowns or class resources. Outside genuine combat, a Cooldown spell becomes available again 1 minute after use unless the spell states a longer restriction. Short-Rest and Long-Rest spells regain uses after the named rest. Casting Time is binding. Casting multiple spells in one turn is allowed only when the character actually has the required Actions and no class or spell restriction forbids it. Wings of Atreia has no universal D&D bonus-action-spell restriction. Spellcasting Classes The finalized spellcasting classes are Sorcerer, Spiritmaster, Cleric, Chanter, and Songweaver. This handbook integrates the complete 106-spell library: Sorcerer 24, Spiritmaster 22, Cleric 20, Chanter 16, and Songweaver 24. Required Implements and Components Sorcerer. Must have an equipped Magical Orb or Spellbook. Spiritmaster. Must have an equipped Magical Orb or Spellbook. Songweaver. Must have an equipped Lute or Lyre. Cleric. No mandatory casting implement. Chanter. No mandatory casting implement. Narrative speech, gestures, music, prayer, or Aetheric movements may describe casting but are not universal mechanical components. Merely being unable to speak or hear does not automatically prevent casting. There are no universal component pouches, reagent costs, gemstones, Refined Aether costs, or Kinah costs unless the particular effect explicitly says so. Required Implement Loss. A required implement must be equipped and usable according to its hand requirement; merely carrying it is insufficient. Losing, dropping, stowing, being disarmed of, or otherwise unequipping a required implement prevents only new spells and class features that require that implement until an appropriate implement is equipped again. It does not disable the rest of the class, automatically end a spell already successfully cast, or automatically dismiss an already-summoned Spirit unless the specific spell or class feature explicitly requires continued implement use. Casting and Conditions A creature cannot cast if an existing Condition prevents the required Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction. Incapacitated, and therefore Stunned/Paralyzed/Unconscious when they include Incapacitated, prevents casting. Grappled, Restrained, Prone, Blinded, or Deafened do not automatically prevent casting, though individual targeting or implement requirements may make a spell impossible. Spell Interruption Once a spell is legally used, it resolves normally unless an explicit Reaction, feature, Condition, or effect interrupts or prevents it. Ordinary damage never creates a universal spell-interruption check. Concentration Concentration does not use checks or saving throws as a general mechanic. A creature can maintain only one Concentration effect at a time. Beginning another Concentration effect immediately ends the previous one. Damage, attacks, forced movement, falling, and similar events do not test Concentration. Concentration ends when the creature becomes Incapacitated, voluntarily ends it, begins another Concentration effect, or an explicit rule says the Concentration ends. Spell Resolution Rules Spell Attacks and Saves. Spell Attack = Proficiency Bonus + the class’s spellcasting ability modifier. Spell Save DC = 8 + Proficiency Bonus + that ability modifier. Sorcerer, Spiritmaster, and Chanter use Intelligence; Cleric uses Wisdom; Songweaver uses Charisma for spells. Class features that use another ability retain their own rule. Effect-Removal Check DC. When Aether Dispel, a Cleric Purification Check, or another effect explicitly calls for a check against a hostile magical or removable effect’s DC, use that effect’s listed save DC, removal DC, or feature DC when one exists. If no applicable DC is listed, use DC 15. A spell that supplies its own different DC uses that value. Successfully Affect. For hostile spell interactions, a spell Successfully Affects a creature if the creature takes damage, is hit, fails a save, or suffers a meaningful hostile Condition, penalty, forced movement, or other combat effect. Harmless targeting, immunity, or an effect that changes nothing does not count. Area Resolution. Unless stated otherwise, each creature in an area rolls its own save once per application. A creature is affected only if its space intersects the spell area and Line of Effect exists. Cover and Line of Effect. Half Cover applies normally to spell attacks and Dexterity saving throws. Full Cover blocks the relevant Line of Effect and therefore blocks the spell unless the spell explicitly says otherwise. Origin, range, and Cover are measured from the caster unless a class feature explicitly changes the origin. Self-Range Projection. A Self-range spell cannot be projected from another creature or Spirit unless a rule explicitly allows it. Critical Hits. When a spell attack critically hits, double all damage dice rolled as part of that attack, including direct spell riders. Independent later damage, zones, damage-over-time ticks, and separate trap or Spirit effects do not double unless explicitly part of the Critical Hit. Damage-over-Time and Repeated Zones. A creature normally takes a spell’s repeated damage no more than once per turn from that casting unless the spell explicitly says otherwise. A creature cannot repeatedly enter and leave the same area during one turn to multiply a once-per-turn effect. Suppression vs. Ending. Ending a spell removes it. Suppression pauses its mechanics while its duration continues. When suppression ends, the spell resumes if duration remains. Stacking. Multiple copies of the same named spell on the same creature do not stack unless the spell says otherwise; use the strongest applicable numeric effect. Different named spells stack unless a class or global rule says they do not. Flat class-feature save or attack penalties do not stack unless explicitly stated. Cooldown Terminology. The legacy term “1-Round Cooldown” means Cooldown 2: after use, the spell is unavailable on the caster’s next turn and becomes available again on the following turn. A class feature that permits an At-Will or 1-Round-Cooldown spell therefore permits an eligible, currently available Cooldown 2 spell; it does not permit Cooldown 3 unless explicitly stated. Restoration of Uses. Short-Rest-limited spells recover after a completed Short or Long Rest. Long-Rest-limited spells recover only after a Long Rest. A rest cannot be repeatedly interrupted or manufactured solely to farm uses contrary to genuine play. NPCs and Monsters. NPC and monster spell-like abilities may use simplified statblock recharge rules. Player spell-access and Spell Advancement rules apply only to player-class spellcasting unless a creature explicitly uses a player class. Repeatable Healing Safeguard At-Will or Cooldown healing used outside genuine combat can restore a target only up to half maximum HP unless an explicit exception says otherwise. This prevents artificial noncombat cycling from replacing rest and finite recovery. Final Spellcasting Progression Sorcerer, Spiritmaster, Cleric, and Songweaver cap at Spell Level 9: SL1 at character level 1; SL2 at levels 2–3; SL3 at 4–5; SL4 at 6–7; SL5 at 8–9; SL6 at 10–11; SL7 at 12–13; SL8 at 14–16; SL9 at 17–20. Each gains +2 Spell Advancements at every level after Lev

text: Aether Core. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Bastion Pilot • Aether Core • Heat • Adaptive Weapons Combat Aethertech “Steel, meet face. Face, meet steel.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. On this page Overview Chassis Core Mechanics Action Reference Specializations Progression Examples ↑ Top The Aethertech fights from one piloted Large Bastion platform. The pilot and Bastion are one character’s action economy, not two independent turns. The class alternates between integrated Bastion armaments, Aether Core expenditures, controlled Heat accumulation, venting, repairs, and system integration. The Bastion is a separate physical HP pool that enemies can damage without directly healing or harming the pilot unless an effect specifically targets the pilot. Class Identity Aethertechs are technist warriors who channel Aether through a Bastion: a magical-mechanical combat platform that transforms how the Daeva occupies the battlefield. The class combines personal skill, engineered systems, heavy protection, and controlled bursts of power. Aether Core and Heat represent the constant balance between available energy and the strain created by pushing the Bastion harder. Tradition & Outlook Aethertech is a comparatively modern Daeva discipline born from the recovery, study, and weaponization of advanced magical technology. The wider Aion tradition connects the class to Daeva analysis of Danuar technology and the lessons surrounding Hyperion; Wings of Atreia preserves that technological identity while its own campaign chronology and mechanics remain authoritative. Aethertechs often value ingenuity, technical discipline, experimentation, and the belief that knowledge taken from dangerous enemies can be turned toward Atreia’s defense. Appearance & Adventuring An Aethertech is visually defined by the Bastion and the contrast between a Daeva operator and an imposing Aether-powered war platform. Outside it, the Aethertech remains a trained combatant using the class’s approved weapons and equipment. Aethertechs adventure to recover technology, test designs under real conditions, oppose Balaur war machines, protect expeditions with a durable mobile platform, or prove that engineering can stand beside sword and spell as a heroic discipline. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Ability Intelligence Secondary Ability Constitution Hit Die d8 Saving Throws Intelligence, Constitution Armor Chain Armor Skills Choose 2 from 6: Arcana, Athletics, Investigation, Perception, Sleight of Hand, Survival Weapons Shortswords, Maces, Hammers Signature Resources Aether Core and Heat Signature Mechanic Piloted Bastion Bastion Size Large Class Save DC 8 + PB + INT modifier Extra Attack Level 5; two Bastion weapon attacks only Spellcasting None Bastion Targeting and Chassis The pilot and Bastion have separate HP and temporary HP. Repairs restore Bastion HP and are not healing. While occupied, ordinary physical attacks targeting the Aethertech generally strike the Bastion first. Mental, emotional, biological, and similar effects target the pilot when appropriate. One area effect normally does not double-hit both pilot and Bastion. Bastion physical STR/DEX/CON saves use PB + INT modifier. Mental saves use the pilot’s relevant save. When the Bastion reaches 0 HP it is Disabled. The pilot is ejected to the nearest legal space, takes 1d6 Force damage, and does not provoke Opportunity Attacks from the ejection. A disabled Bastion retains its current Core and Heat; a fresh chassis does not replace it. A Short Rest repairs a Disabled or damaged Bastion by half its maximum HP. A Long Rest repairs the Bastion to its maximum HP. These restorations are repairs, not healing. Once the Bastion has at least 1 HP, it is operational. Entering or re-entering a deployed Bastion uses an Action when otherwise legal. A defeated or voluntarily replaced Bastion never functions as a companion or second PC. Contesting STR checks with the Bastion e.g Grapple, pushing, pulling, except for skill or ability effects, will have the PC use this formula: 1d20+8+INT modifier+PB considering that a Bastion is a Large entity. Target must contest with their choice of Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics). Level Band Bastion AC Bastion Maximum HP 1–4 11 + PB 8 + (5 × Aethertech level) + INT 5–10 12 + PB 8 + (5 × level) + INT 11–17 13 + PB 12 + (6 × level) + INT 18–20 13 + PB 16 + (7 × level) + INT Whenever a chassis improvement raises maximum HP, increase current Bastion HP by the same amount; this is a maximum-HP adjustment rather than healing. Bastion Weapon Synchronization While piloting a Bastion, designate one eligible carried weapon with which you are proficient as your Synchronized Weapon. A Bastion weapon attack roll is 1d20 + PB + INT modifier + the Synchronized Weapon's current equipment-quality bonus to Hit

text: Aether Disturbance. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Ranged Striker • Focus • Traps • Tactical Repositioning Ranger “Chase me or run away. Either way, you'll only die tired.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Focus Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Ranger is a nonmagical ranged hunter that controls enemy movement with persistent battlefield traps, spends Focus on precision or evasive shots, and is rewarded for exploiting targets that walk into prepared terrain. Its sustained damage comes from two ranged attacks, not from spellcasting or a third standard attack. Class Identity Rangers are mobile ranged specialists who control distance through marksmanship, movement, traps, and battlefield awareness. They are most effective when they can read terrain before committing, choose favorable lines of attack, and punish enemies that approach carelessly. Focus represents the Ranger’s ability to convert patience and perception into precise action. Tradition & Outlook The Ranger tradition also descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines, but where Assassins close with a chosen target, Rangers cultivate distance, fieldcraft, and control of the approach. Rangers are common among scouts, hunters, pathfinders, border wardens, reconnaissance troops, and independent Daevas accustomed to surviving beyond secure settlements. They tend to value preparedness, observation, mobility, and freedom of movement. Appearance & Adventuring Rangers usually wear mobile armor and carry bows, ammunition, traps, and field equipment suited to extended movement. Their gear often reflects the terrain in which they learned their craft. Rangers adventure to explore dangerous regions, hunt monsters or enemy operatives, guide expeditions, secure routes, protect remote communities, or prove that no battlefield is truly open ground when preparation and range are on their side. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Ability Dexterity Secondary Ability Wisdom Hit Die d10 Saving Throws Dexterity, Strength Armor Leather Armor Weapons Longbows, Shortbows, Crossbows Skills Choose 2 from 6: Animal Handling, Athletics, Investigation, Nature, Perception, Survival Class Save DC 8 + PB + WIS modifier Signature Resource Focus Signature Mechanic Ranger Traps Extra Attack Level 5; two attacks only Spellcasting None Core Engine — Focus Maximum Focus equals your PB + WIS modifier, minimum 2. A Long Rest restores all expended Focus. A Short Rest restores Focus equal to PB, up to your maximum. Focus is a tactical reserve rather than ammunition or a tax on ordinary ranged attacks; Ranger Traps normally cost no Focus. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Starting State Focus is a rest-based reserve and does not reset merely because combat begins or ends. After a Long Rest it is normally full. Maximum PB + WIS modifier, minimum 2. Rest Recovery Long Rest restores all expended Focus. Short Rest restores Focus equal to PB, up to your maximum. Combat Recovery Hunter’s Rhythm and certain later Ranger/specialization features can regain Focus during genuine combat when their tactical conditions are actually satisfied. How You Spend It Precision Shot 1 Focus; Pinning Shot 1 Focus; Evasive Step 1 Focus; Deadeye Perfect Shot 1 Focus. Other Ranger features spend Focus only when their text states a cost. Refunds / Recovery A combat refund or recovery is not a new attack, trap trigger, or separate technique. It simply restores Focus up to your maximum. Persistence Unused Focus persists between encounters until spent or restored; there is no automatic combat-end reset. Does Not Generate Standing still and firing, harmless staged interactions, or ordinary trap placement do not create Focus unless an explicit recovery feature is actually triggered.
