text: Aether Environment, Interaction & Gathering. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Aether & Spellcasting Aether environment and interaction, universal spellcasting, and Spell Advancement. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Aether Environment, Interaction & Gathering Aether Interaction Aether Sources Refined Aether Gathering Aether Hazards Universal Spellcasting Universal Model Spell Acquisition Aether Environment, Interaction & Gathering Aether Interaction Aether Interaction uses Intelligence (Arcana) for intellectual analysis and Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) for physical manipulation. Typical DC guidance is 10, 12, 15, 18, or 20+ according to complexity and danger. Aether Sources Nodes, Currents, Fissures, and other environmental Aether phenomena can provide opportunities, hazards, travel effects, or Refined Aether. Their exact scene behavior is defined by the source. Refined Aether Gathering Gathering Refined Aether uses Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) against the source DC. Aether Level DC Yield Range Default Yield 1 8 2–6 4 2 10 6–12 9 3 12 12–24 18 4 15 24–40 32 5 18 40–60 50 The GM identifies a valid source and its Aether Level. Only the interacting character rolls. Apply normal modifiers and Help only if actually meaningful. On success, gain a yield within the listed range based on source richness; if no special richness is established, use the Default Yield. A successful gathering normally exhausts that source. Multiple deposits exist only when the GM explicitly establishes them. Failure gives no Refined Aether and does not automatically exhaust the source, but a new attempt requires a meaningful change in circumstances. Another party member does not automatically create a fresh attempt. Normal gathering is not performed during active combat unless gathering itself is an explicit encounter objective. Already-refined Aether recovered from caches or stores is ordinary loot and requires no gathering check. Aether Hazards Aether Hazards use the universal sequence Trigger → Save → DC → Effect → Duration. Standard severity bands are Minor DC 10–11, Moderate DC 12–14, Severe DC 15–17, and Extreme DC 18–20+. The four approved hazard families are Aether Storm, Aether Surge, Aether Eruption, and Unstable Zone. Each specific hazard defines its actual Trigger, Save, Effect, and Duration. Dangerous Aether changes are normally telegraphed in advance unless the hazard is specifically concealed. Strategic Refined Aether uses not defined in this handbook are deferred unless a future subsystem explicitly establishes them. Vehicle-related Refined Aether rules remain deferred with vehicle rules, and the current Abyss Warfront system uses no universal Refined Aether conversion for Fortress power. Universal Spellcasting Universal Model WoA has no spell slots and no cantrip category. Each spell is individually At-Will, Cooldown-based, Short-Rest limited, or Long-Rest limited. Class resources may modify spells but are not universal casting costs. Spell Acquisition Spells are class-granted abilities. They cannot be bought, sold, looted, copied from spellbooks or scrolls, learned from vendors, or acquired by commerce or exploration. A spell becomes available only when the character reaches its Unlock Level and, when applicable, satisfies the immediately preceding spell in its linear prerequisite chain. Unlocking a later spell never removes the earlier spell. Newly unlocked spells begin at Spell Level 1 unless explicitly stated otherwise. Spell Advancement — Final Rule. A class grants Spell Advancements according to its finalized progression. One Spell Advancement raises one eligible unlocked spell by 1 Spell Level, subject to that class’s Maximum Spell Level and listed prerequisites. Unspent Spell Advancements may be banked indefinitely, but banked or newly earned Spell Advancements may be spent only when the character gains a level; they cannot normally be spent during an adventure, between encounters, or during a rest. A character cannot spend more Spell Advancements than they have earned. Spell Retraining. There is no universal spell retraining. Once a Spell Advancement is spent, it is permanent unless a specific class feature, explicit story effect, or GM-approved exceptional circumstance directly permits reassignment. Casting Frequency and Action Economy At-Will spells may be cast whenever action economy permits. Cooldown X spells become available at the start of the caster’s Xth turn after the casting turn. Round-based cooldowns advance only during genuine combat; artificial Initiative cannot refresh, farm, or manipulate cooldowns or class resources. Outside genuine combat, a Cooldown spell becomes available again 1 minute after use unless the spell states a longer restriction. Short-Rest and Long-Rest spells regain uses after the named rest

Aether Level DC Yield Range Default Yield 1 8 2–6 4 2 10 6–12 9 3 12 12–24 18 4 15 24–40 32 5 18 40–60 50 The GM identifies a valid source and its Aether Level. Only the interacting character rolls. Apply normal modifiers and Help only if actually meaningful. On success, gain a yield within the listed range based on source richness; if no special richness is established, use the Default Yield. A successful gathering normally exhausts that source. Multiple deposits exist only when the GM explicitly establishes them. Failure gives no Refined Aether and does not automatically exhaust the source, but a new attempt requires a meaningful change in circumstances. Another party member does not automatically create a fresh attempt. Normal gathering is not performed during active combat unless gathering itself is an explicit encounter objective. Already-refined Aether recovered from caches or stores is ordinary loot and requires no gathering check. Aether Hazards Aether Hazards use the universal sequence Trigger → Save → DC → Effect → Duration. Standard severity bands are Minor DC 10–11, Moderate DC 12–14, Severe DC 15–17, and Extreme DC 18–20+. The four approved hazard families are Aether Storm, Aether Surge, Aether Eruption, and Unstable Zone. Each specific hazard defines its actual Trigger, Save, Effect, and Duration. Dangerous Aether changes are normally telegraphed in advance unless the hazard is specifically concealed. Strategic Refined Aether uses not defined in this handbook are deferred unless a future subsystem explicitly establishes them. Vehicle-related Refined Aether rules remain deferred with vehicle rules, and the current Abyss Warfront system uses no universal Refined Aether conversion for Fortress power. Universal Spellcasting Universal Model WoA has no spell slots and no cantrip category. Each spell is individually At-Will, Cooldown-based, Short-Rest limited, or Long-Rest limited. Class resources may modify spells but are not universal casting costs. Spell Acquisition Spells are class-granted abilities. They cannot be bought, sold, looted, copied from spellbooks or scrolls, learned from vendors, or acquired by commerce or exploration. A spell becomes available only when the character reaches its Unlock Level and, when applicable, satisfies the immediately preceding spell in its linear prerequisite chain. Unlocking a later spell never removes the earlier spell. Newly unlocked spells begin at Spell Level 1 unless explicitly stated otherwise. Spell Advancement — Final Rule. A class grants Spell Advancements according to its finalized progression. One Spell Advancement raises one eligible unlocked spell by 1 Spell Level, subject to that class’s Maximum Spell Level and listed prerequisites. Unspent Spell Advancements may be banked indefinitely, but banked or newly earned Spell Advancements may be spent only when the character gains a level; they cannot normally be spent during an adventure, between encounters, or during a rest. A character cannot spend more Spell Advancements than they have earned. Spell Retraining. There is no universal spell retraining. Once a Spell Advancement is spent, it is permanent unless a specific class feature, explicit story effect, or GM-approved exceptional circumstance directly permits reassignment. Casting Frequency and Action Economy At-Will spells may be cast whenever action economy permits. Cooldown X spells become available at the start of the caster’s Xth turn after the casting turn. Round-based cooldowns advance only during genuine combat; artificial Initiative cannot refresh, farm, or manipulate cooldowns or class resources. Outside genuine combat, a Cooldown spell becomes available again 1 minute after use unless the spell states a longer restriction. Short-Rest and Long-Rest spells regain uses after the named rest. Flight & Aerial Combat Altitude Layers 3D Distance Melee Descending Attack Physical Ranged Attacks Flight Slots Aether State Interaction Flight & Aerial Combat Altitude Layers Layer Height Access Low 30 ft All functional Wings Mid 60 ft All functional Wings High 90 ft All functional Wings Legendary 120 ft Legendary Wings only Ground level is 0 feet and is not an altitude layer. There are four airborne altitude layers: Low (30 ft), Mid (60 ft), High (90 ft), and Legendary (120 ft). Voluntarily ascending or descending one altitude layer consumes all movement for that turn. A creature cannot both ascend and descend voluntarily in the same turn. Dash does not permit an additional altitude-layer change. A Daeva without Legendary Wings cannot voluntarily ascend above the High layer at 90 feet. 3D Distance For WoA aerial targeting, total distance = the greater of horizontal distance or vertical distance. Do not use Pythagorean distance and do not add horizontal and vertical distance together. Melee Airborne melee uses ordinary reach: usually 5 feet, or 10 feet for a Reach weapon. Being on the same altitude layer does not remove the need to physically move into reach. Descending Attack If a melee attacker begins its turn higher than the target, descends at least 25 feet, and then makes its first qualifying melee attack against that lower target, the attack has Advantage. Physical Ranged Attacks Universal Close-Range Rule. If the target of a physical ranged weapon attack is within 5 feet of the attacker, the attack roll has Disadvantage. This applies whether the attacker is grounded or airborne and does not change the weapon’s listed Normal Range or Maximum Range. A lower-altitude physical ranged attacker has Advantage against a higher-altitude winged airborne target because the wings are exposed. This Exposed Wings rule does not apply to wingless creatures flying through Saturated Aether. A higher-altitude ranged attacker gains no automatic Advantage merely for being above the target. When the physical ranged attacker is above the target, increase only the weapon’s Maximum Range by half the vertical distance, rounded up. The weapon’s Normal Range is unchanged. Magical attacks do not gain this extension. Flight Slots Level Base Max Slots 1–3 2 4–6 3 7–9 4 10–12 5 13–16 6 17–19 7 20 8 A stable airborne Daeva spends 1 Flight Slot at the end of each of its turns. A grounded Daeva recovers 1 Flight Slot at the end of each grounded turn. Short Rest restores half maximum, rounded down; Long Rest restores all. When a creature runs out of Flight Slots while airborne, it immediately falls. Aether State Interaction Depleted Aether. Flight is fully restricted. Stable Aether. Normal flight rules. Saturated Aether. Daevas spend no combat Flight Slots, though exploration Flight Time limits still apply. Wingless creatures capable of movement may gain flight equal to normal Speed while Saturated; they do not use Flight Slots and are not subject to Exposed Wings. Unstable Zone / Aether Instability. This is hazard-defined scene behavior rather than a universal Aether State. The three universal States are Stable, Depleted, and Saturated. Use the specific Aether Hazard rules for the area. Aether-State Changes and Boundaries Aether-State changes take effect immediately. Crossing into a new Aether State immediately applies the entered State. In Depleted Aether, Aether-supported flight is unavailable; an airborne Daeva entering a Depleted area loses flight and falls, using the normal DC 12 Dexterity Emergency Landing Reaction if eligible. Saturated → Stable: Daevas resume normal Flight Slot expenditure. A creature flying only because Saturated Aether granted it flight loses that flight and falls. Saturated → Depleted: affected airborne creatures immediately lose Aether-supported flight and fall. Stable → Saturated: Daevas stop spending Combat Flight Slots, and eligible wingless creatures gain access to Aether-supported flight equal to normal Speed, but no creature automatically takes off. Falling and Emergency Landing Falling damage is 1d6 per 10 feet fallen, maximum 20d6. A falling creature normally lands Prone unless an explicit effect says otherwise. When Flight Slot depletion causes a fall, the creature may use its Reaction for a DC 12 Dexterity save. Success halves fall damage; failure or no Reaction takes full damage. Controlled Descent changes a successful Emergency Landing to 0 fall damage according to that feat. Falling Onto Creatures The lower creature makes a DC 12 Dexterity save. On success it avoids the collision and the falling creature

Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Sneak Attack and Rune Marks Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Assassin is a precision melee striker that builds target-bound Rune Marks, converts them into burst damage or execution riders, and uses Shadow Step to remain difficult to pin down. Unlike a conventional Extra Attack martial, its Level 5 Assassination Sequence is a conditional follow-up attack tied to a successful Sneak Attack. Class Identity Assassins are precision predators who win through positioning, timing, concealment, and carefully prepared execution. Their art is not simply “attacking from stealth.” An Assassin studies a target, creates the right opening, carves Rune Marks, and converts preparation into a sudden lethal advantage. Their greatest strength is the ability to decide where and when a close-range confrontation becomes dangerous. Tradition & Outlook The Assassin tradition descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines and is practiced by infiltrators, covert operatives, hunters of dangerous individuals, intelligence agents, and Daevas who favor certainty over spectacle. Assassins often prize patience, awareness, self-control, and economy of motion. Their motives vary widely: service to a faction, revenge, professional duty, protection through preemptive action, or the pursuit of perfect technique. Appearance & Adventuring Assassins favor equipment that permits mobility and unobstructed movement, with Shortswords and Daggers forming the class’s approved weapon identity in Wings of Atreia. Their appearance may be subdued or ceremonial, but practical Assassins avoid anything that compromises movement or control. They adventure when a threat must be found before it strikes, a route must be infiltrated, an enemy leader must be neutralized, or a mystery demands someone comfortable operating unseen. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Bastion Pilot • Aether Core • Heat • Adaptive Weapons Combat Aethertech “Steel, meet face. Face, meet steel.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. On this page Overview Chassis Core Mechanics Action Reference Specializations Progression Examples ↑ Top The Aethertech fights from one piloted Large Bastion platform. The pilot and Bastion are one character’s action economy, not two independent turns. The class alternates between integrated Bastion armaments, Aether Core expenditures, controlled Heat accumulation, venting, repairs, and system integration. The Bastion is a separate physical HP pool that enemies can damage without directly healing or harming the pilot unless an effect specifically targets the pilot. Class Identity Aethertechs are technist warriors who channel Aether through a Bastion: a magical-mechanical combat platform that transforms how the Daeva occupies the battlefield. The class combines personal skill, engineered systems, heavy protection, and controlled bursts of power. Aether Core and Heat represent the constant balance between available energy and the strain created by pushing the Bastion harder. Tradition & Outlook Aethertech is a comparatively modern Daeva discipline born from the recovery, study, and weaponization of advanced magical technology. The wider Aion tradition connects the class to Daeva analysis of Danuar technology and the lessons surrounding Hyperion; Wings of Atreia preserves that technological identity while its own campaign chronology and mechanics remain authoritative. Aethertechs often value ingenuity, technical discipline, experimentation, and the belief that knowledge taken from dangerous enemies can be turned toward Atreia’s defense. Appearance & Adventuring An Aethertech is visually defined by the Bastion and the contrast between a Daeva operator and an imposing Aether-powered war platform. Outside it, the Aethertech remains a trained combatant using the class’s approved weapons and equipment. Aethertechs adventure to recover technology, test designs under real conditions, oppose Balaur war machines, protect expeditions with a durable mobile platform, or prove that engineering can stand beside sword and spell as a heroic discipline. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Ability Intelligence Secondary Ability Constitution Hit Die d8 Saving Throws Intelligence, Constitution Armor Chain Armor Skills Choose 2 from 6: Arcana, Athletics, Investigation, Perception, Sleight of Hand, Survival Weapons Shortswords, Maces, Hammers Signature Resources Aether Core and Heat Signature Mechanic Piloted Bastion Bastion Size Large Class Save DC 8 + PB + INT modifier Extra Attack Level 5; two Bastion weapon attacks only Spellcasting None Bastion Targeting and Chassis The pilot and Bastion have separate HP and temporary HP. Repairs restore Bastion HP and are not healing. While occupied, ordinary physical attacks targeting the Aethertech generally strike the Bastion first. Mental, emotional, biological, and similar effects target the pilot when appropriate. One area effect normally does not double-hit both pilot and Bastion. Bastion physical STR/DEX/CON saves use PB + INT modifier. Mental saves use the pilot’s relevant save. When the Bastion reaches 0 HP it is Disabled. The pilot is ejected to the nearest legal space, takes 1d6 Force damage, and does not provoke Opportunity Attacks from the ejection. A disabled Bastion retains its current Core and Heat; a fresh chassis does not replace it. A Short Rest repairs a Disabled or damaged Bastion by half its maximum HP. A Long Rest repairs the Bastion to its maximum HP. These restorations are repairs, not healing. Once the Bastion has at least 1 HP, it is operational. Entering or re-entering a deployed Bastion uses an Action when otherwise legal. A defeated or voluntarily replaced Bastion never functions as a companion or second PC. Contesting STR checks with the Bastion e.g Grapple, pushing, pulling, except for skill or ability effects, will have the PC use this formula: 1d20+8+INT modifier+PB considering that a Bastion is a Large entity. Target must contest with their choice of Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics). View Sorcerer Spell List → Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Aether Focus Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Spell List Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Spellcasting Example Specialization Reassignment The Sorcerer is the raw magical-damage benchmark. It casts through Fire, Ice, Lightning, and Wind spell chains, then spends Aether Focus only when a particular spell needs more damage, area, control pressure, or reliability. Aether Focus enhances spells; it is never the fuel required to cast ordinary Sorcerer spells. Class Identity Sorcerers are masters of direct Aetheric spellcraft, combining destructive magic with the ability to control the shape and tempo of a fight. They can punish clustered enemies, deny movement or action, and unleash powerful spells when an opening appears. Aether Focus represents the concentration and arcane discipline required to turn immense magical potential into reliable battlefield power. Tradition & Outlook The Sorcerer tradition grows from Atreia’s mage disciplines and is associated with formal magical study, experimentation, academies, battlefield arcanists, and Daevas fascinated by the structure of Aether itself. Sorcerers commonly value knowledge, precision, preparation, and intellectual mastery, although their personalities range from scholarly restraint to spectacular confidence. For many, magic is both a weapon and a language through which Atreia can be understood. Appearance & Adventuring Sorcerers favor cloth armor and magical implements such as Orbs and Spellbooks under the Wings of Atreia equipment rules. Their appearance may reflect academic, military, ceremonial, or highly individual magical traditions. They adventure to recover lost knowledge, study Aetheric phenomena, test magical theories, defend their people with overwhelming spellcraft, or confront powers that ordinary weapons cannot adequately answer. The resource is an enhancement reserve: casting an ordinary Sorcerer spell never requires Aether Focus unless a spell or class feature explicitly says otherwise. After a Long Rest it is normally full. Maximum PB + INT modifier, minimum 2. Aether Sage and the Level 20 capstone can explicitly increase this maximum. Rest Recovery Long Rest restores all expended Aether Focus. Short Rest restores Focus equal to PB, up to maximum; Aether Sage can improve this recovery. Base Generation The base Sorcerer does not generate Aether Focus from ordinary spell hits or damage. Combat refunds exist only where a class or specialization feature explicitly grants them. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Combat Turn structure, actions, movement, attacks, damage, conditions, death, rests, and survival. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative Round and Turn Action Economy Attack Action Universal Actions Ready Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative, rounds, and combat-only resources are used only for genuine combat or another situation where structured turn order is necessary. Characters cannot manufacture artificial combat to farm cooldowns, resources, or timing triggers. Initiative Initiative = 1d20 + Dexterity modifier. Do not add PB unless an explicit feature says so. Alert adds +2 Initiative. There is no Surprise Round and Surprise does not grant Advantage on Initiative. When one side genuinely catches another side unaware, the GM may, at discretion, allow one appropriate pre-Initiative attack roll against the target's normal defense before Initiative is rolled. This is not an extra round, is not automatic, and does not create a general Surprise action economy. After that resolution, roll Initiative normally. Round and Turn One combat round represents approximately six seconds in the game world. Each participant normally takes one turn in Initiative order. All turns in the round abstract actions occurring within the same six-second span; do not add each turn as another six seconds. Action Economy Action. One per turn. Movement. Up to the creature’s available movement, subject to terrain and conditions. Bonus Action. Up to one, but only when a feature grants something that uses a Bonus Action. Reaction. Normally one per round, refreshing at the start of the creature’s turn unless an explicit class rule says otherwise. Object interaction. One free simple object interaction per turn. There is no universal Action-to-Bonus-Action or Bonus-Action-to-Action conversion. Unused movement or Actions are not stored for later turns. Attack Action The Attack Action makes one attack unless a feature such as Extra Attack says otherwise. Grapple and Shove are full Actions and do not replace one attack within Extra Attack. Player Weapon Requirement. A player character must be wielding an approved class weapon to take the normal Attack Action. Unarmed Attacks and Improvised Weapons are not player combat options unless a later explicit feature creates a specific exception. Opportunity Attacks. Opportunity Attacks remain part of the core combat rules. When a hostile creature you can perceive voluntarily leaves your melee reach, you may use your Reaction to make one melee attack against it, resolving the attack before it leaves that reach. Forced movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Universal Actions Dash. Gain additional movement equal to your current Speed for the turn. Difficult Terrain and other movement costs still apply. While flying, Dash adds horizontal movement but does not grant an additional altitude-layer change. Disengage. Until the end of your turn, your movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks. Dodge. Until the start of your next turn, attacks against you have Disadvantage if you can perceive the attacker, and you have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws. Dodge ends if you become Incapacitated or your Speed becomes 0. Hide. You must have meaningful concealment or another circumstance that allows hiding. Make Dexterity (Stealth) against Passive Perception or active Perception as appropriate. You cannot Hide while clearly seen. Hidden is not Invisible. Making an attack reveals your position after that attack resolves. Search. Deliberately search using a GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation). Use Object. Use this Action for substantial manipulation beyond the one free simple object interaction. A specific item’s activation rule controls when it states another cost. Ready A creature can prepare one Action for a perceivable trigger. When the trigger occurs, the creature may use its Reaction to perform the readied Action. Ready does not store ordinary movement, but Dash can be readied as the Action. Readied attacks retain all weapon properties. A readied spell must still meet implement and targeting requirements when released. Losing a mandatory implement before release prevents release. Concentration begins when the spell actually resolves. Ready never bypasses aerial restrictions, range, or other universal rules. Simultaneous Effects Effects resolve one at a time. text: WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Bastion Pilot • Aether Core • Heat • Adaptive Weapons Combat Aethertech “Steel, meet face. Face, meet steel.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. On this page Overview Chassis Core Mechanics Action Reference Specializations Progression Examples ↑ Top The Aethertech fights from one piloted Large Bastion platform. The pilot and Bastion are one character’s action economy, not two independent turns. The class alternates between integrated Bastion armaments, Aether Core expenditures, controlled Heat accumulation, venting, repairs, and system integration. The Bastion is a separate physical HP pool that enemies can damage without directly healing or harming the pilot unless an effect specifically targets the pilot. Class Identity Aethertechs are technist warriors who channel Aether through a Bastion: a magical-mechanical combat platform that transforms how the Daeva occupies the battlefield. The class combines personal skill, engineered systems, heavy protection, and controlled bursts of power. Aether Core and Heat represent the constant balance between available energy and the strain created by pushing the Bastion harder. Tradition & Outlook Aethertech is a comparatively modern Daeva discipline born from the recovery, study, and weaponization of advanced magical technology. The wider Aion tradition connects the class to Daeva analysis of Danuar technology and the lessons surrounding Hyperion; Wings of Atreia preserves that technological identity while its own campaign chronology and mechanics remain authoritative. Aethertechs often value ingenuity, technical discipline, experimentation, and the belief that knowledge taken from dangerous enemies can be turned toward Atreia’s defense. Appearance & Adventuring An Aethertech is visually defined by the Bastion and the contrast between a Daeva operator and an imposing Aether-powered war platform. Outside it, the Aethertech remains a trained combatant using the class’s approved weapons and equipment. Aethertechs adventure to recover technology, test designs under real conditions, oppose Balaur war machines, protect expeditions with a durable mobile platform, or prove that engineering can stand beside sword and spell as a heroic discipline. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Ability Intelligence Secondary Ability Constitution Hit Die d8 Saving Throws Intelligence, Constitution Armor Chain Armor Skills Choose 2 from 6: Arcana, Athletics, Investigation, Perception, Sleight of Hand, Survival Weapons Shortswords, Maces, Hammers Signature Resources Aether Core and Heat Signature Mechanic Piloted Bastion Bastion Size Large Class Save DC 8 + PB + INT modifier Extra Attack Level 5; two Bastion weapon attacks only Spellcasting None Bastion Targeting and Chassis The pilot and Bastion have separate HP and temporary HP. Repairs restore Bastion HP and are not healing. While occupied, ordinary physical attacks targeting the Aethertech generally strike the Bastion first. Mental, emotional, biological, and similar effects target the pilot when appropriate. One area effect normally does not double-hit both pilot and Bastion. Bastion physical STR/DEX/CON saves use PB + INT modifier. Mental saves use the pilot’s relevant save. When the Bastion reaches 0 HP it is Disabled. The pilot is ejected to the nearest legal space, takes 1d6 Force damage, and does not provoke Opportunity Attacks from the ejection. A disabled Bastion retains its current Core and Heat; a fresh chassis does not replace it. A Short Rest repairs a Disabled or damaged Bastion by half its maximum HP. A Long Rest repairs the Bastion to its maximum HP. These restorations are repairs, not healing. Once the Bastion has at least 1 HP, it is operational. Entering or re-entering a deployed Bastion uses an Action when otherwise legal. A defeated or voluntarily replaced Bastion never functions as a companion or second PC. Contesting STR checks with the Bastion e.g Grapple, pushing, pulling, except for skill or ability effects, will have the PC use this formula: 1d20+8+INT modifier+PB considering that a Bastion is a Large entity. Target must contest with their choice of Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics). Level Band Bastion AC Bastion Maximum HP 1–4 11 + PB 8 + (5 × Aethertech level) + INT 5–10 12 + PB 8 + (5 × level) + INT 11–17 13 + PB 12 + (6 × level) + INT 18–20 13 + PB 16 + (7 × level) + INT Whenever a chassis improvement raises maximum HP, increase current Bastion HP by the same amount; this is a maximum-HP adjustment rather than healing. Bastion Weapon Synchronization While piloting a Bastion, designate one eligible carried weapon with which you are proficient as your Synchronized Weapon. A Bastion weapon attack roll is 1d20 + PB + INT modifier + the Synchronized Weapon's current equipment-quality bonus to Hit. Only that quality bonus transfers. The Bastion does not inherit the carried weapon's damage dice, damage type, properties, Critical Edge, reload mechanics, critical effects, or other traits. Only one Synchronized Weapon applies at a time; bonuses from multiple weapons never stack. Synchronization does not alter Bastion damage or save DCs. Targeting Array remains a separate once-per-turn +1 class-feature bonus and applies normally. Aether Core Maximum Aether Core equals PB + INT modifier, minimum 3; Level 9 increases this maximum by 1. A Long Rest restores all Core and a Short Rest restores PB. Core powers Bastion systems rather than ordinary movement or basic cannon attacks. Core Cycling later rewards making attacks without spending Core on the attack itself. Heat Heat returns to 0 after 1 minute outside genuine combat without intensive Bastion operation and is produced only by systems or features that explicitly say they gain Heat. Heat maximum is 5 at Levels 1–4, 6 at 5–8, 7 at 9–14, 8 at 15–19, and 9 at Level 20. Stable Heat is 0–2. At 3+ Heat the reactor is Pressurized and your Bastion weapon damage gains the class’s Pressurized bonus: +1 early, +2 from Level 9 onward. At maximum Heat you cannot voluntarily activate a system that would generate more Heat unless a feature explicitly permits it. If an allowed effect raises Heat above maximum, resolve that effect and then Overheat. Vent: Bonus Action, reduce Heat by 2. At Level 15 Vent reduces by 3; Cooling Fins increases the amount by 1. Overheat: take 2d6 Force damage to the Bastion, then reset Heat to 3; from Level 15 reset to 4. Your own Emergency Plating cannot reduce Overheat damage. Controlled Critical at Level 9: if you start your turn at maximum Heat, the first Bastion weapon hit that turn adds PB damage. Heat reduction from “preventing Heat gain” is not the same as Venting/cooling for features that care about cooling. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Aether Core — Maximum PB + INT modifier, minimum 3; Level 9 increases this maximum by 1. Aether Core — Recovery Long Rest restores all Core. Short Rest restores Core equal to PB, up to maximum. Core Cycling, Flux Engineer, and later features can explicitly restore Core during play. Aether Core — Spending Powered Shot 1 Core + 1 Heat; Repulsion Blast 1 Core + 1 Heat; Emergency Plating 1 Core + 1 Heat; Field Mechanic 1 Core; Combat Repair 1 Core; Flux Engineer Heat Conversion 1 Core (or gain 2 Heat to restore 1 Core); Siege Engineer Bombardment Round +1 Core +1 Heat; Flux Engineer Thermal Reversal 1 Core; Siege Engineer Devastation Cannon 2 Core +2 Heat; Bulwark Protective Field 1 Core +1 Heat. Heat is operating pressure, not a spendable point pool. Heat — Starting State Heat is 0 outside intensive Bastion operation. Leaving the Bastion during combat does not automatically erase current Heat. Heat — Maximum 5 at Levels 1–4; 6 at 5–8; 7 at 9–14; 8 at 15–19; 9 at Level 20. Heat — How It Rises Powered Shot and other systems explicitly say when they gain Heat. Heat is an operating-pressure track, not a spendable point pool. Heat — Cooling Vent is normally a Bonus Action that reduces Heat by 2; Level 15 improves the base reduction to 3, and Cooling Fins increases the amount by 1. Other features can reduce or prevent Heat at their stated timing. Overheat / Reset If an explicit feature allows Heat to exceed maximum, resolve that system then Overheat: the Bastion takes 2d6 Force damage and Heat resets to 3, or 4 from Level 15. Ordinary noncombat cooling returns Heat to 0 after 1 minute without intensive Bastion operation. this is repair, not healing. 2 Vent Bonus Action — Heat above 0 Reduce Heat by the current Vent amount; Controlled Venting may add one rider. 2 Controlled Venting After Vent / No Action — Meaningfully Vent Heat; once per Vent After cooling, choose Aetheric Pulse, Defensive Reclamation, or Thruster Reposition. 2 Emergency Capacitor Triggered / No Action 1/Short or Long Rest Activate an Aethertech feature while exactly 1 Core short of its cost Supply the missing 1 Core for that immediate feature cost only. 3 Heat Conversion (Flux Engineer) Triggered / No Action 1 Core or +2 Heat Once on your turn Spend 1 Core to cool Heat, or gain 2 Heat to restore 1 Core; Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative Round and Turn Action Economy Attack Action Universal Actions Ready Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative, rounds, and combat-only resources are used only for genuine combat or another situation where structured turn order is necessary. Characters cannot manufacture artificial combat to farm cooldowns, resources, or timing triggers. Initiative Initiative = 1d20 + Dexterity modifier. Do not add PB unless an explicit feature says so. Alert adds +2 Initiative. There is no Surprise Round and Surprise does not grant Advantage on Initiative. When one side genuinely catches another side unaware, the GM may, at discretion, allow one appropriate pre-Initiative attack roll against the target's normal defense before Initiative is rolled. This is not an extra round, is not automatic, and does not create a general Surprise action economy. After that resolution, roll Initiative normally. Round and Turn One combat round represents approximately six seconds in the game world. Each participant normally takes one turn in Initiative order. All turns in the round abstract actions occurring within the same six-second span; do not add each turn as another six seconds. Action Economy Action. One per turn. Movement. Up to the creature’s available movement, subject to terrain and conditions. Bonus Action. Up to one, but only when a feature grants something that uses a Bonus Action. Reaction. Normally one per round, refreshing at the start of the creature’s turn unless an explicit class rule says otherwise. Object interaction. One free simple object interaction per turn. There is no universal Action-to-Bonus-Action or Bonus-Action-to-Action conversion. Unused movement or Actions are not stored for later turns. Attack Action The Attack Action makes one attack unless a feature such as Extra Attack says otherwise. Grapple and Shove are full Actions and do not replace one attack within Extra Attack. Player Weapon Requirement. A player character must be wielding an approved class weapon to take the normal Attack Action. Unarmed Attacks and Improvised Weapons are not player combat options unless a later explicit feature creates a specific exception. Opportunity Attacks. Opportunity Attacks remain part of the core combat rules. When a hostile creature you can perceive voluntarily leaves your melee reach, you may use your Reaction to make one melee attack against it, resolving the attack before it leaves that reach. Forced movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Universal Actions Dash. Gain additional movement equal to your current Speed for the turn. Difficult Terrain and other movement costs still apply. While flying, Dash adds horizontal movement but does not grant an additional altitude-layer change. Disengage. Until the end of your turn, your movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks. Dodge. Until the start of your next turn, attacks against you have Disadvantage if you can perceive the attacker, and you have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws. Dodge ends if you become Incapacitated or your Speed becomes 0. Hide. You must have meaningful concealment or another circumstance that allows hiding. Make Dexterity (Stealth) against Passive Perception or active Perception as appropriate. You cannot Hide while clearly seen. Hidden is not Invisible. Making an attack reveals your position after that attack resolves. Search. Deliberately search using a GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation). Use Object. Use this Action for substantial manipulation beyond the one free simple object interaction. A specific item’s activation rule controls when it states another cost. Ready A creature can prepare one Action for a perceivable trigger. When the trigger occurs, the creature may use its Reaction to perform the readied Action. Ready does not store ordinary movement, but Dash can be readied as the Action. Readied attacks retain all weapon properties. A readied spell must still meet implement and targeting requirements when released. Losing a mandatory implement before release prevents release. Concentration begins when the spell actually resolves. Ready never bypasses aerial restrictions, range, or other universal rules. Simultaneous Effects Effects resolve one at a time. The active creature orders its own simultaneous effects; the GM orders GM-controlled simultaneous effects. Flight & Aerial Combat Altitude Layers 3D Distance Melee Descending Attack Physical Ranged Attacks Flight Slots Aether State Interaction Flight & Aerial Combat Altitude Layers Layer Height Access Low 30 ft All functional Wings Mid 60 ft All functional Wings High 90 ft All functional Wings Legendary 120 ft Legendary Wings only Ground level is 0 feet and is not an altitude layer. There are four airborne altitude layers: Low (30 ft), Mid (60 ft), High (90 ft), and Legendary (120 ft). Voluntarily ascending or descending one altitude layer consumes all movement for that turn. A creature cannot both ascend and descend voluntarily in the same turn. Dash does not permit an additional altitude-layer change. A Daeva without Legendary Wings cannot voluntarily ascend above the High layer at 90 feet. 3D Distance For WoA aerial targeting, total distance = the greater of horizontal distance or vertical distance. Do not use Pythagorean distance and do not add horizontal and vertical distance together. Melee Airborne melee uses ordinary reach: usually 5 feet, or 10 feet for a Reach weapon. Being on the same altitude layer does not remove the need to physically move into reach. Descending Attack If a melee attacker begins its turn higher than the target, descends at least 25 feet, and then makes its first qualifying melee attack against that lower target, the attack has Advantage. Physical Ranged Attacks Universal Close-Range Rule. If the target of a physical ranged weapon attack is within 5 feet of the attacker, the attack roll has Disadvantage. This applies whether the attacker is grounded or airborne and does not change the weapon’s listed Normal Range or Maximum Range. A lower-altitude physical ranged attacker has Advantage against a higher-altitude winged airborne target because the wings are exposed. This Exposed Wings rule does not apply to wingless creatures flying through Saturated Aether. A higher-altitude ranged attacker gains no automatic Advantage merely for being above the target. When the physical ranged attacker is above the target, increase only the weapon’s Maximum Range by half the vertical distance, rounded up. The weapon’s Normal Range is unchanged. Magical attacks do not gain this extension. Flight Slots Level Base Max Slots 1–3 2 4–6 3 7–9 4 10–12 5 13–16 6 17–19 7 20 8 A stable airborne Daeva spends 1 Flight Slot at the end of each of its turns. A grounded Daeva recovers 1 Flight Slot at the end of each grounded turn. Short Rest restores half maximum, rounded down; Long Rest restores all. When a creature runs out of Flight Slots while airborne, it immediately falls. Aether State Interaction Depleted Aether. Flight is fully restricted. Stable Aether. Normal flight rules. Saturated Aether. Daevas spend no combat Flight Slots, though exploration Flight Time limits still apply. Wingless creatures capable of movement may gain flight equal to normal Speed while Saturated; they do not use Flight Slots and are not subject to Exposed Wings. Unstable Zone / Aether Instability. This is hazard-defined scene behavior rather than a universal Aether State. The three universal States are Stable, Depleted, and Saturated. Use the specific Aether Hazard rules for the area. Aether-State Changes and Boundaries Aether-State changes take effect immediately. Crossing into a new Aether State immediately applies the entered State. In Depleted Aether, Aether-supported flight is unavailable; an airborne Daeva entering a Depleted area loses flight and falls, using the normal DC 12 Dexterity Emergency Landing Reaction if eligible. Saturated → Stable: Daevas resume normal Flight Slot expenditure. A creature flying only because Saturated Aether granted it flight loses that flight and falls. Saturated → Depleted: affected airborne creatures immediately lose Aether-supported flight and fall. Stable → Saturated: Daevas stop spending Combat Flight Slots, and eligible wingless creatures gain access to Aether-supported flight equal to normal Speed, but no creature automatically takes off. Falling and Emergency Landing Falling damage is 1d6 per 10 feet fallen, maximum 20d6. A falling creature normally lands Prone unless an explicit effect says otherwise. When Flight Slot depletion causes a fall, the creature may use its Reaction for a DC 12 Dexterity save. Success halves fall damage; failure or no Reaction takes full damage. Controlled Descent changes a successful Emergency Landing to 0 fall damage according to that feat. Falling Onto Creatures The lower creature makes a DC 12 Dexterity save. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Bastion Pilot • Aether Core • Heat • Adaptive Weapons Combat Aethertech “Steel, meet face. Face, meet steel.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. On this page Overview Chassis Core Mechanics Action Reference Specializations Progression Examples ↑ Top The Aethertech fights from one piloted Large Bastion platform. The pilot and Bastion are one character’s action economy, not two independent turns. The class alternates between integrated Bastion armaments, Aether Core expenditures, controlled Heat accumulation, venting, repairs, and system integration. The Bastion is a separate physical HP pool that enemies can damage without directly healing or harming the pilot unless an effect specifically targets the pilot. Class Identity Aethertechs are technist warriors who channel Aether through a Bastion: a magical-mechanical combat platform that transforms how the Daeva occupies the battlefield. The class combines personal skill, engineered systems, heavy protection, and controlled bursts of power. Aether Core and Heat represent the constant balance between available energy and the strain created by pushing the Bastion harder. Tradition & Outlook Aethertech is a comparatively modern Daeva discipline born from the recovery, study, and weaponization of advanced magical technology. The wider Aion tradition connects the class to Daeva analysis of Danuar technology and the lessons surrounding Hyperion; Wings of Atreia preserves that technological identity while its own campaign chronology and mechanics remain authoritative. Aethertechs often value ingenuity, technical discipline, experimentation, and the belief that knowledge taken from dangerous enemies can be turned toward Atreia’s defense. Appearance & Adventuring An Aethertech is visually defined by the Bastion and the contrast between a Daeva operator and an imposing Aether-powered war platform. Outside it, the Aethertech remains a trained combatant using the class’s approved weapons and equipment. Aethertechs adventure to recover technology, test designs under real conditions, oppose Balaur war machines, protect expeditions with a durable mobile platform, or prove that engineering can stand beside sword and spell as a heroic discipline. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Ability Intelligence Secondary Ability Constitution Hit Die d8 Saving Throws Intelligence, Constitution Armor Chain Armor Skills Choose 2 from 6: Arcana, Athletics, Investigation, Perception, Sleight of Hand, Survival Weapons Shortswords, Maces, Hammers Signature Resources Aether Core and Heat Signature Mechanic Piloted Bastion Bastion Size Large Class Save DC 8 + PB + INT modifier Extra Attack Level 5; two Bastion weapon attacks only Spellcasting None Bastion Targeting and Chassis The pilot and Bastion have separate HP and temporary HP. Repairs restore Bastion HP and are not healing. While occupied, ordinary physical attacks targeting the Aethertech generally strike the Bastion first. Mental, emotional, biological, and similar effects target the pilot when appropriate. One area effect normally does not double-hit both pilot and Bastion. Bastion physical STR/DEX/CON saves use PB + INT modifier. Mental saves use the pilot’s relevant save. When the Bastion reaches 0 HP it is Disabled. The pilot is ejected to the nearest legal space, takes 1d6 Force damage, and does not provoke Opportunity Attacks from the ejection. A disabled Bastion retains its current Core and Heat; a fresh chassis does not replace it. A Short Rest repairs a Disabled or damaged Bastion by half its maximum HP. A Long Rest repairs the Bastion to its maximum HP. These restorations are repairs, not healing. Once the Bastion has at least 1 HP, it is operational. Entering or re-entering a deployed Bastion uses an Action when otherwise legal. A defeated or voluntarily replaced Bastion never functions as a companion or second PC. Contesting STR checks with the Bastion e.g Grapple, pushing, pulling, except for skill or ability effects, will have the PC use this formula: 1d20+8+INT modifier+PB considering that a Bastion is a Large entity. Target must contest with their choice of Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics). View Sorcerer Spell List → Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Aether Focus Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Spell List Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Spellcasting Example Specialization Reassignment The Sorcerer is the raw magical-damage benchmark. It casts through Fire, Ice, Lightning, and Wind spell chains, then spends Aether Focus only when a particular spell needs more damage, area, control pressure, or reliability. Aether Focus enhances spells; it is never the fuel required to cast ordinary Sorcerer spells. Class Identity Sorcerers are masters of direct Aetheric spellcraft, combining destructive magic with the ability to control the shape and tempo of a fight. They can punish clustered enemies, deny movement or action, and unleash powerful spells when an opening appears. Aether Focus represents the concentration and arcane discipline required to turn immense magical potential into reliable battlefield power. Tradition & Outlook The Sorcerer tradition grows from Atreia’s mage disciplines and is associated with formal magical study, experimentation, academies, battlefield arcanists, and Daevas fascinated by the structure of Aether itself. Sorcerers commonly value knowledge, precision, preparation, and intellectual mastery, although their personalities range from scholarly restraint to spectacular confidence. For many, magic is both a weapon and a language through which Atreia can be understood. Appearance & Adventuring Sorcerers favor cloth armor and magical implements such as Orbs and Spellbooks under the Wings of Atreia equipment rules. Their appearance may reflect academic, military, ceremonial, or highly individual magical traditions. They adventure to recover lost knowledge, study Aetheric phenomena, test magical theories, defend their people with overwhelming spellcraft, or confront powers that ordinary weapons cannot adequately answer. A Long Rest restores all expended Aether Focus. A Short Rest restores Aether Focus equal to PB, up to your maximum. The resource is an enhancement reserve: casting an ordinary Sorcerer spell never requires Aether Focus unless a spell or class feature explicitly says otherwise. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Starting State Aether Focus is a rest-based enhancement reserve and does not reset merely because combat begins or ends. After a Long Rest it is normally full. Maximum PB + INT modifier, minimum 2. Aether Sage and the Level 20 capstone can explicitly increase this maximum. Rest Recovery Long Rest restores all expended Aether Focus. Short Rest restores Focus equal to PB, up to maximum; Aether Sage can improve this recovery. Base Generation The base Sorcerer does not generate Aether Focus from ordinary spell hits or damage. Combat refunds exist only where a class or specialization feature explicitly grants them. How You Spend It Intensify 1 Focus; Widen 1 Focus; Potent Control 1 Focus; other Sorcerer features spend Aether Focus only when their text states a cost. Ordinary spellcasting costs no Focus. Refunds / Discounts Aether Sage and later features may discount a shaping cost or refund Focus after a qualifying shaped spell. A refund is not a second casting or a new spell trigger. Persistence Unused Aether Focus persists between encounters until spent or restored. Important Distinction Aether Focus is a Sorcerer class resource. It is not environmental Aether, Refined Aether, an Aether State, or a universal damage type. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Martial Support • Mantras • Cadence • Harmonic Warfare Chanter “Stay close, stay safe.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Spellcasting Reference: Chanter has a dedicated spell-list page for quick browsing. View Chanter Spell List → Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Cadence Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Spell List Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Rhythm Sequence Specialization Reassignment The Chanter wins by alternating weapon attacks, spells, and active Mantra management. Cadence is earned by changing categories rather than repeating one action, then spent on damage, protection, healing, and tactical movement. It is a secondary healer and hybrid support, not a replacement for the Cleric or a dedicated martial striker. Class Identity Chanters are martial support specialists who combine staff technique, enchantment, restorative magic, and Mantras into a continuous rhythm of battle. Rather than solving every problem through one large spell, a Chanter improves the party’s performance over time and responds to changing pressure with Cadence. Their presence is felt in how effectively the entire group moves, strikes, and recovers together. Tradition & Outlook The Chanter tradition grows from Atreia’s priestly disciplines but emphasizes disciplined body, voice, repetition, and the shaping of Aether through words and practiced forms. Chanters are often teachers, battle companions, spiritual guides, martial ascetics, or morale-keepers. They tend to value harmony between individual excellence and collective strength: the ideal Chanter does not merely stand beside allies but helps those allies become more capable. Appearance & Adventuring Chanters are strongly associated with Staff and Quarterstaff techniques in Wings of Atreia. Their clothing and armor tend to allow movement while retaining the ceremonial or disciplined character of a priestly warrior. They adventure to guide companions, strengthen military or exploratory groups, carry teachings into dangerous places, preserve morale during long campaigns, or prove that disciplined cooperation can overcome enemies stronger than any one Daeva. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Ability Intelligence Secondary Ability Charisma Hit Die d8 Saving Throws Constitution, Intelligence Armor Chain Armor Weapons Staff, Quarterstaff Skills Choose 2 from 6: History, Insight, Medicine, Performance, Persuasion, Religion Spellcasting Ability INT Mantra Ability CHA Signature Resource Cadence Spell Advancements +1 each level after 1; 19 total Maximum Spell Level 7 Extra Attack Level 5; two attacks only Core Engine — Cadence Cadence is a genuine-combat resource. It begins at 0 when combat starts, resets to 0 when combat ends, and artificial initiative cannot create or restore it. Maximum Cadence is 3 at Levels 1–4, 4 at 5–8, 5 at 9–12, 6 at 13–16, and 7 at 17–20. Category Qualifying Event Martial You hit a hostile creature with a weapon attack. Spell A Chanter spell meaningfully affects a creature by hit, damage, failed save, actual healing, meaningful prevention, or another significant effect. Chant You activate, replace, or deliberately invoke a Mantra/Chant and it meaningfully changes at least one creature. Passive maintenance never qualifies. Your previous qualifying category is always the most recent successful qualifying category, whether or not that event generated Cadence. When you successfully complete a qualifying event whose category differs from your previous successful qualifying category, gain 1 Cadence, subject to the normal generation limit. Your first successful qualifying event in a combat establishes your previous category; it does not generate Cadence by itself. Normal Cadence generation is limited to 1 per turn unless a feature explicitly grants more. Secondary Chanter riders do not recursively generate Cadence, Resonant Network triggers, Mantra Weaving, or other support sequences unless explicit. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Starting State Cadence begins at 0 when genuine combat starts and resets to 0 when combat ends. Maximum 3 at Levels 1–4; 4 at 5–8; 5 at 9–12; 6 at 13–16; 7 at 17–20. Qualifying Categories Martial: a weapon attack hits a hostile. Spell: a Chanter spell meaningfully affects a creature. Chant: you activate, replace, or deliberately invoke a Mantra/Chant and it meaningfully changes at least one creature; passive maintenance does not qualify. How You Gain It When a successful qualifying event uses a category different from your previous successful qualifying category, gain 1 Cadence. The first successful qualifying event of a combat only establishes the previous category. Generation Limits

WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Melee Striker • Sneak Attack • Rune Marks • Execution Assassin “You'll know I'm there when you're dead.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Sneak Attack and Rune Marks Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Assassin is a precision melee striker that builds target-bound Rune Marks, converts them into burst damage or execution riders, and uses Shadow Step to remain difficult to pin down. Unlike a conventional Extra Attack martial, its Level 5 Assassination Sequence is a conditional follow-up attack tied to a successful Sneak Attack. Class Identity Assassins are precision predators who win through positioning, timing, concealment, and carefully prepared execution. Their art is not simply “attacking from stealth.” An Assassin studies a target, creates the right opening, carves Rune Marks, and converts preparation into a sudden lethal advantage. Their greatest strength is the ability to decide where and when a close-range confrontation becomes dangerous. Tradition & Outlook The Assassin tradition descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines and is practiced by infiltrators, covert operatives, hunters of dangerous individuals, intelligence agents, and Daevas who favor certainty over spectacle. Assassins often prize patience, awareness, self-control, and economy of motion. Their motives vary widely: service to a faction, revenge, professional duty, protection through preemptive action, or the pursuit of perfect technique. Appearance & Adventuring Assassins favor equipment that permits mobility and unobstructed movement, with Shortswords and Daggers forming the class’s approved weapon identity in Wings of Atreia. Their appearance may be subdued or ceremonial, but practical Assassins avoid anything that compromises movement or control. They adventure when a threat must be found before it strikes, a route must be infiltrated, an enemy leader must be neutralized, or a mystery demands someone comfortable operating unseen. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Tempo, Firearms, and Reload Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Tradition & Outlook Specialization Reassignment The Gunslinger is a mobile firearm martial whose power comes from maintaining Tempo through successful firearm play. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Fire. Move. Reload. Keep the rhythm alive long enough to turn Tempo into control, defense, and lethal pressure. Class Identity Gunslingers are technist marksmen who turn Aether-assisted firearms into speed, precision, and controlled ranged pressure. Pistols support rapid, mobile sequences through Quick Shot and Akimbo, while Muskets provide deliberate two-handed fire that concentrates Tempo into stronger individual hits through Deliberate Shot. Tempo represents the Gunslinger’s ability to build combat rhythm through successful action rather than treating every shot as an isolated event. Tradition & Outlook Gunslingers belong to Atreia’s newer technological traditions. The wider Aion tradition describes early firearm research being dismissed as technist tinkering until battlefield success forced major institutions to recognize the discipline. Wings of Atreia keeps that identity of innovation earning legitimacy through results while using Pistols and Muskets as the class’s only firearm categories. Gunslingers often value nerve, technical familiarity, accuracy, independence, and adaptability. Appearance & Adventuring Gunslingers favor mobile equipment, ammunition management, firearm maintenance, and a practical awareness of range and firing position. Their weapons can make them look strikingly modern beside older martial traditions, but their discipline remains Aetheric and distinctly Atreian. They adventure to test new techniques, serve as ranged specialists, hunt dangerous targets, protect expeditions from positions others cannot exploit, or demonstrate that innovation has earned its place in the war for Atreia. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols Ranged Gunslinger One-handed Weapon Attack. Range 30/90 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d8 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. A Gunslinger can wield two Pistols, but doing so does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols are compatible with Quick Shot and Akimbo. Muskets Ranged Gunslinger Two-handed Weapon Attack. Range 60/180 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d12 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. Ammunition capacity is fixed at 2. Muskets cannot use Quick Shot or Akimbo. Gunslinger ammunition-restoration features can restore Musket shots normally, but a Musket can never hold more than 2 shots. Standard one-handed firearm capacity increases do not apply to Muskets. Reload Every firearm attack consumes one shot. A firearm with no shots remaining is Empty and cannot make firearm attacks until at least one shot is restored. View Songweaver Spell List → Class Identity Class Chassis Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Spell List Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Performance Sequence Tradition & Outlook Specialization Reassignment The Songweaver changes battlefield purpose from moment to moment. Every Songweaver spell belongs to Harmony, Guard, Dissonance, or Requiem. Successful performances create short-lived Refrains, changing Song Roles builds Resonance, and Resonance is spent to amplify, sustain, counter, or conduct the performance. Class Identity Songweavers shape Aether through music, using performance as destructive spellcraft, support, control, and restoration. Their strength lies in versatility: the same class can pressure an enemy, sustain an ally, or shift the emotional and tactical rhythm of an encounter. Resonance represents the accumulating harmony between performance, spellcraft, and the unfolding battle. Tradition & Outlook The Songweaver tradition is rooted in Atreia’s Muses and in remembrance of Siel. The wider Aion tradition describes Muses who continued their studies after the Cataclysm and eventually joined music with Aether in service to their people; their battlefield contribution led to recognition as an established Daeva class. Songweavers may therefore approach performance as remembrance, artistry, scholarship, service, or a declaration that beauty still has power in a broken world. Appearance & Adventuring Songweavers use Lutes and Lyres as their approved implements, often making instrument, costume, gesture, and magical display part of a single visible identity. Their appearance can range from formal performer to traveling battle-musician without changing class mechanics. They adventure to preserve stories, honor Siel, inspire allies, master Aetheric music, carry culture into war-torn regions, or use beauty and sound as weapons against forces that would reduce Atreia to silence. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Spellcasting Reference: Cleric has a dedicated spell-list page for quick browsing. View Cleric Spell List → Class Identity Class Chassis Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Spell List Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Support Sequence Tradition & Outlook Specialization Reassignment The Cleric is Wings of Atreia’s primary restorative spellcaster. It is deliberately more durable than the d6 full casters and is rewarded for meaningful intervention: healing an ally in real danger, actually preventing damage, or removing a significant hostile effect. Divine Grace then converts that successful support into more emergency power. Class Identity Clerics are Atreia’s foremost restorative and protective spellcasters. Their calling is not limited to healing wounds after the fact: they preserve the party through recovery, cleansing, protection, and timely intervention while retaining the ability to fight when necessary. Divine Grace represents the reserve of sacred and restorative power through which a Cleric answers moments of genuine need. Tradition & Outlook The Cleric tradition grows from Atreia’s priestly disciplines and is associated with healers, battlefield ministers, temple servants, protectors of communities, and Daevas who understand survival as a collective responsibility. Clerics often value service, perseverance, mercy, duty, or faith, but they need not share one personality or theology. A militant Cleric and a gentle healer may practice the same class through very different convictions. Appearance & Adventuring Clerics commonly combine durable armor with practical healing or ritual equipment. In Wings of Atreia they may use Maces, Hammers, Staffs, Quarterstaffs, and shields from Round Shields to Medium Shields according to their approved access. They adventure to protect lives, confront corruption or supernatural danger, recover sacred knowledge, serve a cause, or ensure that an expedition can survive places where retreat and ordinary medicine are not enough. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Ability Wisdom Secondary Ability Constitution Hit Die d8; additionally +2 maximum HP per Cleric level Saving Throws Wisdom, Constitution Armor Chain Armor Weapons Mace, Hammer, Staff, Quarterstaff, Round Shield, Medium Shield Skills Choose 2 from 6: History, Insight, Medicine, Nature, Perception, Religion Spellcasting Ability WIS Spell Save DC 8 + PB + WIS modifier Spell Attack PB + WIS modifier Signature Resource Divine Grace Spell Advancements +2 each level after 1; 38 total Maximum Spell Level 9 Extra Attack None Meaningful Support and Divine Grace Maximum Divine Grace equals PB + WIS modifier, minimum 2. Long Rest restores all; Short Rest restores PB. Once per round, when you Meaningfully Support yourself or an ally with a Cleric spell or feature, regain 1 Grace. Your normal once-per-round generation becomes available again at the start of your turn, allowing an off-turn protection to qualify without double-dipping around initiative boundaries. Meaningful Support means one of the following actually occurs: restore HP while the creature was below half maximum HP; prevent or reduce damage by at least PB; or suppress/remove a mechanically significant hostile condition or effect. Healing a full-HP creature, preventing 0 damage, refreshing temporary HP without increasing it, cosmetic effects, or intentionally manufactured harmless damage do not qualify. Self-support must satisfy the same standard. Temporary HP are not healing and cannot restore a creature from 0 HP. Passive aura bonuses and passive AC do not generate Divine Grace unless a feature explicitly says so. A secondary Cleric rider created by another Cleric feature does not recursively trigger Twin Devotion, Sacred Intervention, Graceful Channeling, Empowered Restoration, or another support sequence unless explicit. Only one Cleric rolled-healing class rider normally modifies the same individual healing instance, except Graceful Restoration may coexist with one specialization rolled-healing rider. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Melee Striker • Sneak Attack • Rune Marks • Execution Assassin “You'll know I'm there when you're dead.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Sneak Attack and Rune Marks Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Assassin is a precision melee striker that builds target-bound Rune Marks, converts them into burst damage or execution riders, and uses Shadow Step to remain difficult to pin down. Unlike a conventional Extra Attack martial, its Level 5 Assassination Sequence is a conditional follow-up attack tied to a successful Sneak Attack. Class Identity Assassins are precision predators who win through positioning, timing, concealment, and carefully prepared execution. Their art is not simply “attacking from stealth.” An Assassin studies a target, creates the right opening, carves Rune Marks, and converts preparation into a sudden lethal advantage. Their greatest strength is the ability to decide where and when a close-range confrontation becomes dangerous. Tradition & Outlook The Assassin tradition descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines and is practiced by infiltrators, covert operatives, hunters of dangerous individuals, intelligence agents, and Daevas who favor certainty over spectacle. Assassins often prize patience, awareness, self-control, and economy of motion. Their motives vary widely: service to a faction, revenge, professional duty, protection through preemptive action, or the pursuit of perfect technique. Appearance & Adventuring Assassins favor equipment that permits mobility and unobstructed movement, with Shortswords and Daggers forming the class’s approved weapon identity in Wings of Atreia. Their appearance may be subdued or ceremonial, but practical Assassins avoid anything that compromises movement or control. They adventure when a threat must be found before it strikes, a route must be infiltrated, an enemy leader must be neutralized, or a mystery demands someone comfortable operating unseen. Sneak Attack damage scales from 1d6 at Level 1 to 10d6 at Level 19. Rune Carving: once on your turn, a qualifying melee hit that actually deals Sneak Attack places 1 Rune Mark after that hit resolves. Alternatively, hitting the same creature with two different melee attacks during your turn can place 1 Rune Mark after the second hit. Normal attack-based Rune placement is limited to 1 Mark per turn unless a feature explicitly increases it. Newly created Rune Marks cannot be consumed by the same hit that created them. If you exceed your current marked-target limit, choose one previously marked creature and remove all of your Marks from it. Marks disappear when consumed, when the marked creature is defeated, or when the encounter ends. A creature carries your Marks until they are consumed or removed. Maximum Up to 3 Rune Marks per creature. Marked-target capacity is 1 creature through Level 8, 2 from Levels 9–16, and 3 from Level 17 onward. Alternatively, two different melee hits against the same creature during your turn can place 1 Mark after the second hit. Placement Limits Normal attack-based placement is limited to 1 Mark per turn unless an explicit feature increases it. A newly created Mark cannot be consumed by the hit that created it. text: Apex Focus Techniques. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Ranged Striker • Focus • Traps • Tactical Repositioning Ranger “Chase me or run away. Either way, you'll only die tired.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Focus Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Ranger is a nonmagical ranged hunter that controls enemy movement with persistent battlefield traps, spends Focus on precision or evasive shots, and is rewarded for exploiting targets that walk into prepared terrain. Its sustained damage comes from two ranged attacks, not from spellcasting or a third standard attack. Class Identity Rangers are mobile ranged specialists who control distance through marksmanship, movement, traps, and battlefield awareness. They are most effective when they can read terrain before committing, choose favorable lines of attack, and punish enemies that approach carelessly. Focus represents the Ranger’s ability to convert patience and perception into precise action. Tradition & Outlook The Ranger tradition also descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines, but where Assassins close with a chosen target, Rangers cultivate distance, fieldcraft, and control of the approach. Rangers are common among scouts, hunters, pathfinders, border wardens, reconnaissance troops, and independent Daevas accustomed to surviving beyond secure settlements. They tend to value preparedness, observation, mobility, and freedom of movement. Appearance & Adventuring Rangers usually wear mobile armor and carry bows, ammunition, traps, and field equipment suited to extended movement. Their gear often reflects the terrain in which they learned their craft. Rangers adventure to explore dangerous regions, hunt monsters or enemy operatives, guide expeditions, secure routes, protect remote communities, or prove that no battlefield is truly open ground when preparation and range are on their side. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Ability Dexterity Secondary Ability Wisdom Hit Die d10 Saving Throws Dexterity, Strength Armor Leather Armor Weapons Longbows, Shortbows, Crossbows Skills Choose 2 from 6: Animal Handling, Athletics, Investigation, Nature, Perception, Survival Class Save DC 8 + PB + WIS modifier Signature Resource Focus Signature Mechanic Ranger Traps Extra Attack Level 5; two attacks only Spellcasting None Core Engine — Focus Maximum Focus equals your PB + WIS modifier, minimum 2. A Long Rest restores all expended Focus. A Short Rest restores Focus equal to PB, up to your maximum. Focus is a tactical reserve rather than ammunition or a tax on ordinary ranged attacks; Ranger Traps normally cost no Focus. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Starting State Focus is a rest-based reserve and does not reset merely because combat begins or ends. After a Long Rest it is normally full. Maximum PB + WIS modifier, minimum 2. Rest Recovery Long Rest restores all expended Focus. Short Rest restores Focus equal to PB, up to your maximum. Combat Recovery Hunter’s Rhythm and certain later Ranger/specialization features can regain Focus during genuine combat when their tactical conditions are actually satisfied. One active elemental spirit shares the Spiritmaster’s turn and action economy; together they equal one complete player character. The class establishes two battlefield positions, casts through the spirit, and earns Spirit Bond only through meaningful master-spirit coordination. Class Identity Spiritmasters are binders and commanders of elemental spirits who fight as a partnership rather than as a solitary caster. Their strength comes from coordinating their own spellcraft with a Greater Spirit, applying pressure, disruption, and control across more than one position on the battlefield. Spirit Bond represents the relationship and command structure that makes this divided presence function as one class. Tradition & Outlook The Spiritmaster tradition develops from Atreia’s mage disciplines but turns outward toward spirits, elemental forces, and the difficult art of directing entities shaped by Aether. Spiritmasters are often patient observers, researchers, summoners, or specialists in threats that cannot be understood through ordinary physical study. Their beliefs about spirits differ: some emphasize command, others partnership, responsibility, curiosity, or respect for elemental power. Appearance & Adventuring Spiritmasters use cloth armor and magical implements, while the visible presence of a summoned spirit often defines their silhouette more strongly than clothing does. Their equipment may include ritual, scholarly, or elemental motifs without creating additional mechanics. They adventure to understand unusual spirits, recover lost summoning knowledge, counter supernatural threats, serve as versatile magical operatives, or deepen the bond between Daeva and elemental ally.
