text: WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Primary Healer • Divine Grace • Protection • Purification Cleric “Protect me and you shall never fall.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Spellcasting Reference: Cleric has a dedicated spell-list page for quick browsing. View Cleric Spell List → Class Identity Class Chassis Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Spell List Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Support Sequence Tradition & Outlook Specialization Reassignment The Cleric is Wings of Atreia’s primary restorative spellcaster. It is deliberately more durable than the d6 full casters and is rewarded for meaningful intervention: healing an ally in real danger, actually preventing damage, or removing a significant hostile effect. Divine Grace then converts that successful support into more emergency power. Class Identity Clerics are Atreia’s foremost restorative and protective spellcasters. Their calling is not limited to healing wounds after the fact: they preserve the party through recovery, cleansing, protection, and timely intervention while retaining the ability to fight when necessary. Divine Grace represents the reserve of sacred and restorative power through which a Cleric answers moments of genuine need. Tradition & Outlook The Cleric tradition grows from Atreia’s priestly disciplines and is associated with healers, battlefield ministers, temple servants, protectors of communities, and Daevas who understand survival as a collective responsibility. Clerics often value service, perseverance, mercy, duty, or faith, but they need not share one personality or theology. A militant Cleric and a gentle healer may practice the same class through very different convictions. Appearance & Adventuring Clerics commonly combine durable armor with practical healing or ritual equipment. In Wings of Atreia they may use Maces, Hammers, Staffs, Quarterstaffs, and shields from Round Shields to Medium Shields according to their approved access. They adventure to protect lives, confront corruption or supernatural danger, recover sacred knowledge, serve a cause, or ensure that an expedition can survive places where retreat and ordinary medicine are not enough. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Ability Wisdom Secondary Ability Constitution Hit Die d8; additionally +2 maximum HP per Cleric level Saving Throws Wisdom, Constitution Armor Chain Armor Weapons Mace, Hammer, Staff, Quarterstaff, Round Shield, Medium Shield Skills Choose 2 from 6: History, Insight, Medicine, Nature, Perception, Religion Spellcasting Ability WIS Spell Save DC 8 + PB + WIS modifier Spell Attack PB + WIS modifier Signature Resource Divine Grace Spell Advancements +2 each level after 1; 38 total Maximum Spell Level 9 Extra Attack None Meaningful Support and Divine Grace Maximum Divine Grace equals PB + WIS modifier, minimum 2. Long Rest restores all; Short Rest restores PB. Once per round, when you Meaningfully Support yourself or an ally with a Cleric spell or feature, regain 1 Grace. Your normal once-per-round generation becomes available again at the start of your turn, allowing an off-turn protection to qualify without double-dipping around initiative boundaries. Meaningful Support means one of the following actually occurs: restore HP while the creature was below half maximum HP; prevent or reduce damage by at least PB; or suppress/remove a mechanically significant hostile condition or effect. Healing a full-HP creature, preventing 0 damage, refreshing temporary HP without increasing it, cosmetic effects, or intentionally manufactured harmless damage do not qualify. Self-support must satisfy the same standard. Temporary HP are not healing and cannot restore a creature from 0 HP. Passive aura bonuses and passive AC do not generate Divine Grace unless a feature explicitly says so. A secondary Cleric rider created by another Cleric feature does not recursively trigger Twin Devotion, Sacred Intervention, Graceful Channeling, Empowered Restoration, or another support sequence unless explicit. Only one Cleric rolled-healing class rider normally modifies the same individual healing instance, except Graceful Restoration may coexist with one specialization rolled-healing rider. Flat Cleric save penalties do not stack; use the largest. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Starting State Divine Grace is a rest-based reserve. It does not automatically reset to 0 when combat starts or ends; later features can establish a minimum starting amount. Maximum PB + WIS modifier, minimum 2. Rest Recovery Long Rest restores all Divine Grace. Short Rest restores Grace equal to PB, up to maximum. How You Gain It Once per round, regain 1 Grace when a Cleric spell or feature Meaningfully Supports you or an ally: healing while the recipient was below half HP, preventing/reducing at least PB damage, or suppressing/removing a mechanically significant hostile condition or effect. Generation Timing Your normal once-per-round generation becomes available again at the start of your turn. This lets a qualifying off-turn protection generate Grace without double-dipping across initiative boundaries. Does Not Qualify Healing a full-HP creature, preventing 0 damage, refreshing temporary HP without increasing it, passive aura/AC alone, cosmetic effects, or manufactured harmless damage do not generate Grace. How You Spend It Graceful Restoration 1 Grace; Protective Grace 1 Grace; Cleansing Grace 1 Grace; Purifier Absolute Purification 1 Grace; Level 20 Divine Presence save reroll 1 Grace. Other Cleric features spend Grace only when their text states a cost. Grace Momentum can reduce the first eligible technique cost. text: Close-Quarters Gunplay. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Tempo • Firearm Rhythm • Reload Mastery • Mobile Precision Gunslinger “A bullet sounds the same to everybody.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Tempo, Firearms, and Reload Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Tradition & Outlook Specialization Reassignment The Gunslinger is a mobile firearm martial whose power comes from maintaining Tempo through successful firearm play. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Fire. Move. Reload. Keep the rhythm alive long enough to turn Tempo into control, defense, and lethal pressure. Class Identity Gunslingers are technist marksmen who turn Aether-assisted firearms into speed, precision, and controlled ranged pressure. Pistols support rapid, mobile sequences through Quick Shot and Akimbo, while Muskets provide deliberate two-handed fire that concentrates Tempo into stronger individual hits through Deliberate Shot. Tempo represents the Gunslinger’s ability to build combat rhythm through successful action rather than treating every shot as an isolated event. Tradition & Outlook Gunslingers belong to Atreia’s newer technological traditions. The wider Aion tradition describes early firearm research being dismissed as technist tinkering until battlefield success forced major institutions to recognize the discipline. Wings of Atreia keeps that identity of innovation earning legitimacy through results while using Pistols and Muskets as the class’s only firearm categories. Gunslingers often value nerve, technical familiarity, accuracy, independence, and adaptability. Appearance & Adventuring Gunslingers favor mobile equipment, ammunition management, firearm maintenance, and a practical awareness of range and firing position. Their weapons can make them look strikingly modern beside older martial traditions, but their discipline remains Aetheric and distinctly Atreian. They adventure to test new techniques, serve as ranged specialists, hunt dangerous targets, protect expeditions from positions others cannot exploit, or demonstrate that innovation has earned its place in the war for Atreia. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Role Ranged weapon damage Secondary Role Mobility, precision, disruption Primary Ability DEX Secondary Ability INT Hit Die d8 Saving Throws DEX, INT Armor Leather Skills Choose 2 from 6: Acrobatics, Deception, Investigation, Perception, Sleight of Hand, Survival Weapons Pistols, Muskets Signature Resource Tempo Signature Mechanic Firearm sequencing and reload rhythm Core Engine — Tempo, Firearms, and Reload The Gunslinger is a mobile firearm martial whose power comes from maintaining Tempo through successful firearm play. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols Ranged Gunslinger One-handed Weapon Attack. Range 30/90 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d8 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. A Gunslinger can wield two Pistols, but doing so does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols are compatible with Quick Shot and Akimbo. Muskets Ranged Gunslinger Two-handed Weapon Attack. Range 60/180 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d12 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. Ammunition capacity is fixed at 2. Muskets cannot use Quick Shot or Akimbo. Gunslinger ammunition-restoration features can restore Musket shots normally, but a Musket can never hold more than 2 shots. Standard one-handed firearm capacity increases do not apply to Muskets. Reload Every firearm attack consumes one shot. A firearm with no shots remaining is Empty and cannot make firearm attacks until at least one shot is restored. Normal Bonus Action Reload: an Empty firearm is restored to its full Reload capacity. Ammunition restoration is not the Reload action unless a feature explicitly says so. Ammunition-restoration features can restore shots to either Pistols or Muskets up to that firearm's maximum capacity. A Musket's maximum capacity remains 2. Switching between carried one-handed Gunslinger firearms as part of a firearm attack requires no separate object interaction. Standard one-handed firearm capacity progression: Ammo Capacity 4 at Levels 1-4, Ammo Capacity 5 at 5-8, Ammo Capacity 6 at 9-14, and Ammo Capacity 7 at 15-20. Increasing capacity does not automatically reload an Empty firearm. Tempo Tempo is a genuine-combat resource representing firing rhythm, accuracy, and momentum. It begins at 0, resets to 0 when combat ends, and artificial initiative cannot generate it. Maximum Tempo: Levels 1-4 = 3; 5-8 = 4; 9-12 = 5; 13-16 = 6; 17-20 = 7. Clean Hit: after you hit

text: WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Combat Turn structure, actions, movement, attacks, damage, conditions, death, rests, and survival. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative Round and Turn Action Economy Attack Action Universal Actions Ready Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative, rounds, and combat-only resources are used only for genuine combat or another situation where structured turn order is necessary. Characters cannot manufacture artificial combat to farm cooldowns, resources, or timing triggers. Initiative Initiative = 1d20 + Dexterity modifier. Do not add PB unless an explicit feature says so. Alert adds +2 Initiative. There is no Surprise Round and Surprise does not grant Advantage on Initiative. When one side genuinely catches another side unaware, the GM may, at discretion, allow one appropriate pre-Initiative attack roll against the target's normal defense before Initiative is rolled. This is not an extra round, is not automatic, and does not create a general Surprise action economy. After that resolution, roll Initiative normally. Round and Turn One combat round represents approximately six seconds in the game world. Each participant normally takes one turn in Initiative order. All turns in the round abstract actions occurring within the same six-second span; do not add each turn as another six seconds. Action Economy Action. One per turn. Movement. Up to the creature’s available movement, subject to terrain and conditions. Bonus Action. Up to one, but only when a feature grants something that uses a Bonus Action. Reaction. Normally one per round, refreshing at the start of the creature’s turn unless an explicit class rule says otherwise. Object interaction. One free simple object interaction per turn. There is no universal Action-to-Bonus-Action or Bonus-Action-to-Action conversion. Unused movement or Actions are not stored for later turns. Attack Action The Attack Action makes one attack unless a feature such as Extra Attack says otherwise. Grapple and Shove are full Actions and do not replace one attack within Extra Attack. Player Weapon Requirement. A player character must be wielding an approved class weapon to take the normal Attack Action. Unarmed Attacks and Improvised Weapons are not player combat options unless a later explicit feature creates a specific exception. Opportunity Attacks. Opportunity Attacks remain part of the core combat rules. When a hostile creature you can perceive voluntarily leaves your melee reach, you may use your Reaction to make one melee attack against it, resolving the attack before it leaves that reach. Forced movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Universal Actions Dash. Gain additional movement equal to your current Speed for the turn. Difficult Terrain and other movement costs still apply. While flying, Dash adds horizontal movement but does not grant an additional altitude-layer change. Disengage. Until the end of your turn, your movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks. Dodge. Until the start of your next turn, attacks against you have Disadvantage if you can perceive the attacker, and you have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws. Dodge ends if you become Incapacitated or your Speed becomes 0. Hide. You must have meaningful concealment or another circumstance that allows hiding. Make Dexterity (Stealth) against Passive Perception or active Perception as appropriate. You cannot Hide while clearly seen. Hidden is not Invisible. Making an attack reveals your position after that attack resolves. Search. Deliberately search using a GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation). Use Object. Use this Action for substantial manipulation beyond the one free simple object interaction. A specific item’s activation rule controls when it states another cost. Ready A creature can prepare one Action for a perceivable trigger. When the trigger occurs, the creature may use its Reaction to perform the readied Action. Ready does not store ordinary movement, but Dash can be readied as the Action. Readied attacks retain all weapon properties. A readied spell must still meet implement and targeting requirements when released. Losing a mandatory implement before release prevents release. Concentration begins when the spell actually resolves. Ready never bypasses aerial restrictions, range, or other universal rules. Simultaneous Effects Effects resolve one at a time. The active creature orders its own simultaneous effects; the GM orders GM-controlled simultaneous effects. For opposing same-time effects, resolve the active creature first, then use Initiative if needed. Damage resolves before state changes caused by that damage. Start-of-turn and end-of-turn timing is literal. Reactions follow their trigger wording and are not inserted retroactively after the consequence has already resolved unless a rule explicitly allows it. Movement, Positioning & Physical Interaction Ground Movement Base Walk. 30 feet for a Daeva unless modified. Difficult Terrain. Costs 2 feet of movement for every 1 foot traveled. Prone. Standing from Prone requires one full Action and does not consume movement. A creature can move normally afterward if movement remains available. No universal Flanking. Opposite sides do not automatically grant Advantage. No universal Facing. Being behind a creature does not automatically grant Advantage. Occupied Spaces. A creature may move through a willing allied creature's space, treating that space as difficult terrain unless an explicit feature says otherwise. A creature cannot move through an enemy or neutral creature's occupied space unless an explicit rule permits it, and cannot end movement in another creature's occupied space unless an explicit rule allows it. Grapple and Shove Grapple and Shove each require a full Action. The target must be within reach and no more than one Size larger than you. Make Strength (Athletics) contested by the target’s choice of Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics). On a successful Grapple, the target becomes Grappled; it may use its Action to escape by repeating the contest. Moving a Grappled creature costs 2 feet of movement for every 1 foot moved unless the target is at least two Sizes smaller than you. On a successful Shove, choose to push the target 5 feet or knock it Prone. Grapple and Shove do not replace attacks within the Attack Action and cannot substitute for Extra Attack. Player Weapon Requirement. Player characters do not use a universal Unarmed Attack damage rule; the normal Attack Action requires an approved class weapon unless an explicit feature says otherwise. Disarm Disarm is a full Action. The attacker uses Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Sleight of Hand), contested by the defender’s Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics). The target must be a reachable, removable held object. Two-handed held items grant the defender +2 on the contest. On success, the item drops nearby unless a direct snatch is physically feasible and the attacker has a free hand. Disarm does not remove worn armor, Wings, integrated equipment, or normally strapped shields. Creature Carrying and Dragging Same size or one size smaller. Movement costs 2 feet per 1 foot. Two sizes smaller. Normal movement. More than one size larger. Normally requires helpers, a vehicle, a feature, or GM adjudication. Pickup. Picking up a creature in combat normally requires an Action; setting it down in a reasonable space is free. Unwilling creature. Must first be grappled or otherwise controlled. Aerial carrying. Uses the same 2:1 movement rule when applicable, allows no voluntary ascent while burdened, and still consumes normal Flight Slots. Attacks, Damage, Healing & Temporary HP Attack Rolls Ranged Weapon Attacks. Physical ranged weapon attacks use the weapon’s listed Normal Range and Maximum Range. Beyond Normal Range and within Maximum Range, the attack roll has Disadvantage; beyond Maximum Range, the attack automatically misses. If the target is within 5 feet of the attacker, the attack roll also has Disadvantage. These rules apply unless a specific feature explicitly changes them. Attack roll = 1d20 + relevant ability modifier + PB if proficient. Natural 1. Automatic miss on an attack roll. Natural 20. Automatic hit and a critical hit. Critical hit. Double only the rolled damage dice. Flat modifiers are not doubled. Damage Types WoA uses exactly twelve universal damage types: Bludgeoning, Piercing, Slashing, Fire, Cold, Lightning, Acid, Poison, Radiant, Necrotic, Psychic, and Force. Thunder is not a universal damage type, and Aether is not a damage type. Resistance, Vulnerability and Reduction Apply flat damage reduction before Resistance or Vulnerability. Resistance halves damage, rounded down. Vulnerability doubles damage. Multiple damage types are resolved separately when their defensive interactions differ. Monster Defenses. A monster has Resistance, Immunity, or Vulnerability only when that trait is explicitly listed in its statblock. Monster rank does not grant any of these automatically. Unless Wings of Atreia explicitly overrides the term, Resistance, Immunity, and Vulnerability use their normal core meanings. 0 HP and Excess Damage HP never goes below 0. Ordinary excess damage beyond 0 is discarded; there is no massive-damage instant-death rule. Ordinary damage received while already at 0 HP has no effect on HP or Death Saves and cannot kill unless an explicit exceptional effect says otherwise. Healing Healing cannot raise current HP above maximum HP. Valid healing that raises a creature at 0 HP to at least 1 HP ends the ordinary Dying/0-HP Unconscious state, clears accumulated Death Save successes and failures, and wakes the creature unless another independent effect still causes Unconsciousness. A Stable creature at 0 HP also wakes if healed to at least 1 HP. Nonlethally defeated creatures follow the same rule. Healing does not automatically remove Unconsciousness caused by an unrelated spell, condition, Exhaustion 6, or special effect. Temporary HP Separate buffer. Temporary HP is not healing and does not increase current or maximum HP. No stacking. If a creature receives a new Temporary HP amount, it keeps the higher amount unless an effect explicitly allows stacking. Damage order. After defensive modifications, damage removes Temporary HP first; excess carries into current HP. At 0 HP. Temporary HP does not wake, stabilize, end Dying, or substitute for actual HP. Duration. Temporary HP tied to a duration disappears when that granting effect ends; otherwise it lasts until depleted or replaced. Area Effects and Friendly Fire An area effect affects every valid creature or object in its area unless its text excludes or selectively chooses targets. Allies and the caster are not automatically immune. Objects are affected only when the effect says so. Cover applies normally. Overlapping separate effects resolve separately. Forced movement caused by an area only occurs if the effect explicitly says so. In aerial spaces, use the normal WoA 3D-distance rule. Targeting and Valid Targets Legal wording. An effect can affect only a target permitted by its text. Range. Check range when the effect is used. Line of Effect. Normally required unless the effect says otherwise. “Can see.” Requires both visibility and a valid unobstructed line for the effect. Unseen target. Use the base unseen-attacker/target procedure. If you attack a creature you cannot see but whose location you know, the attack has Disadvantage. If its location is unknown, you must first choose the space you are attacking; the attack automatically misses if the creature is not there. A spell requiring 'a creat

WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Aether & Spellcasting Aether environment and interaction, universal spellcasting, and Spell Advancement. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Aether Environment, Interaction & Gathering Aether Interaction Aether Sources Refined Aether Gathering Aether Hazards Universal Spellcasting Universal Model Spell Acquisition Aether Environment, Interaction & Gathering Aether Interaction Aether Interaction uses Intelligence (Arcana) for intellectual analysis and Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) for physical manipulation. Typical DC guidance is 10, 12, 15, 18, or 20+ according to complexity and danger. Aether Sources Nodes, Currents, Fissures, and other environmental Aether phenomena can provide opportunities, hazards, travel effects, or Refined Aether. Their exact scene behavior is defined by the source. Refined Aether Gathering Gathering Refined Aether uses Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) against the source DC. Aether Level DC Yield Range Default Yield 1 8 2–6 4 2 10 6–12 9 3 12 12–24 18 4 15 24–40 32 5 18 40–60 50 The GM identifies a valid source and its Aether Level. Only the interacting character rolls. Apply normal modifiers and Help only if actually meaningful. On success, gain a yield within the listed range based on source richness; if no special richness is established, use the Default Yield. A successful gathering normally exhausts that source. Multiple deposits exist only when the GM explicitly establishes them. Failure gives no Refined Aether and does not automatically exhaust the source, but a new attempt requires a meaningful change in circumstances. Another party member does not automatically create a fresh attempt. Normal gathering is not performed during active combat unless gathering itself is an explicit encounter objective. Already-refined Aether recovered from caches or stores is ordinary loot and requires no gathering check. Aether Hazards Aether Hazards use the universal sequence Trigger → Save → DC → Effect → Duration. Standard severity bands are Minor DC 10–11, Moderate DC 12–14, Severe DC 15–17, and Extreme DC 18–20+. The four approved hazard families are Aether Storm, Aether Surge, Aether Eruption, and Unstable Zone. Each specific hazard defines its actual Trigger, Save, Effect, and Duration. Dangerous Aether changes are normally telegraphed in advance unless the hazard is specifically concealed. Strategic Refined Aether uses not defined in this handbook are deferred unless a future subsystem explicitly establishes them. Vehicle-related Refined Aether rules remain deferred with vehicle rules, and the current Abyss Warfront system uses no universal Refined Aether conversion for Fortress power. Universal Spellcasting Universal Model WoA has no spell slots and no cantrip category. Each spell is individually At-Will, Cooldown-based, Short-Rest limited, or Long-Rest limited. Class resources may modify spells but are not universal casting costs. Spell Acquisition Spells are class-granted abilities. They cannot be bought, sold, looted, copied from spellbooks or scrolls, learned from vendors, or acquired by commerce or exploration. A spell becomes available only when the character reaches its Unlock Level and, when applicable, satisfies the immediately preceding spell in its linear prerequisite chain. Unlocking a later spell never removes the earlier spell. Newly unlocked spells begin at Spell Level 1 unless explicitly stated otherwise. Spell Advancement — Final Rule. A class grants Spell Advancements according to its finalized progression. One Spell Advancement raises one eligible unlocked spell by 1 Spell Level, subject to that class’s Maximum Spell Level and listed prerequisites. Unspent Spell Advancements may be banked indefinitely, but banked or newly earned Spell Advancements may be spent only when the character gains a level; they cannot normally be spent during an adventure, between encounters, or during a rest. A character cannot spend more Spell Advancements than they have earned. Spell Retraining. There is no universal spell retraining. Once a Spell Advancement is spent, it is permanent unless a specific class feature, explicit story effect, or GM-approved exceptional circumstance directly permits reassignment. Casting Frequency and Action Economy At-Will spells may be cast whenever action economy permits. Cooldown X spells become available at the start of the caster’s Xth turn after the casting turn. Round-based cooldowns advance only during genuine combat; artificial Initiative cannot refresh, farm, or manipulate cooldowns or class resources. Outside genuine combat, a Cooldown spell becomes available again 1 minute after use unless the spell states a longer restriction. Short-Rest and Long-Rest spells regain uses after the named rest. Casting Time is binding. Cas

Forced movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Universal Actions Dash. Gain additional movement equal to your current Speed for the turn. Difficult Terrain and other movement costs still apply. While flying, Dash adds horizontal movement but does not grant an additional altitude-layer change. Disengage. Until the end of your turn, your movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks. Dodge. Until the start of your next turn, attacks against you have Disadvantage if you can perceive the attacker, and you have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws. Dodge ends if you become Incapacitated or your Speed becomes 0. Hide. You must have meaningful concealment or another circumstance that allows hiding. Make Dexterity (Stealth) against Passive Perception or active Perception as appropriate. You cannot Hide while clearly seen. Hidden is not Invisible. Making an attack reveals your position after that attack resolves. Search. Deliberately search using a GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation). Use Object. Use this Action for substantial manipulation beyond the one free simple object interaction. A specific item’s activation rule controls when it states another cost. Ready A creature can prepare one Action for a perceivable trigger. When the trigger occurs, the creature may use its Reaction to perform the readied Action. Ready does not store ordinary movement, but Dash can be readied as the Action. Readied attacks retain all weapon properties. A readied spell must still meet implement and targeting requirements when released. Losing a mandatory implement before release prevents release. Concentration begins when the spell actually resolves. Ready never bypasses aerial restrictions, range, or other universal rules. Simultaneous Effects Effects resolve one at a time. The active creature orders its own simultaneous effects; the GM orders GM-controlled simultaneous effects. For opposing same-time effects, resolve the active creature first, then use Initiative if needed. Damage resolves before state changes

text: Core Engine — Aether Focus. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Full Caster • Elemental Damage • Aether Focus • Spell Shaping Sorcerer “This will only hurt for a second.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Spellcasting Reference: Sorcerer has a dedicated spell-list page for quick browsing. View Sorcerer Spell List → Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Aether Focus Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Spell List Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Spellcasting Example Specialization Reassignment The Sorcerer is the raw magical-damage benchmark. It casts through Fire, Ice, Lightning, and Wind spell chains, then spends Aether Focus only when a particular spell needs more damage, area, control pressure, or reliability. Aether Focus enhances spells; it is never the fuel required to cast ordinary Sorcerer spells. Class Identity Sorcerers are masters of direct Aetheric spellcraft, combining destructive magic with the ability to control the shape and tempo of a fight. They can punish clustered enemies, deny movement or action, and unleash powerful spells when an opening appears. Aether Focus represents the concentration and arcane discipline required to turn immense magical potential into reliable battlefield power. Tradition & Outlook The Sorcerer tradition grows from Atreia’s mage disciplines and is associated with formal magical study, experimentation, academies, battlefield arcanists, and Daevas fascinated by the structure of Aether itself. Sorcerers commonly value knowledge, precision, preparation, and intellectual mastery, although their personalities range from scholarly restraint to spectacular confidence. For many, magic is both a weapon and a language through which Atreia can be understood. Appearance & Adventuring Sorcerers favor cloth armor and magical implements such as Orbs and Spellbooks under the Wings of Atreia equipment rules. Their appearance may reflect academic, military, ceremonial, or highly individual magical traditions. They adventure to recover lost knowledge, study Aetheric phenomena, test magical theories, defend their people with overwhelming spellcraft, or confront powers that ordinary weapons cannot adequately answer. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Ability Intelligence Secondary Ability Wisdom Hit Die d6 Saving Throws Constitution, Intelligence Armor Cloth Implements Magical Orbs, Spellbooks Spellcasting Ability INT Spell Save DC 8 + PB + INT modifier Spell Attack PB + INT modifier Signature Resource Aether Focus Spell Advancements +2 every class level after 1; 38 total Maximum Spell Level 9 Extra Attack None Core Engine — Aether Focus Maximum Aether Focus equals PB + INT modifier, minimum 2. A Long Rest restores all expended Aether Focus. A Short Rest restores Aether Focus equal to PB, up to your maximum. The resource is an enhancement reserve: casting an ordinary Sorcerer spell never requires Aether Focus unless a spell or class feature explicitly says otherwise. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Starting State Aether Focus is a rest-based enhancement reserve and does not reset merely because combat begins or ends. After a Long Rest it is normally full. Maximum PB + INT modifier, minimum 2. Aether Sage and the Level 20 capstone can explicitly increase this maximum. Rest Recovery Long Rest restores all expended Aether Focus. Short Rest restores Focus equal to PB, up to maximum; Aether Sage can improve this recovery. Base Generation The base Sorcerer does not generate Aether Focus from ordinary spell hits or damage. Combat refunds exist only where a class or specialization feature explicitly grants them. How You Spend It Intensify 1 Focus; Widen 1 Focus; Potent Control 1 Focus; other Sorcerer features spend Aether Focus only when their text states a cost. Ordinary spellcasting costs no Focus. Refunds / Discounts Aether Sage and later features may discount a shaping cost or refund Focus after a qualifying shaped spell. A refund is not a second casting or a new spell trigger. Persistence Unused Aether Focus persists between encounters until spent or restored. Important Distinction Aether Focus is a Sorcerer class resource. It is not environmental Aether, Refined Aether, an Aether State, or a universal damage type. text: Core Engine — Cadence. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Martial Support • Mantras • Cadence • Harmonic Warfare Chanter “Stay close, stay safe.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Spellcasting Reference: Chanter has a dedicated spell-list page for quick browsing. View Chanter Spell List → Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Cadence Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Spell List Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Rhythm Sequence Specialization Reassignment The Chanter wins by alternating weapon attacks, spells, and active Mantra management. Cadence is earned by changing categories rather than repeating one action, then spent on damage, protection, healing, and tactical movement. It is a secondary healer and hybrid support, not a replacement for the Cleric or a dedicated martial striker. Class Identity Chanters are martial support specialists who combine staff technique, enchantment, restorative magic, and Mantras into a continuous rhythm of battle. Rather than solving every problem through one large spell, a Chanter improves the party’s performance over time and responds to changing pressure with Cadence. Their presence is felt in how effectively the entire group moves, strikes, and recovers together. Tradition & Outlook The Chanter tradition grows from Atreia’s priestly disciplines but emphasizes disciplined body, voice, repetition, and the shaping of Aether through words and practiced forms. Chanters are often teachers, battle companions, spiritual guides, martial ascetics, or morale-keepers. They tend to value harmony between individual excellence and collective strength: the ideal Chanter does not merely stand beside allies but helps those allies become more capable. Appearance & Adventuring Chanters are strongly associated with Staff and Quarterstaff techniques in Wings of Atreia. Their clothing and armor tend to allow movement while retaining the ceremonial or disciplined character of a priestly warrior. They adventure to guide companions, strengthen military or exploratory groups, carry teachings into dangerous places, preserve morale during long campaigns, or prove that disciplined cooperation can overcome enemies stronger than any one Daeva. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Ability Intelligence Secondary Ability Charisma Hit Die d8 Saving Throws Constitution, Intelligence Armor Chain Armor Weapons Staff, Quarterstaff Skills Choose 2 from 6: History, Insight, Medicine, Performance, Persuasion, Religion Spellcasting Ability INT Mantra Ability CHA Signature Resource Cadence Spell Advancements +1 each level after 1; 19 total Maximum Spell Level 7 Extra Attack Level 5; two attacks only Core Engine — Cadence Cadence is a genuine-combat resource. It begins at 0 when combat starts, resets to 0 when combat ends, and artificial initiative cannot create or restore it. Maximum Cadence is 3 at Levels 1–4, 4 at 5–8, 5 at 9–12, 6 at 13–16, and 7 at 17–20. Category Qualifying Event Martial You hit a hostile creature with a weapon attack. Spell A Chanter spell meaningfully affects a creature by hit, damage, failed save, actual healing, meaningful prevention, or another significant effect. Chant You activate, replace, or deliberately invoke a Mantra/Chant and it meaningfully changes at least one creature. Passive maintenance never qualifies. Your previous qualifying category is always the most recent successful qualifying category, whether or not that event generated Cadence. When you successfully complete a qualifying event whose category differs from your previous successful qualifying category, gain 1 Cadence, subject to the normal generation limit. Your first successful qualifying event in a combat establishes your previous category; it does not generate Cadence by itself. Normal Cadence generation is limited to 1 per turn unless a feature explicitly grants more. Secondary Chanter riders do not recursively generate Cadence, Resonant Network triggers, Mantra Weaving, or other support sequences unless explicit. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Starting State Cadence begins at 0 when genuine combat starts and resets to 0 when combat ends. Maximum 3 at Levels 1–4; 4 at 5–8; 5 at 9–12; 6 at 13–16; 7 at 17–20. Qualifying Categories Martial: a weapon attack hits a hostile. Spell: a Chanter spell meaningfully affects a creature. Chant: you activate, replace, or deliberately invoke a Mantra/Chant and it meaningfully changes at least one creature; passive maintenance does not qualify. How You Gain It When a successful qualifying event uses a category different from your previous successful qualifying category, gain 1 Cadence. The first successful qualifying event of a combat only establishes the previous category. Generation Limits

text: Core Engine — Focus. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Ranged Striker • Focus • Traps • Tactical Repositioning Ranger “Chase me or run away. Either way, you'll only die tired.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Focus Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Ranger is a nonmagical ranged hunter that controls enemy movement with persistent battlefield traps, spends Focus on precision or evasive shots, and is rewarded for exploiting targets that walk into prepared terrain. Its sustained damage comes from two ranged attacks, not from spellcasting or a third standard attack. Class Identity Rangers are mobile ranged specialists who control distance through marksmanship, movement, traps, and battlefield awareness. They are most effective when they can read terrain before committing, choose favorable lines of attack, and punish enemies that approach carelessly. Focus represents the Ranger’s ability to convert patience and perception into precise action. Tradition & Outlook The Ranger tradition also descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines, but where Assassins close with a chosen target, Rangers cultivate distance, fieldcraft, and control of the approach. Rangers are common among scouts, hunters, pathfinders, border wardens, reconnaissance troops, and independent Daevas accustomed to surviving beyond secure settlements. They tend to value preparedness, observation, mobility, and freedom of movement. Appearance & Adventuring Rangers usually wear mobile armor and carry bows, ammunition, traps, and field equipment suited to extended movement. Their gear often reflects the terrain in which they learned their craft. Rangers adventure to explore dangerous regions, hunt monsters or enemy operatives, guide expeditions, secure routes, protect remote communities, or prove that no battlefield is truly open ground when preparation and range are on their side. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Ability Dexterity Secondary Ability Wisdom Hit Die d10 Saving Throws Dexterity, Strength Armor Leather Armor Weapons Longbows, Shortbows, Crossbows Skills Choose 2 from 6: Animal Handling, Athletics, Investigation, Nature, Perception, Survival Class Save DC 8 + PB + WIS modifier Signature Resource Focus Signature Mechanic Ranger Traps Extra Attack Level 5; two attacks only Spellcasting None Core Engine — Focus Maximum Focus equals your PB + WIS modifier, minimum 2. A Long Rest restores all expended Focus. A Short Rest restores Focus equal to PB, up to your maximum. Focus is a tactical reserve rather than ammunition or a tax on ordinary ranged attacks; Ranger Traps normally cost no Focus. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Starting State Focus is a rest-based reserve and does not reset merely because combat begins or ends. After a Long Rest it is normally full. Maximum PB + WIS modifier, minimum 2. Rest Recovery Long Rest restores all expended Focus. Short Rest restores Focus equal to PB, up to your maximum. Combat Recovery Hunter’s Rhythm and certain later Ranger/specialization features can regain Focus during genuine combat when their tactical conditions are actually satisfied. How You Spend It Precision Shot 1 Focus; Pinning Shot 1 Focus; Evasive Step 1 Focus; Deadeye Perfect Shot 1 Focus. Other Ranger features spend Focus only when their text states a cost. Refunds / Recovery A combat refund or recovery is not a new attack, trap trigger, or separate technique. It simply restores Focus up to your maximum. Persistence Unused Focus persists between encounters until spent or restored; there is no automatic combat-end reset. Does Not Generate Standing still and firing, harmless staged interactions, or ordinary trap placement do not create Focus unless an explicit recovery feature is actually triggered. desc: Core Engine — Sneak Attack and Rune Marks — Wings of Atreia reference section.
text: Core Engine — Sneak Attack and Rune Marks. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Melee Striker • Sneak Attack • Rune Marks • Execution Assassin “You'll know I'm there when you're dead.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Sneak Attack and Rune Marks Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Assassin is a precision melee striker that builds target-bound Rune Marks, converts them into burst damage or execution riders, and uses Shadow Step to remain difficult to pin down. Unlike a conventional Extra Attack martial, its Level 5 Assassination Sequence is a conditional follow-up attack tied to a successful Sneak Attack. Class Identity Assassins are precision predators who win through positioning, timing, concealment, and carefully prepared execution. Their art is not simply “attacking from stealth.” An Assassin studies a target, creates the right opening, carves Rune Marks, and converts preparation into a sudden lethal advantage. Their greatest strength is the ability to decide where and when a close-range confrontation becomes dangerous. Tradition & Outlook The Assassin tradition descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines and is practiced by infiltrators, covert operatives, hunters of dangerous individuals, intelligence agents, and Daevas who favor certainty over spectacle. Assassins often prize patience, awareness, self-control, and economy of motion. Their motives vary widely: service to a faction, revenge, professional duty, protection through preemptive action, or the pursuit of perfect technique. Appearance & Adventuring Assassins favor equipment that permits mobility and unobstructed movement, with Shortswords and Daggers forming the class’s approved weapon identity in Wings of Atreia. Their appearance may be subdued or ceremonial, but practical Assassins avoid anything that compromises movement or control. They adventure when a threat must be found before it strikes, a route must be infiltrated, an enemy leader must be neutralized, or a mystery demands someone comfortable operating unseen. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Ability Dexterity Secondary Ability Constitution Hit Die d8 Saving Throws Dexterity, Intelligence Armor Leather Armor Weapons Shortswords, Daggers Skills Choose 2 from 6: Acrobatics, Deception, Investigation, Perception, Sleight of Hand, Stealth Class Save DC 8 + PB + DEX modifier Signature Resource Rune Marks placed on enemies Signature Mechanics Sneak Attack, Rune Carving, Rune Burst, Shadow Step Extra Attack No standard Extra Attack; Assassination Sequence at Level 5 Spellcasting None Core Engine — Sneak Attack and Rune Marks Sneak Attack applies once on each of your own turns when an eligible finesse melee weapon attack has Advantage, or when another qualifying enemy is adjacent to the target and you do not have Disadvantage. Sneak Attack damage scales from 1d6 at Level 1 to 10d6 at Level 19. Levels Sneak Attack Rune Die Marked Targets 1–2 1d6 d4 1 3–4 2d6 d4 1 5–6 3d6 d6 1 7–8 4d6 d6 1 9–10 5d6 d6 2 11–12 6d6 d8 2 13–14 7d6 d8 2 15–16 8d6 d8 2 17–18 9d6 d10 3 19–20 10d6 d10 3 A creature can carry up to 3 of your Rune Marks. Rune Carving: once on your turn, a qualifying melee hit that actually deals Sneak Attack places 1 Rune Mark after that hit resolves. Alternatively, hitting the same creature with two different melee attacks during your turn can place 1 Rune Mark after the second hit. Normal attack-based Rune placement is limited to 1 Mark per turn unless a feature explicitly increases it. Newly created Rune Marks cannot be consumed by the same hit that created them. If you exceed your current marked-target limit, choose one previously marked creature and remove all of your Marks from it. Marks disappear when consumed, when the marked creature is defeated, or when the encounter ends. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Resource Form Rune Marks are target-bound counters, not a generic personal pool. A creature carries your Marks until they are consumed or removed. Maximum Up to 3 Rune Marks per creature. Marked-target capacity is 1 creature through Level 8, 2 from Levels 9–16, and 3 from Level 17 onward. How You Place Marks Once on your turn, a qualifying melee hit that actually deals Sneak Attack places 1 Mark after the hit resolves. Alternatively, two different melee hits against the same creature during your turn can place 1 Mark after the second hit. Placement Limits Normal attack-based placement is limited to 1 Mark per turn unless an explicit feature increases it. A newly created Mark cannot be consumed by the hit that created it. How You Spend Them On a hit against a marked creature

View Spiritmaster Spell List → Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Summon Spirit Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Spell List Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequence Specialization Reassignment The Spiritmaster is a two-body tactical caster. One active elemental spirit shares the Spiritmaster’s turn and action economy; together they equal one complete player character. The class establishes two battlefield positions, casts through the spirit, and earns Spirit Bond only through meaningful master-spirit coordination. Class Identity Spiritmasters are binders and commanders of elemental spirits who fight as a partnership rather than as a solitary caster. Their strength comes from coordinating their own spellcraft with a Greater Spirit, applying pressure, disruption, and control across more than one position on the battlefield. Spirit Bond represents the relationship and command structure that makes this divided presence function as one class. Tradition & Outlook The Spiritmaster tradition develops from Atreia’s mage disciplines but turns outward toward spirits, elemental forces, and the difficult art of directing entities shaped by Aether. Spiritmasters are often patient observers, researchers, summoners, or specialists in threats that cannot be understood through ordinary physical study. Their beliefs about spirits differ: some emphasize command, others partnership, responsibility, curiosity, or respect for elemental power. Appearance & Adventuring Spiritmasters use cloth armor and magical implements, while the visible presence of a summoned spirit often defines their silhouette more strongly than clothing does. Their equipment may include ritual, scholarly, or elemental motifs without creating additional mechanics. They adventure to understand unusual spirits, recover lost summoning knowledge, counter supernatural threats, serve as versatile magical operatives, or deepen the bond between Daeva and elemental ally. A defeated spirit disperses into Aether, makes no death saves, and cannot be resummoned until the start of your next turn. text: Core Engine — Tempo, Firearms, and Reload. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Tempo • Firearm Rhythm • Reload Mastery • Mobile Precision Gunslinger “A bullet sounds the same to everybody.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Tempo, Firearms, and Reload Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Tradition & Outlook Specialization Reassignment The Gunslinger is a mobile firearm martial whose power comes from maintaining Tempo through successful firearm play. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Fire. Move. Reload. Keep the rhythm alive long enough to turn Tempo into control, defense, and lethal pressure. Class Identity Gunslingers are technist marksmen who turn Aether-assisted firearms into speed, precision, and controlled ranged pressure. Pistols support rapid, mobile sequences through Quick Shot and Akimbo, while Muskets provide deliberate two-handed fire that concentrates Tempo into stronger individual hits through Deliberate Shot. Tempo represents the Gunslinger’s ability to build combat rhythm through successful action rather than treating every shot as an isolated event. Tradition & Outlook Gunslingers belong to Atreia’s newer technological traditions. The wider Aion tradition describes early firearm research being dismissed as technist tinkering until battlefield success forced major institutions to recognize the discipline. Wings of Atreia keeps that identity of innovation earning legitimacy through results while using Pistols and Muskets as the class’s only firearm categories. Gunslingers often value nerve, technical familiarity, accuracy, independence, and adaptability. Appearance & Adventuring Gunslingers favor mobile equipment, ammunition management, firearm maintenance, and a practical awareness of range and firing position. Their weapons can make them look strikingly modern beside older martial traditions, but their discipline remains Aetheric and distinctly Atreian. They adventure to test new techniques, serve as ranged specialists, hunt dangerous targets, protect expeditions from positions others cannot exploit, or demonstrate that innovation has earned its place in the war for Atreia. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Role Ranged weapon damage Secondary Role Mobility, precision, disruption Primary Ability DEX Secondary Ability INT Hit Die d8 Saving Throws DEX, INT Armor Leather Skills Choose 2 from 6: Acrobatics, Deception, Investigation, Perception, Sleight of Hand, Survival Weapons Pistols, Muskets Signature Resource Tempo Signature Mechanic Firearm sequencing and reload rhythm Core Engine — Tempo, Firearms, and Reload The Gunslinger is a mobile firearm martial whose power comes from maintaining Tempo through successful firearm play. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols Ranged Gunslinger One-handed Weapon Attack. Range 30/90 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d8 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. A Gunslinger can wield two Pistols, but doing so does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols are compatible with Quick Shot and Akimbo. Muskets Ranged Gunslinger Two-handed Weapon Attack. Range 60/180 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d12 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. Ammunition capacity is fixed at 2. Muskets cannot use Quick Shot or Akimbo. Gunslinger ammunition-restoration features can restore Musket shots normally, but a Musket can never hold more than 2 shots. Standard one-handed firearm capacity increases do not apply to Muskets. Reload Every firearm attack consumes one shot. A firearm with no shots remaining is Empty and cannot make firearm attacks until at least one shot is restored. Normal Bonus Action Reload: an Empty firearm is restored to its full Reload capacity. Ammunition restoration is not the Reload action unless a feature explicitly says so. Ammunition-restoration features can restore shots to either Pistols or Muskets up to that firearm's maximum capacity. A Musket's maximum capacity remains 2. Switching between carried one-handed Gunslinger firearms as part of a firearm attack requires no separate object interaction. Standard one-handed firearm capacity progression: Ammo Capacity 4 at Levels 1-4, Ammo Capacity 5 at 5-8, Ammo Capacity 6 at 9-14, and Ammo Capacity 7 at 15-20. Increasing capacity does not automatically reload an Empty firearm. Tempo Tempo is a genuine-combat resource representing firing rhythm, accuracy, and momentum. It begins at 0, resets to 0 when combat ends, and artificial initiative cannot generate it. Maximum Tempo: Levels 1-4 = 3; 5-8 = 4; 9-12 = 5; 13-16 = 6; 17-20 = 7. Clean

title: Core Resolution | Wings of Atreia
desc: The d20 test framework used for meaningful uncertain outcomes.
text: WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Core Resolution The d20 test framework used for meaningful uncertain outcomes. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. d20 Tests & Core Resolution d20 Tests Ability Checks Saving Throws Save DCs Advantage and Disadvantage Help Passive Perception, Passive Investigation & Search d20 Tests & Core Resolution d20 Tests Ability Checks, attack rolls, and saving throws use a d20. Roll only when the outcome is uncertain and meaningful. If success is automatic, impossible, or consequence-free, no roll is needed. Ability Checks Choose the ability that best fits the approach, then add Proficiency Bonus if the character is proficient in the relevant skill. Expertise doubles the PB contribution for that proficiency. WoA retains six abilities and eighteen skills. A specialized Background can authorize a character to attempt obscure knowledge, but it does not automatically modify the roll. Saving Throws A saving throw uses the specified ability modifier and adds PB only if the creature is proficient in that saving throw. Ties are resolved according to the specific system; otherwise meeting a DC succeeds. Save DCs Default effect Save DC = 8 + Proficiency Bonus + the relevant ability modifier, unless an explicit class, spell, item, monster, or environmental rule gives a different DC. Advantage and Disadvantage When a rule grants Advantage, roll two d20s and use the higher. When it grants Disadvantage, roll two and use the lower. If both apply, they cancel unless a specific rule says otherwise. Resolve Advantage/Disadvantage before applying numeric modifiers. Help Help never grants Advantage. A meaningful helper grants +2 to one Ability Check. Normally only one helper can contribute. There is no Assist Attack and Help cannot modify Death Saves. Passive Perception, Passive Investigation & Search Passive Perception = 10 + your Wisdom (Perception) modifier. Passive Investigation = 10 + your Intelligence (Investigation) modifier. Advantage on the relevant check adds +5 to the passive score; Disadvantage subtracts 5. Multiple instances of the same source do not stack, and Advantage and Disadvantage cancel normally. Hide is opposed by Passive Perception; ties favor the observer. An active Search uses the GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation), against the relevant DC or opposing Stealth; ties favor the Searcher where opposed. Repeated checks require a meaningful change in circumstances. ← Back to Rules Wings of Atreia · Created & Designed by Clark Michael Zafra (“ArchQwynn”) · Non-commercial fan project.

text: Cover, Line of Sight & Line of Effect. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Exploration & Interaction Vision, stealth, traps, locks, theft, hazards, social rules, chases, and loot. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Vision, Stealth, Traps, Locks & Theft Vision and Light Cover, Line of Sight & Line of Effect Stealth and Infiltration Traps and Non-Aether Hazards Locks Theft and Pickpocket Social Interaction, Information & Captivity Vision, Stealth, Traps, Locks & Theft Vision and Light Light states are Bright Light, Dim Light, and Darkness. Obscuration states are Lightly Obscured and Heavily Obscured. Dim Light lightly obscures; Darkness heavily obscures a creature that cannot otherwise see through it. Daeva Darkvision treats Darkness within 60 feet as Dim Light, not Bright Light. A recommended ordinary light source has a stated Bright radius plus an equal additional Dim radius unless its own text says otherwise. Bright light does not universally prohibit Stealth. Obscurity and Invisibility do not automatically make a creature Hidden. Cover, Line of Sight & Line of Effect No Cover. No defensive benefit from Cover. Half Cover. A creature or object behind meaningful partial obstruction gains +2 AC and +2 to Dexterity saving throws against effects originating from the covered direction. Intervening creatures can provide Half Cover when they materially obstruct the line. Full Cover. Full Cover blocks the relevant Line of Effect and prevents direct targeting through that obstruction unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Three-Quarters Cover does not exist in Wings of Atreia. Cover does not stack; use the best applicable Cover. Altitude neither inherently grants nor ignores Cover. Line of Sight and Line of Effect are distinct. Line of Sight determines whether you can see a target or point. Line of Effect determines whether an attack, spell, or effect can physically reach it. Heavy obscurement is not Cover by itself. Stealth and Infiltration Use scene states Undetected, Suspicious, and Alerted; these are not Conditions. Stealth must exceed Passive Perception; ties favor the observer. An active Search uses the GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation), against the relevant DC or opposing Stealth; ties favor the Searcher where opposed. Do not reroll Stealth every 5 feet; roll again only when circumstances materially change. For group Stealth, at least half the group must succeed. A failed check may create Suspicion rather than immediate full alarm when appropriate. Distractions create an opportunity to Hide rather than automatic success. Disguises are primarily social. Invisibility is not the same as Hidden. Wings do not automatically prevent Stealth. Traps and Non-Aether Hazards Describe a hazard with Trigger, Detection, Avoid/Disable method, Save/Check, Effect, and Reset/Duration. Hazards may be obvious, concealed, or hidden. Detection normally uses Passive Perception, active Perception, or Investigation. Disable methods depend on the mechanism and can use Sleight of Hand, Investigation, Athletics, or another appropriate Skill. There is no mandatory Thieves’ Tools system. Failure triggers the hazard only when the hazard says so. Damage and Conditions use existing universal rules. Forced movement is horizontal unless the hazard explicitly creates vertical displacement. Hazards normally resolve when triggered rather than taking their own Initiative turns. Repeat attempts require changed circumstances. Locks Mechanical Lock DC Simple 10 Standard 12 Secure 15 High Security 18 Exceptional 20+ The correct key opens a normal lock without a check. Mechanical locks generally use Dexterity (Sleight of Hand). Unusual mechanisms can use Intelligence (Investigation). Forcing uses Strength (Athletics); destroying a lock or door uses normal object/destruction adjudication. Failure does not automatically break or trigger a lock unless its design says so. Aether locks use Aether Interaction. If a task is impossible, do not assign an absurd DC—state that it cannot be done by that method. Theft and Pickpocket A theft attempt requires a plausible opportunity. Taking an accessible small item uses Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) against Passive Perception and must exceed it. If the target is actively watching, oppose with active Perception; ties favor the observer. Secured items can require a different approach. Failure may create suspicion or alarm. Success means the theft was unnoticed at that moment; later discovery remains possible. Distraction creates opportunity rather than automatic success. Help can grant +2 when genuinely meaningful. Worn armor, shields, Wings, wielded weapons, and equipped mandatory implements cannot simply be pickpocketed. Repeated attempts require changed circumstances. Social Interaction,

Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative Round and Turn Action Economy Attack Action Universal Actions Ready Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative, rounds, and combat-only resources are used only for genuine combat or another situation where structured turn order is necessary. Characters cannot manufacture artificial combat to farm cooldowns, resources, or timing triggers. Initiative Initiative = 1d20 + Dexterity modifier. Do not add PB unless an explicit feature says so. Alert adds +2 Initiative. There is no Surprise Round and Surprise does not grant Advantage on Initiative. When one side genuinely catches another side unaware, the GM may, at discretion, allow one appropriate pre-Initiative attack roll against the target's normal defense before Initiative is rolled. This is not an extra round, is not automatic, and does not create a general Surprise action economy. After that resolution, roll Initiative normally. Round and Turn One combat round represents approximately six seconds in the game world. Each participant normally takes one turn in Initiative order. All turns in the round abstract actions occurring within the same six-second span; do not add each turn as another six seconds. Action Economy Action. One per turn. Movement. Up to the creature’s available movement, subject to terrain and conditions. Bonus Action. Up to one, but only when a feature grants something that uses a Bonus Action. Reaction. Normally one per round, refreshing at the start of the creature’s turn unless an explicit class rule says otherwise. Object interaction. One free simple object interaction per turn. There is no universal Action-to-Bonus-Action or Bonus-Action-to-Action conversion. Unused movement or Actions are not stored for later turns. Attack Action The Attack Action makes one attack unless a feature such as Extra Attack says otherwise. Grapple and Shove are full Actions and do not replace one attack within Extra Attack. Player Weapon Requirement. A player character must be wielding an approved class weapon to take the normal Attack Action. Unarmed Attacks and Improvised Weapons are not player combat options unless a later explicit feature creates a specific exception. Opportunity Attacks. Opportunity Attacks remain part of the core combat rules. When a hostile creature you can perceive voluntarily leaves your melee reach, you may use your Reaction to make one melee attack against it, resolving the attack before it leaves that reach. Forced movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Universal Actions Dash. Gain additional movement equal to your current Speed for the turn. Difficult Terrain and other movement costs still apply. While flying, Dash adds horizontal movement but does not grant an additional altitude-layer change. Disengage. Until the end of your turn, your movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks. Dodge. Until the start of your next turn, attacks against you have Disadvantage if you can perceive the attacker, and you have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws. Dodge ends if you become Incapacitated or your Speed becomes 0. Hide. You must have meaningful concealment or another circumstance that allows hiding. Make Dexterity (Stealth) against Passive Perception or active Perception as appropriate. You cannot Hide while clearly seen. Hidden is not Invisible. Making an attack reveals your position after that attack resolves. Search. Deliberately search using a GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation). Use Object. Use this Action for substantial manipulation beyond the one free simple object interaction. A specific item’s activation rule controls when it states another cost. Ready A creature can prepare one Action for a perceivable trigger. When the trigger occurs, the creature may use its Reaction to perform the readied Action. Ready does not store ordinary movement, but Dash can be readied as the Action. Readied attacks retain all weapon properties. A readied spell must still meet implement and targeting requirements when released. Losing a mandatory implement before release prevents release. Concentration begins when the spell actually resolves. Ready never bypasses aerial restrictions, range, or other universal rules. Simultaneous Effects Effects resolve one at a time. The active creature orders its own simultaneous effects; the GM orders GM-controlled simultaneous effects. For opposing same-time effects, resolve the active creature first, then use Initiative if needed. Damage resolves before state changes caused by t

WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Glossary & Core Terms A player-facing A–Z reference for the vocabulary used throughout Wings of Atreia, with direct links to the full rules and lore pages. How to use this page: definitions here are quick-reference summaries. Follow the “Read more” link whenever you need the complete rule, class text, or world context. A B C D E F G I K L M P R S U W 46 terms A Action Your main turn action. Many attacks, spells, class features, and other options specify that they use your Action. Read more: Combat → Advantage / Disadvantage Roll two d20s and use the higher result for Advantage or the lower result for Disadvantage. Read more: Core Resolution → Aether The supernatural power that underlies Daeva abilities, spellcasting, flight, and many extraordinary phenomena in Atreia. Read more: Aether & Spellcasting → Aether Enhancement The higher equipment-quality path beyond Profession +2. Aether upgrades are level-gated and handled separately from ordinary Profession work. Read more: Equipment → Ascension The transformation by which a mortal becomes a Daeva and receives Wings. WoA begins with this event in Session 0. Read more: Character Creation → At-Will A spell or ability frequency that may be used whenever its normal action and other requirements are met. Read more: Aether & Spellcasting → B Background A character-creation choice representing experience and identity before or around Ascension; it provides its defined skills and related benefits. Read more: Backgrounds → Bonus Action A secondary turn action available only when a feature, spell, or rule explicitly gives an option that uses it. Read more: Combat → C Character Manager The official WoA character-management method for creation records, advancement, current resources, equipment, spells, and other tracked character data. Read more: Character Creation → Class Your Daeva’s primary mechanical path. WoA uses eleven classes and does not use multiclassing. Read more: Classes → Class Resource A class-specific pool, charge, stance, meter, or other tracked mechanic defined by that class. Read more: Quick Reference → Class Save DC Normally 8 + Proficiency Bonus + the class ability identified by your class, unless a rule states otherwise. Read more: Core Resolution → Concentration A spell/effect limit: only one Concentration effect can be maintained at a time, and Incapacitated ends it. WoA does not use Concentration saving throws. Read more: Aether & Spellcasting → Condition A named rules state such as Poisoned or Incapacitated that changes what a creature can do or how rolls affect it. Read more: Combat → Cooldown A spell or ability frequency that becomes unavailable after use until its stated cooldown is satisfied; WoA also uses the universal out-of-combat cooldown rule where applicable. Read more: Aether & Spellcasting → D Daeva An Ascended immortal warrior of Atreia. Player characters in Wings of Atreia are Daevas. Read more: Character Creation → Daeva Points (DP) A resource unlocked at Level 10 and earned through participation in genuine combat victories. DP powers Ultimate Abilities and persists through rests. Read more: Daeva Points & Ultimates → E Empyrean Boon A powerful universal character option gained at Level 19 according to the advancement rules. Read more: Feats & Empyrean Boons → Empyrean Lord One of the great Daeva Lords whose authority and legacy shape Elyos and Asmodian civilization, together with the two historic Tower Guardians. Read more: World → F Faction Your character’s allegiance as Elyos or Asmodian. Faction affects culture, homeland, and campaign relationships rather than class statistics. Read more: Flight → G Genuine Combat A real encounter using initiative and combat timing. Artificial encounters cannot be used to farm resources such as Daeva Points. title: d20 Tests
desc: d20 Tests — Wings of Atreia reference section.
text: d20 Tests. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Core Resolution The d20 test framework used for meaningful uncertain outcomes. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. d20 Tests & Core Resolution d20 Tests Ability Checks Saving Throws Save DCs Advantage and Disadvantage Help Passive Perception, Passive Investigation & Search d20 Tests & Core Resolution d20 Tests Ability Checks, attack rolls, and saving throws use a d20. Roll only when the outcome is uncertain and meaningful. If success is automatic, impossible, or consequence-free, no roll is needed. Ability Checks Choose the ability that best fits the approach, then add Proficiency Bonus if the character is proficient in the relevant skill. Expertise doubles the PB contribution for that proficiency. WoA retains six abilities and eighteen skills. A specialized Background can authorize a character to attempt obscure knowledge, but it does not automatically modify the roll. Saving Throws A saving throw uses the specified ability modifier and adds PB only if the creature is proficient in that saving throw. Ties are resolved according to the specific system; otherwise meeting a DC succeeds. Save DCs Default effect Save DC = 8 + Proficiency Bonus + the relevant ability modifier, unless an explicit class, spell, item, monster, or environmental rule gives a different DC. Advantage and Disadvantage When a rule grants Advantage, roll two d20s and use the higher. When it grants Disadvantage, roll two and use the lower. If both apply, they cancel unless a specific rule says otherwise. Resolve Advantage/Disadvantage before applying numeric modifiers. Help Help never grants Advantage. A meaningful helper grants +2 to one Ability Check. Normally only one helper can contribute. There is no Assist Attack and Help cannot modify Death Saves. Passive Perception, Passive Investigation & Search Passive Perception = 10 + your Wisdom (Perception) modifier. Passive Investigation = 10 + your Intelligence (Investigation) modifier. Advantage on the relevant check adds +5 to the passive score; Disadvantage subtracts 5. Multiple instances of the same source do not stack, and Advantage and Disadvantage cancel normally. Hide is opposed by Passive Perception; ties favor the observer. An active Search uses the GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation), against the relevant DC or opposing Stealth; ties favor the Searcher where opposed. Repeated checks require a meaningful change in circumstances. ← Back to Rules Wings of Atreia · Created & Designed by Clark Michael Zafra (“ArchQwynn”) · Non-commercial fan project.
