text: Daeva Points & Ultimate Abilities. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Daeva Points & Ultimates Level 10+ Daeva Points, Ultimate Ability activation, miss choices, and Ultimate Recovery. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Daeva Points & Ultimate Abilities Daeva Points & Ultimate Abilities LEVEL 10 UNIVERSAL FEATURE. Beginning at Level 10, a Daeva can accumulate up to 100 Daeva Points (DP). At 100 DP, the Daeva's class Ultimate Ability is ready and may be attempted. A successful Ultimate attack expends all 100 DP. If the Ultimate attack misses, the player chooses Release the Power or Hold the Power after the miss is confirmed, as described below. Earning DP. At the end of genuine combat, the GM totals the DP values of eligible hostile creatures defeated in that combat. Every Level 10 or higher Daeva who meaningfully participated gains that full total; the award is not divided and never depends on the killing blow. DP is awarded only after combat has fully ended, so DP gained from a victory cannot ready another Ultimate during that same combat. Enemy Rank / Significance DP Award No eligible threat / trivial opposition 0 DP Standard 2 DP Veteran 3 DP Elite 5 DP Boss 10 DP Climactic Boss 20 DP Climactic Boss. Climactic Boss is a DP-award designation, not a new Monster Compendium Rank. The GM may use it for a Boss that serves as the decisive threat of a major story arc; an ordinary Boss remains worth 10 DP. Eligible Defeat. A hostile creature counts when the party overcomes it through genuine combat, whether it is killed, reduced to 0 HP, captured, forced to surrender, or decisively driven from the encounter. Training, sparring, staged encounters, deliberately farmed enemies, allied or controlled creatures, summoned creatures, repeated forms of the same creature, and opposition that never represented a genuine threat award 0 DP. The GM makes the final eligibility ruling. Persistence and Restrictions. DP persists between encounters and through Short Rests, Long Rests, and Aetheric Reconstitution. Resting, consumables, spells, equipment, and class-resource effects cannot grant or restore DP. DP cannot exceed 100, be transferred, have its cost reduced, or be spent for any purpose other than the character's class Ultimate unless a future rule explicitly says otherwise. A character below Level 10 cannot earn or bank DP. Warfront Exclusion. DP cannot be gained or spent and Ultimate Abilities cannot be activated during a Warfront operation. This includes character-scale missions embedded in that operation and the Fortress Core Brigadier-General encounter. A character retains existing DP while the Warfront is in progress. Ultimate Attack Roll. Activating an Ultimate consumes both the character's Action and Bonus Action. The character cannot activate it unless both are available, but may still move and take Reactions normally. When the Ultimate requires an attack roll, roll 1d20 + the applicable ability modifier + the character's Proficiency Bonus, with Advantage. Advantage and Disadvantage interact normally, and other explicit modifiers apply normally. The attack is not an Attack action and cannot be duplicated by Extra Attack, Quick Shot, Akimbo, additional-action effects, reactions, or similar features. Fixed Ultimate Output, Miss Choice, and Critical Hits. Damage or healing dice printed as the Ultimate's own direct numerical output are not rolled; use the maximum value of those dice. Normal weapon or Bastion weapon damage and damage dice from other features remain rolled normally. On a hit, resolve normal weapon/Bastion damage when applicable, all fixed Ultimate damage or healing, and the Ultimate's full legal riders, then expend all 100 DP. On a miss, normal weapon/Bastion damage and full-hit riders do not occur. After the miss is confirmed, the player chooses one resolution. Release the Power: expend all 100 DP and resolve one-half, rounded down, of the Ultimate's fixed primary damage and one-half of any direct Ultimate healing, restoration, or repair amount that would have occurred on a hit. Area or secondary-target damage, temporary HP or other protective effects, forced movement, condition or status effects, condition removal, and other riders do not occur. If a restoration or repair sets a target to an HP threshold rather than rolling dice, determine how much HP the full hit would have restored from the target's current state and restore half that amount, rounded down. Hold the Power: resolve no Ultimate damage, healing, restoration, repair, or other effect and retain all 100 DP, but that Ultimate cannot be attempted again until the next dawn. Short Rests, Long Rests, and Aetheric Reconstitution do not end this restriction early. A critical hit does not increase fixed Ultimate output; only rolled normal weapon/Bastion damage di

Regardless of whether the Ultimate hits or which miss option is chosen, after the Ultimate attempt resolves the character's next turn is an Ultimate Recovery turn. During that turn, the character cannot make weapon attacks or spell attacks, deal damage, restore Hit Points, or impose conditions or harmful status effects on enemies. The character may move or fly normally, Dash, Disengage, Dodge, Search, Use Object, provide Help or other non-healing aid, interact with objects or the environment, and use other legal non-offensive utility or defensive options that do not violate those restrictions. An Ultimate remains a class feature, not a spell, class resource, Attack action, or ordinary Bastion system; it does not consume ammunition, a spell use, a cooldown use, or another class resource unless its text explicitly says so. Ordinary on-hit riders apply only when their own triggers are satisfied, and no effect can repeat the Ultimate or multiply its fixed output. Use the Ultimate values for the character's current class-level band: Levels 10-14, Levels 15-19, or Level 20. ← Back to Rules Wings of Atreia · Created & Designed by Clark Michael Zafra (“ArchQwynn”) · Non-commercial fan project.

WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Combat Turn structure, actions, movement, attacks, damage, conditions, death, rests, and survival. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative Round and Turn Action Economy Attack Action Universal Actions Ready Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative, rounds, and combat-only resources are used only for genuine combat or another situation where structured turn order is necessary. Characters cannot manufacture artificial combat to farm cooldowns, resources, or timing triggers. Initiative Initiative = 1d20 + Dexterity modifier. Do not add PB unless an explicit feature says so. Alert adds +2 Initiative. There is no Surprise Round and Surprise does not grant Advantage on Initiative. When one side genuinely catches another side unaware, the GM may, at discretion, allow one appropriate pre-Initiative attack roll against the target's normal defense before Initiative is rolled. This is not an extra round, is not automatic, and does not create a general Surprise action economy. After that resolution, roll Initiative normally. Round and Turn One combat round represents approximately six seconds in the game world. Each participant normally takes one turn in Initiative order. All turns in the round abstract actions occurring within the same six-second span; do not add each turn as another six seconds. Action Economy Action. One per turn. Movement. Up to the creature’s available movement, subject to terrain and conditions. Bonus Action. Up to one, but only when a feature grants something that uses a Bonus Action. Reaction. Normally one per round, refreshing at the start of the creature’s turn unless an explicit class rule says otherwise. Object interaction. One free simple object interaction per turn. There is no universal Action-to-Bonus-Action or Bonus-Action-to-Action conversion. Unused movement or Actions are not stored for later turns. Attack Action The Attack Action makes one attack unless a feature such as Extra Attack says otherwise. Grapple and Shove are full Actions and do not replace one attack within Extra Attack. Player Weapon Requirement. A player character must be wielding an approved class weapon to take the normal Attack Action. Unarmed Attacks and Improvised Weapons are not player combat options unless a later explicit feature creates a specific exception. Opportunity Attacks. Opportunity Attacks remain part of the core combat rules. When a hostile creature you can perceive voluntarily leaves your melee reach, you may use your Reaction to make one melee attack against it, resolving the attack before it leaves that reach. Forced movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Universal Actions Dash. Gain additional movement equal to your current Speed for the turn. Difficult Terrain and other movement costs still apply. While flying, Dash adds horizontal movement but does not grant an additional altitude-layer change. Disengage. Until the end of your turn, your movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks. Dodge. Until the start of your next turn, attacks against you have Disadvantage if you can perceive the attacker, and you have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws. Dodge ends if you become Incapacitated or your Speed becomes 0. Hide. You must have meaningful concealment or another circumstance that allows hiding. Make Dexterity (Stealth) against Passive Perception or active Perception as appropriate. You cannot Hide while clearly seen. Hidden is not Invisible. Making an attack reveals your position after that attack resolves. Search. Deliberately search using a GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation). Use Object. Use this Action for substantial manipulation beyond the one free simple object interaction. A specific item’s activation rule controls when it states another cost. Ready A creature can prepare one Action for a perceivable trigger. When the trigger occurs, the creature may use its Reaction to perform the readied Action. Ready does not store ordinary movement, but Dash can be readied as the Action. Readied attacks retain all weapon properties. A readied spell must still meet implement and targeting requirements when released. Losing a mandatory implement before release prevents release. Concentration begins when the spell actually resolves. Ready never bypasses aerial restrictions, range, or other universal rules. Simultaneous Effects Effects resolve one at a time. The active creature orders its own simultaneous effects; the GM orders GM-controlled simultaneous effects. For opposing same-time effects, resolve the active creature first, then use Initiative if needed. Damage resolves before state changes caused by that damage. Start-

text: Death's Eclipse — Ultimate Ability. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Melee Striker • Sneak Attack • Rune Marks • Execution Assassin “You'll know I'm there when you're dead.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Sneak Attack and Rune Marks Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Assassin is a precision melee striker that builds target-bound Rune Marks, converts them into burst damage or execution riders, and uses Shadow Step to remain difficult to pin down. Unlike a conventional Extra Attack martial, its Level 5 Assassination Sequence is a conditional follow-up attack tied to a successful Sneak Attack. Class Identity Assassins are precision predators who win through positioning, timing, concealment, and carefully prepared execution. Their art is not simply “attacking from stealth.” An Assassin studies a target, creates the right opening, carves Rune Marks, and converts preparation into a sudden lethal advantage. Their greatest strength is the ability to decide where and when a close-range confrontation becomes dangerous. Tradition & Outlook The Assassin tradition descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines and is practiced by infiltrators, covert operatives, hunters of dangerous individuals, intelligence agents, and Daevas who favor certainty over spectacle. Assassins often prize patience, awareness, self-control, and economy of motion. Their motives vary widely: service to a faction, revenge, professional duty, protection through preemptive action, or the pursuit of perfect technique. Appearance & Adventuring Assassins favor equipment that permits mobility and unobstructed movement, with Shortswords and Daggers forming the class’s approved weapon identity in Wings of Atreia. Their appearance may be subdued or ceremonial, but practical Assassins avoid anything that compromises movement or control. They adventure when a threat must be found before it strikes, a route must be infiltrated, an enemy leader must be neutralized, or a mystery demands someone comfortable operating unseen. Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative Round and Turn Action Economy Attack Action Universal Actions Ready Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative, rounds, and combat-only resources are used only for genuine combat or another situation where structured turn order is necessary. Characters cannot manufacture artificial combat to farm cooldowns, resources, or timing triggers. Initiative Initiative = 1d20 + Dexterity modifier. Do not add PB unless an explicit feature says so. Alert adds +2 Initiative. There is no Surprise Round and Surprise does not grant Advantage on Initiative. When one side genuinely catches another side unaware, the GM may, at discretion, allow one appropriate pre-Initiative attack roll against the target's normal defense before Initiative is rolled. This is not an extra round, is not automatic, and does not create a general Surprise action economy. After that resolution, roll Initiative normally. Round and Turn One combat round represents approximately six seconds in the game world. Each participant normally takes one turn in Initiative order. All turns in the round abstract actions occurring within the same six-second span; do not add each turn as another six seconds. Action Economy Action. One per turn. Movement. Up to the creature’s available movement, subject to terrain and conditions. Bonus Action. Up to one, but only when a feature grants something that uses a Bonus Action. Reaction. Normally one per round, refreshing at the start of the creature’s turn unless an explicit class rule says otherwise. Object interaction. One free simple object interaction per turn. There is no universal Action-to-Bonus-Action or Bonus-Action-to-Action conversion. Unused movement or Actions are not stored for later turns. Attack Action The Attack Action makes one attack unless a feature such as Extra Attack says otherwise. Grapple and Shove are full Actions and do not replace one attack within Extra Attack. Player Weapon Requirement. A player character must be wielding an approved class weapon to take the normal Attack Action. Unarmed Attacks and Improvised Weapons are not player combat options unless a later explicit feature creates a specific exception. Opportunity Attacks. Opportunity Attacks remain part of the core combat rules. When a hostile creature you can perceive voluntarily leaves your melee reach, you may use your Reaction to make one melee attack against it, resolving the attack before it leaves that reach. Forced movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Universal Actions Dash. Gain additional movement equal to your current Speed for the turn. Difficult Terrain and other movement costs still apply. While flying, Dash adds horizontal movement but does not grant an additional altitude-layer change. Disengage. Until the end of your turn, your movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks. Dodge. Until the start of your next turn, attacks against you have Disadvantage if you can perceive the attacker, and you have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws. Dodge ends if you become Incapacitated or your Speed becomes 0. Hide. You must have meaningful concealment or another circumstance that allows hiding. Make Dexterity (Stealth) against Passive Perception or active Perception as appropriate. You cannot Hide while clearly seen. Hidden is not Invisible. Making an attack reveals your position after that attack resolves. Search. Deliberately search using a GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation). Use Object. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Tempo, Firearms, and Reload Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Tradition & Outlook Specialization Reassignment The Gunslinger is a mobile firearm martial whose power comes from maintaining Tempo through successful firearm play. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Fire. Move. Reload. Keep the rhythm alive long enough to turn Tempo into control, defense, and lethal pressure. Class Identity Gunslingers are technist marksmen who turn Aether-assisted firearms into speed, precision, and controlled ranged pressure. Pistols support rapid, mobile sequences through Quick Shot and Akimbo, while Muskets provide deliberate two-handed fire that concentrates Tempo into stronger individual hits through Deliberate Shot. Tempo represents the Gunslinger’s ability to build combat rhythm through successful action rather than treating every shot as an isolated event. Tradition & Outlook Gunslingers belong to Atreia’s newer technological traditions. The wider Aion tradition describes early firearm research being dismissed as technist tinkering until battlefield success forced major institutions to recognize the discipline. Wings of Atreia keeps that identity of innovation earning legitimacy through results while using Pistols and Muskets as the class’s only firearm categories. Gunslingers often value nerve, technical familiarity, accuracy, independence, and adaptability. Appearance & Adventuring Gunslingers favor mobile equipment, ammunition management, firearm maintenance, and a practical awareness of range and firing position. Their weapons can make them look strikingly modern beside older martial traditions, but their discipline remains Aetheric and distinctly Atreian. They adventure to test new techniques, serve as ranged specialists, hunt dangerous targets, protect expeditions from positions others cannot exploit, or demonstrate that innovation has earned its place in the war for Atreia. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Flight & Aerial Combat Altitude Layers 3D Distance Melee Descending Attack Physical Ranged Attacks Flight Slots Aether State Interaction Flight & Aerial Combat Altitude Layers Layer Height Access Low 30 ft All functional Wings Mid 60 ft All functional Wings High 90 ft All functional Wings Legendary 120 ft Legendary Wings only Ground level is 0 feet and is not an altitude layer. There are four airborne altitude layers: Low (30 ft), Mid (60 ft), High (90 ft), and Legendary (120 ft). Voluntarily ascending or descending one altitude layer consumes all movement for that turn. A creature cannot both ascend and descend voluntarily in the same turn. Dash does not permit an additional altitude-layer change. A Daeva without Legendary Wings cannot voluntarily ascend above the High layer at 90 feet. 3D Distance For WoA aerial targeting, total distance = the greater of horizontal distance or vertical distance. Do not use Pythagorean distance and do not add horizontal and vertical distance together. Melee Airborne melee uses ordinary reach: usually 5 feet, or 10 feet for a Reach weapon. Being on the same altitude layer does not remove the need to physically move into reach. Descending Attack If a melee attacker begins its turn higher than the target, descends at least 25 feet, and then makes its first qualifying melee attack against that lower target, the attack has Advantage. Physical Ranged Attacks Universal Close-Range Rule. If the target of a physical ranged weapon attack is within 5 feet of the attacker, the attack roll has Disadvantage. This applies whether the attacker is grounded or airborne and does not change the weapon’s listed Normal Range or Maximum Range. A lower-altitude physical ranged attacker has Advantage against a higher-altitude winged airborne target because the wings are exposed. This Exposed Wings rule does not apply to wingless creatures flying through Saturated Aether. A higher-altitude ranged attacker gains no automatic Advantage merely for being above the target. When the physical ranged attacker is above the target, increase only the weapon’s Maximum Range by half the vertical distance, rounded up. The weapon’s Normal Range is unchanged. Magical attacks do not gain this extension. Flight Slots Level Base Max Slots 1–3 2 4–6 3 7–9 4 10–12 5 13–16 6 17–19 7 20 8 A stable airborne Daeva spends 1 Flight Slot at the end of each of its turns. A grounded Daeva recovers 1 Flight Slot at the end of each grounded turn. Short Rest restores half maximum, rounded down; Long Rest restores all. When a creature runs out of Flight Slots while airborne, it immediately falls. Aether State Interaction Depleted Aether. Flight is fully restricted. Stable Aether. Normal flight rules. Saturated Aether. Daevas spend no combat Flight Slots, though exploration Flight Time limits still apply. Wingless creatures capable of movement may gain flight equal to normal Speed while Saturated; they do not use Flight Slots and are not subject to Exposed Wings. Unstable Zone / Aether Instability. This is hazard-defined scene behavior rather than a universal Aether State. The three universal States are Stable, Depleted, and Saturated. Use the specific Aether Hazard rules for the area. Aether-State Changes and Boundaries Aether-State changes take effect immediately. Crossing into a new Aether State immediately applies the entered State. In Depleted Aether, Aether-supported flight is unavailable; an airborne Daeva entering a Depleted area loses flight and falls, using the normal DC 12 Dexterity Emergency Landing Reaction if eligible. Saturated → Stable: Daevas resume normal Flight Slot expenditure. A creature flying only because Saturated Aether granted it flight loses that flight and falls. Saturated → Depleted: affected airborne creatures immediately lose Aether-supported flight and fall. Stable → Saturated: Daevas stop spending Combat Flight Slots, and eligible wingless creatures gain access to Aether-supported flight equal to normal Speed, but no creature automatically takes off. Falling and Emergency Landing Falling damage is 1d6 per 10 feet fallen, maximum 20d6. A falling creature normally lands Prone unless an explicit effect says otherwise. When Flight Slot depletion causes a fall, the creature may use its Reaction for a DC 12 Dexterity save. Success halves fall damage; failure or no Reaction takes full damage. Pistols support rapid, mobile sequences through Quick Shot and Akimbo, while Muskets provide deliberate two-handed fire that concentrates Tempo into stronger individual hits through Deliberate Shot. Tempo represents the Gunslinger’s ability to build combat rhythm through successful action rather than treating every shot as an isolated event. Tradition & Outlook Gunslingers belong to Atreia’s newer technological traditions. The wider Aion tradition describes early firearm research being dismissed as technist tinkering until battlefield success forced major institutions to recognize the discipline. Wings of Atreia keeps that identity of innovation earning legitimacy through results while using Pistols and Muskets as the class’s only firearm categories. Gunslingers often value nerve, technical familiarity, accuracy, independence, and adaptability. Appearance & Adventuring Gunslingers favor mobile equipment, ammunition management, firearm maintenance, and a practical awareness of range and firing position. Their weapons can make them look strikingly modern beside older martial traditions, but their discipline remains Aetheric and distinctly Atreian. They adventure to test new techniques, serve as ranged specialists, hunt dangerous targets, protect expeditions from positions others cannot exploit, or demonstrate that innovation has earned its place in the war for Atreia. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols Ranged Gunslinger One-handed Weapon Attack. Range 30/90 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d8 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. A Gunslinger can wield two Pistols, but doing so does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols are compatible with Quick Shot and Akimbo. Muskets Ranged Gunslinger Two-handed Weapon Attack. Range 60/180 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d12 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. Ammunition capacity is fixed at 2. Muskets cannot use Quick Shot or Akimbo. Gunslinger ammunition-restoration features can restore Musket shots normally, but a Musket can never hold more than 2 shots. Standard one-handed firearm capacity increases do not apply to Muskets. Reload Every firearm attack consumes one shot. A firearm with no shots remaining is Empty and cannot make firearm attacks until at least one shot is restored. Normal Bonus Action Reload: an Empty firearm is restored to its full Reload capacity. Ammunition restoration is not the Reload action unless a feature explicitly says so. Ammunition-restoration features can restore shots to either Pistols or Muskets up to that firearm's maximum capacity. A Musket's maximum capacity remains 2. Switching between carried one-handed Gunslinger firearms as part of a firearm attack requires no separate object interaction. Standard one-handed firearm capacity progression: Ammo Capacity 4 at Levels 1-4, Ammo Capacity 5 at 5-8, Ammo Capacity 6 at 9-14, and Ammo Capacity 7 at 15-20. Increasing capacity does not automatically reload an Empty firearm. Tempo Tempo is a genuine-combat resource representing firing rhythm, accuracy, and momentum. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Flight & Aerial Combat Altitude Layers 3D Distance Melee Descending Attack Physical Ranged Attacks Flight Slots Aether State Interaction Flight & Aerial Combat Altitude Layers Layer Height Access Low 30 ft All functional Wings Mid 60 ft All functional Wings High 90 ft All functional Wings Legendary 120 ft Legendary Wings only Ground level is 0 feet and is not an altitude layer. There are four airborne altitude layers: Low (30 ft), Mid (60 ft), High (90 ft), and Legendary (120 ft). Voluntarily ascending or descending one altitude layer consumes all movement for that turn. A creature cannot both ascend and descend voluntarily in the same turn. Dash does not permit an additional altitude-layer change. A Daeva without Legendary Wings cannot voluntarily ascend above the High layer at 90 feet. 3D Distance For WoA aerial targeting, total distance = the greater of horizontal distance or vertical distance. Do not use Pythagorean distance and do not add horizontal and vertical distance together. Melee Airborne melee uses ordinary reach: usually 5 feet, or 10 feet for a Reach weapon. Being on the same altitude layer does not remove the need to physically move into reach. Descending Attack If a melee attacker begins its turn higher than the target, descends at least 25 feet, and then makes its first qualifying melee attack against that lower target, the attack has Advantage. Physical Ranged Attacks Universal Close-Range Rule. If the target of a physical ranged weapon attack is within 5 feet of the attacker, the attack roll has Disadvantage. This applies whether the attacker is grounded or airborne and does not change the weapon’s listed Normal Range or Maximum Range. A lower-altitude physical ranged attacker has Advantage against a higher-altitude winged airborne target because the wings are exposed. This Exposed Wings rule does not apply to wingless creatures flying through Saturated Aether. A higher-altitude ranged attacker gains no automatic Advantage merely for being above the target. When the physical ranged attacker is above the target, increase only the weapon’s Maximum Range by half the vertical distance, rounded up. The weapon’s Normal Range is unchanged. Magical attacks do not gain this extension. Flight Slots Level Base Max Slots 1–3 2 4–6 3 7–9 4 10–12 5 13–16 6 17–19 7 20 8 A stable airborne Daeva spends 1 Flight Slot at the end of each of its turns. A grounded Daeva recovers 1 Flight Slot at the end of each grounded turn. Short Rest restores half maximum, rounded down; Long Rest restores all. When a creature runs out of Flight Slots while airborne, it immediately falls. Aether State Interaction Depleted Aether. Flight is fully restricted. Stable Aether. Normal flight rules. Saturated Aether. Daevas spend no combat Flight Slots, though exploration Flight Time limits still apply. Wingless creatures capable of movement may gain flight equal to normal Speed while Saturated; they do not use Flight Slots and are not subject to Exposed Wings. Unstable Zone / Aether Instability. This is hazard-defined scene behavior rather than a universal Aether State. The three universal States are Stable, Depleted, and Saturated. Use the specific Aether Hazard rules for the area. Aether-State Changes and Boundaries Aether-State changes take effect immediately. Crossing into a new Aether State immediately applies the entered State. In Depleted Aether, Aether-supported flight is unavailable; an airborne Daeva entering a Depleted area loses flight and falls, using the normal DC 12 Dexterity Emergency Landing Reaction if eligible. Saturated → Stable: Daevas resume normal Flight Slot expenditure. A creature flying only because Saturated Aether granted it flight loses that flight and falls. Saturated → Depleted: affected airborne creatures immediately lose Aether-supported flight and fall. Stable → Saturated: Daevas stop spending Combat Flight Slots, and eligible wingless creatures gain access to Aether-supported flight equal to normal Speed, but no creature automatically takes off. Falling and Emergency Landing Falling damage is 1d6 per 10 feet fallen, maximum 20d6. A falling creature normally lands Prone unless an explicit effect says otherwise. When Flight Slot depletion causes a fall, the creature may use its Reaction for a DC 12 Dexterity save. Success halves fall damage; failure or no Reaction takes full damage. Controlled Descent changes a successful Emergency Landing to 0 fall damage according to that feat. Falling Onto Creatures The lower creature makes a DC 12 Dexterity save. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Combat Turn structure, actions, movement, attacks, damage, conditions, death, rests, and survival. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative Round and Turn Action Economy Attack Action Universal Actions Ready Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative, rounds, and combat-only resources are used only for genuine combat or another situation where structured turn order is necessary. Characters cannot manufacture artificial combat to farm cooldowns, resources, or timing triggers. Initiative Initiative = 1d20 + Dexterity modifier. Do not add PB unless an explicit feature says so. Alert adds +2 Initiative. There is no Surprise Round and Surprise does not grant Advantage on Initiative. When one side genuinely catches another side unaware, the GM may, at discretion, allow one appropriate pre-Initiative attack roll against the target's normal defense before Initiative is rolled. This is not an extra round, is not automatic, and does not create a general Surprise action economy. After that resolution, roll Initiative normally. Round and Turn One combat round represents approximately six seconds in the game world. Each participant normally takes one turn in Initiative order. All turns in the round abstract actions occurring within the same six-second span; do not add each turn as another six seconds. Action Economy Action. One per turn. Movement. Up to the creature’s available movement, subject to terrain and conditions. Bonus Action. Up to one, but only when a feature grants something that uses a Bonus Action. Reaction. Normally one per round, refreshing at the start of the creature’s turn unless an explicit class rule says otherwise. Object interaction. One free simple object interaction per turn. There is no universal Action-to-Bonus-Action or Bonus-Action-to-Action conversion. Unused movement or Actions are not stored for later turns. Attack Action The Attack Action makes one attack unless a feature such as Extra Attack says otherwise. Grapple and Shove are full Actions and do not replace one attack within Extra Attack. Player Weapon Requirement. A player character must be wielding an approved class weapon to take the normal Attack Action. Unarmed Attacks and Improvised Weapons are not player combat options unless a later explicit feature creates a specific exception. Opportunity Attacks. Opportunity Attacks remain part of the core combat rules. When a hostile creature you can perceive voluntarily leaves your melee reach, you may use your Reaction to make one melee attack against it, resolving the attack before it leaves that reach. Forced movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Universal Actions Dash. Gain additional movement equal to your current Speed for the turn. Difficult Terrain and other movement costs still apply. While flying, Dash adds horizontal movement but does not grant an additional altitude-layer change. Disengage. Until the end of your turn, your movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks. Dodge. Until the start of your next turn, attacks against you have Disadvantage if you can perceive the attacker, and you have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws. Dodge ends if you become Incapacitated or your Speed becomes 0. Hide. You must have meaningful concealment or another circumstance that allows hiding. Make Dexterity (Stealth) against Passive Perception or active Perception as appropriate. You cannot Hide while clearly seen. Hidden is not Invisible. Making an attack reveals your position after that attack resolves. Search. Deliberately search using a GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation). Use Object. Use this Action for substantial manipulation beyond the one free simple object interaction. A specific item’s activation rule controls when it states another cost. Ready A creature can prepare one Action for a perceivable trigger. When the trigger occurs, the creature may use its Reaction to perform the readied Action. Ready does not store ordinary movement, but Dash can be readied as the Action. Readied attacks retain all weapon properties. A readied spell must still meet implement and targeting requirements when released. Losing a mandatory implement before release prevents release. Concentration begins when the spell actually resolves. Ready never bypasses aerial restrictions, range, or other universal rules. Simultaneous Effects Effects resolve one at a time. The active creature orders its own simultaneous effects; the GM orders GM-controlled simultaneous effects. For opposing same-time effects, resolve the active creature first, then use Initiative if needed. Damage resolves before state changes caused by that damage. Start

WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Glossary & Core Terms A player-facing A–Z reference for the vocabulary used throughout Wings of Atreia, with direct links to the full rules and lore pages. How to use this page: definitions here are quick-reference summaries. Follow the “Read more” link whenever you need the complete rule, class text, or world context. A B C D E F G I K L M P R S U W 46 terms A Action Your main turn action. Many attacks, spells, class features, and other options specify that they use your Action. Read more: Combat → Advantage / Disadvantage Roll two d20s and use the higher result for Advantage or the lower result for Disadvantage. Read more: Core Resolution → Aether The supernatural power that underlies Daeva abilities, spellcasting, flight, and many extraordinary phenomena in Atreia. Read more: Aether & Spellcasting → Aether Enhancement The higher equipment-quality path beyond Profession +2. Aether upgrades are level-gated and handled separately from ordinary Profession work. Read more: Equipment → Ascension The transformation by which a mortal becomes a Daeva and receives Wings. WoA begins with this event in Session 0. Read more: Character Creation → At-Will A spell or ability frequency that may be used whenever its normal action and other requirements are met. Read more: Aether & Spellcasting → B Background A character-creation choice representing experience and identity before or around Ascension; it provides its defined skills and related benefits. Read more: Backgrounds → Bonus Action A secondary turn action available only when a feature, spell, or rule explicitly gives an option that uses it. Read more: Combat → C Character Manager The official WoA character-management method for creation records, advancement, current resources, equipment, spells, and other tracked character data. Read more: Character Creation → Class Your Daeva’s primary mechanical path. WoA uses eleven classes and does not use multiclassing. Read more: Classes → Class Resource A class-specific pool, charge, stance, meter, or other tracked mechanic defined by that class. Read more: Quick Reference → Class Save DC Normally 8 + Proficiency Bonus + the class ability identified by your class, unless a rule states otherwise. Read more: Core Resolution → Concentration A spell/effect limit: only one Concentration effect can be maintained at a time, and Incapacitated ends it. WoA does not use Concentration saving throws. Read more: Aether & Spellcasting → Condition A named rules state such as Poisoned or Incapacitated that changes what a creature can do or how rolls affect it. Read more: Combat → Cooldown A spell or ability frequency that becomes unavailable after use until its stated cooldown is satisfied; WoA also uses the universal out-of-combat cooldown rule where applicable. Read more: Aether & Spellcasting → D Daeva An Ascended immortal warrior of Atreia. Player characters in Wings of Atreia are Daevas. Read more: Character Creation → Daeva Points (DP) A resource unlocked at Level 10 and earned through participation in genuine combat victories. DP powers Ultimate Abilities and persists through rests. Read more: Daeva Points & Ultimates → E Empyrean Boon A powerful universal character option gained at Level 19 according to the advancement rules. Read more: Feats & Empyrean Boons → Empyrean Lord One of the great Daeva Lords whose authority and legacy shape Elyos and Asmodian civilization, together with the two historic Tower Guardians. Read more: World → F Faction Your character’s allegiance as Elyos or Asmodian. Faction affects culture, homeland, and campaign relationships rather than class statistics. Read more: Character Creation → Feat A universal character option chosen at designated advancement points instead of an Ability Score Improvement where the rules allow it. Read more: Feats & Empyrean Boons → Flight Slot A tracked unit of a Daeva’s flight capacity. The number of Flight Slots increases with character level. Read more: Flight → G Genuine Combat A real encounter using initiative and combat timing. Artificial encounters cannot be used to farm resources such as Daeva Points. Read more: Combat → I Implement A spellcasting equipment category that can follow the established quality and enhancement progression. Read more: Equipment → K Kinah The standard currency used for purchases, profession training, supplies, and other economic transactions. Read more: Professions & Economy → L Legendary Equipment Story-driven top-tier equipment above the Aether enhancement tiers. Legendary items are not ordinary Profession products. Read more: Equipment → Long Rest An 8-hour recovery period. What it restores depends on the specific class, spell, feature, or rule. Read more: Combat → Lord Action The dedicated off-turn action framework used by Empyrean Lords and Dragon Lords. Read more: Combat → M Milestone Advancement WoA’s advancement method. text: Elemental Spirits. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Full Caster • Elemental Spirit • Spirit Bond • Debuffs Spiritmaster “Never fight alone. Your spirit is with you.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Spellcasting Reference: Spiritmaster has a dedicated spell-list page for quick browsing. View Spiritmaster Spell List → Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Summon Spirit Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Spell List Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequence Specialization Reassignment The Spiritmaster is a two-body tactical caster. One active elemental spirit shares the Spiritmaster’s turn and action economy; together they equal one complete player character. The class establishes two battlefield positions, casts through the spirit, and earns Spirit Bond only through meaningful master-spirit coordination. Class Identity Spiritmasters are binders and commanders of elemental spirits who fight as a partnership rather than as a solitary caster. Their strength comes from coordinating their own spellcraft with a Greater Spirit, applying pressure, disruption, and control across more than one position on the battlefield. Spirit Bond represents the relationship and command structure that makes this divided presence function as one class. Tradition & Outlook The Spiritmaster tradition develops from Atreia’s mage disciplines but turns outward toward spirits, elemental forces, and the difficult art of directing entities shaped by Aether. Spiritmasters are often patient observers, researchers, summoners, or specialists in threats that cannot be understood through ordinary physical study. Their beliefs about spirits differ: some emphasize command, others partnership, responsibility, curiosity, or respect for elemental power. Appearance & Adventuring Spiritmasters use cloth armor and magical implements, while the visible presence of a summoned spirit often defines their silhouette more strongly than clothing does. Their equipment may include ritual, scholarly, or elemental motifs without creating additional mechanics. They adventure to understand unusual spirits, recover lost summoning knowledge, counter supernatural threats, serve as versatile magical operatives, or deepen the bond between Daeva and elemental ally. Only one Spiritmaster spirit may normally be active. Summoning uses an Action and places the spirit in a visible unoccupied space within 15 feet. A defeated spirit disperses into Aether, makes no death saves, and cannot be resummoned until the start of your next turn. Outside combat a newly summoned spirit appears at full HP; voluntary replacement during combat preserves the dismissed spirit’s current HP percentage rather than healing by switching forms. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Tempo, Firearms, and Reload Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Tradition & Outlook Specialization Reassignment The Gunslinger is a mobile firearm martial whose power comes from maintaining Tempo through successful firearm play. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Fire. Move. Reload. Keep the rhythm alive long enough to turn Tempo into control, defense, and lethal pressure. Class Identity Gunslingers are technist marksmen who turn Aether-assisted firearms into speed, precision, and controlled ranged pressure. Pistols support rapid, mobile sequences through Quick Shot and Akimbo, while Muskets provide deliberate two-handed fire that concentrates Tempo into stronger individual hits through Deliberate Shot. Tempo represents the Gunslinger’s ability to build combat rhythm through successful action rather than treating every shot as an isolated event. Tradition & Outlook Gunslingers belong to Atreia’s newer technological traditions. The wider Aion tradition describes early firearm research being dismissed as technist tinkering until battlefield success forced major institutions to recognize the discipline. Wings of Atreia keeps that identity of innovation earning legitimacy through results while using Pistols and Muskets as the class’s only firearm categories. Gunslingers often value nerve, technical familiarity, accuracy, independence, and adaptability. Appearance & Adventuring Gunslingers favor mobile equipment, ammunition management, firearm maintenance, and a practical awareness of range and firing position. Their weapons can make them look strikingly modern beside older martial traditions, but their discipline remains Aetheric and distinctly Atreian. They adventure to test new techniques, serve as ranged specialists, hunt dangerous targets, protect expeditions from positions others cannot exploit, or demonstrate that innovation has earned its place in the war for Atreia. View Songweaver Spell List → Class Identity Class Chassis Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Spell List Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Performance Sequence Tradition & Outlook Specialization Reassignment The Songweaver changes battlefield purpose from moment to moment. Every Songweaver spell belongs to Harmony, Guard, Dissonance, or Requiem. Successful performances create short-lived Refrains, changing Song Roles builds Resonance, and Resonance is spent to amplify, sustain, counter, or conduct the performance. Class Identity Songweavers shape Aether through music, using performance as destructive spellcraft, support, control, and restoration. Their strength lies in versatility: the same class can pressure an enemy, sustain an ally, or shift the emotional and tactical rhythm of an encounter. Resonance represents the accumulating harmony between performance, spellcraft, and the unfolding battle. Tradition & Outlook The Songweaver tradition is rooted in Atreia’s Muses and in remembrance of Siel. The wider Aion tradition describes Muses who continued their studies after the Cataclysm and eventually joined music with Aether in service to their people; their battlefield contribution led to recognition as an established Daeva class. Songweavers may therefore approach performance as remembrance, artistry, scholarship, service, or a declaration that beauty still has power in a broken world. Appearance & Adventuring Songweavers use Lutes and Lyres as their approved implements, often making instrument, costume, gesture, and magical display part of a single visible identity. Their appearance can range from formal performer to traveling battle-musician without changing class mechanics. They adventure to preserve stories, honor Siel, inspire allies, master Aetheric music, carry culture into war-torn regions, or use beauty and sound as weapons against forces that would reduce Atreia to silence. Resonance is genuine-combat only: it begins at 0, resets to 0 at combat end, and artificial initiative cannot generate it. Maximum Resonance is 3 at Levels 1–4, 4 at 5–8, 5 at 9–12, 6 at 13–16, and 7 at 17–20. After a Songweaver spell resolves, if that casting satisfies at least one of the generation conditions below, gain 1 Resonance, subject to the normal per-turn limit. The first successful Song Role in a combat establishes role history for Contrasting Verse; it cannot contrast with a role that does not yet exist. Harmonic Support: a single Songweaver spell meaningfully benefits two or more creatures. Dissonant Performance: a single Songweaver spell meaningfully affects two or more hostile creatures. Contrasting Verse: you successfully cast a Songweaver spell whose Song Role differs from your previous successful Song Role. Each generation condition triggers at most once per casting. Normal generation is capped at 1 Resonance per turn unless a feature explicitly increases it. A Refrain, Chorus Echo, Resonance rider, specialization rider, or other secondary Songweaver effect cannot recursively generate Resonance, create/trigger another Refrain, or activate another Songweaver rider unless explicit. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Spellcasting Reference: Cleric has a dedicated spell-list page for quick browsing. View Cleric Spell List → Class Identity Class Chassis Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Spell List Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Support Sequence Tradition & Outlook Specialization Reassignment The Cleric is Wings of Atreia’s primary restorative spellcaster. It is deliberately more durable than the d6 full casters and is rewarded for meaningful intervention: healing an ally in real danger, actually preventing damage, or removing a significant hostile effect. Divine Grace then converts that successful support into more emergency power. Class Identity Clerics are Atreia’s foremost restorative and protective spellcasters. Their calling is not limited to healing wounds after the fact: they preserve the party through recovery, cleansing, protection, and timely intervention while retaining the ability to fight when necessary. Divine Grace represents the reserve of sacred and restorative power through which a Cleric answers moments of genuine need. Tradition & Outlook The Cleric tradition grows from Atreia’s priestly disciplines and is associated with healers, battlefield ministers, temple servants, protectors of communities, and Daevas who understand survival as a collective responsibility. Clerics often value service, perseverance, mercy, duty, or faith, but they need not share one personality or theology. A militant Cleric and a gentle healer may practice the same class through very different convictions. Appearance & Adventuring Clerics commonly combine durable armor with practical healing or ritual equipment. In Wings of Atreia they may use Maces, Hammers, Staffs, Quarterstaffs, and shields from Round Shields to Medium Shields according to their approved access. They adventure to protect lives, confront corruption or supernatural danger, recover sacred knowledge, serve a cause, or ensure that an expedition can survive places where retreat and ordinary medicine are not enough. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Ability Wisdom Secondary Ability Constitution Hit Die d8; additionally +2 maximum HP per Cleric level Saving Throws Wisdom, Constitution Armor Chain Armor Weapons Mace, Hammer, Staff, Quarterstaff, Round Shield, Medium Shield Skills Choose 2 from 6: History, Insight, Medicine, Nature, Perception, Religion Spellcasting Ability WIS Spell Save DC 8 + PB + WIS modifier Spell Attack PB + WIS modifier Signature Resource Divine Grace Spell Advancements +2 each level after 1; 38 total Maximum Spell Level 9 Extra Attack None Meaningful Support and Divine Grace Maximum Divine Grace equals PB + WIS modifier, minimum 2. Long Rest restores all; Short Rest restores PB. Once per round, when you Meaningfully Support yourself or an ally with a Cleric spell or feature, regain 1 Grace. Your normal once-per-round generation becomes available again at the start of your turn, allowing an off-turn protection to qualify without double-dipping around initiative boundaries. Meaningful Support means one of the following actually occurs: restore HP while the creature was below half maximum HP; prevent or reduce damage by at least PB; or suppress/remove a mechanically significant hostile condition or effect. Healing a full-HP creature, preventing 0 damage, refreshing temporary HP without increasing it, cosmetic effects, or intentionally manufactured harmless damage do not qualify. Self-support must satisfy the same standard. Temporary HP are not healing and cannot restore a creature from 0 HP. Passive aura bonuses and passive AC do not generate Divine Grace unless a feature explicitly says so. A secondary Cleric rider created by another Cleric feature does not recursively trigger Twin Devotion, Sacred Intervention, Graceful Channeling, Empowered Restoration, or another support sequence unless explicit. Only one Cleric rolled-healing class rider normally modifies the same individual healing instance, except Graceful Restoration may coexist with one specialization rolled-healing rider. Flat Cleric save penalties do not stack; use the largest. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Starting State Divine Grace is a rest-based reserve. It does not automatically reset to 0 when combat starts or ends; later features can establish a minimum starting amount. Maximum PB + WIS modifier, minimum 2. Source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page is a player-facing reference extracted from the handbook rather than a replacement ruleset. Background Rules Soldier Scholar Acolyte Noble Outlander Underworld Artisan Merchant Entertainer Languages Background Rules Skill Selection: Choose exactly 2 Background Skills from the six options listed for your Background. Duplicate selections are prohibited. A Skill selected as a Class Skill cannot also be selected as a Background Skill. The four selected Class and Background Skill Proficiencies must therefore be four different Skills. Background Choose 2 Skills Soldier Athletics, Intimidation, Perception, Survival, Medicine, Religion Scholar Arcana, History, Investigation, Religion, Medicine, Perception Acolyte History, Insight, Medicine, Religion, Athletics, Survival Noble History, Insight, Persuasion, Performance, Investigation, Sleight of Hand Outlander Athletics, Nature, Perception, Survival, Persuasion, Stealth Underworld Deception, Insight, Sleight of Hand, Stealth, Investigation, Persuasion Artisan Investigation, Perception, Sleight of Hand, History, Arcana, Persuasion Merchant Insight, Investigation, Persuasion, History, Stealth, Athletics Entertainer Acrobatics, Deception, Performance, Persuasion, Nature, Animal Handling A relevant Background may establish that you have the experience necessary to attempt obscure or specialized knowledge. It does not automatically grant Advantage, Expertise, a numerical bonus, or guaranteed success. Understanding Your Background Your Class describes what your character has learned to do as an adventuring Daeva. Your Background describes the life, training, profession, upbringing, or experiences that helped shape who they were before the campaign began. Faction tells you where you belong, Background helps explain where you came from, and Class describes how you operate as an adventurer. A Background does not determine your morality, personality, beliefs, faction loyalty, or future choices. Two characters with the same Background may have completely different lives and goals. Mechanically, use the Background table above exactly as written: choose two skills from your Background’s listed skill pool. The entries below add roleplaying context and do not grant additional rules benefits. Soldier What Is a Soldier?. A Soldier has meaningful experience with organized military service: troops, guards, scouts, officers, fortress personnel, or other disciplined fighting forces. Life and Origins. Military life may have included patrols, garrison duty, campaigns, escort work, reconnaissance, fortification defense, or service under a commander. That service may have occurred before or after ascension. Motivations and Outlook. Duty, loyalty, comradeship, ambition, patriotism, protection, regret, or the memory of fallen companions may still shape the character. A Soldier may respect military order, resent it, or be deciding what is truly worth fighting for. Playing a Soldier. Decide what kind of service shaped you, who you served beside, and what relationship you now have with authority and your former comrades. Being a Soldier does not require obedience or a martial Class. Scholar What Is a Scholar?. A Scholar has devoted part of their life to seeking, preserving, interpreting, or teaching knowledge. Scholars include researchers, historians, scribes, teachers, philosophers, archivists, investigators, and field specialists. Life and Origins. Study may have taken place under a teacher, within an archive or institution, or independently. Subjects can include history, geography, creatures, Aether, ruins, cultures, warfare, or any other serious field of inquiry. Motivations and Outlook. A Scholar may adventure to recover lost knowledge, investigate mysteries, study ruins or creatures directly, protect important discoveries, or prevent dangerous knowledge from being misused. Playing a Scholar. Choose the subject that fascinates you and decide whether you are an academic, a practical field researcher, or something between. Being scholarly does not require being socially awkward or confined to books. Acolyte What Is an Acolyte?. An Acolyte has meaningful experience with religious or spiritual service, sacred traditions, temples, ceremonies, or communities of worship. Life and Origins. The character may have been raised around a temple, studied under a religious teacher, volunteered in a sacred institution, maintained holy places, assisted ceremonies, or found faith after a life-changing event. Motivations and Outlook. Faith, service, protection, reform, doubt, duty, spiritual curiosity, or concern for a community may lead an Acolyte into adventure. An Acolyte can be devout, questioning, disill

Character Creation Step by Step Universal Daeva Traits Starting Equipment & Kinah Ability Scores Abilities and the 18 Skills Backgrounds and Proficiencies Understanding Your Background Character Creation Step by Step 1. Choose Elyos or Asmodian. 2. Choose one of the 11 classes. 3. Assign 16, 14, 14, 12, 10, 8 among STR, DEX, CON, INT, WIS and CHA. 4. Choose one Background. 5. Enter class saving throws, armor, shield and weapon access in the Character Manager. 6. Choose exactly 2 Class Skills from the six Skill options listed for your Class and exactly 2 Background Skills from the six Skill options listed for your Background. Duplicate selections are prohibited. A Skill selected as a Class Skill cannot also be selected as a Background Skill; the four selected Skill Proficiencies must therefore be four different Skills. 7. Calculate HP, AC, Initiative, class Save DC, Speed, Passive Perception, and Passive Investigation. 8. Enter starting Common equipment, Common Wings and starting Kinah in the Character Manager. 9. Choose name, appearance, wing appearance, personality, history, relationships and motivation. Character Manager. The Wings of Atreia Character Manager is the official character record for creation, live play, and advancement. Enter your character choices and starting values there as you complete the steps above. The Character Manager tracks the character’s current state; the current Player Handbook and Core Rulebook remain authoritative if a displayed value and the governing rule ever differ. Universal Daeva Traits Trait Rule Creature Type Humanoid (Daeva) Size Medium Walking Speed 30 ft Darkvision 60 ft Ageless Living beings who do not age normally. Manifest Wings Every Daeva has functional Common Wings. Aether-Dependent Flight Flight depends on local Aether conditions. Aetheric Reconstitution A Daeva who truly dies may reform through a functioning attuned Obelisk under the reconstitution rules. Starting Equipment & Kinah Every character begins with one fixed base class weapon or implement, one armor set, Common Wings, and starting Kinah. No character automatically receives potions, ammunition bundles, upgraded equipment, extra adventuring gear, or a shield unless a class feature or other explicit rule grants it. Starting Kinah = 500 Kinah + 250 Kinah for each character level above 1. A Level 1 character starts with 500 Kinah; a Level 20 character starts with 5,250 Kinah. Class weapon, shield, armor, and implement access identifies what your class is allowed to use; it does not mean you own every authorized item. Starting equipment determines what you actually begin play with. Equipment-dependent features function only while their stated requirement is satisfied and do not grant the required equipment unless they explicitly say so. Critical Edge applies only to Dagger weapon damage and does not duplicate or multiply Sneak Attack, Rune Burst, Assassination Sequence, or other bonus-damage dice. Not Thrown. Shortsword 1d6 Piercing Finesse, Light Longsword 1d8 Slashing Versatile 1d10 Spear 1d6 Piercing Versatile 1d8; not Thrown Polearm 1d10 Slashing Heavy, Two-Handed, Reach; Chain-Driven: Gladiator Chain Link weapon die becomes 1d12 Mace 1d8 Bludgeoning — Hammer 1d10 Bludgeoning Heavy, Two-Handed Staff 1d6 Bludgeoning Two-Handed, Channeling. While wielding the Staff with two hands, when one of your class spells or class support techniques restores HP, reduces damage, or grants temporary HP, increase that amount by +1. Channeling does not itself generate additional class resources. Quarterstaff 1d6 Bludgeoning Versatile 1d8 The Light property does not create an extra attack unless a class feature explicitly allows one. Each attack expends 1 shot. Normal Bonus Action Reload restores to 2 shots. Cannot use Quick Shot or Akimbo. Gunslinger ammunition-restoration features can restore Musket shots normally, but never above 2. Standard one-handed firearm capacity increases do not apply. Ranged Weapon Range. The first listed range is the weapon’s Normal Range and the second is its Maximum Range. A target within the weapon’s Normal Range is attacked normally unless another modifier applies. A target beyond Normal Range but within Maximum Range can still be targeted, but the ranged weapon attack is made with Disadvantage. Implements Magical Orbs, Spellbooks, Lutes, and Lyres are class implements, not damaging weapons. Implement Type Properties. Implement type defines playstyle separately from quality bonuses. Magical Orb — Power Channel. Once on each of your turns when a class spell deals rolled damage, add +1 damage to one damage resolution. Spellbook — Calculated Casting. Lute — Harmonic Accompaniment. Once on each of your turns, when a Harmony or Guard Songweaver spell restores HP, grants temporary HP, or reduces damage, increase one such amount by +1. Lyre — Resonant Edge. Once on each of your turns, when a Dissonance or Requiem Songweaver spell deals rolled damage, add +1 damage to one damage resolution. Orb. One hand. Spellbook. One hand while readied. Lyre. One hand. Lute. Two hands while actively used. Hands and Equipped Items Hands. A normal Daeva has two usable hands. One-handed item. Occupies one hand when actively held. Two-handed item. Requires both hands while actively used; it may be carried in one hand when not being used. Versatile. Switching grip is free if the second hand is already free; otherwise an occupied object must first be stowed or dropped. Shield. Occupies one hand and must be removed before actively using another two-handed item. Free hand. Required for pickup, catching, snatching, and mechanisms when the fiction demands it. Unconscious. Drops unsecured actively held items. Worn, strapped, sheathed, or stored items remain secured. Prone. Does not by itself cause held items to drop. Changing Equipment Drawing, readying, stowing, or switching one weapon or implement uses the turn’s free object interaction. Dropping an item is free. Picking one up uses the interaction. Another substantial object manipulation normally requires the Use Object Action. Equipping or removing a shield requires a full Action. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Tempo • Firearm Rhythm • Reload Mastery • Mobile Precision Gunslinger “A bullet sounds the same to everybody.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Tempo, Firearms, and Reload Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Tradition & Outlook Specialization Reassignment The Gunslinger is a mobile firearm martial whose power comes from maintaining Tempo through successful firearm play. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Fire. Move. Reload. Keep the rhythm alive long enough to turn Tempo into control, defense, and lethal pressure. Class Identity Gunslingers are technist marksmen who turn Aether-assisted firearms into speed, precision, and controlled ranged pressure. Pistols support rapid, mobile sequences through Quick Shot and Akimbo, while Muskets provide deliberate two-handed fire that concentrates Tempo into stronger individual hits through Deliberate Shot. Tempo represents the Gunslinger’s ability to build combat rhythm through successful action rather than treating every shot as an isolated event. Tradition & Outlook Gunslingers belong to Atreia’s newer technological traditions. The wider Aion tradition describes early firearm research being dismissed as technist tinkering until battlefield success forced major institutions to recognize the discipline. Wings of Atreia keeps that identity of innovation earning legitimacy through results while using Pistols and Muskets as the class’s only firearm categories. Gunslingers often value nerve, technical familiarity, accuracy, independence, and adaptability. Appearance & Adventuring Gunslingers favor mobile equipment, ammunition management, firearm maintenance, and a practical awareness of range and firing position. Their weapons can make them look strikingly modern beside older martial traditions, but their discipline remains Aetheric and distinctly Atreian. They adventure to test new techniques, serve as ranged specialists, hunt dangerous targets, protect expeditions from positions others cannot exploit, or demonstrate that innovation has earned its place in the war for Atreia. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols Ranged Gunslinger One-handed Weapon Attack. Range 30/90 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d8 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. A Gunslinger can wield two Pistols, but doing so does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols are compatible with Quick Shot and Akimbo. Muskets Ranged Gunslinger Two-handed Weapon Attack. Range 60/180 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d12 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. Ammunition capacity is fixed at 2. Muskets cannot use Quick Shot or Akimbo. Gunslinger ammunition-restoration features can restore Musket shots normally, but a Musket can never hold more than 2 shots. Standard one-handed firearm capacity increases do not apply to Muskets. Reload Every firearm attack consumes one shot. A firearm with no shots remaining is Empty and cannot make firearm attacks until at least one shot is restored. Normal Bonus Action Reload: an Empty firearm is restored to its full Reload capacity. Ammunition restoration is not the Reload action unless a feature explicitly says so. Ammunition-restoration features can restore shots to either Pistols or Muskets up to that firearm's maximum capacity. A Musket's maximum capacity remains 2. Switching between carried one-handed Gunslinger firearms as part of a firearm attack requires no separate object interaction. Standard one-handed firearm capacity progression: Ammo Capacity 4 at Levels 1-4, Ammo Capacity 5 at 5-8, Ammo Capacity 6 at 9-14, and Ammo Capacity 7 at 15-20. Increasing capacity does not automatically reload an Empty firearm. Tempo Tempo is a genuine-combat resource representing firing rhythm, accuracy, and momentum. Wings of Atreia keeps that identity of innovation earning legitimacy through results while using Pistols and Muskets as the class’s only firearm categories. Gunslingers often value nerve, technical familiarity, accuracy, independence, and adaptability. Appearance & Adventuring Gunslingers favor mobile equipment, ammunition management, firearm maintenance, and a practical awareness of range and firing position. Their weapons can make them look strikingly modern beside older martial traditions, but their discipline remains Aetheric and distinctly Atreian. They adventure to test new techniques, serve as ranged specialists, hunt dangerous targets, protect expeditions from positions others cannot exploit, or demonstrate that innovation has earned its place in the war for Atreia. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols Ranged Gunslinger One-handed Weapon Attack. Range 30/90 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d8 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. A Gunslinger can wield two Pistols, but doing so does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols are compatible with Quick Shot and Akimbo. Muskets Ranged Gunslinger Two-handed Weapon Attack. Range 60/180 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d12 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. Ammunition capacity is fixed at 2. Muskets cannot use Quick Shot or Akimbo. Gunslinger ammunition-restoration features can restore Musket shots normally, but a Musket can never hold more than 2 shots. Standard one-handed firearm capacity increases do not apply to Muskets. Normal Bonus Action Reload: an Empty firearm is restored to its full Reload capacity. Ammunition restoration is not the Reload action unless a feature explicitly says so. Ammunition-restoration features can restore shots to either Pistols or Muskets up to that firearm's maximum capacity. A Musket's maximum capacity remains 2. Switching between carried one-handed Gunslinger firearms as part of a firearm attack requires no separate object interaction. Standard one-handed firearm capacity progression: Ammo Capacity 4 at Levels 1-4, Ammo Capacity 5 at 5-8, Ammo Capacity 6 at 9-14, and Ammo Capacity 7 at 15-20. Increasing capacity does not automatically reload an Empty firearm. Tempo Tempo is a genuine-combat resource representing firing rhythm, accuracy, and momentum. One active elemental spirit shares the Spiritmaster’s turn and action economy; together they equal one complete player character. The class establishes two battlefield positions, casts through the spirit, and earns Spirit Bond only through meaningful master-spirit coordination. Class Identity Spiritmasters are binders and commanders of elemental spirits who fight as a partnership rather than as a solitary caster. Their strength comes from coordinating their own spellcraft with a Greater Spirit, applying pressure, disruption, and control across more than one position on the battlefield. Spirit Bond represents the relationship and command structure that makes this divided presence function as one class. Tradition & Outlook The Spiritmaster tradition develops from Atreia’s mage disciplines but turns outward toward spirits, elemental forces, and the difficult art of directing entities shaped by Aether. Spiritmasters are often patient observers, researchers, summoners, or specialists in threats that cannot be understood through ordinary physical study. Their beliefs about spirits differ: some emphasize command, others partnership, responsibility, curiosity, or respect for elemental power. Appearance & Adventuring Spiritmasters use cloth armor and magical implements, while the visible presence of a summoned spirit often defines their silhouette more strongly than clothing does. Their equipment may include ritual, scholarly, or elemental motifs without creating additional mechanics. They adventure to understand unusual spirits, recover lost summoning knowledge, counter supernatural threats, serve as versatile magical operatives, or deepen the bond between Daeva and elemental ally. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Sneak Attack and Rune Marks Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Assassin is a precision melee striker that builds target-bound Rune Marks, converts them into burst damage or execution riders, and uses Shadow Step to remain difficult to pin down. Unlike a conventional Extra Attack martial, its Level 5 Assassination Sequence is a conditional follow-up attack tied to a successful Sneak Attack. Class Identity Assassins are precision predators who win through positioning, timing, concealment, and carefully prepared execution. Their art is not simply “attacking from stealth.” An Assassin studies a target, creates the right opening, carves Rune Marks, and converts preparation into a sudden lethal advantage. Their greatest strength is the ability to decide where and when a close-range confrontation becomes dangerous. Tradition & Outlook The Assassin tradition descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines and is practiced by infiltrators, covert operatives, hunters of dangerous individuals, intelligence agents, and Daevas who favor certainty over spectacle. Assassins often prize patience, awareness, self-control, and economy of motion. Their motives vary widely: service to a faction, revenge, professional duty, protection through preemptive action, or the pursuit of perfect technique. Appearance & Adventuring Assassins favor equipment that permits mobility and unobstructed movement, with Shortswords and Daggers forming the class’s approved weapon identity in Wings of Atreia. Their appearance may be subdued or ceremonial, but practical Assassins avoid anything that compromises movement or control. They adventure when a threat must be found before it strikes, a route must be infiltrated, an enemy leader must be neutralized, or a mystery demands someone comfortable operating unseen. Either way, you'll only die tired.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Focus Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Ranger is a nonmagical ranged hunter that controls enemy movement with persistent battlefield traps, spends Focus on precision or evasive shots, and is rewarded for exploiting targets that walk into prepared terrain. Its sustained damage comes from two ranged attacks, not from spellcasting or a third standard attack. Class Identity Rangers are mobile ranged specialists who control distance through marksmanship, movement, traps, and battlefield awareness. They are most effective when they can read terrain before committing, choose favorable lines of attack, and punish enemies that approach carelessly. Focus represents the Ranger’s ability to convert patience and perception into precise action. Tradition & Outlook The Ranger tradition also descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines, but where Assassins close with a chosen target, Rangers cultivate distance, fieldcraft, and control of the approach. Rangers are common among scouts, hunters, pathfinders, border wardens, reconnaissance troops, and independent Daevas accustomed to surviving beyond secure settlements. They tend to value preparedness, observation, mobility, and freedom of movement. Appearance & Adventuring Rangers usually wear mobile armor and carry bows, ammunition, traps, and field equipment suited to extended movement. Their gear often reflects the terrain in which they learned their craft. Rangers adventure to explore dangerous regions, hunt monsters or enemy operatives, guide expeditions, secure routes, protect remote communities, or prove that no battlefield is truly open ground when preparation and range are on their side. View Songweaver Spell List → Class Identity Class Chassis Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Spell List Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Performance Sequence Tradition & Outlook Specialization Reassignment The Songweaver changes battlefield purpose from moment to moment. Every Songweaver spell belongs to Harmony, Guard, Dissonance, or Requiem. Successful performances create short-lived Refrains, changing Song Roles builds Resonance, and Resonance is spent to amplify, sustain, counter, or conduct the performance. Class Identity Songweavers shape Aether through music, using performance as destructive spellcraft, support, control, and restoration. Their strength lies in versatility: the same class can pressure an enemy, sustain an ally, or shift the emotional and tactical rhythm of an encounter. Resonance represents the accumulating harmony between performance, spellcraft, and the unfolding battle. Tradition & Outlook The Songweaver tradition is rooted in Atreia’s Muses and in remembrance of Siel. The wider Aion tradition describes Muses who continued their studies after the Cataclysm and eventually joined music with Aether in service to their people; their battlefield contribution led to recognition as an established Daeva class. Songweavers may therefore approach performance as remembrance, artistry, scholarship, service, or a declaration that beauty still has power in a broken world. Appearance & Adventuring Songweavers use Lutes and Lyres as their approved implements, often making instrument, costume, gesture, and magical display part of a single visible identity. Their appearance can range from formal performer to traveling battle-musician without changing class mechanics. They adventure to preserve stories, honor Siel, inspire allies, master Aetheric music, carry culture into war-torn regions, or use beauty and sound as weapons against forces that would reduce Atreia to silence.
