Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols Ranged Gunslinger One-handed Weapon Attack. Range 30/90 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d8 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. A Gunslinger can wield two Pistols, but doing so does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols are compatible with Quick Shot and Akimbo. Muskets Ranged Gunslinger Two-handed Weapon Attack. Range 60/180 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d12 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. Ammunition capacity is fixed at 2. Muskets cannot use Quick Shot or Akimbo. Gunslinger ammunition-restoration features can restore Musket shots normally, but a Musket can never hold more than 2 shots. Standard one-handed firearm capacity increases do not apply to Muskets. Reload Every firearm attack consumes one shot. A firearm with no shots remaining is Empty and cannot make firearm attacks until at least one shot is restored. Normal Bonus Action Reload: an Empty firearm is restored to its full Reload capacity. Ammunition restoration is not the Reload action unless a feature explicitly says so. Ammunition-restoration features can restore shots to either Pistols or Muskets up to that firearm's maximum capacity. A Musket's maximum capacity remains 2. Switching between carried one-handed Gunslinger firearms as part of a firearm attack requires no separate object interaction. Standard one-handed firearm capacity progression: Ammo Capacity 4 at Levels 1-4, Ammo Capacity 5 at 5-8, Ammo Capacity 6 at 9-14, and Ammo Capacity 7 at 15-20. Increasing capacity does not automatically reload an Empty firearm. Tempo Tempo is a genuine-combat resource representing firing rhythm, accuracy, and momentum. It begins at 0, resets to 0 when combat ends, and artificial initiative cannot generate it. Maximum Tempo: Levels 1-4 = 3; 5-8 = 4; 9-12 = 5; 13-16 = 6; 17-20 = 7.

It casts through Fire, Ice, Lightning, and Wind spell chains, then spends Aether Focus only when a particular spell needs more damage, area, control pressure, or reliability. Aether Focus enhances spells; it is never the fuel required to cast ordinary Sorcerer spells. Class Identity Sorcerers are masters of direct Aetheric spellcraft, combining destructive magic with the ability to control the shape and tempo of a fight. They can punish clustered enemies, deny movement or action, and unleash powerful spells when an opening appears. Aether Focus represents the concentration and arcane discipline required to turn immense magical potential into reliable battlefield power. Tradition & Outlook The Sorcerer tradition grows from Atreia’s mage disciplines and is associated with formal magical study, experimentation, academies, battlefield arcanists, and Daevas fascinated by the structure of Aether itself. Sorcerers commonly value knowledge, precision, preparation, and intellectual mastery, although their personalities range from scholarly restraint to spectacular confidence. For many, magic is both a weapon and a language through which Atreia can be understood. Appearance & Adventuring Sorcerers favor cloth armor and magical implements such as Orbs and Spellbooks under the Wings of Atreia equipment rules. Their appearance may reflect academic, military, ceremonial, or highly individual magical traditions. They adventure to recover lost knowledge, study Aetheric phenomena, test magical theories, defend their people with overwhelming spellcraft, or confront powers that ordinary weapons cannot adequately answer. Either way, you'll only die tired.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Focus Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Ranger is a nonmagical ranged hunter that controls enemy movement with persistent battlefield traps, spends Focus on precision or evasive shots, and is rewarded for exploiting targets that walk into prepared terrain. Its sustained damage comes from two ranged attacks, not from spellcasting or a third standard attack. Class Identity Rangers are mobile ranged specialists who control distance through marksmanship, movement, traps, and battlefield awareness. They are most effective when they can read terrain before committing, choose favorable lines of attack, and punish enemies that approach carelessly. Focus represents the Ranger’s ability to convert patience and perception into precise action. Tradition & Outlook The Ranger tradition also descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines, but where Assassins close with a chosen target, Rangers cultivate distance, fieldcraft, and control of the approach. Rangers are common among scouts, hunters, pathfinders, border wardens, reconnaissance troops, and independent Daevas accustomed to surviving beyond secure settlements. They tend to value preparedness, observation, mobility, and freedom of movement. Appearance & Adventuring Rangers usually wear mobile armor and carry bows, ammunition, traps, and field equipment suited to extended movement. Their gear often reflects the terrain in which they learned their craft. Rangers adventure to explore dangerous regions, hunt monsters or enemy operatives, guide expeditions, secure routes, protect remote communities, or prove that no battlefield is truly open ground when preparation and range are on their side. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Sneak Attack and Rune Marks Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Assassin is a precision melee striker that builds target-bound Rune Marks, converts them into burst damage or execution riders, and uses Shadow Step to remain difficult to pin down. Unlike a conventional Extra Attack martial, its Level 5 Assassination Sequence is a conditional follow-up attack tied to a successful Sneak Attack. Class Identity Assassins are precision predators who win through positioning, timing, concealment, and carefully prepared execution. Their art is not simply “attacking from stealth.” An Assassin studies a target, creates the right opening, carves Rune Marks, and converts preparation into a sudden lethal advantage. Their greatest strength is the ability to decide where and when a close-range confrontation becomes dangerous. Tradition & Outlook The Assassin tradition descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines and is practiced by infiltrators, covert operatives, hunters of dangerous individuals, intelligence agents, and Daevas who favor certainty over spectacle. Assassins often prize patience, awareness, self-control, and economy of motion. Their motives vary widely: service to a faction, revenge, professional duty, protection through preemptive action, or the pursuit of perfect technique. Appearance & Adventuring Assassins favor equipment that permits mobility and unobstructed movement, with Shortswords and Daggers forming the class’s approved weapon identity in Wings of Atreia. Their appearance may be subdued or ceremonial, but practical Assassins avoid anything that compromises movement or control. They adventure when a threat must be found before it strikes, a route must be infiltrated, an enemy leader must be neutralized, or a mystery demands someone comfortable operating unseen. Face, meet steel.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. On this page Overview Chassis Core Mechanics Action Reference Specializations Progression Examples ↑ Top The Aethertech fights from one piloted Large Bastion platform. The pilot and Bastion are one character’s action economy, not two independent turns. The class alternates between integrated Bastion armaments, Aether Core expenditures, controlled Heat accumulation, venting, repairs, and system integration. The Bastion is a separate physical HP pool that enemies can damage without directly healing or harming the pilot unless an effect specifically targets the pilot. Class Identity Aethertechs are technist warriors who channel Aether through a Bastion: a magical-mechanical combat platform that transforms how the Daeva occupies the battlefield. The class combines personal skill, engineered systems, heavy protection, and controlled bursts of power. Aether Core and Heat represent the constant balance between available energy and the strain created by pushing the Bastion harder. Tradition & Outlook Aethertech is a comparatively modern Daeva discipline born from the recovery, study, and weaponization of advanced magical technology. The wider Aion tradition connects the class to Daeva analysis of Danuar technology and the lessons surrounding Hyperion; Wings of Atreia preserves that technological identity while its own campaign chronology and mechanics remain authoritative. Aethertechs often value ingenuity, technical discipline, experimentation, and the belief that knowledge taken from dangerous enemies can be turned toward Atreia’s defense. Appearance & Adventuring An Aethertech is visually defined by the Bastion and the contrast between a Daeva operator and an imposing Aether-powered war platform. Outside it, the Aethertech remains a trained combatant using the class’s approved weapons and equipment. Aethertechs adventure to recover technology, test designs under real conditions, oppose Balaur war machines, protect expeditions with a durable mobile platform, or prove that engineering can stand beside sword and spell as a heroic discipline. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Ability Intelligence Secondary Ability Constitution Hit Die d8 Saving Throws Intelligence, Constitution Armor Chain Armor Skills Choose 2 from 6: Arcana, Athletics, Investigation, Perception, Sleight of Hand, Survival Weapons Shortswords, Maces, Hammers Signature Resources Aether Core and Heat Signature Mechanic Piloted Bastion Bastion Size Large Class Save DC 8 + PB + INT modifier Extra Attack Level 5; two Bastion weapon attacks only Spellcasting None Bastion Targeting and Chassis The pilot and Bastion have separate HP and temporary HP. Repairs restore Bastion HP and are not healing. While occupied, ordinary physical attacks targeting the Aethertech generally strike the Bastion first. Mental, emotional, biological, and similar effects target the pilot when appropriate. One area effect normally does not double-hit both pilot and Bastion. Bastion physical STR/DEX/CON saves use PB + INT modifier. Mental saves use the pilot’s relevant save. When the Bastion reaches 0 HP it is Disabled. The pilot is ejected to the nearest legal space, takes 1d6 Force damage, and does not provoke Opportunity Attacks from the ejection. A disabled Bastion retains its current Core and Heat; a fresh chassis does not replace it. A Short Rest repairs a Disabled or damaged Bastion by half its maximum HP. A Long Rest repairs the Bastion to its maximum HP. These restorations are repairs, not healing. Once the Bastion has at least 1 HP, it is operational. Entering or re-entering a deployed Bastion uses an Action when otherwise legal. A defeated or voluntarily replaced Bastion never functions as a companion or second PC. Contesting STR checks with the Bastion e.g Grapple, pushing, pulling, except for skill or ability effects, will have the PC use this formula: 1d20+8+INT modifier+PB considering that a Bastion is a Large entity. Target must contest with their choice of Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics). This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Spellcasting Reference: Chanter has a dedicated spell-list page for quick browsing. View Chanter Spell List → Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Cadence Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Spell List Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Rhythm Sequence Specialization Reassignment The Chanter wins by alternating weapon attacks, spells, and active Mantra management. Cadence is earned by changing categories rather than repeating one action, then spent on damage, protection, healing, and tactical movement. It is a secondary healer and hybrid support, not a replacement for the Cleric or a dedicated martial striker. Class Identity Chanters are martial support specialists who combine staff technique, enchantment, restorative magic, and Mantras into a continuous rhythm of battle. Rather than solving every problem through one large spell, a Chanter improves the party’s performance over time and responds to changing pressure with Cadence. Their presence is felt in how effectively the entire group moves, strikes, and recovers together. Tradition & Outlook The Chanter tradition grows from Atreia’s priestly disciplines but emphasizes disciplined body, voice, repetition, and the shaping of Aether through words and practiced forms. Chanters are often teachers, battle companions, spiritual guides, martial ascetics, or morale-keepers. They tend to value harmony between individual excellence and collective strength: the ideal Chanter does not merely stand beside allies but helps those allies become more capable. Appearance & Adventuring Chanters are strongly associated with Staff and Quarterstaff techniques in Wings of Atreia. Their clothing and armor tend to allow movement while retaining the ceremonial or disciplined character of a priestly warrior. They adventure to guide companions, strengthen military or exploratory groups, carry teachings into dangerous places, preserve morale during long campaigns, or prove that disciplined cooperation can overcome enemies stronger than any one Daeva. View Cleric Spell List → Class Identity Class Chassis Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Spell List Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Support Sequence Tradition & Outlook Specialization Reassignment The Cleric is Wings of Atreia’s primary restorative spellcaster. It is deliberately more durable than the d6 full casters and is rewarded for meaningful intervention: healing an ally in real danger, actually preventing damage, or removing a significant hostile effect. Divine Grace then converts that successful support into more emergency power. Class Identity Clerics are Atreia’s foremost restorative and protective spellcasters. Their calling is not limited to healing wounds after the fact: they preserve the party through recovery, cleansing, protection, and timely intervention while retaining the ability to fight when necessary. Divine Grace represents the reserve of sacred and restorative power through which a Cleric answers moments of genuine need. Tradition & Outlook The Cleric tradition grows from Atreia’s priestly disciplines and is associated with healers, battlefield ministers, temple servants, protectors of communities, and Daevas who understand survival as a collective responsibility. Clerics often value service, perseverance, mercy, duty, or faith, but they need not share one personality or theology. A militant Cleric and a gentle healer may practice the same class through very different convictions. Appearance & Adventuring Clerics commonly combine durable armor with practical healing or ritual equipment. In Wings of Atreia they may use Maces, Hammers, Staffs, Quarterstaffs, and shields from Round Shields to Medium Shields according to their approved access. They adventure to protect lives, confront corruption or supernatural danger, recover sacred knowledge, serve a cause, or ensure that an expedition can survive places where retreat and ordinary medicine are not enough. Keep the rhythm alive long enough to turn Tempo into control, defense, and lethal pressure. Class Identity Gunslingers are technist marksmen who turn Aether-assisted firearms into speed, precision, and controlled ranged pressure. Pistols support rapid, mobile sequences through Quick Shot and Akimbo, while Muskets provide deliberate two-handed fire that concentrates Tempo into stronger individual hits through Deliberate Shot. Tempo represents the Gunslinger’s ability to build combat rhythm through successful action rather than treating every shot as an isolated event. Tradition & Outlook Gunslingers belong to Atreia’s newer technological traditions. The wider Aion tradition describes early firearm research being dismissed as technist tinkering until battlefield success forced major institutions to recognize the discipline. Wings of Atreia keeps that identity of innovation earning legitimacy through results while using Pistols and Muskets as the class’s only firearm categories. Gunslingers often value nerve, technical familiarity, accuracy, independence, and adaptability. Appearance & Adventuring Gunslingers favor mobile equipment, ammunition management, firearm maintenance, and a practical awareness of range and firing position. Their weapons can make them look strikingly modern beside older martial traditions, but their discipline remains Aetheric and distinctly Atreian. They adventure to test new techniques, serve as ranged specialists, hunt dangerous targets, protect expeditions from positions others cannot exploit, or demonstrate that innovation has earned its place in the war for Atreia. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Focus Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Ranger is a nonmagical ranged hunter that controls enemy movement with persistent battlefield traps, spends Focus on precision or evasive shots, and is rewarded for exploiting targets that walk into prepared terrain. Its sustained damage comes from two ranged attacks, not from spellcasting or a third standard attack. Class Identity Rangers are mobile ranged specialists who control distance through marksmanship, movement, traps, and battlefield awareness. They are most effective when they can read terrain before committing, choose favorable lines of attack, and punish enemies that approach carelessly. Focus represents the Ranger’s ability to convert patience and perception into precise action. Tradition & Outlook The Ranger tradition also descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines, but where Assassins close with a chosen target, Rangers cultivate distance, fieldcraft, and control of the approach. Rangers are common among scouts, hunters, pathfinders, border wardens, reconnaissance troops, and independent Daevas accustomed to surviving beyond secure settlements. They tend to value preparedness, observation, mobility, and freedom of movement. Appearance & Adventuring Rangers usually wear mobile armor and carry bows, ammunition, traps, and field equipment suited to extended movement. Their gear often reflects the terrain in which they learned their craft. Rangers adventure to explore dangerous regions, hunt monsters or enemy operatives, guide expeditions, secure routes, protect remote communities, or prove that no battlefield is truly open ground when preparation and range are on their side. Every Songweaver spell belongs to Harmony, Guard, Dissonance, or Requiem. Successful performances create short-lived Refrains, changing Song Roles builds Resonance, and Resonance is spent to amplify, sustain, counter, or conduct the performance. Class Identity Songweavers shape Aether through music, using performance as destructive spellcraft, support, control, and restoration. Their strength lies in versatility: the same class can pressure an enemy, sustain an ally, or shift the emotional and tactical rhythm of an encounter. Resonance represents the accumulating harmony between performance, spellcraft, and the unfolding battle. Tradition & Outlook The Songweaver tradition is rooted in Atreia’s Muses and in remembrance of Siel. The wider Aion tradition describes Muses who continued their studies after the Cataclysm and eventually joined music with Aether in service to their people; their battlefield contribution led to recognition as an established Daeva class. Songweavers may therefore approach performance as remembrance, artistry, scholarship, service, or a declaration that beauty still has power in a broken world. Appearance & Adventuring Songweavers use Lutes and Lyres as their approved implements, often making instrument, costume, gesture, and magical display part of a single visible identity. Their appearance can range from formal performer to traveling battle-musician without changing class mechanics. They adventure to preserve stories, honor Siel, inspire allies, master Aetheric music, carry culture into war-torn regions, or use beauty and sound as weapons against forces that would reduce Atreia to silence. It casts through Fire, Ice, Lightning, and Wind spell chains, then spends Aether Focus only when a particular spell needs more damage, area, control pressure, or reliability. Aether Focus enhances spells; it is never the fuel required to cast ordinary Sorcerer spells. Class Identity Sorcerers are masters of direct Aetheric spellcraft, combining destructive magic with the ability to control the shape and tempo of a fight. They can punish clustered enemies, deny movement or action, and unleash powerful spells when an opening appears. Aether Focus represents the concentration and arcane discipline required to turn immense magical potential into reliable battlefield power. Tradition & Outlook The Sorcerer tradition grows from Atreia’s mage disciplines and is associated with formal magical study, experimentation, academies, battlefield arcanists, and Daevas fascinated by the structure of Aether itself. Sorcerers commonly value knowledge, precision, preparation, and intellectual mastery, although their personalities range from scholarly restraint to spectacular confidence. For many, magic is both a weapon and a language through which Atreia can be understood. Appearance & Adventuring Sorcerers favor cloth armor and magical implements such as Orbs and Spellbooks under the Wings of Atreia equipment rules. Their appearance may reflect academic, military, ceremonial, or highly individual magical traditions. They adventure to recover lost knowledge, study Aetheric phenomena, test magical theories, defend their people with overwhelming spellcraft, or confront powers that ordinary weapons cannot adequately answer. One active elemental spirit shares the Spiritmaster’s turn and action economy; together they equal one complete player character. The class establishes two battlefield positions, casts through the spirit, and earns Spirit Bond only through meaningful master-spirit coordination. Class Identity Spiritmasters are binders and commanders of elemental spirits who fight as a partnership rather than as a solitary caster. Their strength comes from coordinating their own spellcraft with a Greater Spirit, applying pressure, disruption, and control across more than one position on the battlefield. Spirit Bond represents the relationship and command structure that makes this divided presence function as one class. Tradition & Outlook The Spiritmaster tradition develops from Atreia’s mage disciplines but turns outward toward spirits, elemental forces, and the difficult art of directing entities shaped by Aether. Spiritmasters are often patient observers, researchers, summoners, or specialists in threats that cannot be understood through ordinary physical study. Their beliefs about spirits differ: some emphasize command, others partnership, responsibility, curiosity, or respect for elemental power. Appearance & Adventuring Spiritmasters use cloth armor and magical implements, while the visible presence of a summoned spirit often defines their silhouette more strongly than clothing does. Their equipment may include ritual, scholarly, or elemental motifs without creating additional mechanics. They adventure to understand unusual spirits, recover lost summoning knowledge, counter supernatural threats, serve as versatile magical operatives, or deepen the bond between Daeva and elemental ally. Vision, Stealth, Traps, Locks & Theft Vision and Light Cover, Line of Sight & Line of Effect Stealth and Infiltration Traps and Non-Aether Hazards Locks Theft and Pickpocket Social Interaction, Information & Captivity Vision, Stealth, Traps, Locks & Theft Vision and Light Light states are Bright Light, Dim Light, and Darkness. Obscuration states are Lightly Obscured and Heavily Obscured. Dim Light lightly obscures; Darkness heavily obscures a creature that cannot otherwise see through it. Daeva Darkvision treats Darkness within 60 feet as Dim Light, not Bright Light. A recommended ordinary light source has a stated Bright radius plus an equal additional Dim radius unless its own text says otherwise. Bright light does not universally prohibit Stealth. Obscurity and Invisibility do not automatically make a creature Hidden. Cover, Line of Sight & Line of Effect No Cover. No defensive benefit from Cover. Half Cover. A creature or object behind meaningful partial obstruction gains +2 AC and +2 to Dexterity saving throws against effects originating from the covered direction. Intervening creatures can provide Half Cover when they materially obstruct the line. Full Cover. Full Cover blocks the relevant Line of Effect and prevents direct targeting through that obstruction unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Three-Quarters Cover does not exist in Wings of Atreia. Cover does not stack; use the best applicable Cover. Altitude neither inherently grants nor ignores Cover. Line of Sight and Line of Effect are distinct. Line of Sight determines whether you can see a target or point. Line of Effect determines whether an attack, spell, or effect can physically reach it. Heavy obscurement is not Cover by itself. Stealth and Infiltration Use scene states Undetected, Suspicious, and Alerted; these are not Conditions. Stealth must exceed Passive Perception; ties favor the observer. An active Search uses the GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation), against the relevant DC or opposing Stealth; ties favor the Searcher where opposed. Do not reroll Stealth every 5 feet; roll again only when circumstances materially change. For group Stealth, at least half the group must succeed. A failed check may create Suspicion rather than immediate full alarm when appropriate. Distractions create an opportunity to Hide rather than automatic success. Disguises are primarily social. Invisibility is not the same as Hidden. Wings do not automatically prevent Stealth. Traps and Non-Aether Hazards Describe a hazard with Trigger, Detection, Avoid/Disable method, Save/Check, Effect, and Reset/Duration. Hazards may be obvious, concealed, or hidden. Detection normally uses Passive Perception, active Perception, or Investigation. Disable methods depend on the mechanism and can use Sleight of Hand, Investigation, Athletics, or another appropriate Skill. There is no mandatory Thieves’ Tools system. Failure triggers the hazard only when the hazard says so. Damage and Conditions use existing universal rules. Forced movement is horizontal unless the hazard explicitly creates vertical displacement. Hazards normally resolve when triggered rather than taking their own Initiative turns. Repeat attempts require changed circumstances. Locks Mechanical Lock DC Simple 10 Standard 12 Secure 15 High Security 18 Exceptional 20+ The correct key opens a normal lock without a check. Mechanical locks generally use Dexterity (Sleight of Hand). Unusual mechanisms can use Intelligence (Investigation). Forcing uses Strength (Athletics); destroying a lock or door uses normal object/destruction adjudication. Failure does not automatically break or trigger a lock unless its design says so. Aether locks use Aether Interaction. If a task is impossible, do not assign an absurd DC—state that it cannot be done by that method. Theft and Pickpocket A theft attempt requires a plausible opportunity. Taking an accessible small item uses Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) against Passive Perception and must exceed it. If the target is actively watching, oppose with active Perception; ties favor the observer. Secured items can require a different approach. Failure may create suspicion or alarm. Success means the theft was unnoticed at that moment; later discovery remains possible. Distraction creates opportunity rather than automatic success. Help can grant +2 when genuinely meaningful. Worn armor, shields, Wings, wielded weapons, and equipped mandatory implements cannot simply be pickpocketed. Repeated attempts require changed circumstances. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Combat Turn structure, actions, movement, attacks, damage, conditions, death, rests, and survival. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative Round and Turn Action Economy Attack Action Universal Actions Ready Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative, rounds, and combat-only resources are used only for genuine combat or another situation where structured turn order is necessary. Characters cannot manufacture artificial combat to farm cooldowns, resources, or timing triggers. Initiative Initiative = 1d20 + Dexterity modifier. Do not add PB unless an explicit feature says so. Alert adds +2 Initiative. There is no Surprise Round and Surprise does not grant Advantage on Initiative. When one side genuinely catches another side unaware, the GM may, at discretion, allow one appropriate pre-Initiative attack roll against the target's normal defense before Initiative is rolled. This is not an extra round, is not automatic, and does not create a general Surprise action economy. After that resolution, roll Initiative normally. Round and Turn One combat round represents approximately six seconds in the game world. Each participant normally takes one turn in Initiative order. All turns in the round abstract actions occurring within the same six-second span; do not add each turn as another six seconds. Action Economy Action. One per turn. Movement. Up to the creature’s available movement, subject to terrain and conditions. Bonus Action. Up to one, but only when a feature grants something that uses a Bonus Action. Reaction. Normally one per round, refreshing at the start of the creature’s turn unless an explicit class rule says otherwise. Object interaction. One free simple object interaction per turn. There is no universal Action-to-Bonus-Action or Bonus-Action-to-Action conversion. Unused movement or Actions are not stored for later turns. Attack Action The Attack Action makes one attack unless a feature such as Extra Attack says otherwise. Grapple and Shove are full Actions and do not replace one attack within Extra Attack. Player Weapon Requirement. A player character must be wielding an approved class weapon to take the normal Attack Action. Unarmed Attacks and Improvised Weapons are not player combat options unless a later explicit feature creates a specific exception. Opportunity Attacks. Opportunity Attacks remain part of the core combat rules. When a hostile creature you can perceive voluntarily leaves your melee reach, you may use your Reaction to make one melee attack against it, resolving the attack before it leaves that reach. Forced movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Universal Actions Dash. Gain additional movement equal to your current Speed for the turn. Difficult Terrain and other movement costs still apply. While flying, Dash adds horizontal movement but does not grant an additional altitude-layer change. Disengage. Until the end of your turn, your movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks. Dodge. Until the start of your next turn, attacks against you have Disadvantage if you can perceive the attacker, and you have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws. Dodge ends if you become Incapacitated or your Speed becomes 0. Hide. You must have meaningful concealment or another circumstance that allows hiding. Make Dexterity (Stealth) against Passive Perception or active Perception as appropriate. You cannot Hide while clearly seen. Hidden is not Invisible. Making an attack reveals your position after that attack resolves. Search. Deliberately search using a GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation). Use Object. Use this Action for substantial manipulation beyond the one free simple object interaction. A specific item’s activation rule controls when it states another cost. Ready A creature can prepare one Action for a perceivable trigger. When the trigger occurs, the creature may use its Reaction to perform the readied Action. Ready does not store ordinary movement, but Dash can be readied as the Action. Readied attacks retain all weapon properties. A readied spell must still meet implement and targeting requirements when released. Losing a mandatory implement before release prevents release. Concentration begins when the spell actually resolves. Ready never bypasses aerial restrictions, range, or other universal rules. Simultaneous Effects Effects resolve one at a time. The active creature orders its own simultaneous effects; the GM orders GM-controlled simultaneous effects. For opposing same-time effects, resolve the active creature first, then use Initiative if needed. Damage resolves before state changes caused by that damage. Start-of-

WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Glossary & Core Terms A player-facing A–Z reference for the vocabulary used throughout Wings of Atreia, with direct links to the full rules and lore pages. How to use this page: definitions here are quick-reference summaries. Follow the “Read more” link whenever you need the complete rule, class text, or world context. A B C D E F G I K L M P R S U W 46 terms A Action Your main turn action. Many attacks, spells, class features, and other options specify that they use your Action. Read more: Combat → Advantage / Disadvantage Roll two d20s and use the higher result for Advantage or the lower result for Disadvantage. Read more: Core Resolution → Aether The supernatural power that underlies Daeva abilities, spellcasting, flight, and many extraordinary phenomena in Atreia. Read more: Aether & Spellcasting → Aether Enhancement The higher equipment-quality path beyond Profession +2. Aether upgrades are level-gated and handled separately from ordinary Profession work. Read more: Equipment → Ascension The transformation by which a mortal becomes a Daeva and receives Wings. WoA begins with this event in Session 0. Read more: Character Creation → At-Will A spell or ability frequency that may be used whenever its normal action and other requirements are met. Read more: Aether & Spellcasting → B Background A character-creation choice representing experience and identity before or around Ascension; it provides its defined skills and related benefits. Read more: Backgrounds → Bonus Action A secondary turn action available only when a feature, spell, or rule explicitly gives an option that uses it. Read more: Combat → C Character Manager The official WoA character-management method for creation records, advancement, current resources, equipment, spells, and other tracked character data. Read more: Character Creation → Class Your Daeva’s primary mechanical path. WoA uses eleven classes and does not use multiclassing. Read more: Classes → Class Resource A class-specific pool, charge, stance, meter, or other tracked mechanic defined by that class. Read more: Quick Reference → Class Save DC Normally 8 + Proficiency Bonus + the class ability identified by your class, unless a rule states otherwise. Read more: Core Resolution → Concentration A spell/effect limit: only one Concentration effect can be maintained at a time, and Incapacitated ends it. WoA does not use Concentration saving throws. Read more: Aether & Spellcasting → Condition A named rules state such as Poisoned or Incapacitated that changes what a creature can do or how rolls affect it. Read more: Combat → Cooldown A spell or ability frequency that becomes unavailable after use until its stated cooldown is satisfied; WoA also uses the universal out-of-combat cooldown rule where applicable. Read more: Aether & Spellcasting → D Daeva An Ascended immortal warrior of Atreia. Player characters in Wings of Atreia are Daevas. Read more: Character Creation → Daeva Points (DP) A resource unlocked at Level 10 and earned through participation in genuine combat victories. DP powers Ultimate Abilities and persists through rests. Read more: Daeva Points & Ultimates → E Empyrean Boon A powerful universal character option gained at Level 19 according to the advancement rules. Read more: Feats & Empyrean Boons → Empyrean Lord One of the great Daeva Lords whose authority and legacy shape Elyos and Asmodian civilization, together with the two historic Tower Guardians. Read more: World → F Faction Your character’s allegiance as Elyos or Asmodian. Faction affects culture, homeland, and campaign relationships rather than class statistics. Read more: Character Creation → Feat A universal character option chosen at designated advancement points instead of an Ability Score Improvement where the rules allow it. Read more: Feats & Empyrean Boons → Flight Slot A tracked unit of a Daeva’s flight capacity. The number of Flight Slots increases with character level. Read more: Flight → G Genuine Combat A real encounter using initiative and combat timing. Artificial encounters cannot be used to farm resources such as Daeva Points. Read more: Combat → I Implement A spellcasting equipment category that can follow the established quality and enhancement progression. Read more: Equipment → K Kinah The standard currency used for purchases, profession training, supplies, and other economic transactions. Read more: Professions & Economy → L Legendary Equipment Story-driven top-tier equipment above the Aether enhancement tiers. Legendary items are not ordinary Profession products. Read more: Equipment → Long Rest An 8-hour recovery period. What it restores depends on the specific class, spell, feature, or rule. Read more: Combat → Lord Action The dedicated off-turn action framework used by Empyrean Lords and Dragon Lords. Read more: Combat → M Milestone Advancement WoA’s advancement method. Class Sorcerer Chain Wind Unlock Level 17 Prerequisite Cyclone Field Spell Level 7 Casting Time Action Range 120 ft Frequency Long Rest 1 Duration Instantaneous Concentration No Role Apex Zone / Control Base Effect. Create a 30-foot-radius maelstrom within 120 feet until the end of your next turn. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Martial Support • Mantras • Cadence • Harmonic Warfare Chanter “Stay close, stay safe.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Spellcasting Reference: Chanter has a dedicated spell-list page for quick browsing. View Chanter Spell List → Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Cadence Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Spell List Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Rhythm Sequence Specialization Reassignment The Chanter wins by alternating weapon attacks, spells, and active Mantra management. Cadence is earned by changing categories rather than repeating one action, then spent on damage, protection, healing, and tactical movement. It is a secondary healer and hybrid support, not a replacement for the Cleric or a dedicated martial striker. Class Identity Chanters are martial support specialists who combine staff technique, enchantment, restorative magic, and Mantras into a continuous rhythm of battle. Rather than solving every problem through one large spell, a Chanter improves the party’s performance over time and responds to changing pressure with Cadence. Their presence is felt in how effectively the entire group moves, strikes, and recovers together. Tradition & Outlook The Chanter tradition grows from Atreia’s priestly disciplines but emphasizes disciplined body, voice, repetition, and the shaping of Aether through words and practiced forms. Chanters are often teachers, battle companions, spiritual guides, martial ascetics, or morale-keepers. They tend to value harmony between individual excellence and collective strength: the ideal Chanter does not merely stand beside allies but helps those allies become more capable. Appearance & Adventuring Chanters are strongly associated with Staff and Quarterstaff techniques in Wings of Atreia. Their clothing and armor tend to allow movement while retaining the ceremonial or disciplined character of a priestly warrior. They adventure to guide companions, strengthen military or exploratory groups, carry teachings into dangerous places, preserve morale during long campaigns, or prove that disciplined cooperation can overcome enemies stronger than any one Daeva. It begins at 0 when combat starts, resets to 0 when combat ends, and artificial initiative cannot create or restore it. Maximum Cadence is 3 at Levels 1–4, 4 at 5–8, 5 at 9–12, 6 at 13–16, and 7 at 17–20. Category Qualifying Event Martial You hit a hostile creature with a weapon attack. Spell A Chanter spell meaningfully affects a creature by hit, damage, failed save, actual healing, meaningful prevention, or another significant effect. Chant You activate, replace, or deliberately invoke a Mantra/Chant and it meaningfully changes at least one creature. Passive maintenance never qualifies. Your previous qualifying category is always the most recent successful qualifying category, whether or not that event generated Cadence. When you successfully complete a qualifying event whose category differs from your previous successful qualifying category, gain 1 Cadence, subject to the normal generation limit. Your first successful qualifying event in a combat establishes your previous category; it does not generate Cadence by itself. Normal Cadence generation is limited to 1 per turn unless a feature explicitly grants more. Secondary Chanter riders do not recursively generate Cadence, Resonant Network triggers, Mantra Weaving, or other support sequences unless explicit. Chant: you activate, replace, or deliberately invoke a Mantra/Chant and it meaningfully changes at least one creature; passive maintenance does not qualify. How You Gain It When a successful qualifying event uses a category different from your previous successful qualifying category, gain 1 Cadence. text: WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Chanter Spell Marching Hymn Supplemental Chant · Movement Support Source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 , Integrated Spell Compendium. Class Chanter Chain Supplemental Chant Unlock Level 6 Prerequisite — Casting Time Action Range Self aura Frequency Short Rest 1 Duration Until start of your next turn Concentration No Role Movement Support Base Effect. Allies in your Mantra radius gain +10 feet Speed and ignore the first 10 feet of difficult terrain they move through before the start of your next turn. Spell-Level Scaling. This spell improves at Spell Levels 3, 5, and 7 as listed below. Class Identity Gunslingers are technist marksmen who turn Aether-assisted firearms into speed, precision, and controlled ranged pressure. Appearance & Adventuring Gunslingers favor mobile equipment, ammunition management, firearm maintenance, and a practical awareness of range and firing position. Their weapons can make them look strikingly modern beside older martial traditions, but their discipline remains Aetheric and distinctly Atreian. They adventure to test new techniques, serve as ranged specialists, hunt dangerous targets, protect expeditions from positions others cannot exploit, or demonstrate that innovation has earned its place in the war for Atreia. Either way, you'll only die tired.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Focus Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Ranger is a nonmagical ranged hunter that controls enemy movement with persistent battlefield traps, spends Focus on precision or evasive shots, and is rewarded for exploiting targets that walk into prepared terrain. Its sustained damage comes from two ranged attacks, not from spellcasting or a third standard attack. Class Identity Rangers are mobile ranged specialists who control distance through marksmanship, movement, traps, and battlefield awareness. They are most effective when they can read terrain before committing, choose favorable lines of attack, and punish enemies that approach carelessly. Focus represents the Ranger’s ability to convert patience and perception into precise action. Tradition & Outlook The Ranger tradition also descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines, but where Assassins close with a chosen target, Rangers cultivate distance, fieldcraft, and control of the approach. Rangers are common among scouts, hunters, pathfinders, border wardens, reconnaissance troops, and independent Daevas accustomed to surviving beyond secure settlements. They tend to value preparedness, observation, mobility, and freedom of movement. Appearance & Adventuring Rangers usually wear mobile armor and carry bows, ammunition, traps, and field equipment suited to extended movement. Their gear often reflects the terrain in which they learned their craft. Rangers adventure to explore dangerous regions, hunt monsters or enemy operatives, guide expeditions, secure routes, protect remote communities, or prove that no battlefield is truly open ground when preparation and range are on their side. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Melee Striker • Sneak Attack • Rune Marks • Execution Assassin “You'll know I'm there when you're dead.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Sneak Attack and Rune Marks Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Assassin is a precision melee striker that builds target-bound Rune Marks, converts them into burst damage or execution riders, and uses Shadow Step to remain difficult to pin down. Unlike a conventional Extra Attack martial, its Level 5 Assassination Sequence is a conditional follow-up attack tied to a successful Sneak Attack. Class Identity Assassins are precision predators who win through positioning, timing, concealment, and carefully prepared execution. Their art is not simply “attacking from stealth.” An Assassin studies a target, creates the right opening, carves Rune Marks, and converts preparation into a sudden lethal advantage. Their greatest strength is the ability to decide where and when a close-range confrontation becomes dangerous. Tradition & Outlook The Assassin tradition descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines and is practiced by infiltrators, covert operatives, hunters of dangerous individuals, intelligence agents, and Daevas who favor certainty over spectacle. Assassins often prize patience, awareness, self-control, and economy of motion. Their motives vary widely: service to a faction, revenge, professional duty, protection through preemptive action, or the pursuit of perfect technique. Appearance & Adventuring Assassins favor equipment that permits mobility and unobstructed movement, with Shortswords and Daggers forming the class’s approved weapon identity in Wings of Atreia. Their appearance may be subdued or ceremonial, but practical Assassins avoid anything that compromises movement or control. They adventure when a threat must be found before it strikes, a route must be infiltrated, an enemy leader must be neutralized, or a mystery demands someone comfortable operating unseen. text: Meaningful Support and Divine Grace. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Primary Healer • Divine Grace • Protection • Purification Cleric “Protect me and you shall never fall.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Spellcasting Reference: Cleric has a dedicated spell-list page for quick browsing. View Cleric Spell List → Class Identity Class Chassis Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Spell List Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Support Sequence Tradition & Outlook Specialization Reassignment The Cleric is Wings of Atreia’s primary restorative spellcaster. It is deliberately more durable than the d6 full casters and is rewarded for meaningful intervention: healing an ally in real danger, actually preventing damage, or removing a significant hostile effect. Divine Grace then converts that successful support into more emergency power. Class Identity Clerics are Atreia’s foremost restorative and protective spellcasters. Their calling is not limited to healing wounds after the fact: they preserve the party through recovery, cleansing, protection, and timely intervention while retaining the ability to fight when necessary. Divine Grace represents the reserve of sacred and restorative power through which a Cleric answers moments of genuine need. Tradition & Outlook The Cleric tradition grows from Atreia’s priestly disciplines and is associated with healers, battlefield ministers, temple servants, protectors of communities, and Daevas who understand survival as a collective responsibility. Clerics often value service, perseverance, mercy, duty, or faith, but they need not share one personality or theology. A militant Cleric and a gentle healer may practice the same class through very different convictions. Appearance & Adventuring Clerics commonly combine durable armor with practical healing or ritual equipment. In Wings of Atreia they may use Maces, Hammers, Staffs, Quarterstaffs, and shields from Round Shields to Medium Shields according to their approved access. They adventure to protect lives, confront corruption or supernatural danger, recover sacred knowledge, serve a cause, or ensure that an expedition can survive places where retreat and ordinary medicine are not enough. Your normal once-per-round generation becomes available again at the start of your turn, allowing an off-turn protection to qualify without double-dipping around initiative boundaries. Meaningful Support means one of the following actually occurs: restore HP while the creature was below half maximum HP; prevent or reduce damage by at least PB; or suppress/remove a mechanically significant hostile condition or effect. Passive aura bonuses and passive AC do not generate Divine Grace unless a feature explicitly says so. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Flight Exploration flight, Combat Flight Slots, airborne movement, gliding, falling, and Aether restrictions. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Flight & Aerial Combat Altitude Layers 3D Distance Melee Descending Attack Physical Ranged Attacks Flight Slots Aether State Interaction Flight & Aerial Combat Altitude Layers Layer Height Access Low 30 ft All functional Wings Mid 60 ft All functional Wings High 90 ft All functional Wings Legendary 120 ft Legendary Wings only Ground level is 0 feet and is not an altitude layer. There are four airborne altitude layers: Low (30 ft), Mid (60 ft), High (90 ft), and Legendary (120 ft). Voluntarily ascending or descending one altitude layer consumes all movement for that turn. A creature cannot both ascend and descend voluntarily in the same turn. Dash does not permit an additional altitude-layer change. A Daeva without Legendary Wings cannot voluntarily ascend above the High layer at 90 feet. 3D Distance For WoA aerial targeting, total distance = the greater of horizontal distance or vertical distance. Do not use Pythagorean distance and do not add horizontal and vertical distance together. Melee Airborne melee uses ordinary reach: usually 5 feet, or 10 feet for a Reach weapon. Being on the same altitude layer does not remove the need to physically move into reach. Descending Attack If a melee attacker begins its turn higher than the target, descends at least 25 feet, and then makes its first qualifying melee attack against that lower target, the attack has Advantage. Physical Ranged Attacks Universal Close-Range Rule. If the target of a physical ranged weapon attack is within 5 feet of the attacker, the attack roll has Disadvantage. This applies whether the attacker is grounded or airborne and does not change the weapon’s listed Normal Range or Maximum Range. A lower-altitude physical ranged attacker has Advantage against a higher-altitude winged airborne target because the wings are exposed. This Exposed Wings rule does not apply to wingless creatures flying through Saturated Aether. A higher-altitude ranged attacker gains no automatic Advantage merely for being above the target. When the physical ranged attacker is above the target, increase only the weapon’s Maximum Range by half the vertical distance, rounded up. The weapon’s Normal Range is unchanged. Magical attacks do not gain this extension. Flight Slots Level Base Max Slots 1–3 2 4–6 3 7–9 4 10–12 5 13–16 6 17–19 7 20 8 A stable airborne Daeva spends 1 Flight Slot at the end of each of its turns. A grounded Daeva recovers 1 Flight Slot at the end of each grounded turn. Short Rest restores half maximum, rounded down; Long Rest restores all. When a creature runs out of Flight Slots while airborne, it immediately falls. Aether State Interaction Depleted Aether. Flight is fully restricted. Stable Aether. Normal flight rules. Saturated Aether. Daevas spend no combat Flight Slots, though exploration Flight Time limits still apply. Wingless creatures capable of movement may gain flight equal to normal Speed while Saturated; they do not use Flight Slots and are not subject to Exposed Wings. Unstable Zone / Aether Instability. This is hazard-defined scene behavior rather than a universal Aether State. The three universal States are Stable, Depleted, and Saturated. Use the specific Aether Hazard rules for the area. Aether-State Changes and Boundaries Aether-State changes take effect immediately. Crossing into a new Aether State immediately applies the entered State. In Depleted Aether, Aether-supported flight is unavailable; an airborne Daeva entering a Depleted area loses flight and falls, using the normal DC 12 Dexterity Emergency Landing Reaction if eligible. Saturated → Stable: Daevas resume normal Flight Slot expenditure. A creature flying only because Saturated Aether granted it flight loses that flight and falls. Saturated → Depleted: affected airborne creatures immediately lose Aether-supported flight and fall. Stable → Saturated: Daevas stop spending Combat Flight Slots, and eligible wingless creatures gain access to Aether-supported flight equal to normal Speed, but no creature automatically takes off. Falling and Emergency Landing Falling damage is 1d6 per 10 feet fallen, maximum 20d6. A falling creature normally lands Prone unless an explicit effect says otherwise. When Flight Slot depletion causes a fall, the creature may use its Reaction for a DC 12 Dexterity save. Success halves fall damage; failure or no Reaction takes full damage. Controlled Descent changes a successful Emergency Landing to 0 fall damage according to that feat. Falling Onto Creatures The lower creature makes a DC 12 Dexterity save. On success it avoids the collision and the falling creature takes normal fall d

Each attack expends 1 shot. Normal Bonus Action Reload restores to 2 shots. Cannot use Quick Shot or Akimbo. Gunslinger ammunition-restoration features can restore Musket shots normally, but never above 2. Standard one-handed firearm capacity increases do not apply. Ranged Weapon Range. The first listed range is the weapon’s Normal Range and the second is its Maximum Range. A target within the weapon’s Normal Range is attacked normally unless another modifier applies. A target beyond Normal Range but within Maximum Range can still be targeted, but the ranged weapon attack is made with Disadvantage. A target beyond Maximum Range cannot be hit and the attack automatically misses. If the target is within 5 feet of the attacker, the ranged weapon attack is made with Disadvantage regardless of which listed range applies. Multiple sources of Disadvantage do not stack. Straight-Line Fire Crossbows, Pistols, and Muskets use Straight-Line. If an allied creature intersects the line between shooter and target, the nearest such ally makes DC 15 Dexterity. On success, the shot proceeds. On failure, the ally is hit and takes normal damage; the original target is not hit. The intercepted hit cannot inherit a Natural-20 critical result rolled against the original target. Resolve multiple possible interceptors nearest first. The same rule applies in 3D aerial lines. Ammunition All fired ammunition is lost. Fired Arrows, Bolts, Pistol Bullets, and Musket Bullets are never recovered. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Legions & Complete Abyss Warfront System Player-created Legions plus the complete player-operable Warfront rules, unit catalogue, War Asset costs, Fortress procedures, and Open Abyss procedures. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Core Rulebook v4.2 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026 , synchronized with Player Handbook v3.10 . This page exposes the complete player-operable Warfront subsystem. Explicitly GM-facing enemy statblocks, hidden force composition, and closed GM-only resolution tables remain off the public player site. Legions Warfront Overview War Assets Unit Statistics Battle Exchange Unit Catalogue Unit Costs PC Participation Fortress Wars Open Abyss Reinforcements Quick Reference PLAYER-CREATED LEGIONS A player-created Legion is a lightweight organization for shared identity, missions, resources, and cross-faction cooperation when the campaign permits it. Legion membership does not create a new character progression track or grant automatic combat bonuses. When a Legion Can Be Founded Campaign Gate. The Campaign Director or controlling GM must explicitly declare Legion Founding available. Reaching Level 11 by itself does not unlock the system. Founding Player. One Founding Player must be Level 11 or higher. That character becomes the initial Legion Leader. Other members. Every other founding or joining member must be Level 3 or higher before joining and must already have reached their Specialization or Archetype choice where applicable. A Level 1-2 character cannot join early. Membership has no maximum size. There is no minimum number of additional founders; a qualifying Founding Player may establish the Legion alone if all other founding requirements are satisfied. Elyos and Asmodians may belong to the same Legion once the required campaign state is active. Every member retains their original faction identity and its normal consequences. Founding Fund and Treasury Founding requires 5,000 Kinah deposited into the new Legion Treasury. Eligible founding members may contribute toward the total. Before establishment, the Founding Fund cannot be withdrawn. If founding is abandoned, each contributor receives their contribution back. Once established, the 5,000 Kinah remains usable Treasury money. Any Legion member may deposit Kinah. Only the Legion Leader may withdraw Kinah or authorize spending. Legion missions may reward participating members, the Treasury, or both as determined by the GM. There is no passive Legion income, automatic salary, interest, business-profit engine, or mandatory recurring membership dues. Leadership and Membership The only default roles are Legion Leader and Legion Member. The Legion Leader admits and removes members, controls permissions for Legion assets, may transfer leadership, and may formally dissolve the Legion. Leadership may be transferred to any existing legal Legion member. The new Leader does not need to be Level 11; Level 11 is a founding requirement only. Member Benefits Members may display the Legion name, colors, crest, and insignia. Ordinary Legion identification occupies no Inventory Slot. Members may accept Legion missions and may use resources, facilities, contacts, and support the Legion actually possesses when the Legion Leader permits it. Where the campaign's cross-faction arrangements recognize the Legion, its insignia provides a legitimate reason for Elyos and Asmodian members to operate together. It does not grant diplomatic immunity or unrestricted access. Legion membership grants no automatic Hit, AC, damage, HP, saving throw, skill, Advantage, Spell DC, DP, class-resource, equipment-quality, or personal Inventory bonus. Legion Storage and Headquarters An established Legion has one secure shared Storage location with a capacity of 100 Inventory Slots. Normal Inventory Slot and stacking rules apply; Kinah remains in the Treasury and uses no Storage Slots. Any Legion member may deposit eligible items. Only the Legion Leader may withdraw items or authorize another member to retrieve them. Legion Storage is stationary and cannot be accessed remotely. It never increases a member's personal Inventory capacity in the field. A Legion may designate one legitimate location as its Headquarters. The Headquarters is simply its meeting place and Storage location; it grants no automatic bonuses and has no upgrade track. Lightweight Rule. There is no Legion XP, Legion Level, officer hierarchy, skill tree, research tree, reputation meter, headquarters progression, or other default Legion management subsystem. Abyss Warfront System Warfronts resolve formation-scale warfare separately from ordinary character-scale combat. They are used for Fortress Wars and Open Abyss Battles. Strategic travel and marching between major engagements are handled narratively, off-table, or during downtime. Shared Warfront Command The player side uses one shared strategic board

Background Rules Soldier Scholar Acolyte Noble Outlander Underworld Artisan Merchant Entertainer Languages Background Rules Skill Selection: Choose exactly 2 Background Skills from the six options listed for your Background. Duplicate selections are prohibited. A Skill selected as a Class Skill cannot also be selected as a Background Skill. The four selected Class and Background Skill Proficiencies must therefore be four different Skills. Background Choose 2 Skills Soldier Athletics, Intimidation, Perception, Survival, Medicine, Religion Scholar Arcana, History, Investigation, Religion, Medicine, Perception Acolyte History, Insight, Medicine, Religion, Athletics, Survival Noble History, Insight, Persuasion, Performance, Investigation, Sleight of Hand Outlander Athletics, Nature, Perception, Survival, Persuasion, Stealth Underworld Deception, Insight, Sleight of Hand, Stealth, Investigation, Persuasion Artisan Investigation, Perception, Sleight of Hand, History, Arcana, Persuasion Merchant Insight, Investigation, Persuasion, History, Stealth, Athletics Entertainer Acrobatics, Deception, Performance, Persuasion, Nature, Animal Handling A relevant Background may establish that you have the experience necessary to attempt obscure or specialized knowledge. It does not automatically grant Advantage, Expertise, a numerical bonus, or guaranteed success. Understanding Your Background Your Class describes what your character has learned to do as an adventuring Daeva. Your Background describes the life, training, profession, upbringing, or experiences that helped shape who they were before the campaign began. Faction tells you where you belong, Background helps explain where you came from, and Class describes how you operate as an adventurer. A Background does not determine your morality, personality, beliefs, faction loyalty, or future choices. Two characters with the same Background may have completely different lives and goals. Mechanically, use the Background table above exactly as written: choose two skills from your Background’s listed skill pool. The entries below add roleplaying context and do not grant additional rules benefits. Soldier What Is a Soldier?. A Soldier has meaningful experience with organized military service: troops, guards, scouts, officers, fortress personnel, or other disciplined fighting forces. Life and Origins. Military life may have included patrols, garrison duty, campaigns, escort work, reconnaissance, fortification defense, or service under a commander. That service may have occurred before or after ascension. Motivations and Outlook. Duty, loyalty, comradeship, ambition, patriotism, protection, regret, or the memory of fallen companions may still shape the character. A Soldier may respect military order, resent it, or be deciding what is truly worth fighting for. Playing a Soldier. Decide what kind of service shaped you, who you served beside, and what relationship you now have with authority and your former comrades. Being a Soldier does not require obedience or a martial Class. Scholar What Is a Scholar?. A Scholar has devoted part of their life to seeking, preserving, interpreting, or teaching knowledge. Scholars include researchers, historians, scribes, teachers, philosophers, archivists, investigators, and field specialists. Life and Origins. Study may have taken place under a teacher, within an archive or institution, or independently. Subjects can include history, geography, creatures, Aether, ruins, cultures, warfare, or any other serious field of inquiry. Motivations and Outlook. A Scholar may adventure to recover lost knowledge, investigate mysteries, study ruins or creatures directly, protect important discoveries, or prevent dangerous knowledge from being misused. Playing a Scholar. Choose the subject that fascinates you and decide whether you are an academic, a practical field researcher, or something between. Being scholarly does not require being socially awkward or confined to books. Acolyte What Is an Acolyte?. An Acolyte has meaningful experience with religious or spiritual service, sacred traditions, temples, ceremonies, or communities of worship. Life and Origins. The character may have been raised around a temple, studied under a religious teacher, volunteered in a sacred institution, maintained holy places, assisted ceremonies, or found faith after a life-changing event. Motivations and Outlook. Faith, service, protection, reform, doubt, duty, spiritual curiosity, or concern for a community may lead an Acolyte into adventure. Vision, Stealth, Traps, Locks & Theft Vision and Light Cover, Line of Sight & Line of Effect Stealth and Infiltration Traps and Non-Aether Hazards Locks Theft and Pickpocket Social Interaction, Information & Captivity Vision, Stealth, Traps, Locks & Theft Vision and Light Light states are Bright Light, Dim Light, and Darkness. Obscuration states are Lightly Obscured and Heavily Obscured. Dim Light lightly obscures; Darkness heavily obscures a creature that cannot otherwise see through it. Daeva Darkvision treats Darkness within 60 feet as Dim Light, not Bright Light. A recommended ordinary light source has a stated Bright radius plus an equal additional Dim radius unless its own text says otherwise. Bright light does not universally prohibit Stealth. Obscurity and Invisibility do not automatically make a creature Hidden. Cover, Line of Sight & Line of Effect No Cover. No defensive benefit from Cover. Half Cover. A creature or object behind meaningful partial obstruction gains +2 AC and +2 to Dexterity saving throws against effects originating from the covered direction. Intervening creatures can provide Half Cover when they materially obstruct the line. Full Cover. Full Cover blocks the relevant Line of Effect and prevents direct targeting through that obstruction unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Three-Quarters Cover does not exist in Wings of Atreia. Cover does not stack; use the best applicable Cover. Altitude neither inherently grants nor ignores Cover. Line of Sight and Line of Effect are distinct. Line of Sight determines whether you can see a target or point. Line of Effect determines whether an attack, spell, or effect can physically reach it. Heavy obscurement is not Cover by itself. Stealth and Infiltration Use scene states Undetected, Suspicious, and Alerted; these are not Conditions. Stealth must exceed Passive Perception; ties favor the observer. An active Search uses the GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation), against the relevant DC or opposing Stealth; ties favor the Searcher where opposed. Do not reroll Stealth every 5 feet; roll again only when circumstances materially change. For group Stealth, at least half the group must succeed. A failed check may create Suspicion rather than immediate full alarm when appropriate. Distractions create an opportunity to Hide rather than automatic success. Disguises are primarily social. Invisibility is not the same as Hidden. Wings do not automatically prevent Stealth. Traps and Non-Aether Hazards Describe a hazard with Trigger, Detection, Avoid/Disable method, Save/Check, Effect, and Reset/Duration. Hazards may be obvious, concealed, or hidden. Detection normally uses Passive Perception, active Perception, or Investigation. Disable methods depend on the mechanism and can use Sleight of Hand, Investigation, Athletics, or another appropriate Skill. There is no mandatory Thieves’ Tools system. Failure triggers the hazard only when the hazard says so. Damage and Conditions use existing universal rules. Forced movement is horizontal unless the hazard explicitly creates vertical displacement. Hazards normally resolve when triggered rather than taking their own Initiative turns. Repeat attempts require changed circumstances. Locks Mechanical Lock DC Simple 10 Standard 12 Secure 15 High Security 18 Exceptional 20+ The correct key opens a normal lock without a check. Mechanical locks generally use Dexterity (Sleight of Hand). Unusual mechanisms can use Intelligence (Investigation). Forcing uses Strength (Athletics); destroying a lock or door uses normal object/destruction adjudication. Failure does not automatically break or trigger a lock unless its design says so. Aether locks use Aether Interaction. If a task is impossible, do not assign an absurd DC—state that it cannot be done by that method. Theft and Pickpocket A theft attempt requires a plausible opportunity. Taking an accessible small item uses Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) against Passive Perception and must exceed it. If the target is actively watching, oppose with active Perception; ties favor the observer. Secured items can require a different approach. Failure may create suspicion or alarm. Success means the theft was unnoticed at that moment; later discovery remains possible. Distraction creates opportunity rather than automatic success. Help can grant +2 when genuinely meaningful. Worn armor, shields, Wings, wielded weapons, and equipped mandatory implements cannot simply be pickpocketed. Repeated attempts require changed circumstances. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Tempo, Firearms, and Reload Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Tradition & Outlook Specialization Reassignment The Gunslinger is a mobile firearm martial whose power comes from maintaining Tempo through successful firearm play. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Fire. Move. Reload. Keep the rhythm alive long enough to turn Tempo into control, defense, and lethal pressure. Class Identity Gunslingers are technist marksmen who turn Aether-assisted firearms into speed, precision, and controlled ranged pressure. Pistols support rapid, mobile sequences through Quick Shot and Akimbo, while Muskets provide deliberate two-handed fire that concentrates Tempo into stronger individual hits through Deliberate Shot. Tempo represents the Gunslinger’s ability to build combat rhythm through successful action rather than treating every shot as an isolated event. Tradition & Outlook Gunslingers belong to Atreia’s newer technological traditions. The wider Aion tradition describes early firearm research being dismissed as technist tinkering until battlefield success forced major institutions to recognize the discipline. Wings of Atreia keeps that identity of innovation earning legitimacy through results while using Pistols and Muskets as the class’s only firearm categories. Gunslingers often value nerve, technical familiarity, accuracy, independence, and adaptability. Appearance & Adventuring Gunslingers favor mobile equipment, ammunition management, firearm maintenance, and a practical awareness of range and firing position. Their weapons can make them look strikingly modern beside older martial traditions, but their discipline remains Aetheric and distinctly Atreian. They adventure to test new techniques, serve as ranged specialists, hunt dangerous targets, protect expeditions from positions others cannot exploit, or demonstrate that innovation has earned its place in the war for Atreia. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols Ranged Gunslinger One-handed Weapon Attack. Range 30/90 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d8 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. A Gunslinger can wield two Pistols, but doing so does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols are compatible with Quick Shot and Akimbo. Muskets Ranged Gunslinger Two-handed Weapon Attack. Range 60/180 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d12 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. Ammunition capacity is fixed at 2. Muskets cannot use Quick Shot or Akimbo. Gunslinger ammunition-restoration features can restore Musket shots normally, but a Musket can never hold more than 2 shots. Standard one-handed firearm capacity increases do not apply to Muskets. Reload Every firearm attack consumes one shot. A firearm with no shots remaining is Empty and cannot make firearm attacks until at least one shot is restored. Normal Bonus Action Reload: an Empty firearm is restored to its full Reload capacity. Ammunition restoration is not the Reload action unless a feature explicitly says so. Ammunition-restoration features can restore shots to either Pistols or Muskets up to that firearm's maximum capacity. A Musket's maximum capacity remains 2. Switching between carried one-handed Gunslinger firearms as part of a firearm attack requires no separate object interaction. Standard one-handed firearm capacity progression: Ammo Capacity 4 at Levels 1-4, Ammo Capacity 5 at 5-8, Ammo Capacity 6 at 9-14, and Ammo Capacity 7 at 15-20. Increasing capacity does not automatically reload an Empty firearm. Tempo Tempo is a genuine-combat resource representing firing rhythm, accuracy, and momentum.
