Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Tempo, Firearms, and Reload Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Tradition & Outlook Specialization Reassignment The Gunslinger is a mobile firearm martial whose power comes from maintaining Tempo through successful firearm play. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Fire. Move. Reload. Keep the rhythm alive long enough to turn Tempo into control, defense, and lethal pressure. Class Identity Gunslingers are technist marksmen who turn Aether-assisted firearms into speed, precision, and controlled ranged pressure. Pistols support rapid, mobile sequences through Quick Shot and Akimbo, while Muskets provide deliberate two-handed fire that concentrates Tempo into stronger individual hits through Deliberate Shot. Tempo represents the Gunslinger’s ability to build combat rhythm through successful action rather than treating every shot as an isolated event. Tradition & Outlook Gunslingers belong to Atreia’s newer technological traditions. The wider Aion tradition describes early firearm research being dismissed as technist tinkering until battlefield success forced major institutions to recognize the discipline. Wings of Atreia keeps that identity of innovation earning legitimacy through results while using Pistols and Muskets as the class’s only firearm categories. Gunslingers often value nerve, technical familiarity, accuracy, independence, and adaptability. Appearance & Adventuring Gunslingers favor mobile equipment, ammunition management, firearm maintenance, and a practical awareness of range and firing position. Their weapons can make them look strikingly modern beside older martial traditions, but their discipline remains Aetheric and distinctly Atreian. They adventure to test new techniques, serve as ranged specialists, hunt dangerous targets, protect expeditions from positions others cannot exploit, or demonstrate that innovation has earned its place in the war for Atreia. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols Ranged Gunslinger One-handed Weapon Attack. Range 30/90 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d8 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. A Gunslinger can wield two Pistols, but doing so does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols are compatible with Quick Shot and Akimbo. Muskets Ranged Gunslinger Two-handed Weapon Attack. Range 60/180 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d12 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. Ammunition capacity is fixed at 2. Muskets cannot use Quick Shot or Akimbo. Gunslinger ammunition-restoration features can restore Musket shots normally, but a Musket can never hold more than 2 shots. Standard one-handed firearm capacity increases do not apply to Muskets. Reload Every firearm attack consumes one shot. A firearm with no shots remaining is Empty and cannot make firearm attacks until at least one shot is restored. Normal Bonus Action Reload: an Empty firearm is restored to its full Reload capacity. Ammunition restoration is not the Reload action unless a feature explicitly says so. Ammunition-restoration features can restore shots to either Pistols or Muskets up to that firearm's maximum capacity. A Musket's maximum capacity remains 2. Switching between carried one-handed Gunslinger firearms as part of a firearm attack requires no separate object interaction. Increasing capacity does not automatically reload an Empty firearm. Tempo Tempo is a genuine-combat resource representing firing rhythm, accuracy, and momentum. It begins at 0, resets to 0 when combat ends, and artificial initiative cannot generate it. Maximum Tempo: Levels 1-4 = 3; 5-8 = 4; 9-12 = 5; 13-16 = 6; 17-20 = 7. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Vision, Stealth, Traps, Locks & Theft Vision and Light Cover, Line of Sight & Line of Effect Stealth and Infiltration Traps and Non-Aether Hazards Locks Theft and Pickpocket Social Interaction, Information & Captivity Vision, Stealth, Traps, Locks & Theft Vision and Light Light states are Bright Light, Dim Light, and Darkness. Obscuration states are Lightly Obscured and Heavily Obscured. Dim Light lightly obscures; Darkness heavily obscures a creature that cannot otherwise see through it. Daeva Darkvision treats Darkness within 60 feet as Dim Light, not Bright Light. A recommended ordinary light source has a stated Bright radius plus an equal additional Dim radius unless its own text says otherwise. Bright light does not universally prohibit Stealth. Obscurity and Invisibility do not automatically make a creature Hidden. Cover, Line of Sight & Line of Effect No Cover. No defensive benefit from Cover. Half Cover. A creature or object behind meaningful partial obstruction gains +2 AC and +2 to Dexterity saving throws against effects originating from the covered direction. Intervening creatures can provide Half Cover when they materially obstruct the line. Full Cover. Full Cover blocks the relevant Line of Effect and prevents direct targeting through that obstruction unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Three-Quarters Cover does not exist in Wings of Atreia. Cover does not stack; use the best applicable Cover. Altitude neither inherently grants nor ignores Cover. Line of Sight and Line of Effect are distinct. Line of Sight determines whether you can see a target or point. Line of Effect determines whether an attack, spell, or effect can physically reach it. Heavy obscurement is not Cover by itself. Stealth and Infiltration Use scene states Undetected, Suspicious, and Alerted; these are not Conditions. Stealth must exceed Passive Perception; ties favor the observer. An active Search uses the GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation), against the relevant DC or opposing Stealth; ties favor the Searcher where opposed. Do not reroll Stealth every 5 feet; roll again only when circumstances materially change. For group Stealth, at least half the group must succeed. A failed check may create Suspicion rather than immediate full alarm when appropriate. Distractions create an opportunity to Hide rather than automatic success. Disguises are primarily social. Invisibility is not the same as Hidden. Wings do not automatically prevent Stealth. Traps and Non-Aether Hazards Describe a hazard with Trigger, Detection, Avoid/Disable method, Save/Check, Effect, and Reset/Duration. Hazards may be obvious, concealed, or hidden. Detection normally uses Passive Perception, active Perception, or Investigation. Disable methods depend on the mechanism and can use Sleight of Hand, Investigation, Athletics, or another appropriate Skill. There is no mandatory Thieves’ Tools system. Failure triggers the hazard only when the hazard says so. Damage and Conditions use existing universal rules. Forced movement is horizontal unless the hazard explicitly creates vertical displacement. Hazards normally resolve when triggered rather than taking their own Initiative turns. Repeat attempts require changed circumstances. Locks Mechanical Lock DC Simple 10 Standard 12 Secure 15 High Security 18 Exceptional 20+ The correct key opens a normal lock without a check. Mechanical locks generally use Dexterity (Sleight of Hand). Unusual mechanisms can use Intelligence (Investigation). Forcing uses Strength (Athletics); destroying a lock or door uses normal object/destruction adjudication. Failure does not automatically break or trigger a lock unless its design says so. Aether locks use Aether Interaction. If a task is impossible, do not assign an absurd DC—state that it cannot be done by that method. Theft and Pickpocket A theft attempt requires a plausible opportunity. Taking an accessible small item uses Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) against Passive Perception and must exceed it. If the target is actively watching, oppose with active Perception; ties favor the observer. Secured items can require a different approach. Failure may create suspicion or alarm. Success means the theft was unnoticed at that moment; later discovery remains possible. Distraction creates opportunity rather than automatic success. Help can grant +2 when genuinely meaningful. Worn armor, shields, Wings, wielded weapons, and equipped mandatory implements cannot simply be pickpocketed. Repeated attempts require changed circumstances. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Legions & Complete Abyss Warfront System Player-created Legions plus the complete player-operable Warfront rules, unit catalogue, War Asset costs, Fortress procedures, and Open Abyss procedures. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Core Rulebook v4.2 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026 , synchronized with Player Handbook v3.10 . This page exposes the complete player-operable Warfront subsystem. Explicitly GM-facing enemy statblocks, hidden force composition, and closed GM-only resolution tables remain off the public player site. Legions Warfront Overview War Assets Unit Statistics Battle Exchange Unit Catalogue Unit Costs PC Participation Fortress Wars Open Abyss Reinforcements Quick Reference PLAYER-CREATED LEGIONS A player-created Legion is a lightweight organization for shared identity, missions, resources, and cross-faction cooperation when the campaign permits it. Legion membership does not create a new character progression track or grant automatic combat bonuses. When a Legion Can Be Founded Campaign Gate. The Campaign Director or controlling GM must explicitly declare Legion Founding available. Reaching Level 11 by itself does not unlock the system. Founding Player. One Founding Player must be Level 11 or higher. That character becomes the initial Legion Leader. Other members. Every other founding or joining member must be Level 3 or higher before joining and must already have reached their Specialization or Archetype choice where applicable. A Level 1-2 character cannot join early. Membership has no maximum size. There is no minimum number of additional founders; a qualifying Founding Player may establish the Legion alone if all other founding requirements are satisfied. Elyos and Asmodians may belong to the same Legion once the required campaign state is active. Every member retains their original faction identity and its normal consequences. Founding Fund and Treasury Founding requires 5,000 Kinah deposited into the new Legion Treasury. Eligible founding members may contribute toward the total. Before establishment, the Founding Fund cannot be withdrawn. If founding is abandoned, each contributor receives their contribution back. Once established, the 5,000 Kinah remains usable Treasury money. Any Legion member may deposit Kinah. Only the Legion Leader may withdraw Kinah or authorize spending. Legion missions may reward participating members, the Treasury, or both as determined by the GM. There is no passive Legion income, automatic salary, interest, business-profit engine, or mandatory recurring membership dues. Leadership and Membership The only default roles are Legion Leader and Legion Member. The Legion Leader admits and removes members, controls permissions for Legion assets, may transfer leadership, and may formally dissolve the Legion. Leadership may be transferred to any existing legal Legion member. The new Leader does not need to be Level 11; Level 11 is a founding requirement only. Member Benefits Members may display the Legion name, colors, crest, and insignia. Ordinary Legion identification occupies no Inventory Slot. Members may accept Legion missions and may use resources, facilities, contacts, and support the Legion actually possesses when the Legion Leader permits it. Where the campaign's cross-faction arrangements recognize the Legion, its insignia provides a legitimate reason for Elyos and Asmodian members to operate together. It does not grant diplomatic immunity or unrestricted access. Legion membership grants no automatic Hit, AC, damage, HP, saving throw, skill, Advantage, Spell DC, DP, class-resource, equipment-quality, or personal Inventory bonus. Legion Storage and Headquarters An established Legion has one secure shared Storage location with a capacity of 100 Inventory Slots. Normal Inventory Slot and stacking rules apply; Kinah remains in the Treasury and uses no Storage Slots. Any Legion member may deposit eligible items. Only the Legion Leader may withdraw items or authorize another member to retrieve them. Legion Storage is stationary and cannot be accessed remotely. It never increases a member's personal Inventory capacity in the field. A Legion may designate one legitimate location as its Headquarters. The Headquarters is simply its meeting place and Storage location; it grants no automatic bonuses and has no upgrade track. Lightweight Rule. There is no Legion XP, Legion Level, officer hierarchy, skill tree, research tree, reputation meter, headquarters progression, or other default Legion management subsystem. Abyss Warfront System Warfronts resolve formation-scale warfare separately from ordinary character-scale combat. They are used for Fortress Wars and Open Abyss Battles. title: Player FAQ | Wings of Atreia
desc: Player-safe Wings of Atreia FAQ covering the rules most likely to be misread or confused with other d20 games.
text: WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player FAQ A player-safe reference for Wings of Atreia rules that are easy to misread by habit or commonly need clarification at the table. Authority. The FAQ explains the rules; it does not replace them. When a FAQ answer and the current governing rule differ, use the current Player Handbook/Core Rulebook and later explicitly approved synchronized rulings. This website version incorporates the current Ultimate miss procedure and the approved Spell Advancement clarification. Character Combat Spellcasting DP & Ultimates Flight Equipment Warfronts Classes Character Creation & Advancement Do I choose a race or species? No. Every standard player character is a Daeva . Choose Elyos or Asmodian as faction/culture. The two factions use the same universal Daeva mechanical foundation. How do I assign Ability Scores? Assign 16, 14, 14, 12, 10, and 8 freely among STR, DEX, CON, INT, WIS, and CHA. There is no ability-score rolling or point buy. Can I multiclass? No. A Daeva advances in one class from Level 1 through Level 20. Do characters gain XP? No. Advancement is Milestone only . The GM awards levels for meaningful campaign progress. When do I choose an ASI or Feat? Universal ASI/Feat choices occur at Levels 4, 8, 12, and 16 . Level 19 grants an Empyrean Boon , not another normal ASI/Feat choice. What does a Background give me? A Background gives exactly two Skill Proficiencies chosen from that Background's eligible skill list and can establish narrative relevance or permission where appropriate. It does not automatically grant Advantage, Expertise, or guaranteed success. Does duplicate proficiency become Expertise? No. Proficiency adds PB once. Expertise exists only when an explicit feature grants it. Can I change my Specialization after choosing it? Yes, but only at the normal reassignment checkpoints. Choose your initial Specialization at Level 3 . When gaining Level 6, Level 10, and Level 14 , you may either continue your current Specialization or switch to another Specialization available to your class. The Level 14 decision is the final normal Specialization choice through Level 20. If I switch Specializations, do I keep features from my old path? No. Remove every feature granted by the previous Specialization and replace it with the new Specialization's complete feature package through the current checkpoint. Features from different paths cannot be mixed or retained. Make any choices required by newly gained features, and remove, reselect, or recalculate path-dependent options, capacities, and maxima as necessary. Reassignment itself restores no HP or class resources, and current values cannot remain above a new maximum. Can I change Specialization during downtime or by training? No. Normal reassignment happens only while gaining Level 6, 10, or 14. Rest, downtime, training, ordinary retraining, or time between adventures does not create an extra reassignment opportunity. d20 Tests, Actions & Combat Are natural 1 and natural 20 automatic on every d20 Test? No. Ability Checks and Saving Throws compare the final total to the DC. Attack rolls keep their explicit natural-1 automatic miss and natural-20 automatic hit/critical rules. How does Help work? A meaningful helper gives +2 to one Ability Check . Help does not grant Advantage. There is no Assist Attack, and Help does not modify Death Saves. Can Grapple or Shove replace one attack from Extra Attack? No. Grapple and Shove are each a full Action . How do I stand from Prone? Standing from Prone requires your full Action and consumes no movement. Does flanking automatically grant Advantage? No. Wings of Atreia has no universal Flanking rule and no universal Facing rule. Is there a Surprise Round? No. In a genuine ambush, the GM may allow one appropriate pre-Initiative attack. That is discretionary and is not an extra round. How is 3D distance measured? When horizontal and vertical separation both matter, use the greater of the two distances rather than adding them. Does taking damage at 0 HP automatically add failed Death Saves? No. Ordinary damage while already at 0 HP does not alter the Death Save track. A natural 1 on a Death Save is exactly one failure. Spellcasting Does Wings of Atreia use spell slots or cantrips? No. There are no spell slots and no cantrip category. Each spell has its own frequency: At-Will, Cooldown, Short Rest, or Long Rest. Does ordinary damage force a Concentration save? No. Ordinary damage does not test Concentration. Concentration ends only according to the Wings of Atreia Concentration rules and explicit effects. Can I buy, copy, or learn spells from scrolls? Not as a universal rule. Spells are class-granted and unlock through class progression and their printed prerequisites. Does every Spell Advancement make the spell mechanically stronger? No. One Spell Advancement raises one eligible unlocked spell by exactly +1 Spell Level . A Spell Level is not automatically a mechanical improvement breakpoint. If the new Spell Level is not listed in that spell's Spell-Level Scaling or Milestone Improvements , record the higher Spell Level normally but do not change damage, healing, range, area, duration, riders, or any other effect. Do not invent compensation. The progression-only Spell Level remains valid permanent progression, may satisfy prerequisites, and counts toward the next listed improvement. Can I skip an unexciting Spell Level and jump to the next improvement? No. Each Spell Advancement increases the selected eligible spell by exactly one Spell Level. Progression-only levels are still real levels. Does casting a Bonus Action spell prevent me from casting another spell that turn? No universal D&D-style Bonus Action spell restriction exists. Follow the actual Action/Bonus Action timing and the individual spell text. Daeva Points & Ultimates When do I gain Daeva Points and unlock my Ultimate? Beginning at Level 10 , eligible Daevas can earn DP from genuine combat. Maximum DP is 100. At 100 DP, the class Ultimate is ready. Does only the character who lands the killing blow gain DP? No. Eligible Level 10+ Daevas who meaningfully participated receive the full qualifying post-combat DP award; it is not divided by killing blows. What happens when my Ultimate attack misses? After the miss is confirmed, the player chooses one of two final resolutions: Release the Power: spend all 100 DP and resolve one-half, rounded down, of the Ultimate's fixed primary damage plus one-half of any direct Ultimate healing, restoration, or repair amount that would have occurred on a hit. Normal weapon/Bastion damage, area or secondary-target damage, temporary HP/protection, forced movement, conditions/status effects, condition removal, and other riders do not occur. There is no next-dawn lockout . Hold the Power: resolve no Ultimate effect, retain all 100 DP, and that Ultimate cannot be attempted again until the next dawn. Rests and Aetheric Reconstitution do not end the lockout early. Ultimate Recovery occurs after either choice. What happens after an Ultimate attempt? Your next turn is an Ultimate Recovery turn whether the Ultimate hit, used Release the Power, or used Hold the Power. During that turn you cannot make weapon or spell attacks, deal damage, restore HP, or impose hostile conditions/status effects. You may still use legal movement, defensive, utility, environmental, and non-healing aid options. Reactions remain available, including Opportunity Attacks. Recovery ends at the end of that turn. Does a critical hit increase an Ultimate's fixed output? No. Fixed Ultimate output is not increased by the critical hit. Only rolled normal weapon/Bastion damage dice double when applicable. Can resting, equipment, consumables, or class features restore DP? No. DP persists through rests and Aetheric Reconstitution but is not restored by those systems. DP cannot exceed 100, be transferred, or have the 100-DP Ultimate cost reduced. Flight Are Wings just cosmetic? No. Every Daeva has functional Wings and uses the dedicated exploration-flight and Combat Flight Slot systems. Does higher altitude automatically grant Advantage? No. Use only explicit aerial rules such as Descending Attack, Exposed Wings, altitude, range, and cover interactions. Equipment, Professions & Economy Does armor inherently give Stealth Advantage or Disadvantage? No. Armor creates no inherent Stealth Advantage or Disadvantage unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Is there a universal magic-item attunement limit? No universal attunement-slot subsystem exists. Can Professions craft complete weapons and armor from nothing? No. Weaponsmithing, Armorcrafting, and Handicrafting are primarily upgrade professions under the approved equipment ladder rather than a general manufacture-from-nothing system. How many Professions can be Active? One Profession is Active at a time. Changing the Active Profession occurs only on level-up. Ranks and prior progress in inactive Professions are retained. Legions & Warfronts Do I use my ordinary AC, damage dice, spells, and class resources directly as Warfront stats? No. Warfront scale is intentionally separate. Use the Warfront rules unless an effect explicitly says it transfers across scales. What are a PC's Warfront values? A participating PC uses ATK 3 while attacking and DEF 3 while defending . PCs are not Units, have no Tier or END, and cost no WA. Can I gain or spend DP or use my Ultimate during a Warfront? No. DP and Ultimates are inaccessible for the entire Warfront operation, including embedded character-scale missions. Existing DP is retained until the operation ends. Can PCs capture Warfront objectives by themselves? No. Objective and grid control follows the Unit rules. PCs do not independently capture Warfront objectives. When are player-created Legions available? Player-created Legions are campaign-gated organizational content. At least one founder must meet the required Level threshold, and the GM must confirm that the campaign has reached the required public state. Reaching the Level threshold by itself does not unlock or reveal hidden campaign information. Class Rules Can I preload class resources by staging fake combat? No. Class resources are generated only by their explicit triggers. Fake Initiative, harmless staged attacks, allies, environmental tricks, unrelated consumables, or manufactured pseudo-combat do not create resources unless a rule explicitly says they do. Does every party need a Templar and Cleric? No. Wings of Atreia does not require an MMO-style tank/healer/DPS composition. Different classes make different problems easier, but legal party composition is not defined by MMO raid roles. Does an Aethertech permanently lose the Bastion if it reaches 0 HP? No. Use the current Aethertech Bastion recovery/redeployment procedure on the Aethertech class page. A disabled Bastion is not a permanent loss of the class chassis. Need the governing rule? Use this FAQ to identify the issue, then open the corresponding Core Rules page , class page , or spell page for the full operative text. ← Back to Rules Wings of Atreia · Created & Designed by Clark Michael Zafra (“ArchQwynn”) · Non-commercial fan project.

text: WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Quick Reference Character creation, level-up, actions, conditions, feats, boons, flight, inventory, Aether enhancement, and class-resource quick tables. Source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page is a player-facing reference extracted from the handbook rather than a replacement ruleset. Character Creation Level Up Actions Conditions Feats Boons Flight Inventory Aether Enhancement Class Resources Appendix A — Character Creation Checklist □ Choose Elyos or Asmodian. □ Choose one of the 11 classes. □ Assign 16, 14, 14, 12, 10, 8 among STR, DEX, CON, INT, WIS and CHA. □ Choose one Background. □ Record class saving throws, armor, shield and weapon access. □ Choose exactly 2 Class Skills from the six Skill options listed for your Class and exactly 2 Background Skills from the six Skill options listed for your Background. Duplicate selections are prohibited. □ Calculate HP, AC, Initiative, class Save DC, Speed and Passive Perception. □ Record the fixed class starting weapon/implement, armor, Common Wings, and starting Kinah (500 + 250 per level above 1). □ Choose name, appearance, wing appearance, personality, history, relationships and motivation. Appendix B — Level-Up Checklist Specialization Reassignment: Choose the initial path at Level 3. When gaining Levels 6, 10, and 14, either continue that path or switch to another class Specialization. Switching removes the previous path's entire feature package and replaces it with the new path's complete package through the current checkpoint. Recalculate path-dependent choices and maxima as required; reassignment restores no HP or resources. Level 14 is the final normal choice. □ Read the full new class-level entry and specialization text. □ Apply fixed HP gain + CON + class durability. □ Update PB if needed. □ Update class resource caps/dice/ranges/chassis. □ Make ASI/Feat choice if granted. □ Choose Empyrean Boon at Level 19. □ Apply Spell Advancements if granted. □ Update Flight Slots, Exploration Flight and Inventory. □ Recalculate DCs, spell attacks, AC and passive values. □ At Level 10, add the Daeva Point tracker and class Ultimate; use the improved values at Levels 15 and 20. Appendix C — Universal Action Reference Action Cost What It Does Attack Action Make one attack unless Extra Attack or an explicit feature changes the number. Dash Action Gain additional movement equal to current Speed for the turn; movement costs still apply. While flying, no extra altitude-layer change. Disengage Action Until end of your turn, your movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks. Dodge Action Until start of your next turn, attacks against you have Disadvantage if you perceive the attacker; you have Advantage on DEX saves. Ends if Incapacitated or Speed 0. Help Action +2 to one meaningful Ability Check; no Advantage; cannot Assist Attack or Death Saves. Hide Action Require meaningful concealment; DEX (Stealth) vs Passive/active Perception. Cannot Hide while clearly seen. Hidden is not Invisible; an attack reveals position after it resolves. Ready Action + later Reaction Prepare one Action for a perceivable trigger; release with Reaction. Search Action when structured timing matters Use the GM-selected check, commonly WIS (Perception) or INT (Investigation), against the relevant DC or Stealth. Use Object Action when substantial manipulation is required Substantial manipulation beyond the free simple object interaction; a specific item’s activation rule controls if it states another cost. Grapple Action Full Action; target in reach and no more than one Size larger; STR (Athletics) vs target STR (Athletics) or DEX (Acrobatics). Escape uses Action. Dragging normally costs 2:1. Shove Action Full Action; same contest and Size/reach limits as Grapple. On success push 5 ft or knock Prone. Stand from Prone Action Full Action; does not consume movement. Equip / Remove Shield Action Full Action. Appendix D — Conditions Fourteen universal Conditions: Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Frightened, Grappled, Incapacitated, Invisible, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained, Stunned, Unconscious. Hidden is not a Condition. Condition Player-Facing Effect Blinded A Blinded creature cannot see and automatically fails Ability Checks that require sight. Attack rolls against it have Advantage, and its attack rolls have Disadvantage. It can still move normally unless another rule limits its movement, and Blinded does not inherently cause an airborne creature to fall. Charmed A Charmed creature cannot willingly attack, damage, or directly target its charmer with a harmful ability or effect. The charmer has Advantage on appropriate social Ability Checks directed at the Charmed creature. Charmed is not total mind control: it does not create automatic obedience, betrayal, disclosure of secrets, or suicidal behavior. Deafened A Deafened creature cannot hear and automatically fails Ability Checks that require hearing. Deafened creates no generic combat penalty by itself, but the creature cannot benefit from an effect that explicitly requires it to hear the source unless that effect says otherwise. Frightened While the source of its fear is within Line of Sight, a Frightened creature has Disadvantage on Ability Checks and attack rolls and cannot willingly move closer to that source. Frightened imposes no general saving-throw penalty. An airborne Frightened creature may remain airborne and may move sideways or away from the source subject to normal flight rules. Grappled A Grappled creature’s Speed becomes 0. The condition ends if the grappler becomes Incapacitated, the target is moved outside the grappler’s reach, or an explicit effect ends the Grapple. The Grappled creature may use its Action to attempt the approved escape contest. Grappled does not inherently cause Prone or falling; airborne movement follows the normal grappling and forced-movement rules. Incapacitated An Incapacitated creature cannot take Actions, Bonus Actions, or Reactions and cannot maintain Concentration. Incapacitated does not itself reduce Speed to 0, cause Prone, or cause an airborne creature to fall. Invisible An Invisible creature cannot normally be seen without a special sense or revealing effect. Attack rolls against it have Disadvantage and its attack rolls have Advantage when the opposing creature cannot otherwise perceive it, subject to the normal unseen-attacker and unseen-target rules. Invisible is not automatically Hidden; sound, footprints, disturbances, and other evidence can still reveal its location. Paralyzed A Paralyzed creature is Incapacitated, its Speed is 0, and it cannot move or speak. It automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saving throws, and attack rolls against it have Advantage. Paralyzed does not cause automatic Critical Hits. If unsupported, the creature becomes Prone; an unsupported airborne Paralyzed creature therefore falls. Petrified A Petrified creature and its carried nonmagical equipment are transformed into inert solid substance. The creature is Incapacitated, its Speed is 0, it is unaware of its surroundings, it automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saving throws, and attack rolls against it have Advantage. It has Resistance to all damage and does not age or require food, water, air, or sleep while Petrified. An airborne Petrified creature becomes Prone and falls. Poisoned A Poisoned creature has Disadvantage on attack rolls and Ability Checks. Poisoned causes no automatic damage unless the effect that imposed it says otherwise. Prone A Prone creature can move only by Crawling unless it stands. Standing from Prone requires a full Action and consumes no movement. Attack rolls against the Prone creature have Advantage when the attacker is within 5 feet and Disadvantage when the attacker is farther than 5 feet. An unsupported airborne creature that becomes Prone immediately falls. Restrained A Restrained creature’s Speed is 0. Attack rolls against it have Advantage, its attack rolls have Disadvantage, and it has Disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws. Restrained does not automatically cause falling; an airborne Daeva hovers while it can otherwise maintain flight and has Flight Slots as required. Stunned A Stunned creature is Incapacitated, its Speed is 0, and it can speak only falteringly. It automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saving throws, and attack rolls against it have Advantage. Stunned does not inherently cause Prone or falling; an airborne Daeva hovers while it can otherwise maintain flight and has Flight Slots as required. Unconscious An Unconscious creature is Incapacitated, its Speed is 0, and it is unaware of its surroundings. It drops unsecured actively held items, automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saving throws, and attack rolls against it have Advantage. It becomes Prone unless physically supported; an unsupported airborne Unconscious creature therefore falls. Unconscious does not cause automatic Critical Hits. When Unconscious because it is Dying at 0 HP, the Dying rules govern damage and Death Saving Throws. Airborne Reminder. Prone is the universal condition that causes an unsupported airborne creature to fall. Unconscious leads to Prone. Other Conditions do not automatically cause falling unless their text creates Prone or explicitly ends flight. Airborne Reminder. Prone is the universal condition that causes an unsupported airborne creature to fall. Unconscious leads to Prone. Other Conditions do not automatically cause falling unless their text creates Prone or explicitly ends flight. Appendix E — Feats Feat Quick Benefit Alert +2 Initiative. You cannot be Surprised while conscious. Skilled Gain proficiency in two Skills. Duplicate proficiency must be replaced with another choice. Expertise Double PB contribution for one proficient Skill. Doubling effects do not stack. Keen Senses +2 passive Perception and passive Investigation. Active checks unchanged. Mobile Walking Speed +10 ft. Dash ignores extra cost of Difficult Terrain for that turn. Does not increase Flight. Sure-Footed Advantage on checks/saves specifically to resist being knocked Prone by terrain, hazards or forced movement. Weapon Specialist Choose one weapon. Once per turn before an attack roll with it, you may gain +2 to that attack roll. Tough HP maximum increases by 2 × character level when selected, then +2 each later level. Resilient Choose a saving throw you lack proficiency in; gain proficiency. Aerial Endurance +2 maximum Flight Slot. Controlled Descent Successful DC 12 DEX Emergency Landing save causes 0 falling damage instead of half. Master Glider Exploration Glide ratio improves 3:1 → 4:1. 1-hour cooldown remains. Aerial Conditioning First grounded Flight Slot recovery after becoming airborne restores 2 instead of 1; reset by becoming airborne again. Aether Adept Choose Arcana or Sleight of Hand; gain proficiency if needed. 1/Long Rest reroll a failed Aether Interaction check using it. Aether Stabilizer 1/Long Rest after failing a qualifying Arcana/Sleight of Hand stabilization/suppression/deactivation/repair check, add 1d6 to the failed check. Appendix F — Empyrean Boons Boon Quick Benefit Transcendence Increase one Ability Score by 2; chosen score may reach 22. The Unbroken When qualifying damage would reduce you to 0 HP without outright killing you, remain at 1 HP. The Relentless +2d8 damage from one attack or qualifying class feature; bonus dice do not double on Critical Hit. The Unbound Sky +1 maximum Flight Slot and grounded combat Flight Slot recovery becomes +2 per round; never bypasses Aether/flight restrictions. Aetheric Mastery Aether-focused Arcana/Sleight of Hand access, +2 on Aether Interaction checks, and basic awareness of current Aether State. Fate After failing a saving throw, reroll and use the new result. Cannot reroll a Death Saving Throw. Appendix G — Flight Level Slots Explora

WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Legions & Complete Abyss Warfront System Player-created Legions plus the complete player-operable Warfront rules, unit catalogue, War Asset costs, Fortress procedures, and Open Abyss procedures. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Core Rulebook v4.2 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026 , synchronized with Player Handbook v3.10 . This page exposes the complete player-operable Warfront subsystem. Explicitly GM-facing enemy statblocks, hidden force composition, and closed GM-only resolution tables remain off the public player site. Legions Warfront Overview War Assets Unit Statistics Battle Exchange Unit Catalogue Unit Costs PC Participation Fortress Wars Open Abyss Reinforcements Quick Reference PLAYER-CREATED LEGIONS A player-created Legion is a lightweight organization for shared identity, missions, resources, and cross-faction cooperation when the campaign permits it. Legion membership does not create a new character progression track or grant automatic combat bonuses. When a Legion Can Be Founded Campaign Gate. The Campaign Director or controlling GM must explicitly declare Legion Founding available. Reaching Level 11 by itself does not unlock the system. Founding Player. One Founding Player must be Level 11 or higher. That character becomes the initial Legion Leader. Other members. Every other founding or joining member must be Level 3 or higher before joining and must already have reached their Specialization or Archetype choice where applicable. A Level 1-2 character cannot join early. Membership has no maximum size. There is no minimum number of additional founders; a qualifying Founding Player may establish the Legion alone if all other founding requirements are satisfied. Elyos and Asmodians may belong to the same Legion once the required campaign state is active. Every member retains their original faction identity and its normal consequences. Founding Fund and Treasury Founding requires 5,000 Kinah deposited into the new Legion Treasury. Eligible founding members may contribute toward the total. Before establishment, the Founding Fund cannot be withdrawn. If founding is abandoned, each contributor receives their contribution back. Once established, the 5,000 Kinah remains usable Treasury money. Any Legion member may deposit Kinah. Only the Legion Leader may withdraw Kinah or authorize spending. Legion missions may reward participating members, the Treasury, or both as determined by the GM. There is no passive Legion income, automatic salary, interest, business-profit engine, or mandatory recurring membership dues. Leadership and Membership The only default roles are Legion Leader and Legion Member. The Legion Leader admits and removes members, controls permissions for Legion assets, may transfer leadership, and may formally dissolve the Legion. Leadership may be transferred to any existing legal Legion member. The new Leader does not need to be Level 11; Level 11 is a founding requirement only. Member Benefits Members may display the Legion name, colors, crest, and insignia. Ordinary Legion identification occupies no Inventory Slot. Members may accept Legion missions and may use resources, facilities, contacts, and support the Legion actually possesses when the Legion Leader permits it. Where the campaign's cross-faction arrangements recognize the Legion, its insignia provides a legitimate reason for Elyos and Asmodian members to operate together. It does not grant diplomatic immunity or unrestricted access. Legion membership grants no automatic Hit, AC, damage, HP, saving throw, skill, Advantage, Spell DC, DP, class-resource, equipment-quality, or personal Inventory bonus. Legion Storage and Headquarters An established Legion has one secure shared Storage location with a capacity of 100 Inventory Slots. Normal Inventory Slot and stacking rules apply; Kinah remains in the Treasury and uses no Storage Slots. Any Legion member may deposit eligible items. Only the Legion Leader may withdraw items or authorize another member to retrieve them. Legion Storage is stationary and cannot be accessed remotely. It never increases a member's personal Inventory capacity in the field. A Legion may designate one legitimate location as its Headquarters. The Headquarters is simply its meeting place and Storage location; it grants no automatic bonuses and has no upgrade track. Lightweight Rule. There is no Legion XP, Legion Level, officer hierarchy, skill tree, research tree, reputation meter, headquarters progression, or other default Legion management subsystem. Abyss Warfront System Warfronts resolve formation-scale warfare separately from ordinary character-scale combat. They are used for Fortress Wars and Open Abyss Battles. Strategic travel and marching between major engagements are handled narratively, off-table, or during downtime. Shared Warfront Command The player side uses one shared strategi

WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Combat Turn structure, actions, movement, attacks, damage, conditions, death, rests, and survival. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative Round and Turn Action Economy Attack Action Universal Actions Ready Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative, rounds, and combat-only resources are used only for genuine combat or another situation where structured turn order is necessary. Characters cannot manufacture artificial combat to farm cooldowns, resources, or timing triggers. Initiative Initiative = 1d20 + Dexterity modifier. Do not add PB unless an explicit feature says so. Alert adds +2 Initiative. There is no Surprise Round and Surprise does not grant Advantage on Initiative. When one side genuinely catches another side unaware, the GM may, at discretion, allow one appropriate pre-Initiative attack roll against the target's normal defense before Initiative is rolled. This is not an extra round, is not automatic, and does not create a general Surprise action economy. After that resolution, roll Initiative normally. Round and Turn One combat round represents approximately six seconds in the game world. Each participant normally takes one turn in Initiative order. All turns in the round abstract actions occurring within the same six-second span; do not add each turn as another six seconds. Action Economy Action. One per turn. Movement. Up to the creature’s available movement, subject to terrain and conditions. Bonus Action. Up to one, but only when a feature grants something that uses a Bonus Action. Reaction. Normally one per round, refreshing at the start of the creature’s turn unless an explicit class rule says otherwise. Object interaction. One free simple object interaction per turn. There is no universal Action-to-Bonus-Action or Bonus-Action-to-Action conversion. Unused movement or Actions are not stored for later turns. Attack Action The Attack Action makes one attack unless a feature such as Extra Attack says otherwise. Grapple and Shove are full Actions and do not replace one attack within Extra Attack. Player Weapon Requirement. A player character must be wielding an approved class weapon to take the normal Attack Action. Unarmed Attacks and Improvised Weapons are not player combat options unless a later explicit feature creates a specific exception. Opportunity Attacks. Opportunity Attacks remain part of the core combat rules. When a hostile creature you can perceive voluntarily leaves your melee reach, you may use your Reaction to make one melee attack against it, resolving the attack before it leaves that reach. Forced movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Universal Actions Dash. Gain additional movement equal to your current Speed for the turn. Difficult Terrain and other movement costs still apply. While flying, Dash adds horizontal movement but does not grant an additional altitude-layer change. Disengage. Until the end of your turn, your movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks. Dodge. Until the start of your next turn, attacks against you have Disadvantage if you can perceive the attacker, and you have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws. Dodge ends if you become Incapacitated or your Speed becomes 0. Hide. You must have meaningful concealment or another circumstance that allows hiding. Make Dexterity (Stealth) against Passive Perception or active Perception as appropriate. You cannot Hide while clearly seen. Hidden is not Invisible. Making an attack reveals your position after that attack resolves. Search. Deliberately search using a GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation). Use Object. Use this Action for substantial manipulation beyond the one free simple object interaction. A specific item’s activation rule controls when it states another cost. Ready A creature can prepare one Action for a perceivable trigger. When the trigger occurs, the creature may use its Reaction to perform the readied Action. Ready does not store ordinary movement, but Dash can be readied as the Action. Readied attacks retain all weapon properties. A readied spell must still meet implement and targeting requirements when released. Losing a mandatory implement before release prevents release. Concentration begins when the spell actually resolves. Ready never bypasses aerial restrictions, range, or other universal rules. Simultaneous Effects Effects resolve one at a time. The active creature orders its own simultaneous effects; the GM orders GM-controlled simultaneous effects. For opposing same-time effects, resolve the active creature first, then use Initiative if needed. Damage resolves before state changes caused by that damage. Start-of-t

WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Tempo • Firearm Rhythm • Reload Mastery • Mobile Precision Gunslinger “A bullet sounds the same to everybody.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Tempo, Firearms, and Reload Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Tradition & Outlook Specialization Reassignment The Gunslinger is a mobile firearm martial whose power comes from maintaining Tempo through successful firearm play. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Fire. Move. Reload. Keep the rhythm alive long enough to turn Tempo into control, defense, and lethal pressure. Class Identity Gunslingers are technist marksmen who turn Aether-assisted firearms into speed, precision, and controlled ranged pressure. Pistols support rapid, mobile sequences through Quick Shot and Akimbo, while Muskets provide deliberate two-handed fire that concentrates Tempo into stronger individual hits through Deliberate Shot. Tempo represents the Gunslinger’s ability to build combat rhythm through successful action rather than treating every shot as an isolated event. Tradition & Outlook Gunslingers belong to Atreia’s newer technological traditions. The wider Aion tradition describes early firearm research being dismissed as technist tinkering until battlefield success forced major institutions to recognize the discipline. Wings of Atreia keeps that identity of innovation earning legitimacy through results while using Pistols and Muskets as the class’s only firearm categories. Gunslingers often value nerve, technical familiarity, accuracy, independence, and adaptability. Appearance & Adventuring Gunslingers favor mobile equipment, ammunition management, firearm maintenance, and a practical awareness of range and firing position. Their weapons can make them look strikingly modern beside older martial traditions, but their discipline remains Aetheric and distinctly Atreian. They adventure to test new techniques, serve as ranged specialists, hunt dangerous targets, protect expeditions from positions others cannot exploit, or demonstrate that innovation has earned its place in the war for Atreia. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Role Ranged weapon damage Secondary Role Mobility, precision, disruption Primary Ability DEX Secondary Ability INT Hit Die d8 Saving Throws DEX, INT Armor Leather Skills Choose 2 from 6: Acrobatics, Deception, Investigation, Perception, Sleight of Hand, Survival Weapons Pistols, Muskets Signature Resource Tempo Signature Mechanic Firearm sequencing and reload rhythm Core Engine — Tempo, Firearms, and Reload The Gunslinger is a mobile firearm martial whose power comes from maintaining Tempo through successful firearm play. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols Ranged Gunslinger One-handed Weapon Attack. Range 30/90 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d8 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. A Gunslinger can wield two Pistols, but doing so does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols are compatible with Quick Shot and Akimbo. Muskets Ranged Gunslinger Two-handed Weapon Attack. Range 60/180 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d12 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. Ammunition capacity is fixed at 2. Muskets cannot use Quick Shot or Akimbo. Gunslinger ammunition-restoration features can restore Musket shots normally, but a Musket can never hold more than 2 shots. Standard one-handed firearm capacity increases do not apply to Muskets. Reload Every firearm attack consumes one shot. A firearm with no shots remaining is Empty and cannot make firearm attacks until at least one shot is restored. Normal Bonus Action Reload: an Empty firearm is restored to its full Reload capacity. Ammunition restoration is not the Reload action unless a feature explicitly says so. Ammunition-restoration features can restore shots to either Pistols or Muskets up to that firearm's maximum capacity. A Musket's maximum capacity remains 2. Switching between carried one-handed Gunslinger firearms as part of a firearm attack requires no separate object interaction. Standard one-handed firearm capacity progression: Ammo Capacity 4 at Levels 1-4, Ammo Capacity 5 at 5-8, Ammo Capacity 6 at 9-14, and Ammo Capacity 7 at 15-20. Increasing capacity does not automatically reload an Empty firearm. Tempo Tempo is a genuine-combat resource representing firing rhythm, accuracy, and momentum. It begins at 0, resets to 0 when combat ends, and artificial initiative cannot generate it. Maximum Tempo: Levels 1-4 = 3; 5-8 = 4; 9-12 = 5; 13-16 = 6; 17-20 = 7. Clean Hit: after you hit a host

WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Melee Striker • Sneak Attack • Rune Marks • Execution Assassin “You'll know I'm there when you're dead.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Sneak Attack and Rune Marks Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Assassin is a precision melee striker that builds target-bound Rune Marks, converts them into burst damage or execution riders, and uses Shadow Step to remain difficult to pin down. Unlike a conventional Extra Attack martial, its Level 5 Assassination Sequence is a conditional follow-up attack tied to a successful Sneak Attack. Class Identity Assassins are precision predators who win through positioning, timing, concealment, and carefully prepared execution. Their art is not simply “attacking from stealth.” An Assassin studies a target, creates the right opening, carves Rune Marks, and converts preparation into a sudden lethal advantage. Their greatest strength is the ability to decide where and when a close-range confrontation becomes dangerous. Tradition & Outlook The Assassin tradition descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines and is practiced by infiltrators, covert operatives, hunters of dangerous individuals, intelligence agents, and Daevas who favor certainty over spectacle. Assassins often prize patience, awareness, self-control, and economy of motion. Their motives vary widely: service to a faction, revenge, professional duty, protection through preemptive action, or the pursuit of perfect technique. Appearance & Adventuring Assassins favor equipment that permits mobility and unobstructed movement, with Shortswords and Daggers forming the class’s approved weapon identity in Wings of Atreia. Their appearance may be subdued or ceremonial, but practical Assassins avoid anything that compromises movement or control. They adventure when a threat must be found before it strikes, a route must be infiltrated, an enemy leader must be neutralized, or a mystery demands someone comfortable operating unseen. text: Preliminary Round, Main Combat, Battle Exchanges, and Decision Windows. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Legions & Complete Abyss Warfront System Player-created Legions plus the complete player-operable Warfront rules, unit catalogue, War Asset costs, Fortress procedures, and Open Abyss procedures. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Core Rulebook v4.2 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026 , synchronized with Player Handbook v3.10 . This page exposes the complete player-operable Warfront subsystem. Explicitly GM-facing enemy statblocks, hidden force composition, and closed GM-only resolution tables remain off the public player site. Legions Warfront Overview War Assets Unit Statistics Battle Exchange Unit Catalogue Unit Costs PC Participation Fortress Wars Open Abyss Reinforcements Quick Reference PLAYER-CREATED LEGIONS A player-created Legion is a lightweight organization for shared identity, missions, resources, and cross-faction cooperation when the campaign permits it. Legion membership does not create a new character progression track or grant automatic combat bonuses. When a Legion Can Be Founded Campaign Gate. The Campaign Director or controlling GM must explicitly declare Legion Founding available. Reaching Level 11 by itself does not unlock the system. Founding Player. One Founding Player must be Level 11 or higher. That character becomes the initial Legion Leader. Other members. Every other founding or joining member must be Level 3 or higher before joining and must already have reached their Specialization or Archetype choice where applicable. A Level 1-2 character cannot join early. Membership has no maximum size. There is no minimum number of additional founders; a qualifying Founding Player may establish the Legion alone if all other founding requirements are satisfied. Elyos and Asmodians may belong to the same Legion once the required campaign state is active. Every member retains their original faction identity and its normal consequences. Founding Fund and Treasury Founding requires 5,000 Kinah deposited into the new Legion Treasury. Eligible founding members may contribute toward the total. Before establishment, the Founding Fund cannot be withdrawn. If founding is abandoned, each contributor receives their contribution back. Once established, the 5,000 Kinah remains usable Treasury money. Any Legion member may deposit Kinah. Only the Legion Leader may withdraw Kinah or authorize spending. Legion missions may reward participating members, the Treasury, or both as determined by the GM. There is no passive Legion income, automatic salary, interest, business-profit engine, or mandatory recurring membership dues. Leadership and Membership The only default roles are Legion Leader and Legion Member. The Legion Leader admits and removes members, controls permissions for Legion assets, may transfer leadership, and may formally dissolve the Legion. Leadership may be transferred to any existing legal Legion member. The new Leader does not need to be Level 11; Level 11 is a founding requirement only. Member Benefits Members may display the Legion name, colors, crest, and insignia. Ordinary Legion identification occupies no Inventory Slot. Members may accept Legion missions and may use resources, facilities, contacts, and support the Legion actually possesses when the Legion Leader permits it. Where the campaign's cross-faction arrangements recognize the Legion, its insignia provides a legitimate reason for Elyos and Asmodian members to operate together. It does not grant diplomatic immunity or unrestricted access. Legion membership grants no automatic Hit, AC, damage, HP, saving throw, skill, Advantage, Spell DC, DP, class-resource, equipment-quality, or personal Inventory bonus. Legion Storage and Headquarters An established Legion has one secure shared Storage location with a capacity of 100 Inventory Slots. Normal Inventory Slot and stacking rules apply; Kinah remains in the Treasury and uses no Storage Slots. Any Legion member may deposit eligible items. Only the Legion Leader may withdraw items or authorize another member to retrieve them. Legion Storage is stationary and cannot be accessed remotely. It never increases a member's personal Inventory capacity in the field. A Legion may designate one legitimate location as its Headquarters. The Headquarters is simply its meeting place and Storage location; it grants no automatic bonuses and has no upgrade track. Lightweight Rule. There is no Legion XP, Legion Level, officer hierarchy, skill tree, research tree, reputation meter, headquarters progression, or other default Legion management subsystem. Abyss Warfront System Warfronts resolve formation-scale warfare separately from ordinary character-scale combat. They are used for Fortress Wars and Open Abyss Battles. Strategic travel and marching between major engagements are handled narratively, off-table, or during downtime. Shared Warfront

text: Prepared Battlefield. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Ranged Striker • Focus • Traps • Tactical Repositioning Ranger “Chase me or run away. Either way, you'll only die tired.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Focus Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Ranger is a nonmagical ranged hunter that controls enemy movement with persistent battlefield traps, spends Focus on precision or evasive shots, and is rewarded for exploiting targets that walk into prepared terrain. Its sustained damage comes from two ranged attacks, not from spellcasting or a third standard attack. Class Identity Rangers are mobile ranged specialists who control distance through marksmanship, movement, traps, and battlefield awareness. They are most effective when they can read terrain before committing, choose favorable lines of attack, and punish enemies that approach carelessly. Focus represents the Ranger’s ability to convert patience and perception into precise action. Tradition & Outlook The Ranger tradition also descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines, but where Assassins close with a chosen target, Rangers cultivate distance, fieldcraft, and control of the approach. Rangers are common among scouts, hunters, pathfinders, border wardens, reconnaissance troops, and independent Daevas accustomed to surviving beyond secure settlements. They tend to value preparedness, observation, mobility, and freedom of movement. Appearance & Adventuring Rangers usually wear mobile armor and carry bows, ammunition, traps, and field equipment suited to extended movement. Their gear often reflects the terrain in which they learned their craft. Rangers adventure to explore dangerous regions, hunt monsters or enemy operatives, guide expeditions, secure routes, protect remote communities, or prove that no battlefield is truly open ground when preparation and range are on their side. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Ability Dexterity Secondary Ability Wisdom Hit Die d10 Saving Throws Dexterity, Strength Armor Leather Armor Weapons Longbows, Shortbows, Crossbows Skills Choose 2 from 6: Animal Handling, Athletics, Investigation, Nature, Perception, Survival Class Save DC 8 + PB + WIS modifier Signature Resource Focus Signature Mechanic Ranger Traps Extra Attack Level 5; two attacks only Spellcasting None Core Engine — Focus Maximum Focus equals your PB + WIS modifier, minimum 2. A Long Rest restores all expended Focus. A Short Rest restores Focus equal to PB, up to your maximum. Focus is a tactical reserve rather than ammunition or a tax on ordinary ranged attacks; Ranger Traps normally cost no Focus. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Starting State Focus is a rest-based reserve and does not reset merely because combat begins or ends. After a Long Rest it is normally full. Maximum PB + WIS modifier, minimum 2. Rest Recovery Long Rest restores all expended Focus. Short Rest restores Focus equal to PB, up to your maximum. Combat Recovery Hunter’s Rhythm and certain later Ranger/specialization features can regain Focus during genuine combat when their tactical conditions are actually satisfied. How You Spend It Precision Shot 1 Focus; Pinning Shot 1 Focus; Evasive Step 1 Focus; Deadeye Perfect Shot 1 Focus. Other Ranger features spend Focus only when their text states a cost. Refunds / Recovery A combat refund or recovery is not a new attack, trap trigger, or separate technique. It simply restores Focus up to your maximum. Persistence Unused Focus persists between encounters until spent or restored; there is no automatic combat-end reset. Does Not Generate Standing still and firing, harmless staged interactions, or ordinary trap placement do not create Focus unless an explicit recovery feature is actually triggered. Your spirit is with you.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Spellcasting Reference: Spiritmaster has a dedicated spell-list page for quick browsing. View Spiritmaster Spell List → Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Summon Spirit Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Spell List Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequence Specialization Reassignment The Spiritmaster is a two-body tactical caster. One active elemental spirit shares the Spiritmaster’s turn and action economy; together they equal one complete player character. The class establishes two battlefield positions, casts through the spirit, and earns Spirit Bond only through meaningful master-spirit coordination. Class Identity Spiritmasters are binders and commanders of elemental spirits who fight as a partnership rather than as a solitary caster. Their strength comes from coordinating their own spellcraft with a Greater Spirit, applying pressure, disruption, and control across more than one position on the battlefield. Spirit Bond represents the relationship and command structure that makes this divided presence function as one class. Tradition & Outlook The Spiritmaster tradition develops from Atreia’s mage disciplines but turns outward toward spirits, elemental forces, and the difficult art of directing entities shaped by Aether. Spiritmasters are often patient observers, researchers, summoners, or specialists in threats that cannot be understood through ordinary physical study. Their beliefs about spirits differ: some emphasize command, others partnership, responsibility, curiosity, or respect for elemental power. Appearance & Adventuring Spiritmasters use cloth armor and magical implements, while the visible presence of a summoned spirit often defines their silhouette more strongly than clothing does. Their equipment may include ritual, scholarly, or elemental motifs without creating additional mechanics. They adventure to understand unusual spirits, recover lost summoning knowledge, counter supernatural threats, serve as versatile magical operatives, or deepen the bond between Daeva and elemental ally. Only one Spiritmaster spirit may normally be active. Summoning uses an Action and places the spirit in a visible unoccupied space within 15 feet. A defeated spirit disperses into Aether, makes no death saves, and cannot be resummoned until the start of your next turn. Outside combat a newly summoned spirit appears at full HP; voluntary replacement during combat preserves the dismissed spirit’s current HP percentage rather than healing by switching forms. It moves normally during your turn without consuming your action. Normally you spend your Bonus Action to command its basic Spirit Action. If not commanded, it may move, Dodge, or remain in place. A spirit normally makes only one basic Spirit Attack per turn unless a feature explicitly allows otherwise. Spirit attacks are class features, not spells. Preparation requires 1 hour per consumable. If interrupted, no product is created and reagents are not consumed; reagents are consumed only when preparation is successfully completed. One hour prepares a batch of up to 6 servings of the same Meal type and rank. Every serving consumes its full ingredient cost. Different Meal types or ranks require separate batches. text: Prone. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Combat Turn structure, actions, movement, attacks, damage, conditions, death, rests, and survival. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative Round and Turn Action Economy Attack Action Universal Actions Ready Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative, rounds, and combat-only resources are used only for genuine combat or another situation where structured turn order is necessary. Characters cannot manufacture artificial combat to farm cooldowns, resources, or timing triggers. Initiative Initiative = 1d20 + Dexterity modifier. Do not add PB unless an explicit feature says so. Alert adds +2 Initiative. There is no Surprise Round and Surprise does not grant Advantage on Initiative. When one side genuinely catches another side unaware, the GM may, at discretion, allow one appropriate pre-Initiative attack roll against the target's normal defense before Initiative is rolled. This is not an extra round, is not automatic, and does not create a general Surprise action economy. After that resolution, roll Initiative normally. Round and Turn One combat round represents approximately six seconds in the game world. Each participant normally takes one turn in Initiative order. All turns in the round abstract actions occurring within the same six-second span; do not add each turn as another six seconds. Action Economy Action. One per turn. Movement. Up to the creature’s available movement, subject to terrain and conditions. Bonus Action. Up to one, but only when a feature grants something that uses a Bonus Action. Reaction. Normally one per round, refreshing at the start of the creature’s turn unless an explicit class rule says otherwise. Object interaction. One free simple object interaction per turn. There is no universal Action-to-Bonus-Action or Bonus-Action-to-Action conversion. Unused movement or Actions are not stored for later turns. Attack Action The Attack Action makes one attack unless a feature such as Extra Attack says otherwise. Grapple and Shove are full Actions and do not replace one attack within Extra Attack. Player Weapon Requirement. A player character must be wielding an approved class weapon to take the normal Attack Action. Unarmed Attacks and Improvised Weapons are not player combat options unless a later explicit feature creates a specific exception. Opportunity Attacks. Opportunity Attacks remain part of the core combat rules. When a hostile creature you can perceive voluntarily leaves your melee reach, you may use your Reaction to make one melee attack against it, resolving the attack before it leaves that reach. Forced movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Universal Actions Dash. Gain additional movement equal to your current Speed for the turn. Difficult Terrain and other movement costs still apply. While flying, Dash adds horizontal movement but does not grant an additional altitude-layer change. Disengage. Until the end of your turn, your movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks. Dodge. Until the start of your next turn, attacks against you have Disadvantage if you can perceive the attacker, and you have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws. Dodge ends if you become Incapacitated or your Speed becomes 0. Hide. You must have meaningful concealment or another circumstance that allows hiding. Make Dexterity (Stealth) against Passive Perception or active Perception as appropriate. You cannot Hide while clearly seen. Hidden is not Invisible. Making an attack reveals your position after that attack resolves. Search. Deliberately search using a GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation). Use Object. Use this Action for substantial manipulation beyond the one free simple object interaction. A specific item’s activation rule controls when it states another cost. Ready A creature can prepare one Action for a perceivable trigger. When the trigger occurs, the creature may use its Reaction to perform the readied Action. Ready does not store ordinary movement, but Dash can be readied as the Action. Readied attacks retain all weapon properties. A readied spell must still meet implement and targeting requirements when released. Losing a mandatory implement before release prevents release. Concentration begins when the spell actually resolves. Ready never bypasses aerial restrictions, range, or other universal rules. Simultaneous Effects Effects resolve one at a time. The active creature orders its own simultaneous effects; the GM orders GM-controlled simultaneous effects. For opposing same-time effects, resolve the active creature first, then use Initiative if needed. Damage resolves before state changes caused by that damage. Start-of-turn

When an ally within 30 feet of you takes damage while your active spirit is within 10 feet of that ally, reduce the damage by 1d8 + INT. Weapons & Ranged Combat Class Weapon Access Melee Weapons Ranged Weapons Straight-Line Fire Ammunition Armor, Shields, Implements & Hands Armor Weapons & Ranged Combat Access Is Not Ownership. Class weapon, shield, armor, and implement access identifies what your class is allowed to use; it does not mean you own every authorized item. Starting equipment determines what you actually begin play with. Equipment-dependent features function only while their stated requirement is satisfied and do not grant the required equipment unless they explicitly say so. Critical Edge applies only to Dagger weapon damage and does not duplicate or multiply Sneak Attack, Rune Burst, Assassination Sequence, or other bonus-damage dice. Not Thrown. Shortsword 1d6 Piercing Finesse, Light Longsword 1d8 Slashing Versatile 1d10 Spear 1d6 Piercing Versatile 1d8; not Thrown Polearm 1d10 Slashing Heavy, Two-Handed, Reach; Chain-Driven: Gladiator Chain Link weapon die becomes 1d12 Mace 1d8 Bludgeoning — Hammer 1d10 Bludgeoning Heavy, Two-Handed Staff 1d6 Bludgeoning Two-Handed, Channeling. While wielding the Staff with two hands, when one of your class spells or class support techniques restores HP, reduces damage, or grants temporary HP, increase that amount by +1. Channeling does not itself generate additional class resources. Quarterstaff 1d6 Bludgeoning Versatile 1d8 The Light property does not create an extra attack unless a class feature explicitly allows one. Ranged Weapons Weapon Damage Normal Range Maximum Range Properties Shortbow 1d6 Piercing 50 ft 100 ft Ammunition, Two-Handed Longbow 1d8 Piercing 60 ft 150 ft Ammunition, Two-Handed Crossbow 1d8 Piercing 30 ft 80 ft Ammunition, Straight-Line, Two-Handed Pistol 1d8 Piercing 30 ft 90 ft Ammunition, Straight-Line, One-Handed Musket 1d12 Piercing 60 ft 180 ft Ammunition, Straight-Line, Two-Handed; fixed 2-shot load. Each attack expends 1 shot. Normal Bonus Action Reload restores to 2 shots. Cannot use Quick Shot or Akimbo. Gunslinger ammunition-restoration features can restore Musket shots normally, but never above 2. Standard one-handed firearm capacity increases do not apply. Ranged Weapon Range. The first listed range is the weapon’s Normal Range and the second is its Maximum Range. A target within the weapon’s Normal Range is attacked normally unless another modifier applies. A target beyond Normal Range but within Maximum Range can still be targeted, but the ranged weapon attack is made with Disadvantage. A target beyond Maximum Range cannot be hit and the attack automatically misses. If the target is within 5 feet of the attacker, the ranged weapon attack is made with Disadvantage regardless of which listed range applies. Multiple sources of Disadvantage do not stack. Straight-Line Fire Crossbows, Pistols, and Muskets use Straight-Line. If an allied creature intersects the line between shooter and target, the nearest such ally makes DC 15 Dexterity. On success, the shot proceeds. On failure, the ally is hit and takes normal damage; the original target is not hit. The intercepted hit cannot inherit a Natural-20 critical result rolled against the original target. Resolve multiple possible interceptors nearest first. The same rule applies in 3D aerial lines. Ammunition All fired ammunition is lost. Fired Arrows, Bolts, Pistol Bullets, and Musket Bullets are never recovered.
