WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Combat Turn structure, actions, movement, attacks, damage, conditions, death, rests, and survival. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative Round and Turn Action Economy Attack Action Universal Actions Ready Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative, rounds, and combat-only resources are used only for genuine combat or another situation where structured turn order is necessary. Characters cannot manufacture artificial combat to farm cooldowns, resources, or timing triggers. Initiative Initiative = 1d20 + Dexterity modifier. Do not add PB unless an explicit feature says so. Alert adds +2 Initiative. There is no Surprise Round and Surprise does not grant Advantage on Initiative. When one side genuinely catches another side unaware, the GM may, at discretion, allow one appropriate pre-Initiative attack roll against the target's normal defense before Initiative is rolled. This is not an extra round, is not automatic, and does not create a general Surprise action economy. After that resolution, roll Initiative normally. Round and Turn One combat round represents approximately six seconds in the game world. Each participant normally takes one turn in Initiative order. All turns in the round abstract actions occurring within the same six-second span; do not add each turn as another six seconds. Action Economy Action. One per turn. Movement. Up to the creature’s available movement, subject to terrain and conditions. Bonus Action. Up to one, but only when a feature grants something that uses a Bonus Action. Reaction. Normally one per round, refreshing at the start of the creature’s turn unless an explicit class rule says otherwise. Object interaction. One free simple object interaction per turn. There is no universal Action-to-Bonus-Action or Bonus-Action-to-Action conversion. Unused movement or Actions are not stored for later turns. Attack Action The Attack Action makes one attack unless a feature such as Extra Attack says otherwise. Grapple and Shove are full Actions and do not replace one attack within Extra Attack. Player Weapon Requirement. A player character must be wielding an approved class weapon to take the normal Attack Action. Unarmed Attacks and Improvised Weapons are not player combat options unless a later explicit feature creates a specific exception. Opportunity Attacks. Opportunity Attacks remain part of the core combat rules. When a hostile creature you can perceive voluntarily leaves your melee reach, you may use your Reaction to make one melee attack against it, resolving the attack before it leaves that reach. Forced movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Universal Actions Dash. Gain additional movement equal to your current Speed for the turn. Difficult Terrain and other movement costs still apply. While flying, Dash adds horizontal movement but does not grant an additional altitude-layer change. Disengage. Until the end of your turn, your movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks. Dodge. Until the start of your next turn, attacks against you have Disadvantage if you can perceive the attacker, and you have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws. Dodge ends if you become Incapacitated or your Speed becomes 0. Hide. You must have meaningful concealment or another circumstance that allows hiding. Make Dexterity (Stealth) against Passive Perception or active Perception as appropriate. You cannot Hide while clearly seen. Hidden is not Invisible. Making an attack reveals your position after that attack resolves. Search. Deliberately search using a GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation). Use Object. Use this Action for substantial manipulation beyond the one free simple object interaction. A specific item’s activation rule controls when it states another cost. Ready A creature can prepare one Action for a perceivable trigger. When the trigger occurs, the creature may use its Reaction to perform the readied Action. Ready does not store ordinary movement, but Dash can be readied as the Action. Readied attacks retain all weapon properties. A readied spell must still meet implement and targeting requirements when released. Losing a mandatory implement before release prevents release. Concentration begins when the spell actually resolves. Ready never bypasses aerial restrictions, range, or other universal rules. Simultaneous Effects Effects resolve one at a time. The active creature orders its own simultaneous effects; the GM orders GM-controlled simultaneous effects. For opposing same-time effects, resolve the active creature first, then use Initiative if needed. Damage resolves before state changes caus

There is no universal Action-to-Bonus-Action or Bonus-Action-to-Action conversion. Unused movement or Actions are not stored for later turns. Attack Action The Attack Action makes one attack unless a feature such as Extra Attack says otherwise. Grapple and Shove are full Actions and do not replace one attack within Extra Attack. Player Weapon Requirement. A player character must be wielding an approved class weapon to take the normal Attack Action. Unarmed Attacks and Improvised Weapons are not player combat options unless a later explicit feature creates a specific exception. Opportunity Attacks. Opportunity Attacks remain part of the core combat rules. When a hostile creature you can perceive voluntarily leaves your melee reach, you may use your Reaction to make one melee attack against it, resolving the attack before it leaves that reach. Forced movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Universal Actions Dash. Gain additional movement equal to your current Speed for the turn. Difficult Terrain and other movement costs still apply. While flying, Dash adds horizontal movement but does not grant an additional altitude-layer change. Disengage. Until the end of your turn, your movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks. Dodge. Until the start of your next turn, attacks against you have Disadvantage if you can perceive the attacker, and you have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws. Dodge ends if you become Incapacitated or your Speed becomes 0. Hide. You must have meaningful concealment or another circumstance that allows hiding. Make Dexterity (Stealth) against Passive Perception or active Perception as appropriate. You cannot Hide while clearly seen. Hidden is not Invisible. Making an attack reveals your position after that attack resolves. Search. Deliberately search using a GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation). Use Object. Use this Action for substantial manipulation beyond the one free simple object interaction. A specific item’s activation rule controls when it states another cost. Ready A creature can prepare one Action for a perceivable trigger. When the trigger occurs, the creature may use its Reaction to perform the readied Action. Ready does not store ordinary movement, but Dash can be readied as the Action. Readied attacks retain all weapon properties. A readied spell must still meet implement and targeting requirements when released. Losing a mandatory implement before release prevents release. Concentration begins when the spell actually resolves. Ready never bypasses aerial restrictions, range, or other universal rules. Simultaneous Effects Effects resolve one at a time. The active creature orders its own simultaneous effects; the GM orders GM-controlled simultaneous effects. For opposing same-time effects, resolve the active creature first, then use Initiative if needed. Damage resolves before state changes caused by that damage. Start-of

Vision, Stealth, Traps, Locks & Theft Vision and Light Cover, Line of Sight & Line of Effect Stealth and Infiltration Traps and Non-Aether Hazards Locks Theft and Pickpocket Social Interaction, Information & Captivity Vision, Stealth, Traps, Locks & Theft Vision and Light Light states are Bright Light, Dim Light, and Darkness. Obscuration states are Lightly Obscured and Heavily Obscured. Dim Light lightly obscures; Darkness heavily obscures a creature that cannot otherwise see through it. Daeva Darkvision treats Darkness within 60 feet as Dim Light, not Bright Light. A recommended ordinary light source has a stated Bright radius plus an equal additional Dim radius unless its own text says otherwise. Bright light does not universally prohibit Stealth. Obscurity and Invisibility do not automatically make a creature Hidden. Cover, Line of Sight & Line of Effect No Cover. No defensive benefit from Cover. Half Cover. A creature or object behind meaningful partial obstruction gains +2 AC and +2 to Dexterity saving throws against effects originating from the covered direction. Intervening creatures can provide Half Cover when they materially obstruct the line. Full Cover. Full Cover blocks the relevant Line of Effect and prevents direct targeting through that obstruction unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Three-Quarters Cover does not exist in Wings of Atreia. Cover does not stack; use the best applicable Cover. Altitude neither inherently grants nor ignores Cover. Line of Sight and Line of Effect are distinct. Line of Sight determines whether you can see a target or point. Line of Effect determines whether an attack, spell, or effect can physically reach it. Heavy obscurement is not Cover by itself. Stealth and Infiltration Use scene states Undetected, Suspicious, and Alerted; these are not Conditions. Stealth must exceed Passive Perception; ties favor the observer. An active Search uses the GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation), against the relevant DC or opposing Stealth; ties favor the Searcher where opposed. Do not reroll Stealth every 5 feet; roll again only when circumstances materially change. For group Stealth, at least half the group must succeed. A failed check may create Suspicion rather than immediate full alarm when appropriate. Distractions create an opportunity to Hide rather than automatic success. Disguises are primarily social. Invisibility is not the same as Hidden. Wings do not automatically prevent Stealth. Traps and Non-Aether Hazards Describe a hazard with Trigger, Detection, Avoid/Disable method, Save/Check, Effect, and Reset/Duration. Hazards may be obvious, concealed, or hidden. Detection normally uses Passive Perception, active Perception, or Investigation. Disable methods depend on the mechanism and can use Sleight of Hand, Investigation, Athletics, or another appropriate Skill. There is no mandatory Thieves’ Tools system. Failure triggers the hazard only when the hazard says so. Damage and Conditions use existing universal rules. Forced movement is horizontal unless the hazard explicitly creates vertical displacement. Hazards normally resolve when triggered rather than taking their own Initiative turns. Repeat attempts require changed circumstances. Locks Mechanical Lock DC Simple 10 Standard 12 Secure 15 High Security 18 Exceptional 20+ The correct key opens a normal lock without a check. Mechanical locks generally use Dexterity (Sleight of Hand). Unusual mechanisms can use Intelligence (Investigation). Forcing uses Strength (Athletics); destroying a lock or door uses normal object/destruction adjudication. Failure does not automatically break or trigger a lock unless its design says so. Aether locks use Aether Interaction. If a task is impossible, do not assign an absurd DC—state that it cannot be done by that method. Theft and Pickpocket A theft attempt requires a plausible opportunity. Taking an accessible small item uses Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) against Passive Perception and must exceed it. If the target is actively watching, oppose with active Perception; ties favor the observer. Secured items can require a different approach. Failure may create suspicion or alarm. Success means the theft was unnoticed at that moment; later discovery remains possible. Distraction creates opportunity rather than automatic success. Help can grant +2 when genuinely meaningful. Worn armor, shields, Wings, wielded weapons, and equipped mandatory implements cannot simply be pickpocketed. Repeated attempts require changed circumstances. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Melee Striker • Sneak Attack • Rune Marks • Execution Assassin “You'll know I'm there when you're dead.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Sneak Attack and Rune Marks Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Assassin is a precision melee striker that builds target-bound Rune Marks, converts them into burst damage or execution riders, and uses Shadow Step to remain difficult to pin down. Unlike a conventional Extra Attack martial, its Level 5 Assassination Sequence is a conditional follow-up attack tied to a successful Sneak Attack. Class Identity Assassins are precision predators who win through positioning, timing, concealment, and carefully prepared execution. Their art is not simply “attacking from stealth.” An Assassin studies a target, creates the right opening, carves Rune Marks, and converts preparation into a sudden lethal advantage. Their greatest strength is the ability to decide where and when a close-range confrontation becomes dangerous. Tradition & Outlook The Assassin tradition descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines and is practiced by infiltrators, covert operatives, hunters of dangerous individuals, intelligence agents, and Daevas who favor certainty over spectacle. Assassins often prize patience, awareness, self-control, and economy of motion. Their motives vary widely: service to a faction, revenge, professional duty, protection through preemptive action, or the pursuit of perfect technique. Appearance & Adventuring Assassins favor equipment that permits mobility and unobstructed movement, with Shortswords and Daggers forming the class’s approved weapon identity in Wings of Atreia. Their appearance may be subdued or ceremonial, but practical Assassins avoid anything that compromises movement or control. They adventure when a threat must be found before it strikes, a route must be infiltrated, an enemy leader must be neutralized, or a mystery demands someone comfortable operating unseen. Sneak Attack damage scales from 1d6 at Level 1 to 10d6 at Level 19. Levels Sneak Attack Rune Die Marked Targets 1–2 1d6 d4 1 3–4 2d6 d4 1 5–6 3d6 d6 1 7–8 4d6 d6 1 9–10 5d6 d6 2 11–12 6d6 d8 2 13–14 7d6 d8 2 15–16 8d6 d8 2 17–18 9d6 d10 3 19–20 10d6 d10 3 A creature can carry up to 3 of your Rune Marks. Rune Carving: once on your turn, a qualifying melee hit that actually deals Sneak Attack places 1 Rune Mark after that hit resolves. Alternatively, hitting the same creature with two different melee attacks during your turn can place 1 Rune Mark after the second hit. Normal attack-based Rune placement is limited to 1 Mark per turn unless a feature explicitly increases it. Newly created Rune Marks cannot be consumed by the same hit that created them. If you exceed your current marked-target limit, choose one previously marked creature and remove all of your Marks from it. Marks disappear when consumed, when the marked creature is defeated, or when the encounter ends. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Resource Form Rune Marks are target-bound counters, not a generic personal pool. A creature carries your Marks until they are consumed or removed. Maximum Up to 3 Rune Marks per creature. Marked-target capacity is 1 creature through Level 8, 2 from Levels 9–16, and 3 from Level 17 onward. How You Place Marks Once on your turn, a qualifying melee hit that actually deals Sneak Attack places 1 Mark after the hit resolves. Alternatively, two different melee hits against the same creature during your turn can place 1 Mark after the second hit. Placement Limits Normal attack-based placement is limited to 1 Mark per turn unless an explicit feature increases it. A newly created Mark cannot be consumed by the hit that created it. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Sneak Attack and Rune Marks Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Assassin is a precision melee striker that builds target-bound Rune Marks, converts them into burst damage or execution riders, and uses Shadow Step to remain difficult to pin down. Unlike a conventional Extra Attack martial, its Level 5 Assassination Sequence is a conditional follow-up attack tied to a successful Sneak Attack. Class Identity Assassins are precision predators who win through positioning, timing, concealment, and carefully prepared execution. Their art is not simply “attacking from stealth.” An Assassin studies a target, creates the right opening, carves Rune Marks, and converts preparation into a sudden lethal advantage. Their greatest strength is the ability to decide where and when a close-range confrontation becomes dangerous. Tradition & Outlook The Assassin tradition descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines and is practiced by infiltrators, covert operatives, hunters of dangerous individuals, intelligence agents, and Daevas who favor certainty over spectacle. Assassins often prize patience, awareness, self-control, and economy of motion. Their motives vary widely: service to a faction, revenge, professional duty, protection through preemptive action, or the pursuit of perfect technique. Appearance & Adventuring Assassins favor equipment that permits mobility and unobstructed movement, with Shortswords and Daggers forming the class’s approved weapon identity in Wings of Atreia. Their appearance may be subdued or ceremonial, but practical Assassins avoid anything that compromises movement or control. They adventure when a threat must be found before it strikes, a route must be infiltrated, an enemy leader must be neutralized, or a mystery demands someone comfortable operating unseen. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Tempo • Firearm Rhythm • Reload Mastery • Mobile Precision Gunslinger “A bullet sounds the same to everybody.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Tempo, Firearms, and Reload Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Tradition & Outlook Specialization Reassignment The Gunslinger is a mobile firearm martial whose power comes from maintaining Tempo through successful firearm play. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Fire. Move. Reload. Keep the rhythm alive long enough to turn Tempo into control, defense, and lethal pressure. Class Identity Gunslingers are technist marksmen who turn Aether-assisted firearms into speed, precision, and controlled ranged pressure. Pistols support rapid, mobile sequences through Quick Shot and Akimbo, while Muskets provide deliberate two-handed fire that concentrates Tempo into stronger individual hits through Deliberate Shot. Tempo represents the Gunslinger’s ability to build combat rhythm through successful action rather than treating every shot as an isolated event. Tradition & Outlook Gunslingers belong to Atreia’s newer technological traditions. The wider Aion tradition describes early firearm research being dismissed as technist tinkering until battlefield success forced major institutions to recognize the discipline. Wings of Atreia keeps that identity of innovation earning legitimacy through results while using Pistols and Muskets as the class’s only firearm categories. Gunslingers often value nerve, technical familiarity, accuracy, independence, and adaptability. Appearance & Adventuring Gunslingers favor mobile equipment, ammunition management, firearm maintenance, and a practical awareness of range and firing position. Their weapons can make them look strikingly modern beside older martial traditions, but their discipline remains Aetheric and distinctly Atreian. They adventure to test new techniques, serve as ranged specialists, hunt dangerous targets, protect expeditions from positions others cannot exploit, or demonstrate that innovation has earned its place in the war for Atreia. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols Ranged Gunslinger One-handed Weapon Attack. Range 30/90 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d8 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. A Gunslinger can wield two Pistols, but doing so does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols are compatible with Quick Shot and Akimbo. Muskets Ranged Gunslinger Two-handed Weapon Attack. Range 60/180 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d12 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. Ammunition capacity is fixed at 2. Muskets cannot use Quick Shot or Akimbo. Gunslinger ammunition-restoration features can restore Musket shots normally, but a Musket can never hold more than 2 shots. Standard one-handed firearm capacity increases do not apply to Muskets. Reload Every firearm attack consumes one shot. A firearm with no shots remaining is Empty and cannot make firearm attacks until at least one shot is restored. Normal Bonus Action Reload: an Empty firearm is restored to its full Reload capacity. Ammunition restoration is not the Reload action unless a feature explicitly says so. Ammunition-restoration features can restore shots to either Pistols or Muskets up to that firearm's maximum capacity. A Musket's maximum capacity remains 2. Switching between carried one-handed Gunslinger firearms as part of a firearm attack requires no separate object interaction. Standard one-handed firearm capacity progression: Ammo Capacity 4 at Levels 1-4, Ammo Capacity 5 at 5-8, Ammo Capacity 6 at 9-14, and Ammo Capacity 7 at 15-20. Increasing capacity does not automatically reload an Empty firearm. Tempo Tempo is a genuine-combat resource representing firing rhythm, accuracy, and momentum. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Glossary & Core Terms A player-facing A–Z reference for the vocabulary used throughout Wings of Atreia, with direct links to the full rules and lore pages. How to use this page: definitions here are quick-reference summaries. Follow the “Read more” link whenever you need the complete rule, class text, or world context. A B C D E F G I K L M P R S U W 46 terms A Action Your main turn action. Many attacks, spells, class features, and other options specify that they use your Action. Read more: Combat → Advantage / Disadvantage Roll two d20s and use the higher result for Advantage or the lower result for Disadvantage. Read more: Core Resolution → Aether The supernatural power that underlies Daeva abilities, spellcasting, flight, and many extraordinary phenomena in Atreia. Read more: Aether & Spellcasting → Aether Enhancement The higher equipment-quality path beyond Profession +2. Aether upgrades are level-gated and handled separately from ordinary Profession work. Read more: Equipment → Ascension The transformation by which a mortal becomes a Daeva and receives Wings. WoA begins with this event in Session 0. Read more: Character Creation → At-Will A spell or ability frequency that may be used whenever its normal action and other requirements are met. Read more: Aether & Spellcasting → B Background A character-creation choice representing experience and identity before or around Ascension; it provides its defined skills and related benefits. Read more: Backgrounds → Bonus Action A secondary turn action available only when a feature, spell, or rule explicitly gives an option that uses it. Read more: Combat → C Character Manager The official WoA character-management method for creation records, advancement, current resources, equipment, spells, and other tracked character data. Read more: Character Creation → Class Your Daeva’s primary mechanical path. WoA uses eleven classes and does not use multiclassing. Read more: Classes → Class Resource A class-specific pool, charge, stance, meter, or other tracked mechanic defined by that class. Read more: Quick Reference → Class Save DC Normally 8 + Proficiency Bonus + the class ability identified by your class, unless a rule states otherwise. Read more: Core Resolution → Concentration A spell/effect limit: only one Concentration effect can be maintained at a time, and Incapacitated ends it. WoA does not use Concentration saving throws. Read more: Aether & Spellcasting → Condition A named rules state such as Poisoned or Incapacitated that changes what a creature can do or how rolls affect it. Read more: Combat → Cooldown A spell or ability frequency that becomes unavailable after use until its stated cooldown is satisfied; WoA also uses the universal out-of-combat cooldown rule where applicable. Read more: Aether & Spellcasting → D Daeva An Ascended immortal warrior of Atreia. Player characters in Wings of Atreia are Daevas. Read more: Character Creation → Daeva Points (DP) A resource unlocked at Level 10 and earned through participation in genuine combat victories. DP powers Ultimate Abilities and persists through rests. Read more: Daeva Points & Ultimates → E Empyrean Boon A powerful universal character option gained at Level 19 according to the advancement rules. Read more: Feats & Empyrean Boons → Empyrean Lord One of the great Daeva Lords whose authority and legacy shape Elyos and Asmodian civilization, together with the two historic Tower Guardians. Read more: World → F Faction Your character’s allegiance as Elyos or Asmodian. Faction affects culture, homeland, and campaign relationships rather than class statistics. Read more: Character Creation → Feat A universal character option chosen at designated advancement points instead of an Ability Score Improvement where the rules allow it. Read more: Feats & Empyrean Boons → Flight Slot A tracked unit of a Daeva’s flight capacity. The number of Flight Slots increases with character level. Read more: Flight → G Genuine Combat A real encounter using initiative and combat timing. Artificial encounters cannot be used to farm resources such as Daeva Points. Read more: Combat → I Implement A spellcasting equipment category that can follow the established quality and enhancement progression. Read more: Equipment → K Kinah The standard currency used for purchases, profession training, supplies, and other economic transactions. Read more: Professions & Economy → L Legendary Equipment Story-driven top-tier equipment above the Aether enhancement tiers. Legendary items are not ordinary Profession products. Read more: Equipment → Long Rest An 8-hour recovery period. What it restores depends on the specific class, spell, feature, or rule. Read more: Combat → Lord Action The dedicated off-turn action framework used by Empyrean Lords and Dragon Lords. Read more: Combat → M Milestone Advancement WoA’s advancement method. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Combat Turn structure, actions, movement, attacks, damage, conditions, death, rests, and survival. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative Round and Turn Action Economy Attack Action Universal Actions Ready Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative, rounds, and combat-only resources are used only for genuine combat or another situation where structured turn order is necessary. Characters cannot manufacture artificial combat to farm cooldowns, resources, or timing triggers. Initiative Initiative = 1d20 + Dexterity modifier. Do not add PB unless an explicit feature says so. Alert adds +2 Initiative. There is no Surprise Round and Surprise does not grant Advantage on Initiative. When one side genuinely catches another side unaware, the GM may, at discretion, allow one appropriate pre-Initiative attack roll against the target's normal defense before Initiative is rolled. This is not an extra round, is not automatic, and does not create a general Surprise action economy. After that resolution, roll Initiative normally. Round and Turn One combat round represents approximately six seconds in the game world. Each participant normally takes one turn in Initiative order. All turns in the round abstract actions occurring within the same six-second span; do not add each turn as another six seconds. Action Economy Action. One per turn. Movement. Up to the creature’s available movement, subject to terrain and conditions. Bonus Action. Up to one, but only when a feature grants something that uses a Bonus Action. Reaction. Normally one per round, refreshing at the start of the creature’s turn unless an explicit class rule says otherwise. Object interaction. One free simple object interaction per turn. There is no universal Action-to-Bonus-Action or Bonus-Action-to-Action conversion. Unused movement or Actions are not stored for later turns. Attack Action The Attack Action makes one attack unless a feature such as Extra Attack says otherwise. Grapple and Shove are full Actions and do not replace one attack within Extra Attack. Player Weapon Requirement. A player character must be wielding an approved class weapon to take the normal Attack Action. Unarmed Attacks and Improvised Weapons are not player combat options unless a later explicit feature creates a specific exception. Opportunity Attacks. Opportunity Attacks remain part of the core combat rules. When a hostile creature you can perceive voluntarily leaves your melee reach, you may use your Reaction to make one melee attack against it, resolving the attack before it leaves that reach. Forced movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Universal Actions Dash. Gain additional movement equal to your current Speed for the turn. Difficult Terrain and other movement costs still apply. While flying, Dash adds horizontal movement but does not grant an additional altitude-layer change. Disengage. Until the end of your turn, your movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks. Dodge. Until the start of your next turn, attacks against you have Disadvantage if you can perceive the attacker, and you have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws. Dodge ends if you become Incapacitated or your Speed becomes 0. Hide. You must have meaningful concealment or another circumstance that allows hiding. Make Dexterity (Stealth) against Passive Perception or active Perception as appropriate. You cannot Hide while clearly seen. Hidden is not Invisible. Making an attack reveals your position after that attack resolves. Search. Deliberately search using a GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation). Use Object. Use this Action for substantial manipulation beyond the one free simple object interaction. A specific item’s activation rule controls when it states another cost. Ready A creature can prepare one Action for a perceivable trigger. When the trigger occurs, the creature may use its Reaction to perform the readied Action. Ready does not store ordinary movement, but Dash can be readied as the Action. Readied attacks retain all weapon properties. A readied spell must still meet implement and targeting requirements when released. Losing a mandatory implement before release prevents release. Concentration begins when the spell actually resolves. Ready never bypasses aerial restrictions, range, or other universal rules. Simultaneous Effects Effects resolve one at a time. The active creature orders its own simultaneous effects; the GM orders GM-controlled simultaneous effects. text: Save DCs. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Core Resolution The d20 test framework used for meaningful uncertain outcomes. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. d20 Tests & Core Resolution d20 Tests Ability Checks Saving Throws Save DCs Advantage and Disadvantage Help Passive Perception, Passive Investigation & Search d20 Tests & Core Resolution d20 Tests Ability Checks, attack rolls, and saving throws use a d20. Roll only when the outcome is uncertain and meaningful. If success is automatic, impossible, or consequence-free, no roll is needed. Ability Checks Choose the ability that best fits the approach, then add Proficiency Bonus if the character is proficient in the relevant skill. Expertise doubles the PB contribution for that proficiency. WoA retains six abilities and eighteen skills. A specialized Background can authorize a character to attempt obscure knowledge, but it does not automatically modify the roll. Saving Throws A saving throw uses the specified ability modifier and adds PB only if the creature is proficient in that saving throw. Ties are resolved according to the specific system; otherwise meeting a DC succeeds. Save DCs Default effect Save DC = 8 + Proficiency Bonus + the relevant ability modifier, unless an explicit class, spell, item, monster, or environmental rule gives a different DC. Advantage and Disadvantage When a rule grants Advantage, roll two d20s and use the higher. When it grants Disadvantage, roll two and use the lower. If both apply, they cancel unless a specific rule says otherwise. Resolve Advantage/Disadvantage before applying numeric modifiers. Help Help never grants Advantage. A meaningful helper grants +2 to one Ability Check. Normally only one helper can contribute. There is no Assist Attack and Help cannot modify Death Saves. Passive Perception, Passive Investigation & Search Passive Perception = 10 + your Wisdom (Perception) modifier. Passive Investigation = 10 + your Intelligence (Investigation) modifier. Advantage on the relevant check adds +5 to the passive score; Disadvantage subtracts 5. Multiple instances of the same source do not stack, and Advantage and Disadvantage cancel normally. Hide is opposed by Passive Perception; ties favor the observer. An active Search uses the GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation), against the relevant DC or opposing Stealth; ties favor the Searcher where opposed. Repeated checks require a meaningful change in circumstances. ← Back to Rules Wings of Atreia · Created & Designed by Clark Michael Zafra (“ArchQwynn”) · Non-commercial fan project.

Source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page is a player-facing reference extracted from the handbook rather than a replacement ruleset. Background Rules Soldier Scholar Acolyte Noble Outlander Underworld Artisan Merchant Entertainer Languages Background Rules Skill Selection: Choose exactly 2 Background Skills from the six options listed for your Background. Duplicate selections are prohibited. A Skill selected as a Class Skill cannot also be selected as a Background Skill. The four selected Class and Background Skill Proficiencies must therefore be four different Skills. Background Choose 2 Skills Soldier Athletics, Intimidation, Perception, Survival, Medicine, Religion Scholar Arcana, History, Investigation, Religion, Medicine, Perception Acolyte History, Insight, Medicine, Religion, Athletics, Survival Noble History, Insight, Persuasion, Performance, Investigation, Sleight of Hand Outlander Athletics, Nature, Perception, Survival, Persuasion, Stealth Underworld Deception, Insight, Sleight of Hand, Stealth, Investigation, Persuasion Artisan Investigation, Perception, Sleight of Hand, History, Arcana, Persuasion Merchant Insight, Investigation, Persuasion, History, Stealth, Athletics Entertainer Acrobatics, Deception, Performance, Persuasion, Nature, Animal Handling A relevant Background may establish that you have the experience necessary to attempt obscure or specialized knowledge. It does not automatically grant Advantage, Expertise, a numerical bonus, or guaranteed success. Understanding Your Background Your Class describes what your character has learned to do as an adventuring Daeva. Your Background describes the life, training, profession, upbringing, or experiences that helped shape who they were before the campaign began. Faction tells you where you belong, Background helps explain where you came from, and Class describes how you operate as an adventurer. A Background does not determine your morality, personality, beliefs, faction loyalty, or future choices. Two characters with the same Background may have completely different lives and goals. Mechanically, use the Background table above exactly as written: choose two skills from your Background’s listed skill pool. The entries below add roleplaying context and do not grant additional rules benefits. Soldier What Is a Soldier?. A Soldier has meaningful experience with organized military service: troops, guards, scouts, officers, fortress personnel, or other disciplined fighting forces. Life and Origins. Military life may have included patrols, garrison duty, campaigns, escort work, reconnaissance, fortification defense, or service under a commander. That service may have occurred before or after ascension. Motivations and Outlook. Duty, loyalty, comradeship, ambition, patriotism, protection, regret, or the memory of fallen companions may still shape the character. A Soldier may respect military order, resent it, or be deciding what is truly worth fighting for. Playing a Soldier. Decide what kind of service shaped you, who you served beside, and what relationship you now have with authority and your former comrades. Being a Soldier does not require obedience or a martial Class. Scholar What Is a Scholar?. A Scholar has devoted part of their life to seeking, preserving, interpreting, or teaching knowledge. Scholars include researchers, historians, scribes, teachers, philosophers, archivists, investigators, and field specialists. Life and Origins. Study may have taken place under a teacher, within an archive or institution, or independently. Subjects can include history, geography, creatures, Aether, ruins, cultures, warfare, or any other serious field of inquiry. Motivations and Outlook. A Scholar may adventure to recover lost knowledge, investigate mysteries, study ruins or creatures directly, protect important discoveries, or prevent dangerous knowledge from being misused. Playing a Scholar. Choose the subject that fascinates you and decide whether you are an academic, a practical field researcher, or something between. Being scholarly does not require being socially awkward or confined to books. Acolyte What Is an Acolyte?. An Acolyte has meaningful experience with religious or spiritual service, sacred traditions, temples, ceremonies, or communities of worship. Life and Origins. The character may have been raised around a temple, studied under a religious teacher, volunteered in a sacred institution, maintained holy places, assisted ceremonies, or found faith after a life-changing event. Motivations and Outlook. Faith, service, protection, reform, doubt, duty, spiritual curiosity, or concern for a community may lead an Acolyte into adventure. An Acolyte can be devout, questioning, disillusio

Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Vision, Stealth, Traps, Locks & Theft Vision and Light Cover, Line of Sight & Line of Effect Stealth and Infiltration Traps and Non-Aether Hazards Locks Theft and Pickpocket Social Interaction, Information & Captivity Vision, Stealth, Traps, Locks & Theft Vision and Light Light states are Bright Light, Dim Light, and Darkness. Obscuration states are Lightly Obscured and Heavily Obscured. Dim Light lightly obscures; Darkness heavily obscures a creature that cannot otherwise see through it. Daeva Darkvision treats Darkness within 60 feet as Dim Light, not Bright Light. A recommended ordinary light source has a stated Bright radius plus an equal additional Dim radius unless its own text says otherwise. Bright light does not universally prohibit Stealth. Obscurity and Invisibility do not automatically make a creature Hidden. Cover, Line of Sight & Line of Effect No Cover. No defensive benefit from Cover. Half Cover. A creature or object behind meaningful partial obstruction gains +2 AC and +2 to Dexterity saving throws against effects originating from the covered direction. Intervening creatures can provide Half Cover when they materially obstruct the line. Full Cover. Full Cover blocks the relevant Line of Effect and prevents direct targeting through that obstruction unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Three-Quarters Cover does not exist in Wings of Atreia. Cover does not stack; use the best applicable Cover. Altitude neither inherently grants nor ignores Cover. Line of Sight and Line of Effect are distinct. Line of Sight determines whether you can see a target or point. Line of Effect determines whether an attack, spell, or effect can physically reach it. Heavy obscurement is not Cover by itself. Stealth and Infiltration Use scene states Undetected, Suspicious, and Alerted; these are not Conditions. Stealth must exceed Passive Perception; ties favor the observer. An active Search uses the GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation), against the relevant DC or opposing Stealth; ties favor the Searcher where opposed. Do not reroll Stealth every 5 feet; roll again only when circumstances materially change. For group Stealth, at least half the group must succeed. A failed check may create Suspicion rather than immediate full alarm when appropriate. Distractions create an opportunity to Hide rather than automatic success. Disguises are primarily social. Invisibility is not the same as Hidden. Wings do not automatically prevent Stealth. Traps and Non-Aether Hazards Describe a hazard with Trigger, Detection, Avoid/Disable method, Save/Check, Effect, and Reset/Duration. Hazards may be obvious, concealed, or hidden. Detection normally uses Passive Perception, active Perception, or Investigation. Disable methods depend on the mechanism and can use Sleight of Hand, Investigation, Athletics, or another appropriate Skill. There is no mandatory Thieves’ Tools system. Failure triggers the hazard only when the hazard says so. Damage and Conditions use existing universal rules. Forced movement is horizontal unless the hazard explicitly creates vertical displacement. Hazards normally resolve when triggered rather than taking their own Initiative turns. Repeat attempts require changed circumstances. Locks Mechanical Lock DC Simple 10 Standard 12 Secure 15 High Security 18 Exceptional 20+ The correct key opens a normal lock without a check. Mechanical locks generally use Dexterity (Sleight of Hand). Unusual mechanisms can use Intelligence (Investigation). Forcing uses Strength (Athletics); destroying a lock or door uses normal object/destruction adjudication. Failure does not automatically break or trigger a lock unless its design says so. Aether locks use Aether Interaction. If a task is impossible, do not assign an absurd DC—state that it cannot be done by that method. Theft and Pickpocket A theft attempt requires a plausible opportunity. Taking an accessible small item uses Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) against Passive Perception and must exceed it. If the target is actively watching, oppose with active Perception; ties favor the observer. Secured items can require a different approach. Failure may create suspicion or alarm. Success means the theft was unnoticed at that moment; later discovery remains possible. Distraction creates opportunity rather than automatic success. Help can grant +2 when genuinely meaningful. Worn armor, shields, Wings, wielded weapons, and equipped mandatory implements cannot simply be pickpocketed. Repeated attempts require changed circumstances. Social Interaction, Information & Cap

WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Melee Striker • Sneak Attack • Rune Marks • Execution Assassin “You'll know I'm there when you're dead.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Sneak Attack and Rune Marks Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Assassin is a precision melee striker that builds target-bound Rune Marks, converts them into burst damage or execution riders, and uses Shadow Step to remain difficult to pin down. Unlike a conventional Extra Attack martial, its Level 5 Assassination Sequence is a conditional follow-up attack tied to a successful Sneak Attack. Class Identity Assassins are precision predators who win through positioning, timing, concealment, and carefully prepared execution. Their art is not simply “attacking from stealth.” An Assassin studies a target, creates the right opening, carves Rune Marks, and converts preparation into a sudden lethal advantage. Their greatest strength is the ability to decide where and when a close-range confrontation becomes dangerous. Tradition & Outlook The Assassin tradition descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines and is practiced by infiltrators, covert operatives, hunters of dangerous individuals, intelligence agents, and Daevas who favor certainty over spectacle. Assassins often prize patience, awareness, self-control, and economy of motion. Their motives vary widely: service to a faction, revenge, professional duty, protection through preemptive action, or the pursuit of perfect technique. Appearance & Adventuring Assassins favor equipment that permits mobility and unobstructed movement, with Shortswords and Daggers forming the class’s approved weapon identity in Wings of Atreia. Their appearance may be subdued or ceremonial, but practical Assassins avoid anything that compromises movement or control. They adventure when a threat must be found before it strikes, a route must be infiltrated, an enemy leader must be neutralized, or a mystery demands someone comfortable operating unseen. Sneak Attack damage scales from 1d6 at Level 1 to 10d6 at Level 19. Your spirit is with you.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Spellcasting Reference: Spiritmaster has a dedicated spell-list page for quick browsing. View Spiritmaster Spell List → Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Summon Spirit Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Spell List Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequence Specialization Reassignment The Spiritmaster is a two-body tactical caster. One active elemental spirit shares the Spiritmaster’s turn and action economy; together they equal one complete player character. The class establishes two battlefield positions, casts through the spirit, and earns Spirit Bond only through meaningful master-spirit coordination. Class Identity Spiritmasters are binders and commanders of elemental spirits who fight as a partnership rather than as a solitary caster. Their strength comes from coordinating their own spellcraft with a Greater Spirit, applying pressure, disruption, and control across more than one position on the battlefield. Spirit Bond represents the relationship and command structure that makes this divided presence function as one class. Tradition & Outlook The Spiritmaster tradition develops from Atreia’s mage disciplines but turns outward toward spirits, elemental forces, and the difficult art of directing entities shaped by Aether. Spiritmasters are often patient observers, researchers, summoners, or specialists in threats that cannot be understood through ordinary physical study. Their beliefs about spirits differ: some emphasize command, others partnership, responsibility, curiosity, or respect for elemental power. Appearance & Adventuring Spiritmasters use cloth armor and magical implements, while the visible presence of a summoned spirit often defines their silhouette more strongly than clothing does. Their equipment may include ritual, scholarly, or elemental motifs without creating additional mechanics. They adventure to understand unusual spirits, recover lost summoning knowledge, counter supernatural threats, serve as versatile magical operatives, or deepen the bond between Daeva and elemental ally. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Ability Intelligence Secondary Ability Charisma Hit Die d6 Saving Throws Wisdom, Charisma Armor Cloth Implements Spellbook, Magical Orb Skills Choose 2 from 6: Arcana, Deception, Insight, Intimidation, Nature, Religion Spellcasting Ability INT Spell Save DC 8 + PB + INT modifier Spell Attack PB + INT modifier Signature Resource Spirit Bond Spell Advancements +2 every level after 1; 38 total Maximum Spell Level 9 Extra Attack None Core Engine — Summon Spirit You know all four fundamental spirits—Fire, Water, Earth, and Wind—and choose among them tactically. Only one Spiritmaster spirit may normally be active. Summoning uses an Action and places the spirit in a visible unoccupied space within 15 feet. A defeated spirit disperses into Aether, makes no death saves, and cannot be resummoned until the start of your next turn. Outside combat a newly summoned spirit appears at full HP; voluntary replacement during combat preserves the dismissed spirit’s current HP percentage rather than healing by switching forms. Spirit Chassis Rule AC 12 + PB; Earth Spirit 15 + PB HP Levels 1–10 8 + (5 × Spiritmaster level) + INT modifier HP Levels 11–20 12 + (6 × Spiritmaster level) + INT modifier Speed 30 ft; Wind Spirit 40 ft Attack Modifier Your Spiritmaster Spell Attack Modifier Save DC Your Spiritmaster Spell Save DC Level 11 Saving Throws Proficient in all saves using PB; Advantage vs Charmed/Frightened The spirit shares your Initiative and acts during your turn. It moves normally during your turn without consuming your action. Normally you spend your Bonus Action to command its basic Spirit Action. If not commanded, it may move, Dodge, or remain in place. A spirit normally makes only one basic Spirit Attack per turn unless a feature explicitly allows otherwise. Spirit attacks are class features, not spells. Spirit AC never inherits your armor or personal AC bonuses unless a feature explicitly says so. Elemental Spirits Spirit Basic Attack Persistent Identity Fire Flame Claw: melee; 1d8 + PB Fire damage. Once/turn on hit, target cannot benefit from resistance to the next amount of Fire damage equal to PB that it takes from you before your next turn. Water Tidal Lash: melee or ranged 30 ft; 1d6 + PB Cold damage. Hit reduces target Speed by 5 ft until your next turn; may move through allied spaces and ignores shallow-liquid difficult terrain. Earth Stone Fist: melee; 1d6 + PB Bludgeoning damage. Hit gives target Disadvantage on next attempt

WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Combat Turn structure, actions, movement, attacks, damage, conditions, death, rests, and survival. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative Round and Turn Action Economy Attack Action Universal Actions Ready Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative, rounds, and combat-only resources are used only for genuine combat or another situation where structured turn order is necessary. Characters cannot manufacture artificial combat to farm cooldowns, resources, or timing triggers. Initiative Initiative = 1d20 + Dexterity modifier. Do not add PB unless an explicit feature says so. Alert adds +2 Initiative. There is no Surprise Round and Surprise does not grant Advantage on Initiative. When one side genuinely catches another side unaware, the GM may, at discretion, allow one appropriate pre-Initiative attack roll against the target's normal defense before Initiative is rolled. This is not an extra round, is not automatic, and does not create a general Surprise action economy. After that resolution, roll Initiative normally. Round and Turn One combat round represents approximately six seconds in the game world. Each participant normally takes one turn in Initiative order. All turns in the round abstract actions occurring within the same six-second span; do not add each turn as another six seconds. Action Economy Action. One per turn. Movement. Up to the creature’s available movement, subject to terrain and conditions. Bonus Action. Up to one, but only when a feature grants something that uses a Bonus Action. Reaction. Normally one per round, refreshing at the start of the creature’s turn unless an explicit class rule says otherwise. Object interaction. One free simple object interaction per turn. There is no universal Action-to-Bonus-Action or Bonus-Action-to-Action conversion. Unused movement or Actions are not stored for later turns. Attack Action The Attack Action makes one attack unless a feature such as Extra Attack says otherwise. Grapple and Shove are full Actions and do not replace one attack within Extra Attack. Player Weapon Requirement. A player character must be wielding an approved class weapon to take the normal Attack Action. Unarmed Attacks and Improvised Weapons are not player combat options unless a later explicit feature creates a specific exception. Opportunity Attacks. Opportunity Attacks remain part of the core combat rules. When a hostile creature you can perceive voluntarily leaves your melee reach, you may use your Reaction to make one melee attack against it, resolving the attack before it leaves that reach. Forced movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Universal Actions Dash. Gain additional movement equal to your current Speed for the turn. Difficult Terrain and other movement costs still apply. While flying, Dash adds horizontal movement but does not grant an additional altitude-layer change. Disengage. Until the end of your turn, your movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks. Dodge. Until the start of your next turn, attacks against you have Disadvantage if you can perceive the attacker, and you have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws. Dodge ends if you become Incapacitated or your Speed becomes 0. Hide. You must have meaningful concealment or another circumstance that allows hiding. Make Dexterity (Stealth) against Passive Perception or active Perception as appropriate. You cannot Hide while clearly seen. Hidden is not Invisible. Making an attack reveals your position after that attack resolves. Search. Deliberately search using a GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation). Use Object. Use this Action for substantial manipulation beyond the one free simple object interaction. A specific item’s activation rule controls when it states another cost. Ready A creature can prepare one Action for a perceivable trigger. When the trigger occurs, the creature may use its Reaction to perform the readied Action. Ready does not store ordinary movement, but Dash can be readied as the Action. Readied attacks retain all weapon properties. A readied spell must still meet implement and targeting requirements when released. Losing a mandatory implement before release prevents release. Concentration begins when the spell actually resolves. Ready never bypasses aerial restrictions, range, or other universal rules. Simultaneous Effects Effects resolve one at a time. The active creature orders its own simultaneous effects; the GM orders GM-controlled simultaneous effects. For opposing same-time effects, resolve the active creature first, then use Initiative if needed. Damage resolves before state changes caused by that damage. Start-of

text: Skirmisher’s Escape. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Ranged Striker • Focus • Traps • Tactical Repositioning Ranger “Chase me or run away. Either way, you'll only die tired.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Focus Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Ranger is a nonmagical ranged hunter that controls enemy movement with persistent battlefield traps, spends Focus on precision or evasive shots, and is rewarded for exploiting targets that walk into prepared terrain. Its sustained damage comes from two ranged attacks, not from spellcasting or a third standard attack. Class Identity Rangers are mobile ranged specialists who control distance through marksmanship, movement, traps, and battlefield awareness. They are most effective when they can read terrain before committing, choose favorable lines of attack, and punish enemies that approach carelessly. Focus represents the Ranger’s ability to convert patience and perception into precise action. Tradition & Outlook The Ranger tradition also descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines, but where Assassins close with a chosen target, Rangers cultivate distance, fieldcraft, and control of the approach. Rangers are common among scouts, hunters, pathfinders, border wardens, reconnaissance troops, and independent Daevas accustomed to surviving beyond secure settlements. They tend to value preparedness, observation, mobility, and freedom of movement. Appearance & Adventuring Rangers usually wear mobile armor and carry bows, ammunition, traps, and field equipment suited to extended movement. Their gear often reflects the terrain in which they learned their craft. Rangers adventure to explore dangerous regions, hunt monsters or enemy operatives, guide expeditions, secure routes, protect remote communities, or prove that no battlefield is truly open ground when preparation and range are on their side. A Long Rest restores all expended Focus. A Short Rest restores Focus equal to PB, up to your maximum. Focus is a tactical reserve rather than ammunition or a tax on ordinary ranged attacks; Ranger Traps normally cost no Focus. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Starting State Focus is a rest-based reserve and does not reset merely because combat begins or ends. After a Long Rest it is normally full. Maximum PB + WIS modifier, minimum 2. Rest Recovery Long Rest restores all expended Focus. Short Rest restores Focus equal to PB, up to your maximum. Combat Recovery Hunter’s Rhythm and certain later Ranger/specialization features can regain Focus during genuine combat when their tactical conditions are actually satisfied. How You Spend It Precision Shot 1 Focus; Pinning Shot 1 Focus; Evasive Step 1 Focus; Deadeye Perfect Shot 1 Focus. Other Ranger features spend Focus only when their text states a cost. Refunds / Recovery A combat refund or recovery is not a new attack, trap trigger, or separate technique. It simply restores Focus up to your maximum. Persistence Unused Focus persists between encounters until spent or restored; there is no automatic combat-end reset. Does Not Generate Standing still and firing, harmless staged interactions, or ordinary trap placement do not create Focus unless an explicit recovery feature is actually triggered. desc: Sneak Attack — Wings of Atreia reference section.
text: Sneak Attack. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Melee Striker • Sneak Attack • Rune Marks • Execution Assassin “You'll know I'm there when you're dead.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Sneak Attack and Rune Marks Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Assassin is a precision melee striker that builds target-bound Rune Marks, converts them into burst damage or execution riders, and uses Shadow Step to remain difficult to pin down. Unlike a conventional Extra Attack martial, its Level 5 Assassination Sequence is a conditional follow-up attack tied to a successful Sneak Attack. Class Identity Assassins are precision predators who win through positioning, timing, concealment, and carefully prepared execution. Their art is not simply “attacking from stealth.” An Assassin studies a target, creates the right opening, carves Rune Marks, and converts preparation into a sudden lethal advantage. Their greatest strength is the ability to decide where and when a close-range confrontation becomes dangerous. Tradition & Outlook The Assassin tradition descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines and is practiced by infiltrators, covert operatives, hunters of dangerous individuals, intelligence agents, and Daevas who favor certainty over spectacle. Assassins often prize patience, awareness, self-control, and economy of motion. Their motives vary widely: service to a faction, revenge, professional duty, protection through preemptive action, or the pursuit of perfect technique. Appearance & Adventuring Assassins favor equipment that permits mobility and unobstructed movement, with Shortswords and Daggers forming the class’s approved weapon identity in Wings of Atreia. Their appearance may be subdued or ceremonial, but practical Assassins avoid anything that compromises movement or control. They adventure when a threat must be found before it strikes, a route must be infiltrated, an enemy leader must be neutralized, or a mystery demands someone comfortable operating unseen. Sneak Attack damage scales from 1d6 at Level 1 to 10d6 at Level 19. Rune Carving: once on your turn, a qualifying melee hit that actually deals Sneak Attack places 1 Rune Mark after that hit resolves. Alternatively, hitting the same creature with two different melee attacks during your turn can place 1 Rune Mark after the second hit. Normal attack-based Rune placement is limited to 1 Mark per turn unless a feature explicitly increases it. Newly created Rune Marks cannot be consumed by the same hit that created them. If you exceed your current marked-target limit, choose one previously marked creature and remove all of your Marks from it. Marks disappear when consumed, when the marked creature is defeated, or when the encounter ends. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Resource Form Rune Marks are target-bound counters, not a generic personal pool. A creature carries your Marks until they are consumed or removed. Maximum Up to 3 Rune Marks per creature. Marked-target capacity is 1 creature through Level 8, 2 from Levels 9–16, and 3 from Level 17 onward. Placement Limits Normal attack-based placement is limited to 1 Mark per turn unless an explicit feature increases it. A newly created Mark cannot be consumed by the hit that created it. text: Social Interaction, Information & Captivity. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Exploration & Interaction Vision, stealth, traps, locks, theft, hazards, social rules, chases, and loot. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Vision, Stealth, Traps, Locks & Theft Vision and Light Cover, Line of Sight & Line of Effect Stealth and Infiltration Traps and Non-Aether Hazards Locks Theft and Pickpocket Social Interaction, Information & Captivity Vision, Stealth, Traps, Locks & Theft Vision and Light Light states are Bright Light, Dim Light, and Darkness. Obscuration states are Lightly Obscured and Heavily Obscured. Dim Light lightly obscures; Darkness heavily obscures a creature that cannot otherwise see through it. Daeva Darkvision treats Darkness within 60 feet as Dim Light, not Bright Light. A recommended ordinary light source has a stated Bright radius plus an equal additional Dim radius unless its own text says otherwise. Bright light does not universally prohibit Stealth. Obscurity and Invisibility do not automatically make a creature Hidden. Cover, Line of Sight & Line of Effect No Cover. No defensive benefit from Cover. Half Cover. A creature or object behind meaningful partial obstruction gains +2 AC and +2 to Dexterity saving throws against effects originating from the covered direction. Intervening creatures can provide Half Cover when they materially obstruct the line. Full Cover. Full Cover blocks the relevant Line of Effect and prevents direct targeting through that obstruction unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Three-Quarters Cover does not exist in Wings of Atreia. Cover does not stack; use the best applicable Cover. Altitude neither inherently grants nor ignores Cover. Line of Sight and Line of Effect are distinct. Line of Sight determines whether you can see a target or point. Line of Effect determines whether an attack, spell, or effect can physically reach it. Heavy obscurement is not Cover by itself. Stealth and Infiltration Use scene states Undetected, Suspicious, and Alerted; these are not Conditions. Stealth must exceed Passive Perception; ties favor the observer. An active Search uses the GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation), against the relevant DC or opposing Stealth; ties favor the Searcher where opposed. Do not reroll Stealth every 5 feet; roll again only when circumstances materially change. For group Stealth, at least half the group must succeed. A failed check may create Suspicion rather than immediate full alarm when appropriate. Distractions create an opportunity to Hide rather than automatic success. Disguises are primarily social. Invisibility is not the same as Hidden. Wings do not automatically prevent Stealth. Traps and Non-Aether Hazards Describe a hazard with Trigger, Detection, Avoid/Disable method, Save/Check, Effect, and Reset/Duration. Hazards may be obvious, concealed, or hidden. Detection normally uses Passive Perception, active Perception, or Investigation. Disable methods depend on the mechanism and can use Sleight of Hand, Investigation, Athletics, or another appropriate Skill. There is no mandatory Thieves’ Tools system. Failure triggers the hazard only when the hazard says so. Damage and Conditions use existing universal rules. Forced movement is horizontal unless the hazard explicitly creates vertical displacement. Hazards normally resolve when triggered rather than taking their own Initiative turns. Repeat attempts require changed circumstances. Locks Mechanical Lock DC Simple 10 Standard 12 Secure 15 High Security 18 Exceptional 20+ The correct key opens a normal lock without a check. Mechanical locks generally use Dexterity (Sleight of Hand). Unusual mechanisms can use Intelligence (Investigation). Forcing uses Strength (Athletics); destroying a lock or door uses normal object/destruction adjudication. Failure does not automatically break or trigger a lock unless its design says so. Aether locks use Aether Interaction. If a task is impossible, do not assign an absurd DC—state that it cannot be done by that method. Theft and Pickpocket A theft attempt requires a plausible opportunity. Taking an accessible small item uses Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) against Passive Perception and must exceed it. If the target is actively watching, oppose with active Perception; ties favor the observer. Secured items can require a different approach. Failure may create suspicion or alarm. Success means the theft was unnoticed at that moment; later discovery remains possible. Distraction creates opportunity rather than automatic success. Help can grant +2 when genuinely meaningful. Worn armor, shields, Wings, wielded weapons, and equipped mandatory implements cannot simply be pickpocketed. Repeated attempts require changed circumstances. Social Interac

Duplicate selections are prohibited. A Skill selected as a Class Skill cannot also be selected as a Background Skill. It does not automatically grant Advantage, Expertise, a numerical bonus, or guaranteed success. Understanding Your Background Your Class describes what your character has learned to do as an adventuring Daeva. Your Background describes the life, training, profession, upbringing, or experiences that helped shape who they were before the campaign began. Faction tells you where you belong, Background helps explain where you came from, and Class describes how you operate as an adventurer. A Background does not determine your morality, personality, beliefs, faction loyalty, or future choices. Two characters with the same Background may have completely different lives and goals. Mechanically, use the Background table above exactly as written: choose two skills from your Background’s listed skill pool. The entries below add roleplaying context and do not grant additional rules benefits. Soldier What Is a Soldier?. A Soldier has meaningful experience with organized military service: troops, guards, scouts, officers, fortress personnel, or other disciplined fighting forces. Life and Origins. Military life may have included patrols, garrison duty, campaigns, escort work, reconnaissance, fortification defense, or service under a commander. That service may have occurred before or after ascension. Motivations and Outlook. Duty, loyalty, comradeship, ambition, patriotism, protection, regret, or the memory of fallen companions may still shape the character. A Soldier may respect military order, resent it, or be deciding what is truly worth fighting for. Playing a Soldier. Decide what kind of service shaped you, who you served beside, and what relationship you now have with authority and your former comrades. Being a Soldier does not require obedience or a martial Class. Scholar What Is a Scholar?. A Scholar has devoted part of their life to seeking, preserving, interpreting, or teaching knowledge. Scholars include researchers, historians, scribes, teachers, philosophers, archivists, investigators, and field specialists. Life and Origins. Study may have taken place under a teacher, within an archive or institution, or independently. Subjects can include history, geography, creatures, Aether, ruins, cultures, warfare, or any other serious field of inquiry. Motivations and Outlook. A Scholar may adventure to recover lost knowledge, investigate mysteries, study ruins or creatures directly, protect important discoveries, or prevent dangerous knowledge from being misused. Playing a Scholar. Choose the subject that fascinates you and decide whether you are an academic, a practical field researcher, or something between. Being scholarly does not require being socially awkward or confined to books. Acolyte What Is an Acolyte?. An Acolyte has meaningful experience with religious or spiritual service, sacred traditions, temples, ceremonies, or communities of worship. Life and Origins. The character may have been raised around a temple, studied under a religious teacher, volunteered in a sacred institution, maintained holy places, assisted ceremonies, or found faith after a life-changing event. Motivations and Outlook. Faith, service, protection, reform, doubt, duty, spiritual curiosity, or concern for a community may lead an Acolyte into adventure. View Songweaver Spell List → Class Identity Class Chassis Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Spell List Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Performance Sequence Tradition & Outlook Specialization Reassignment The Songweaver changes battlefield purpose from moment to moment. Every Songweaver spell belongs to Harmony, Guard, Dissonance, or Requiem. Successful performances create short-lived Refrains, changing Song Roles builds Resonance, and Resonance is spent to amplify, sustain, counter, or conduct the performance. Class Identity Songweavers shape Aether through music, using performance as destructive spellcraft, support, control, and restoration. Their strength lies in versatility: the same class can pressure an enemy, sustain an ally, or shift the emotional and tactical rhythm of an encounter. Resonance represents the accumulating harmony between performance, spellcraft, and the unfolding battle. Tradition & Outlook The Songweaver tradition is rooted in Atreia’s Muses and in remembrance of Siel. The wider Aion tradition describes Muses who continued their studies after the Cataclysm and eventually joined music with Aether in service to their people; their battlefield contribution led to recognition as an established Daeva class. Songweavers may therefore approach performance as remembrance, artistry, scholarship, service, or a declaration that beauty still has power in a broken world. Appearance & Adventuring Songweavers use Lutes and Lyres as their approved implements, often making instrument, costume, gesture, and magical display part of a single visible identity. Their appearance can range from formal performer to traveling battle-musician without changing class mechanics. They adventure to preserve stories, honor Siel, inspire allies, master Aetheric music, carry culture into war-torn regions, or use beauty and sound as weapons against forces that would reduce Atreia to silence. desc: Complete player reference for the Sorcerer class in Wings of Atreia, based on Player Handbook v3.10.
text: WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Full Caster • Elemental Damage • Aether Focus • Spell Shaping Sorcerer “This will only hurt for a second.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Spellcasting Reference: Sorcerer has a dedicated spell-list page for quick browsing. View Sorcerer Spell List → Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Aether Focus Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Spell List Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Spellcasting Example Specialization Reassignment The Sorcerer is the raw magical-damage benchmark. It casts through Fire, Ice, Lightning, and Wind spell chains, then spends Aether Focus only when a particular spell needs more damage, area, control pressure, or reliability. Aether Focus enhances spells; it is never the fuel required to cast ordinary Sorcerer spells. Class Identity Sorcerers are masters of direct Aetheric spellcraft, combining destructive magic with the ability to control the shape and tempo of a fight. They can punish clustered enemies, deny movement or action, and unleash powerful spells when an opening appears. Aether Focus represents the concentration and arcane discipline required to turn immense magical potential into reliable battlefield power. Tradition & Outlook The Sorcerer tradition grows from Atreia’s mage disciplines and is associated with formal magical study, experimentation, academies, battlefield arcanists, and Daevas fascinated by the structure of Aether itself. Sorcerers commonly value knowledge, precision, preparation, and intellectual mastery, although their personalities range from scholarly restraint to spectacular confidence. For many, magic is both a weapon and a language through which Atreia can be understood. Appearance & Adventuring Sorcerers favor cloth armor and magical implements such as Orbs and Spellbooks under the Wings of Atreia equipment rules. Their appearance may reflect academic, military, ceremonial, or highly individual magical traditions. They adventure to recover lost knowledge, study Aetheric phenomena, test magical theories, defend their people with overwhelming spellcraft, or confront powers that ordinary weapons cannot adequately answer. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Ability Intelligence Secondary Ability Wisdom Hit Die d6 Saving Throws Constitution, Intelligence Armor Cloth Implements Magical Orbs, Spellbooks Spellcasting Ability INT Spell Save DC 8 + PB + INT modifier Spell Attack PB + INT modifier Signature Resource Aether Focus Spell Advancements +2 every class level after 1; 38 total Maximum Spell Level 9 Extra Attack None Core Engine — Aether Focus Maximum Aether Focus equals PB + INT modifier, minimum 2. A Long Rest restores all expended Aether Focus. A Short Rest restores Aether Focus equal to PB, up to your maximum. The resource is an enhancement reserve: casting an ordinary Sorcerer spell never requires Aether Focus unless a spell or class feature explicitly says otherwise. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Starting State Aether Focus is a rest-based enhancement reserve and does not reset merely because combat begins or ends. After a Long Rest it is normally full. Maximum PB + INT modifier, minimum 2. Aether Sage and the Level 20 capstone can explicitly increase this maximum. Rest Recovery Long Rest restores all expended Aether Focus. Short Rest restores Focus equal to PB, up to maximum; Aether Sage can improve this recovery. Base Generation The base Sorcerer does not generate Aether Focus from ordinary spell hits or damage. Combat refunds exist only where a class or specialization feature explicitly grants them. How You Spend It Intensify 1 Focus; Widen 1 Focus; Potent Control 1 Focus; other Sorcerer features spend Aether Focus only when their text states a cost. Ordinary spellcasting costs no Focus. Refunds / Discounts Aether Sage and later features may discount a shaping cost or refund Focus after a qualifying shaped spell. A refund is not a second casting or a new spell trigger. Persistence Unused Aether Focus persists between encounters until spent or restored. Important Distinction Aether Focus is a Sorcerer class resource. It is not environmental Aether, Refined Aether, an Aether State, or a universal damage type.
