Coverage. This Level 1–20 reference covers every class option in the current manuscript that creates or materially changes an Action, Bonus Action, Reaction, triggered player choice, or signature-resource expenditure, refund, recovery, overflow conversion, or combat starting state. A level that only changes passive numerical scaling, grants a Feat/ASI or Spell Advancement, or automatically upgrades an already listed option does not need a duplicate row; use the level progression for the new value. Timing rule. “Triggered / No Action” means the option modifies or responds to its stated event without consuming your Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction. Specific feature text remains authoritative. Level 1 Spell Shaping Shaping Cost Exact Level 1 Effect Intensify 1 Focus When an eligible Sorcerer spell deals damage, increase one damage resolution by +1d6. Widen 1 Focus Increase an eligible radius or cone by 5 ft; a line by 10 ft; or a cube by 5 ft on each side. The spell must have an area that can legally be widened. Potent Control 1 Focus Choose one creature affected by an eligible spell whose non-damaging control or movement rider requires a save. That creature has Disadvantage on its first save against that rider for this casting. At Level 1, apply at most one Spell Shaping enhancement to a single spell. You choose and pay the shaping cost when the spell is cast, before its affected rolls are fully resolved unless the feature says otherwise. Shaping never resets a spell’s At-Will/Cooldown/Rest frequency, creates a second casting, or bypasses immunity. Focused Casting At Level 2 choose one Focused Casting doctrine. Focused Casting modifies a spell you shape with Aether Focus; it does not grant another spell, another Action, or a new specialization. Focused Casting Doctrine Exact Benefit Stable Channel Once on each of your turns when you apply Spell Shaping to a Sorcerer spell that deals rolled damage, you may reroll one damage die rolled for that casting that shows 1 or 2. You must use the new result. Only one die can be rerolled for that casting through this doctrine. Precise Projection Once on each of your turns when you apply Spell Shaping to a Sorcerer spell with an area of effect, choose one creature you can see in that area. That creature is unaffected by that casting. This does not change the spell’s origin, range, area size, or Full Cover restrictions. Anchored Concentration When you apply Spell Shaping to a Sorcerer spell that requires Concentration, that Concentration is Anchored. The first time before the start of your next turn that a hostile spell or feature would directly end that Concentration without making you Incapacitated, ignore that effect. Anchored Concentration cannot prevent Concentration from ending because you become Incapacitated, voluntarily end it, or begin another Concentration effect. Specializations — Read Before You Choose Sorcerer chooses an initial Specialization at Level 3. Use this preview before reading the Level 1–20 progression so you can see the playstyle each path develops into. Specialization features are gained at Levels 3, 6, 10, and 14. text: Specialization Reassignment. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Bastion Pilot • Aether Core • Heat • Adaptive Weapons Combat Aethertech “Steel, meet face. Face, meet steel.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. On this page Overview Chassis Core Mechanics Action Reference Specializations Progression Examples ↑ Top The Aethertech fights from one piloted Large Bastion platform. The pilot and Bastion are one character’s action economy, not two independent turns. The class alternates between integrated Bastion armaments, Aether Core expenditures, controlled Heat accumulation, venting, repairs, and system integration. The Bastion is a separate physical HP pool that enemies can damage without directly healing or harming the pilot unless an effect specifically targets the pilot. Class Identity Aethertechs are technist warriors who channel Aether through a Bastion: a magical-mechanical combat platform that transforms how the Daeva occupies the battlefield. The class combines personal skill, engineered systems, heavy protection, and controlled bursts of power. Aether Core and Heat represent the constant balance between available energy and the strain created by pushing the Bastion harder. Tradition & Outlook Aethertech is a comparatively modern Daeva discipline born from the recovery, study, and weaponization of advanced magical technology. The wider Aion tradition connects the class to Daeva analysis of Danuar technology and the lessons surrounding Hyperion; Wings of Atreia preserves that technological identity while its own campaign chronology and mechanics remain authoritative. Aethertechs often value ingenuity, technical discipline, experimentation, and the belief that knowledge taken from dangerous enemies can be turned toward Atreia’s defense. Appearance & Adventuring An Aethertech is visually defined by the Bastion and the contrast between a Daeva operator and an imposing Aether-powered war platform. Outside it, the Aethertech remains a trained combatant using the class’s approved weapons and equipment. Aethertechs adventure to recover technology, test designs under real conditions, oppose Balaur war machines, protect expeditions with a durable mobile platform, or prove that engineering can stand beside sword and spell as a heroic discipline. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Ability Intelligence Secondary Ability Constitution Hit Die d8 Saving Throws Intelligence, Constitution Armor Chain Armor Skills Choose 2 from 6: Arcana, Athletics, Investigation, Perception, Sleight of Hand, Survival Weapons Shortswords, Maces, Hammers Signature Resources Aether Core and Heat Signature Mechanic Piloted Bastion Bastion Size Large Class Save DC 8 + PB + INT modifier Extra Attack Level 5; two Bastion weapon attacks only Spellcasting None Bastion Targeting and Chassis The pilot and Bastion have separate HP and temporary HP. Repairs restore Bastion HP and are not healing. While occupied, ordinary physical attacks targeting the Aethertech generally strike the Bastion first. Mental, emotional, biological, and similar effects target the pilot when appropriate. One area effect normally does not double-hit both pilot and Bastion. Bastion physical STR/DEX/CON saves use PB + INT modifier. Mental saves use the pilot’s relevant save. When the Bastion reaches 0 HP it is Disabled. The pilot is ejected to the nearest legal space, takes 1d6 Force damage, and does not provoke Opportunity Attacks from the ejection. A disabled Bastion retains its current Core and Heat; a fresh chassis does not replace it. A Short Rest repairs a Disabled or damaged Bastion by half its maximum HP. A Long Rest repairs the Bastion to its maximum HP. These restorations are repairs, not healing. Once the Bastion has at least 1 HP, it is operational. Entering or re-entering a deployed Bastion uses an Action when otherwise legal. A defeated or voluntarily replaced Bastion never functions as a companion or second PC. Contesting STR checks with the Bastion e.g Grapple, pushing, pulling, except for skill or ability effects, will have the PC use this formula: 1d20+8+INT modifier+PB considering that a Bastion is a Large entity. Target must contest with their choice of Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics). WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Melee Striker • Sneak Attack • Rune Marks • Execution Assassin “You'll know I'm there when you're dead.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Sneak Attack and Rune Marks Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Assassin is a precision melee striker that builds target-bound Rune Marks, converts them into burst damage or execution riders, and uses Shadow Step to remain difficult to pin down. Unlike a conventional Extra Attack martial, its Level 5 Assassination Sequence is a conditional follow-up attack tied to a successful Sneak Attack. Class Identity Assassins are precision predators who win through positioning, timing, concealment, and carefully prepared execution. Their art is not simply “attacking from stealth.” An Assassin studies a target, creates the right opening, carves Rune Marks, and converts preparation into a sudden lethal advantage. Their greatest strength is the ability to decide where and when a close-range confrontation becomes dangerous. Tradition & Outlook The Assassin tradition descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines and is practiced by infiltrators, covert operatives, hunters of dangerous individuals, intelligence agents, and Daevas who favor certainty over spectacle. Assassins often prize patience, awareness, self-control, and economy of motion. Their motives vary widely: service to a faction, revenge, professional duty, protection through preemptive action, or the pursuit of perfect technique. Appearance & Adventuring Assassins favor equipment that permits mobility and unobstructed movement, with Shortswords and Daggers forming the class’s approved weapon identity in Wings of Atreia. Their appearance may be subdued or ceremonial, but practical Assassins avoid anything that compromises movement or control. They adventure when a threat must be found before it strikes, a route must be infiltrated, an enemy leader must be neutralized, or a mystery demands someone comfortable operating unseen. View Chanter Spell List → Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Cadence Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Spell List Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Rhythm Sequence Specialization Reassignment The Chanter wins by alternating weapon attacks, spells, and active Mantra management. Cadence is earned by changing categories rather than repeating one action, then spent on damage, protection, healing, and tactical movement. It is a secondary healer and hybrid support, not a replacement for the Cleric or a dedicated martial striker. Class Identity Chanters are martial support specialists who combine staff technique, enchantment, restorative magic, and Mantras into a continuous rhythm of battle. Rather than solving every problem through one large spell, a Chanter improves the party’s performance over time and responds to changing pressure with Cadence. Their presence is felt in how effectively the entire group moves, strikes, and recovers together. Tradition & Outlook The Chanter tradition grows from Atreia’s priestly disciplines but emphasizes disciplined body, voice, repetition, and the shaping of Aether through words and practiced forms. Chanters are often teachers, battle companions, spiritual guides, martial ascetics, or morale-keepers. They tend to value harmony between individual excellence and collective strength: the ideal Chanter does not merely stand beside allies but helps those allies become more capable. Appearance & Adventuring Chanters are strongly associated with Staff and Quarterstaff techniques in Wings of Atreia. Their clothing and armor tend to allow movement while retaining the ceremonial or disciplined character of a priestly warrior. They adventure to guide companions, strengthen military or exploratory groups, carry teachings into dangerous places, preserve morale during long campaigns, or prove that disciplined cooperation can overcome enemies stronger than any one Daeva. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Primary Healer • Divine Grace • Protection • Purification Cleric “Protect me and you shall never fall.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Spellcasting Reference: Cleric has a dedicated spell-list page for quick browsing. View Cleric Spell List → Class Identity Class Chassis Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Spell List Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Support Sequence Tradition & Outlook Specialization Reassignment The Cleric is Wings of Atreia’s primary restorative spellcaster. It is deliberately more durable than the d6 full casters and is rewarded for meaningful intervention: healing an ally in real danger, actually preventing damage, or removing a significant hostile effect. Divine Grace then converts that successful support into more emergency power. Class Identity Clerics are Atreia’s foremost restorative and protective spellcasters. Their calling is not limited to healing wounds after the fact: they preserve the party through recovery, cleansing, protection, and timely intervention while retaining the ability to fight when necessary. Divine Grace represents the reserve of sacred and restorative power through which a Cleric answers moments of genuine need. Tradition & Outlook The Cleric tradition grows from Atreia’s priestly disciplines and is associated with healers, battlefield ministers, temple servants, protectors of communities, and Daevas who understand survival as a collective responsibility. Clerics often value service, perseverance, mercy, duty, or faith, but they need not share one personality or theology. A militant Cleric and a gentle healer may practice the same class through very different convictions. Appearance & Adventuring Clerics commonly combine durable armor with practical healing or ritual equipment. In Wings of Atreia they may use Maces, Hammers, Staffs, Quarterstaffs, and shields from Round Shields to Medium Shields according to their approved access. They adventure to protect lives, confront corruption or supernatural danger, recover sacred knowledge, serve a cause, or ensure that an expedition can survive places where retreat and ordinary medicine are not enough. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Martial Striker • Chain Attacks • Momentum • Frontline Pressure Gladiator “Nothing can stand in my way!” The premier sustained melee damage class, built around deliberate attack sequences, Momentum, Chain Links, and Finishers. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. Overview Class Chassis Momentum Chain Attacks Action Reference Specializations Preview Levels 1–20 Combat Examples Specialization Reassignment Class Overview The Gladiator is the premier sustained melee damage class. It wins through sequences rather than single isolated attacks: open a Chain, spend Momentum on Links that alter the battlefield, then cash the sequence out with a Finisher. Polearms provide the highest sustained weapon output, while weapon discipline and specialization determine whether the Gladiator emphasizes execution, cleaving pressure, or relentless pursuit. Class Identity Gladiators are Daevas who turn martial mastery into relentless battlefield pressure. They are not defined by a single weapon or one decisive blow, but by the ability to seize momentum, force an opening, and keep an enemy under pressure until the fight breaks in their favor. In Wings of Atreia, this identity is expressed through Momentum and Chain Attacks: the Gladiator becomes more dangerous when attacks, movement, and finishers are linked into a deliberate sequence. Tradition & Outlook The Gladiator tradition descends from the broad warrior disciplines of Atreia and is associated with soldiers, arena fighters, legion veterans, weapon masters, and Daevas who believe that skill must survive contact with a real battlefield. Gladiators commonly value courage, physical discipline, adaptability, and decisive action. Some fight for glory or personal mastery; others see themselves as the hard edge of a legion, the Daeva who advances when everyone else needs the line to move. Appearance & Adventuring Gladiators usually present themselves as practical combatants: heavy armor, battle-worn weapons, and equipment chosen for reach, leverage, or sustained close combat. Polearms and other approved Gladiator weapons may suggest very different fighting schools, but the class is recognized by an aggressive, forward-driving presence. A Gladiator adventures to test mastery, protect comrades through offensive pressure, earn renown, serve a military cause, or become strong enough to face the threats of the Abyss and Balaurea directly. It exists only in genuine combat and resets to 0 when combat ends. Normal Momentum does not decay simply because you failed to spend it; later features care about maintaining an active Chain instead. First melee hit on your own turn: gain 1 Momentum. Aggressive Momentum: once on each of your turns, gain 1 additional Momentum if a melee hit follows at least 15 feet of movement toward that target, is a critical hit, or reduces a hostile creature to 0 HP. Multiple qualifying conditions on one attack still grant only 1 additional Momentum. Maximum Momentum: 3 at Levels 1–4; 4 at 5–8; 5 at 9–12; 6 at 13–16; 7 at 17–20. A single attack cannot normally grant more than the Momentum allowed by the generation rules above. Refunds occur after the triggering feature resolves and are not new Momentum-generation events unless stated otherwise. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Starting State Momentum exists only in genuine combat and normally begins at 0. A later feature may cause you to begin genuine combat with Momentum instead. Maximum 3 at Levels 1–4; 4 at 5–8; 5 at 9–12; 6 at 13–16; 7 at 17–20. How You Gain It Your first melee hit on your own turn grants 1 Momentum. Once on each of your turns, Aggressive Momentum grants 1 additional Momentum when a melee hit follows at least 15 ft of movement toward that target, is a critical hit, or reduces a hostile creature to 0 HP. Generation Limits Multiple Aggressive Momentum conditions on one hit still grant only 1 additional Momentum. A normal hit cannot repeatedly generate Momentum beyond the explicit first-hit and Aggressive Momentum triggers. How You Spend It Driving Strike 1; Sweeping Strike 1; Crushing Finisher 2; Hamstring Strike 1; Staggering Strike 1; Devastating Finisher 3; Titanic Finisher 4; Endless Assault 1 at Levels 15–19 (0 at Level 20). Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Tempo, Firearms, and Reload Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Tradition & Outlook Specialization Reassignment The Gunslinger is a mobile firearm martial whose power comes from maintaining Tempo through successful firearm play. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Fire. Move. Reload. Keep the rhythm alive long enough to turn Tempo into control, defense, and lethal pressure. Class Identity Gunslingers are technist marksmen who turn Aether-assisted firearms into speed, precision, and controlled ranged pressure. Pistols support rapid, mobile sequences through Quick Shot and Akimbo, while Muskets provide deliberate two-handed fire that concentrates Tempo into stronger individual hits through Deliberate Shot. Tempo represents the Gunslinger’s ability to build combat rhythm through successful action rather than treating every shot as an isolated event. Tradition & Outlook Gunslingers belong to Atreia’s newer technological traditions. The wider Aion tradition describes early firearm research being dismissed as technist tinkering until battlefield success forced major institutions to recognize the discipline. Wings of Atreia keeps that identity of innovation earning legitimacy through results while using Pistols and Muskets as the class’s only firearm categories. Gunslingers often value nerve, technical familiarity, accuracy, independence, and adaptability. Appearance & Adventuring Gunslingers favor mobile equipment, ammunition management, firearm maintenance, and a practical awareness of range and firing position. Their weapons can make them look strikingly modern beside older martial traditions, but their discipline remains Aetheric and distinctly Atreian. They adventure to test new techniques, serve as ranged specialists, hunt dangerous targets, protect expeditions from positions others cannot exploit, or demonstrate that innovation has earned its place in the war for Atreia. Normal Bonus Action Reload: an Empty firearm is restored to its full Reload capacity. Ammunition restoration is not the Reload action unless a feature explicitly says so. Ammunition-restoration features can restore shots to either Pistols or Muskets up to that firearm's maximum capacity. A Musket's maximum capacity remains 2. Switching between carried one-handed Gunslinger firearms as part of a firearm attack requires no separate object interaction. Increasing capacity does not automatically reload an Empty firearm. Tempo Tempo is a genuine-combat resource representing firing rhythm, accuracy, and momentum. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Focus Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Ranger is a nonmagical ranged hunter that controls enemy movement with persistent battlefield traps, spends Focus on precision or evasive shots, and is rewarded for exploiting targets that walk into prepared terrain. Its sustained damage comes from two ranged attacks, not from spellcasting or a third standard attack. Class Identity Rangers are mobile ranged specialists who control distance through marksmanship, movement, traps, and battlefield awareness. They are most effective when they can read terrain before committing, choose favorable lines of attack, and punish enemies that approach carelessly. Focus represents the Ranger’s ability to convert patience and perception into precise action. Tradition & Outlook The Ranger tradition also descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines, but where Assassins close with a chosen target, Rangers cultivate distance, fieldcraft, and control of the approach. Rangers are common among scouts, hunters, pathfinders, border wardens, reconnaissance troops, and independent Daevas accustomed to surviving beyond secure settlements. They tend to value preparedness, observation, mobility, and freedom of movement. Appearance & Adventuring Rangers usually wear mobile armor and carry bows, ammunition, traps, and field equipment suited to extended movement. Their gear often reflects the terrain in which they learned their craft. Rangers adventure to explore dangerous regions, hunt monsters or enemy operatives, guide expeditions, secure routes, protect remote communities, or prove that no battlefield is truly open ground when preparation and range are on their side. Every Songweaver spell belongs to Harmony, Guard, Dissonance, or Requiem. Successful performances create short-lived Refrains, changing Song Roles builds Resonance, and Resonance is spent to amplify, sustain, counter, or conduct the performance. Class Identity Songweavers shape Aether through music, using performance as destructive spellcraft, support, control, and restoration. Their strength lies in versatility: the same class can pressure an enemy, sustain an ally, or shift the emotional and tactical rhythm of an encounter. Resonance represents the accumulating harmony between performance, spellcraft, and the unfolding battle. Tradition & Outlook The Songweaver tradition is rooted in Atreia’s Muses and in remembrance of Siel. The wider Aion tradition describes Muses who continued their studies after the Cataclysm and eventually joined music with Aether in service to their people; their battlefield contribution led to recognition as an established Daeva class. Songweavers may therefore approach performance as remembrance, artistry, scholarship, service, or a declaration that beauty still has power in a broken world. Appearance & Adventuring Songweavers use Lutes and Lyres as their approved implements, often making instrument, costume, gesture, and magical display part of a single visible identity. Their appearance can range from formal performer to traveling battle-musician without changing class mechanics. They adventure to preserve stories, honor Siel, inspire allies, master Aetheric music, carry culture into war-torn regions, or use beauty and sound as weapons against forces that would reduce Atreia to silence. It casts through Fire, Ice, Lightning, and Wind spell chains, then spends Aether Focus only when a particular spell needs more damage, area, control pressure, or reliability. Aether Focus enhances spells; it is never the fuel required to cast ordinary Sorcerer spells. Class Identity Sorcerers are masters of direct Aetheric spellcraft, combining destructive magic with the ability to control the shape and tempo of a fight. They can punish clustered enemies, deny movement or action, and unleash powerful spells when an opening appears. Aether Focus represents the concentration and arcane discipline required to turn immense magical potential into reliable battlefield power. Tradition & Outlook The Sorcerer tradition grows from Atreia’s mage disciplines and is associated with formal magical study, experimentation, academies, battlefield arcanists, and Daevas fascinated by the structure of Aether itself. Sorcerers commonly value knowledge, precision, preparation, and intellectual mastery, although their personalities range from scholarly restraint to spectacular confidence. For many, magic is both a weapon and a language through which Atreia can be understood. Appearance & Adventuring Sorcerers favor cloth armor and magical implements such as Orbs and Spellbooks under the Wings of Atreia equipment rules. Their appearance may reflect academic, military, ceremonial, or highly individual magical traditions. They adventure to recover lost knowledge, study Aetheric phenomena, test magical theories, defend their people with overwhelming spellcraft, or confront powers that ordinary weapons cannot adequately answer. One active elemental spirit shares the Spiritmaster’s turn and action economy; together they equal one complete player character. The class establishes two battlefield positions, casts through the spirit, and earns Spirit Bond only through meaningful master-spirit coordination. Class Identity Spiritmasters are binders and commanders of elemental spirits who fight as a partnership rather than as a solitary caster. Their strength comes from coordinating their own spellcraft with a Greater Spirit, applying pressure, disruption, and control across more than one position on the battlefield. Spirit Bond represents the relationship and command structure that makes this divided presence function as one class. Tradition & Outlook The Spiritmaster tradition develops from Atreia’s mage disciplines but turns outward toward spirits, elemental forces, and the difficult art of directing entities shaped by Aether. Spiritmasters are often patient observers, researchers, summoners, or specialists in threats that cannot be understood through ordinary physical study. Their beliefs about spirits differ: some emphasize command, others partnership, responsibility, curiosity, or respect for elemental power. Appearance & Adventuring Spiritmasters use cloth armor and magical implements, while the visible presence of a summoned spirit often defines their silhouette more strongly than clothing does. Their equipment may include ritual, scholarly, or elemental motifs without creating additional mechanics. They adventure to understand unusual spirits, recover lost summoning knowledge, counter supernatural threats, serve as versatile magical operatives, or deepen the bond between Daeva and elemental ally. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Martial Defender • Resolve • Challenge • Interception Templar “You're only as good as your armor.” The premier martial defender, turning incoming pressure into protection, damage reduction, retaliation, and formation control. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. Overview Class Chassis Resolve Signature Mechanics Action Reference Specializations Preview Levels 1–20 Defensive Examples Specialization Reassignment Class Overview The Templar is the system’s premier martial defender. It does not force enemies to attack it through mind control; instead, Challenge makes ignoring the Templar tactically dangerous while Resolve turns incoming pressure into protection, damage reduction, retaliation, and formation control. Class Identity Templars are guardian-warriors whose strength is measured by what they can endure and whom they can keep standing. They occupy the most dangerous space in a battle, challenge enemies that would otherwise overwhelm vulnerable allies, and turn personal resilience into protection for the group. Resolve is the mechanical expression of this identity: a Templar grows most meaningful when danger is real and protection requires commitment. Tradition & Outlook The Templar tradition grows from Atreia’s warrior disciplines but places duty, discipline, guardianship, and control above personal glory. Templars are found among legion defenders, fortress guardians, sworn protectors, escorts, and Daevas who believe power carries an obligation to stand between danger and others. Individual Templars may be stern, compassionate, devout, pragmatic, or fiercely patriotic, but the class ideal is constancy under pressure. Appearance & Adventuring Templars are commonly associated with plate armor, shields, and the unmistakable silhouette of a heavily protected frontline Daeva. Their equipment tends to emphasize readiness and endurance rather than ornament alone. Templars adventure because someone must hold the line: to defend a community, fulfill an oath, guard companions, reclaim threatened territory, or confront enemies that cannot safely be allowed to reach the rest of the party. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Class Ability Constitution Weapon Ability Strength Hit Die d12 Hit Points at Level 1 16 + CON modifier Hit Points at Higher Levels Roll d12 or use fixed 7, add CON modifier, then add +4 maximum HP from Templar durability each Templar level after 1. text: Spell Acquisition. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Aether & Spellcasting Aether environment and interaction, universal spellcasting, and Spell Advancement. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Aether Environment, Interaction & Gathering Aether Interaction Aether Sources Refined Aether Gathering Aether Hazards Universal Spellcasting Universal Model Spell Acquisition Aether Environment, Interaction & Gathering Aether Interaction Aether Interaction uses Intelligence (Arcana) for intellectual analysis and Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) for physical manipulation. Typical DC guidance is 10, 12, 15, 18, or 20+ according to complexity and danger. Aether Sources Nodes, Currents, Fissures, and other environmental Aether phenomena can provide opportunities, hazards, travel effects, or Refined Aether. Their exact scene behavior is defined by the source. Refined Aether Gathering Gathering Refined Aether uses Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) against the source DC. Aether Level DC Yield Range Default Yield 1 8 2–6 4 2 10 6–12 9 3 12 12–24 18 4 15 24–40 32 5 18 40–60 50 The GM identifies a valid source and its Aether Level. Only the interacting character rolls. Apply normal modifiers and Help only if actually meaningful. On success, gain a yield within the listed range based on source richness; if no special richness is established, use the Default Yield. A successful gathering normally exhausts that source. Multiple deposits exist only when the GM explicitly establishes them. Failure gives no Refined Aether and does not automatically exhaust the source, but a new attempt requires a meaningful change in circumstances. Another party member does not automatically create a fresh attempt. Normal gathering is not performed during active combat unless gathering itself is an explicit encounter objective. Already-refined Aether recovered from caches or stores is ordinary loot and requires no gathering check. Aether Hazards Aether Hazards use the universal sequence Trigger → Save → DC → Effect → Duration. Standard severity bands are Minor DC 10–11, Moderate DC 12–14, Severe DC 15–17, and Extreme DC 18–20+. The four approved hazard families are Aether Storm, Aether Surge, Aether Eruption, and Unstable Zone. Each specific hazard defines its actual Trigger, Save, Effect, and Duration. Dangerous Aether changes are normally telegraphed in advance unless the hazard is specifically concealed. Strategic Refined Aether uses not defined in this handbook are deferred unless a future subsystem explicitly establishes them. Vehicle-related Refined Aether rules remain deferred with vehicle rules, and the current Abyss Warfront system uses no universal Refined Aether conversion for Fortress power. Universal Spellcasting Universal Model WoA has no spell slots and no cantrip category. Each spell is individually At-Will, Cooldown-based, Short-Rest limited, or Long-Rest limited. Class resources may modify spells but are not universal casting costs. Spell Acquisition Spells are class-granted abilities. They cannot be bought, sold, looted, copied from spellbooks or scrolls, learned from vendors, or acquired by commerce or exploration. A spell becomes available only when the character reaches its Unlock Level and, when applicable, satisfies the immediately preceding spell in its linear prerequisite chain. Unlocking a later spell never removes the earlier spell. Newly unlocked spells begin at Spell Level 1 unless explicitly stated otherwise. Spell Advancement — Final Rule. A class grants Spell Advancements according to its finalized progression. One Spell Advancement raises one eligible unlocked spell by 1 Spell Level, subject to that class’s Maximum Spell Level and listed prerequisites. Unspent Spell Advancements may be banked indefinitely, but banked or newly earned Spell Advancements may be spent only when the character gains a level; they cannot normally be spent during an adventure, between encounters, or during a rest. A character cannot spend more Spell Advancements than they have earned. Spell Retraining. There is no universal spell retraining. Once a Spell Advancement is spent, it is permanent unless a specific class feature, explicit story effect, or GM-approved exceptional circumstance directly permits reassignment. Casting Frequency and Action Economy At-Will spells may be cast whenever action economy permits. Cooldown X spells become available at the start of the caster’s Xth turn after the casting turn. Round-based cooldowns advance only during genuine combat; artificial Initiative cannot refresh, farm, or manipulate cooldowns or class resources. Outside genuine combat, a Cooldown spell becomes available again 1 minute after use unless the spell states a longer restriction. Short-Rest and Long-Rest spells regain uses after the named rest. Casting Time is binding.

text: Spell Resolution Rules. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Aether & Spellcasting Aether environment and interaction, universal spellcasting, and Spell Advancement. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Aether Environment, Interaction & Gathering Aether Interaction Aether Sources Refined Aether Gathering Aether Hazards Universal Spellcasting Universal Model Spell Acquisition Aether Environment, Interaction & Gathering Aether Interaction Aether Interaction uses Intelligence (Arcana) for intellectual analysis and Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) for physical manipulation. Typical DC guidance is 10, 12, 15, 18, or 20+ according to complexity and danger. Aether Sources Nodes, Currents, Fissures, and other environmental Aether phenomena can provide opportunities, hazards, travel effects, or Refined Aether. Their exact scene behavior is defined by the source. Refined Aether Gathering Gathering Refined Aether uses Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) against the source DC. Aether Level DC Yield Range Default Yield 1 8 2–6 4 2 10 6–12 9 3 12 12–24 18 4 15 24–40 32 5 18 40–60 50 The GM identifies a valid source and its Aether Level. Only the interacting character rolls. Apply normal modifiers and Help only if actually meaningful. On success, gain a yield within the listed range based on source richness; if no special richness is established, use the Default Yield. A successful gathering normally exhausts that source. Multiple deposits exist only when the GM explicitly establishes them. Failure gives no Refined Aether and does not automatically exhaust the source, but a new attempt requires a meaningful change in circumstances. Another party member does not automatically create a fresh attempt. Normal gathering is not performed during active combat unless gathering itself is an explicit encounter objective. Already-refined Aether recovered from caches or stores is ordinary loot and requires no gathering check. Aether Hazards Aether Hazards use the universal sequence Trigger → Save → DC → Effect → Duration. Standard severity bands are Minor DC 10–11, Moderate DC 12–14, Severe DC 15–17, and Extreme DC 18–20+. The four approved hazard families are Aether Storm, Aether Surge, Aether Eruption, and Unstable Zone. Each specific hazard defines its actual Trigger, Save, Effect, and Duration. Dangerous Aether changes are normally telegraphed in advance unless the hazard is specifically concealed. Strategic Refined Aether uses not defined in this handbook are deferred unless a future subsystem explicitly establishes them. Vehicle-related Refined Aether rules remain deferred with vehicle rules, and the current Abyss Warfront system uses no universal Refined Aether conversion for Fortress power. Universal Spellcasting Universal Model WoA has no spell slots and no cantrip category. Each spell is individually At-Will, Cooldown-based, Short-Rest limited, or Long-Rest limited. Class resources may modify spells but are not universal casting costs. Spell Acquisition Spells are class-granted abilities. They cannot be bought, sold, looted, copied from spellbooks or scrolls, learned from vendors, or acquired by commerce or exploration. A spell becomes available only when the character reaches its Unlock Level and, when applicable, satisfies the immediately preceding spell in its linear prerequisite chain. Unlocking a later spell never removes the earlier spell. Newly unlocked spells begin at Spell Level 1 unless explicitly stated otherwise. Spell Advancement — Final Rule. A class grants Spell Advancements according to its finalized progression. One Spell Advancement raises one eligible unlocked spell by 1 Spell Level, subject to that class’s Maximum Spell Level and listed prerequisites. Unspent Spell Advancements may be banked indefinitely, but banked or newly earned Spell Advancements may be spent only when the character gains a level; they cannot normally be spent during an adventure, between encounters, or during a rest. A character cannot spend more Spell Advancements than they have earned. Spell Retraining. There is no universal spell retraining. Once a Spell Advancement is spent, it is permanent unless a specific class feature, explicit story effect, or GM-approved exceptional circumstance directly permits reassignment. Casting Frequency and Action Economy At-Will spells may be cast whenever action economy permits. Cooldown X spells become available at the start of the caster’s Xth turn after the casting turn. Round-based cooldowns advance only during genuine combat; artificial Initiative cannot refresh, farm, or manipulate cooldowns or class resources. Outside genuine combat, a Cooldown spell becomes available again 1 minute after use unless the spell states a longer restriction. Short-Rest and Long-Rest spells regain uses after the named rest. text: Spellcasting Example. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Full Caster • Elemental Damage • Aether Focus • Spell Shaping Sorcerer “This will only hurt for a second.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Spellcasting Reference: Sorcerer has a dedicated spell-list page for quick browsing. View Sorcerer Spell List → Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Aether Focus Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Spell List Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Spellcasting Example Specialization Reassignment The Sorcerer is the raw magical-damage benchmark. It casts through Fire, Ice, Lightning, and Wind spell chains, then spends Aether Focus only when a particular spell needs more damage, area, control pressure, or reliability. Aether Focus enhances spells; it is never the fuel required to cast ordinary Sorcerer spells. Class Identity Sorcerers are masters of direct Aetheric spellcraft, combining destructive magic with the ability to control the shape and tempo of a fight. They can punish clustered enemies, deny movement or action, and unleash powerful spells when an opening appears. Aether Focus represents the concentration and arcane discipline required to turn immense magical potential into reliable battlefield power. Tradition & Outlook The Sorcerer tradition grows from Atreia’s mage disciplines and is associated with formal magical study, experimentation, academies, battlefield arcanists, and Daevas fascinated by the structure of Aether itself. Sorcerers commonly value knowledge, precision, preparation, and intellectual mastery, although their personalities range from scholarly restraint to spectacular confidence. For many, magic is both a weapon and a language through which Atreia can be understood. Appearance & Adventuring Sorcerers favor cloth armor and magical implements such as Orbs and Spellbooks under the Wings of Atreia equipment rules. Their appearance may reflect academic, military, ceremonial, or highly individual magical traditions. They adventure to recover lost knowledge, study Aetheric phenomena, test magical theories, defend their people with overwhelming spellcraft, or confront powers that ordinary weapons cannot adequately answer. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Ability Intelligence Secondary Ability Wisdom Hit Die d6 Saving Throws Constitution, Intelligence Armor Cloth Implements Magical Orbs, Spellbooks Spellcasting Ability INT Spell Save DC 8 + PB + INT modifier Spell Attack PB + INT modifier Signature Resource Aether Focus Spell Advancements +2 every class level after 1; 38 total Maximum Spell Level 9 Extra Attack None Core Engine — Aether Focus Maximum Aether Focus equals PB + INT modifier, minimum 2. A Long Rest restores all expended Aether Focus. A Short Rest restores Aether Focus equal to PB, up to your maximum. The resource is an enhancement reserve: casting an ordinary Sorcerer spell never requires Aether Focus unless a spell or class feature explicitly says otherwise. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Starting State Aether Focus is a rest-based enhancement reserve and does not reset merely because combat begins or ends. After a Long Rest it is normally full. Maximum PB + INT modifier, minimum 2. Aether Sage and the Level 20 capstone can explicitly increase this maximum. Rest Recovery Long Rest restores all expended Aether Focus. Short Rest restores Focus equal to PB, up to maximum; Aether Sage can improve this recovery. Base Generation The base Sorcerer does not generate Aether Focus from ordinary spell hits or damage. Combat refunds exist only where a class or specialization feature explicitly grants them. How You Spend It Intensify 1 Focus; Widen 1 Focus; Potent Control 1 Focus; other Sorcerer features spend Aether Focus only when their text states a cost. Ordinary spellcasting costs no Focus. Refunds / Discounts Aether Sage and later features may discount a shaping cost or refund Focus after a qualifying shaped spell. A refund is not a second casting or a new spell trigger. Persistence Unused Aether Focus persists between encounters until spent or restored. Important Distinction Aether Focus is a Sorcerer class resource. It is not environmental Aether, Refined Aether, an Aether State, or a universal damage type. Spellcasting Reference: Spiritmaster has a dedicated spell-list page for quick browsing. View Spiritmaster Spell List → Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Summon Spirit Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Spell List Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequence Specialization Reassignment The Spiritmaster is a two-body tactical caster. One active elemental spirit shares the Spiritmaster’s turn and action economy; together they equal one complete player character. The class establishes two battlefield positions, casts through the spirit, and earns Spirit Bond only through meaningful master-spirit coordination. Class Identity Spiritmasters are binders and commanders of elemental spirits who fight as a partnership rather than as a solitary caster. Their strength comes from coordinating their own spellcraft with a Greater Spirit, applying pressure, disruption, and control across more than one position on the battlefield. Spirit Bond represents the relationship and command structure that makes this divided presence function as one class. Tradition & Outlook The Spiritmaster tradition develops from Atreia’s mage disciplines but turns outward toward spirits, elemental forces, and the difficult art of directing entities shaped by Aether. Spiritmasters are often patient observers, researchers, summoners, or specialists in threats that cannot be understood through ordinary physical study. Their beliefs about spirits differ: some emphasize command, others partnership, responsibility, curiosity, or respect for elemental power. Appearance & Adventuring Spiritmasters use cloth armor and magical implements, while the visible presence of a summoned spirit often defines their silhouette more strongly than clothing does. Their equipment may include ritual, scholarly, or elemental motifs without creating additional mechanics. They adventure to understand unusual spirits, recover lost summoning knowledge, counter supernatural threats, serve as versatile magical operatives, or deepen the bond between Daeva and elemental ally. Maximum Bond is 3 at Level 1, 4 at Level 2, 5 at Level 5, and 6 at Level 9; Bondweaver increases this maximum by 1 from Level 3 onward. Once on each of your turns, gain 1 Spirit Bond if both you and your spirit successfully affect hostile creatures during that turn. Successfully Affect means damage, a hit, a failed save, meaningful hostile condition/penalty, forced movement, or another real combat effect. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Combat Turn structure, actions, movement, attacks, damage, conditions, death, rests, and survival. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative Round and Turn Action Economy Attack Action Universal Actions Ready Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative, rounds, and combat-only resources are used only for genuine combat or another situation where structured turn order is necessary. Characters cannot manufacture artificial combat to farm cooldowns, resources, or timing triggers. Initiative Initiative = 1d20 + Dexterity modifier. Do not add PB unless an explicit feature says so. Alert adds +2 Initiative. There is no Surprise Round and Surprise does not grant Advantage on Initiative. When one side genuinely catches another side unaware, the GM may, at discretion, allow one appropriate pre-Initiative attack roll against the target's normal defense before Initiative is rolled. This is not an extra round, is not automatic, and does not create a general Surprise action economy. After that resolution, roll Initiative normally. Round and Turn One combat round represents approximately six seconds in the game world. Each participant normally takes one turn in Initiative order. All turns in the round abstract actions occurring within the same six-second span; do not add each turn as another six seconds. Action Economy Action. One per turn. Movement. Up to the creature’s available movement, subject to terrain and conditions. Bonus Action. Up to one, but only when a feature grants something that uses a Bonus Action. Reaction. Normally one per round, refreshing at the start of the creature’s turn unless an explicit class rule says otherwise. Object interaction. One free simple object interaction per turn. There is no universal Action-to-Bonus-Action or Bonus-Action-to-Action conversion. Unused movement or Actions are not stored for later turns. Attack Action The Attack Action makes one attack unless a feature such as Extra Attack says otherwise. Grapple and Shove are full Actions and do not replace one attack within Extra Attack. Player Weapon Requirement. A player character must be wielding an approved class weapon to take the normal Attack Action. Unarmed Attacks and Improvised Weapons are not player combat options unless a later explicit feature creates a specific exception. Opportunity Attacks. Opportunity Attacks remain part of the core combat rules. When a hostile creature you can perceive voluntarily leaves your melee reach, you may use your Reaction to make one melee attack against it, resolving the attack before it leaves that reach. Forced movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Universal Actions Dash. Gain additional movement equal to your current Speed for the turn. Difficult Terrain and other movement costs still apply. While flying, Dash adds horizontal movement but does not grant an additional altitude-layer change. Disengage. Until the end of your turn, your movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks. Dodge. Until the start of your next turn, attacks against you have Disadvantage if you can perceive the attacker, and you have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws. Dodge ends if you become Incapacitated or your Speed becomes 0. Hide. You must have meaningful concealment or another circumstance that allows hiding. Make Dexterity (Stealth) against Passive Perception or active Perception as appropriate. You cannot Hide while clearly seen. Hidden is not Invisible. Making an attack reveals your position after that attack resolves. Search. Deliberately search using a GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation). Use Object. Use this Action for substantial manipulation beyond the one free simple object interaction. A specific item’s activation rule controls when it states another cost. Ready A creature can prepare one Action for a perceivable trigger. When the trigger occurs, the creature may use its Reaction to perform the readied Action. Ready does not store ordinary movement, but Dash can be readied as the Action. Readied attacks retain all weapon properties. A readied spell must still meet implement and targeting requirements when released. Losing a mandatory implement before release prevents release. Concentration begins when the spell actually resolves. Ready never bypasses aerial restrictions, range, or other universal rules. Simultaneous Effects Effects resolve one at a time. The active creature orders its own simultaneous effects; the GM orders GM-controlled simultaneous effects. For opposing same-time effects, resolve the active creature first, then use Initiative if needed. Damage resolves before state changes caused by that damage. Start-o

Either way, you'll only die tired.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Focus Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Ranger is a nonmagical ranged hunter that controls enemy movement with persistent battlefield traps, spends Focus on precision or evasive shots, and is rewarded for exploiting targets that walk into prepared terrain. Its sustained damage comes from two ranged attacks, not from spellcasting or a third standard attack. Class Identity Rangers are mobile ranged specialists who control distance through marksmanship, movement, traps, and battlefield awareness. They are most effective when they can read terrain before committing, choose favorable lines of attack, and punish enemies that approach carelessly. Focus represents the Ranger’s ability to convert patience and perception into precise action. Tradition & Outlook The Ranger tradition also descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines, but where Assassins close with a chosen target, Rangers cultivate distance, fieldcraft, and control of the approach. Rangers are common among scouts, hunters, pathfinders, border wardens, reconnaissance troops, and independent Daevas accustomed to surviving beyond secure settlements. They tend to value preparedness, observation, mobility, and freedom of movement. Appearance & Adventuring Rangers usually wear mobile armor and carry bows, ammunition, traps, and field equipment suited to extended movement. Their gear often reflects the terrain in which they learned their craft. Rangers adventure to explore dangerous regions, hunt monsters or enemy operatives, guide expeditions, secure routes, protect remote communities, or prove that no battlefield is truly open ground when preparation and range are on their side. A Long Rest restores all expended Focus. A Short Rest restores Focus equal to PB, up to your maximum. Focus is a tactical reserve rather than ammunition or a tax on ordinary ranged attacks; Ranger Traps normally cost no Focus. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Starting State Focus is a rest-based reserve and does not reset merely because combat begins or ends. After a Long Rest it is normally full. Maximum PB + WIS modifier, minimum 2. Rest Recovery Long Rest restores all expended Focus. Short Rest restores Focus equal to PB, up to your maximum. Combat Recovery Hunter’s Rhythm and certain later Ranger/specialization features can regain Focus during genuine combat when their tactical conditions are actually satisfied. How You Spend It Precision Shot 1 Focus; Pinning Shot 1 Focus; Evasive Step 1 Focus; Deadeye Perfect Shot 1 Focus. Other Ranger features spend Focus only when their text states a cost. Refunds / Recovery A combat refund or recovery is not a new attack, trap trigger, or separate technique. It simply restores Focus up to your maximum. Persistence Unused Focus persists between encounters until spent or restored; there is no automatic combat-end reset. Does Not Generate Standing still and firing, harmless staged interactions, or ordinary trap placement do not create Focus unless an explicit recovery feature is actually triggered. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Tempo • Firearm Rhythm • Reload Mastery • Mobile Precision Gunslinger “A bullet sounds the same to everybody.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Tempo, Firearms, and Reload Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Tradition & Outlook Specialization Reassignment The Gunslinger is a mobile firearm martial whose power comes from maintaining Tempo through successful firearm play. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Fire. Move. Reload. Keep the rhythm alive long enough to turn Tempo into control, defense, and lethal pressure. Class Identity Gunslingers are technist marksmen who turn Aether-assisted firearms into speed, precision, and controlled ranged pressure. Pistols support rapid, mobile sequences through Quick Shot and Akimbo, while Muskets provide deliberate two-handed fire that concentrates Tempo into stronger individual hits through Deliberate Shot. Tempo represents the Gunslinger’s ability to build combat rhythm through successful action rather than treating every shot as an isolated event. Tradition & Outlook Gunslingers belong to Atreia’s newer technological traditions. The wider Aion tradition describes early firearm research being dismissed as technist tinkering until battlefield success forced major institutions to recognize the discipline. Wings of Atreia keeps that identity of innovation earning legitimacy through results while using Pistols and Muskets as the class’s only firearm categories. Gunslingers often value nerve, technical familiarity, accuracy, independence, and adaptability. Appearance & Adventuring Gunslingers favor mobile equipment, ammunition management, firearm maintenance, and a practical awareness of range and firing position. Their weapons can make them look strikingly modern beside older martial traditions, but their discipline remains Aetheric and distinctly Atreian. They adventure to test new techniques, serve as ranged specialists, hunt dangerous targets, protect expeditions from positions others cannot exploit, or demonstrate that innovation has earned its place in the war for Atreia. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols Ranged Gunslinger One-handed Weapon Attack. Range 30/90 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d8 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. A Gunslinger can wield two Pistols, but doing so does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols are compatible with Quick Shot and Akimbo. Muskets Ranged Gunslinger Two-handed Weapon Attack. Range 60/180 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d12 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. Ammunition capacity is fixed at 2. Muskets cannot use Quick Shot or Akimbo. Gunslinger ammunition-restoration features can restore Musket shots normally, but a Musket can never hold more than 2 shots. Standard one-handed firearm capacity increases do not apply to Muskets. Reload Every firearm attack consumes one shot. A firearm with no shots remaining is Empty and cannot make firearm attacks until at least one shot is restored. Normal Bonus Action Reload: an Empty firearm is restored to its full Reload capacity. Ammunition restoration is not the Reload action unless a feature explicitly says so. Ammunition-restoration features can restore shots to either Pistols or Muskets up to that firearm's maximum capacity. A Musket's maximum capacity remains 2. Switching between carried one-handed Gunslinger firearms as part of a firearm attack requires no separate object interaction. Standard one-handed firearm capacity progression: Ammo Capacity 4 at Levels 1-4, Ammo Capacity 5 at 5-8, Ammo Capacity 6 at 9-14, and Ammo Capacity 7 at 15-20. Increasing capacity does not automatically reload an Empty firearm. Tempo Tempo is a genuine-combat resource representing firing rhythm, accuracy, and momentum. It begins at 0, resets to 0 when combat ends, and artificial initiative cannot generate it. Maximum Tempo: Levels 1-4 = 3; 5-8 = 4; 9-12 = 5; 13-16 = 6; 17-20 = 7. Clean Hit: after you hit a hostile

WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Exploration & Interaction Vision, stealth, traps, locks, theft, hazards, social rules, chases, and loot. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Vision, Stealth, Traps, Locks & Theft Vision and Light Cover, Line of Sight & Line of Effect Stealth and Infiltration Traps and Non-Aether Hazards Locks Theft and Pickpocket Social Interaction, Information & Captivity Vision, Stealth, Traps, Locks & Theft Vision and Light Light states are Bright Light, Dim Light, and Darkness. Obscuration states are Lightly Obscured and Heavily Obscured. Dim Light lightly obscures; Darkness heavily obscures a creature that cannot otherwise see through it. Daeva Darkvision treats Darkness within 60 feet as Dim Light, not Bright Light. A recommended ordinary light source has a stated Bright radius plus an equal additional Dim radius unless its own text says otherwise. Bright light does not universally prohibit Stealth. Obscurity and Invisibility do not automatically make a creature Hidden. Cover, Line of Sight & Line of Effect No Cover. No defensive benefit from Cover. Half Cover. A creature or object behind meaningful partial obstruction gains +2 AC and +2 to Dexterity saving throws against effects originating from the covered direction. Intervening creatures can provide Half Cover when they materially obstruct the line. Full Cover. Full Cover blocks the relevant Line of Effect and prevents direct targeting through that obstruction unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Three-Quarters Cover does not exist in Wings of Atreia. Cover does not stack; use the best applicable Cover. Altitude neither inherently grants nor ignores Cover. Line of Sight and Line of Effect are distinct. Line of Sight determines whether you can see a target or point. Line of Effect determines whether an attack, spell, or effect can physically reach it. Heavy obscurement is not Cover by itself. Stealth and Infiltration Use scene states Undetected, Suspicious, and Alerted; these are not Conditions. Stealth must exceed Passive Perception; ties favor the observer. An active Search uses the GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation), against the relevant DC or opposing Stealth; ties favor the Searcher where opposed. Do not reroll Stealth every 5 feet; roll again only when circumstances materially change. For group Stealth, at least half the group must succeed. A failed check may create Suspicion rather than immediate full alarm when appropriate. Distractions create an opportunity to Hide rather than automatic success. Disguises are primarily social. Invisibility is not the same as Hidden. Wings do not automatically prevent Stealth. Traps and Non-Aether Hazards Describe a hazard with Trigger, Detection, Avoid/Disable method, Save/Check, Effect, and Reset/Duration. Hazards may be obvious, concealed, or hidden. Detection normally uses Passive Perception, active Perception, or Investigation. Disable methods depend on the mechanism and can use Sleight of Hand, Investigation, Athletics, or another appropriate Skill. There is no mandatory Thieves’ Tools system. Failure triggers the hazard only when the hazard says so. Damage and Conditions use existing universal rules. Forced movement is horizontal unless the hazard explicitly creates vertical displacement. Hazards normally resolve when triggered rather than taking their own Initiative turns. Repeat attempts require changed circumstances. Locks Mechanical Lock DC Simple 10 Standard 12 Secure 15 High Security 18 Exceptional 20+ The correct key opens a normal lock without a check. Mechanical locks generally use Dexterity (Sleight of Hand). Unusual mechanisms can use Intelligence (Investigation). Forcing uses Strength (Athletics); destroying a lock or door uses normal object/destruction adjudication. Failure does not automatically break or trigger a lock unless its design says so. Aether locks use Aether Interaction. If a task is impossible, do not assign an absurd DC—state that it cannot be done by that method. Theft and Pickpocket A theft attempt requires a plausible opportunity. Taking an accessible small item uses Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) against Passive Perception and must exceed it. If the target is actively watching, oppose with active Perception; ties favor the observer. Secured items can require a different approach. Failure may create suspicion or alarm. Success means the theft was unnoticed at that moment; later discovery remains possible. Distraction creates opportunity rather than automatic success. Help can grant +2 when genuinely meaningful. Worn armor, shields, Wings, wielded weapons, and equipped mandatory implements cannot simply be pickpocketed. Repeated attempts require changed circumstances. Social Interaction, Information &

Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative Round and Turn Action Economy Attack Action Universal Actions Ready Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative, rounds, and combat-only resources are used only for genuine combat or another situation where structured turn order is necessary. Characters cannot manufacture artificial combat to farm cooldowns, resources, or timing triggers. Initiative Initiative = 1d20 + Dexterity modifier. Do not add PB unless an explicit feature says so. Alert adds +2 Initiative. There is no Surprise Round and Surprise does not grant Advantage on Initiative. When one side genuinely catches another side unaware, the GM may, at discretion, allow one appropriate pre-Initiative attack roll against the target's normal defense before Initiative is rolled. This is not an extra round, is not automatic, and does not create a general Surprise action economy. After that resolution, roll Initiative normally. Round and Turn One combat round represents approximately six seconds in the game world. Each participant normally takes one turn in Initiative order. All turns in the round abstract actions occurring within the same six-second span; do not add each turn as another six seconds. Action Economy Action. One per turn. Movement. Up to the creature’s available movement, subject to terrain and conditions. Bonus Action. Up to one, but only when a feature grants something that uses a Bonus Action. Reaction. Normally one per round, refreshing at the start of the creature’s turn unless an explicit class rule says otherwise. Object interaction. One free simple object interaction per turn. There is no universal Action-to-Bonus-Action or Bonus-Action-to-Action conversion. Unused movement or Actions are not stored for later turns. Attack Action The Attack Action makes one attack unless a feature such as Extra Attack says otherwise. Grapple and Shove are full Actions and do not replace one attack within Extra Attack. Player Weapon Requirement. A player character must be wielding an approved class weapon to take the normal Attack Action. Unarmed Attacks and Improvised Weapons are not player combat options unless a later explicit feature creates a specific exception. Opportunity Attacks. Opportunity Attacks remain part of the core combat rules. When a hostile creature you can perceive voluntarily leaves your melee reach, you may use your Reaction to make one melee attack against it, resolving the attack before it leaves that reach. Forced movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Universal Actions Dash. Gain additional movement equal to your current Speed for the turn. Difficult Terrain and other movement costs still apply. While flying, Dash adds horizontal movement but does not grant an additional altitude-layer change. Disengage. Until the end of your turn, your movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks. Dodge. Until the start of your next turn, attacks against you have Disadvantage if you can perceive the attacker, and you have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws. Dodge ends if you become Incapacitated or your Speed becomes 0. Hide. You must have meaningful concealment or another circumstance that allows hiding. Make Dexterity (Stealth) against Passive Perception or active Perception as appropriate. You cannot Hide while clearly seen. Hidden is not Invisible. Making an attack reveals your position after that attack resolves. Search. Deliberately search using a GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation). Use Object. Use this Action for substantial manipulation beyond the one free simple object interaction. A specific item’s activation rule controls when it states another cost. Ready A creature can prepare one Action for a perceivable trigger. When the trigger occurs, the creature may use its Reaction to perform the readied Action. Ready does not store ordinary movement, but Dash can be readied as the Action. Readied attacks retain all weapon properties. A readied spell must still meet implement and targeting requirements when released. Losing a mandatory implement before release prevents release. Concentration begins when the spell actually resolves. Ready never bypasses aerial restrictions, range, or other universal rules. Simultaneous Effects Effects resolve one at a time. The active creature orders its own simultaneous effects; the GM orders GM-controlled simultaneous effects. For opposing same-time effects, resolve the active creature first, then use Initiative if needed. Damage resolves before state changes caused by that damage. Start-of-tu

WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Tempo • Firearm Rhythm • Reload Mastery • Mobile Precision Gunslinger “A bullet sounds the same to everybody.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Tempo, Firearms, and Reload Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Tradition & Outlook Specialization Reassignment The Gunslinger is a mobile firearm martial whose power comes from maintaining Tempo through successful firearm play. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Fire. Move. Reload. Keep the rhythm alive long enough to turn Tempo into control, defense, and lethal pressure. Class Identity Gunslingers are technist marksmen who turn Aether-assisted firearms into speed, precision, and controlled ranged pressure. Pistols support rapid, mobile sequences through Quick Shot and Akimbo, while Muskets provide deliberate two-handed fire that concentrates Tempo into stronger individual hits through Deliberate Shot. Tempo represents the Gunslinger’s ability to build combat rhythm through successful action rather than treating every shot as an isolated event. Tradition & Outlook Gunslingers belong to Atreia’s newer technological traditions. The wider Aion tradition describes early firearm research being dismissed as technist tinkering until battlefield success forced major institutions to recognize the discipline. Wings of Atreia keeps that identity of innovation earning legitimacy through results while using Pistols and Muskets as the class’s only firearm categories. Gunslingers often value nerve, technical familiarity, accuracy, independence, and adaptability. Appearance & Adventuring Gunslingers favor mobile equipment, ammunition management, firearm maintenance, and a practical awareness of range and firing position. Their weapons can make them look strikingly modern beside older martial traditions, but their discipline remains Aetheric and distinctly Atreian. They adventure to test new techniques, serve as ranged specialists, hunt dangerous targets, protect expeditions from positions others cannot exploit, or demonstrate that innovation has earned its place in the war for Atreia. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols Ranged Gunslinger One-handed Weapon Attack. Range 30/90 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d8 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. A Gunslinger can wield two Pistols, but doing so does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols are compatible with Quick Shot and Akimbo. Muskets Ranged Gunslinger Two-handed Weapon Attack. Range 60/180 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d12 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. Ammunition capacity is fixed at 2. Muskets cannot use Quick Shot or Akimbo. Gunslinger ammunition-restoration features can restore Musket shots normally, but a Musket can never hold more than 2 shots. Standard one-handed firearm capacity increases do not apply to Muskets. Reload Every firearm attack consumes one shot. A firearm with no shots remaining is Empty and cannot make firearm attacks until at least one shot is restored. Normal Bonus Action Reload: an Empty firearm is restored to its full Reload capacity. Ammunition restoration is not the Reload action unless a feature explicitly says so. Ammunition-restoration features can restore shots to either Pistols or Muskets up to that firearm's maximum capacity. A Musket's maximum capacity remains 2. Switching between carried one-handed Gunslinger firearms as part of a firearm attack requires no separate object interaction. Standard one-handed firearm capacity progression: Ammo Capacity 4 at Levels 1-4, Ammo Capacity 5 at 5-8, Ammo Capacity 6 at 9-14, and Ammo Capacity 7 at 15-20. Increasing capacity does not automatically reload an Empty firearm. Tempo Tempo is a genuine-combat resource representing firing rhythm, accuracy, and momentum.
