title: Templar | Wings of Atreia
desc: Complete player reference for the Templar class in Wings of Atreia, based on Player Handbook v3.10.
text: WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Martial Defender • Resolve • Challenge • Interception Templar “You're only as good as your armor.” The premier martial defender, turning incoming pressure into protection, damage reduction, retaliation, and formation control. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. Overview Class Chassis Resolve Signature Mechanics Action Reference Specializations Preview Levels 1–20 Defensive Examples Specialization Reassignment Class Overview The Templar is the system’s premier martial defender. It does not force enemies to attack it through mind control; instead, Challenge makes ignoring the Templar tactically dangerous while Resolve turns incoming pressure into protection, damage reduction, retaliation, and formation control. Class Identity Templars are guardian-warriors whose strength is measured by what they can endure and whom they can keep standing. They occupy the most dangerous space in a battle, challenge enemies that would otherwise overwhelm vulnerable allies, and turn personal resilience into protection for the group. Resolve is the mechanical expression of this identity: a Templar grows most meaningful when danger is real and protection requires commitment. Tradition & Outlook The Templar tradition grows from Atreia’s warrior disciplines but places duty, discipline, guardianship, and control above personal glory. Templars are found among legion defenders, fortress guardians, sworn protectors, escorts, and Daevas who believe power carries an obligation to stand between danger and others. Individual Templars may be stern, compassionate, devout, pragmatic, or fiercely patriotic, but the class ideal is constancy under pressure. Appearance & Adventuring Templars are commonly associated with plate armor, shields, and the unmistakable silhouette of a heavily protected frontline Daeva. Their equipment tends to emphasize readiness and endurance rather than ornament alone. Templars adventure because someone must hold the line: to defend a community, fulfill an oath, guard companions, reclaim threatened territory, or confront enemies that cannot safely be allowed to reach the rest of the party. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Class Ability Constitution Weapon Ability Strength Hit Die d12 Hit Points at Level 1 16 + CON modifier Hit Points at Higher Levels Roll d12 or use fixed 7, add CON modifier, then add +4 maximum HP from Templar durability each Templar level after 1. Saving Throws Strength, Constitution Armor Chain Armor, Plate Armor, Round/Medium/Tower Shields Skills Choose 2 from 6: Athletics, History, Insight, Intimidation, Medicine, Perception Weapons Longswords, Polearms, Maces Class Save DC 8 + PB + CON modifier Signature Resource Resolve Signature Mechanics Resolute Guard, Challenge, Guardian’s Intercession Extra Attack Level 5; two attacks only Spellcasting None Core Engine — Resolve Resolve represents the Templar converting battlefield pressure into defensive certainty. Unless a later feature states otherwise, Resolve becomes 0 when Initiative is rolled, becomes 0 when combat ends, and cannot be gained while you are Incapacitated. Hold the Line: gain 1 Resolve when a hostile creature you can see hits you with an attack while you are within that creature’s melee reach. Protect the Vulnerable: gain 1 Resolve when a Templar class feature successfully reduces, prevents, redirects, or intercepts damage that would otherwise be dealt to another creature, or when a feature explicitly says the protection qualifies. Defy the Templar: gain 1 Resolve when a creature Challenged by you attacks another creature while you were a valid target for that attack. You can normally gain no more than 1 Resolve during any creature’s turn. One event grants Resolve only once even if it satisfies multiple triggers. Maximum Resolve: 3 at Levels 1–4; 4 at 5–8; 5 at 9–14; 6 at 15–20. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Starting State Resolve normally becomes 0 when Initiative is rolled. Later Templar features explicitly establish starting Resolve. Maximum 3 at Levels 1–4; 4 at 5–8; 5 at 9–14; 6 at 15–20. How You Gain It Hold the Line, Protect the Vulnerable, and Defy the Templar. Generation Limits Normally no more than 1 Resolve during any creature’s turn. One event grants Resolve only once even if it satisfies multiple triggers. No Resolve while Incapacitated. How You Spend It Resolute Guard 1; Guardian’s Rally 1; Bulwark Shared Resolve 1; Resolute Shelter 1; Bulwark Last Wall 1; Refuse to Fall 3. Other features spend Resolve only when their text states a cost. Same-Trigger Timing When a protection feature both resolves and legitimately generates Resolve, newly gained Resolve can pay an eligible same-trigger defensive technique when the feature permits the timing. Reset Resolve becomes 0 when combat ends. Resolve Timing Rules Resolve from Hold the Line may immediately be spent on Resolute Guard against the same triggering attack’s damage. Resolve generated by a successful Guardian’s Intercession is gained before redirected damage is applied, so it may be used against the redirected attack if otherwise legal. Resolve generated because Guardian’s Shelter changed a save from failure to success may immediately pay for Resolute Shelter at Level 14. Challenge may remain on a creature while its penalty is temporarily suppressed because you are out of range, cannot be perceived, or are not a legal target. Signature Defensive Mechanics Resolute Guard When you take damage from an attack, spend 1 Resolve with no action required to reduce that damage by 1 Guard Die + your CON modifier, minimum 0. The Guard Die is d6 at Level 1, d8 from Level 5, d10 from Level 9, and d12 from Level 15. You can normally use Resolute Guard only once per turn unless a Templar feature explicitly says otherwise. Challenge As a Bonus Action, choose one hostile creature you can see within 30 feet. It is Challenged until the start of your next turn. Initially you can maintain one Challenge. While the creature is within 30 feet, can perceive you, and you are a valid target for at least one attack it could make, it has Disadvantage on attack rolls against creatures other than you. Challenge is nonmagical, has no save, and is neither Charm nor Fear. Guardian’s Intercession When an ally within 5 feet is hit by an attack, use your Reaction to redirect that attack to yourself. Use the same attack roll. If it hits your AC, you take the attack and its damage/effects normally; if it misses your AC, the redirected attack misses. A successful interception qualifies for Protect the Vulnerable when it actually prevents the ally from receiving the attack’s damage. Disengage prevents it. 11 Unbreakable Resolve After Guard / No Action — Use Resolute Guard Choose Stand Firm, Reposition, or Press the Threat. 13 Guardian’s Rally Bonus Action 1 Resolve Self or ally within 10 ft Grant Guard Die + CON temporary HP until start of your next turn. 14 Resolute Shelter Triggered / No Action 1 Resolve Protected creature succeeds on save that normally deals half Cause that damage to become 0. 14 Last Wall (Bulwark) Triggered / No Action 1 Resolve Redirected Intercession attack hits Gain resistance to that attack before Resolute Guard. 15 Unshaken Resolve Initiative / No Action — Genuine combat begins Begin combat with 2 Resolve. 17 Unceasing Challenge Start of Turn / No Action — Existing Challenges meet conditions Maintain each qualifying Challenge without Bonus Action. 17 Defiant Resolve Triggered / No Action — First time each round a Challenged creature hits you That attack can grant Resolve even outside melee reach. 18 Second Templar Reaction Passive — Each round Second Reaction usable only for a Templar class feature. 20 Refuse to Fall Triggered / No Action 3 Resolve Damage would reduce you to 0; 1/Long Rest Drop to 1 HP instead if damage would not kill you outright. 20 Battle-Ready Resolve Initiative / No Action — Genuine combat begins Begin combat with 3 Resolve, up to maximum. 20 Resolve Through Sacrifice Triggered / No Action — Intercession or Shelter protects another and Protect the Vulnerable applies Gain 2 Resolve instead of 1; counts as one generation event. Coverage. This reference covers class options that create or materially change an Action, Bonus Action, Reaction, triggered player choice, or Resolve expenditure, refund, recovery, or starting state. Passive numerical scaling and universal advancement remain in the level progression. Specializations — Read Before You Choose Templar chooses an initial Specialization at Level 3. Use this preview before reading the Level 1–20 progression so you can see the playstyle each path develops into. Specialization features are gained at Levels 3, 6, 10, and 14. Specialization Preview Specialization Identity What You Can Expect Bulwark Interception and ally protection Improves Guardian’s Intercession, shared Resolve, emergency saves, and resistance while taking danger meant for allies. Best for players who want the strongest bodyguard identity. Justicar Challenge and retaliation defender Punishes enemies for defying Challenge through stronger reactions, control, and judgment. Best for players who want defense that actively threatens enemies who ignore them. Aegis Space-control defender Turns nearby space into difficult, punishing ground and increasingly prevents enemies from moving through your reach. Best for players who want to hold chokepoints and control positioning. Specialization Advancement Preview Level Bulwark Justicar Aegis 3 Unyielding Intercession — range 10 ft and move into interception. Retributive Challenge — Reaction melee attack after defiance. Hold the Ground — hostile spaces within 5 ft are difficult terrain. 6 Shared Resolve — pay Resolve to Guard an intercepted hit even if Guard was used. Punishing Rebuke — retaliation hit sets Speed 0 for current turn. Unyielding Ground — leaving your 5-ft zone reduces Speed. 10 No One Falls — emergency lethal-damage interception despite spent Reaction. Judgment of Defiance — retaliation hit gains +Guard Die. Impassable Line — movement within reach can provoke once

This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Tempo, Firearms, and Reload Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Tradition & Outlook Specialization Reassignment The Gunslinger is a mobile firearm martial whose power comes from maintaining Tempo through successful firearm play. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Fire. Move. Reload. Keep the rhythm alive long enough to turn Tempo into control, defense, and lethal pressure. Class Identity Gunslingers are technist marksmen who turn Aether-assisted firearms into speed, precision, and controlled ranged pressure. Pistols support rapid, mobile sequences through Quick Shot and Akimbo, while Muskets provide deliberate two-handed fire that concentrates Tempo into stronger individual hits through Deliberate Shot. Tempo represents the Gunslinger’s ability to build combat rhythm through successful action rather than treating every shot as an isolated event. Tradition & Outlook Gunslingers belong to Atreia’s newer technological traditions. The wider Aion tradition describes early firearm research being dismissed as technist tinkering until battlefield success forced major institutions to recognize the discipline. Wings of Atreia keeps that identity of innovation earning legitimacy through results while using Pistols and Muskets as the class’s only firearm categories. Gunslingers often value nerve, technical familiarity, accuracy, independence, and adaptability. Appearance & Adventuring Gunslingers favor mobile equipment, ammunition management, firearm maintenance, and a practical awareness of range and firing position. Their weapons can make them look strikingly modern beside older martial traditions, but their discipline remains Aetheric and distinctly Atreian. They adventure to test new techniques, serve as ranged specialists, hunt dangerous targets, protect expeditions from positions others cannot exploit, or demonstrate that innovation has earned its place in the war for Atreia. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Role Ranged weapon damage Secondary Role Mobility, precision, disruption Primary Ability DEX Secondary Ability INT Hit Die d8 Saving Throws DEX, INT Armor Leather Skills Choose 2 from 6: Acrobatics, Deception, Investigation, Perception, Sleight of Hand, Survival Weapons Pistols, Muskets Signature Resource Tempo Signature Mechanic Firearm sequencing and reload rhythm Core Engine — Tempo, Firearms, and Reload The Gunslinger is a mobile firearm martial whose power comes from maintaining Tempo through successful firearm play. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols Ranged Gunslinger One-handed Weapon Attack. Range 30/90 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d8 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. A Gunslinger can wield two Pistols, but doing so does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols are compatible with Quick Shot and Akimbo. Muskets Ranged Gunslinger Two-handed Weapon Attack. Range 60/180 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d12 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. Ammunition capacity is fixed at 2. Muskets cannot use Quick Shot or Akimbo. Gunslinger ammunition-restoration features can restore Musket shots normally, but a Musket can never hold more than 2 shots. Standard one-handed firearm capacity increases do not apply to Muskets. Reload Every firearm attack consumes one shot. A firearm with no shots remaining is Empty and cannot make firearm attacks until at least one shot is restored. Normal Bonus Action Reload: an Empty firearm is restored to its full Reload capacity. Ammunition restoration is not the Reload action unless a feature explicitly says so. Ammunition-restoration features can restore shots to either Pistols or Muskets up to that firearm's maximum capacity. A Musket's maximum capacity remains 2. Switching between carried one-handed Gunslinger firearms as part of a firearm attack requires no separate object interaction. Standard one-handed firearm capacity progression: Ammo Capacity 4 at Levels 1-4, Ammo Capacity 5 at 5-8, Ammo Capacity 6 at 9-14, and Ammo Capacity 7 at 15-20. Increasing capacity does not automatically reload an Empty firearm. Tempo Tempo is a genuine-combat resource representing firing rhythm, accuracy, and momentum. It begins at 0, resets to 0 when combat ends, and artificial initiative cannot generate it. Maximum Tempo: Levels 1-4 = 3; 5-8 = 4; 9-12 = 5; 13-16 = 6; 17-20 = 7. Clean Hit: after you hit a hostile creatur

WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Combat Turn structure, actions, movement, attacks, damage, conditions, death, rests, and survival. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative Round and Turn Action Economy Attack Action Universal Actions Ready Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative, rounds, and combat-only resources are used only for genuine combat or another situation where structured turn order is necessary. Characters cannot manufacture artificial combat to farm cooldowns, resources, or timing triggers. Initiative Initiative = 1d20 + Dexterity modifier. Do not add PB unless an explicit feature says so. Alert adds +2 Initiative. There is no Surprise Round and Surprise does not grant Advantage on Initiative. When one side genuinely catches another side unaware, the GM may, at discretion, allow one appropriate pre-Initiative attack roll against the target's normal defense before Initiative is rolled. This is not an extra round, is not automatic, and does not create a general Surprise action economy. After that resolution, roll Initiative normally. Round and Turn One combat round represents approximately six seconds in the game world. Each participant normally takes one turn in Initiative order. All turns in the round abstract actions occurring within the same six-second span; do not add each turn as another six seconds. Action Economy Action. One per turn. Movement. Up to the creature’s available movement, subject to terrain and conditions. Bonus Action. Up to one, but only when a feature grants something that uses a Bonus Action. Reaction. Normally one per round, refreshing at the start of the creature’s turn unless an explicit class rule says otherwise. Object interaction. One free simple object interaction per turn. There is no universal Action-to-Bonus-Action or Bonus-Action-to-Action conversion. Unused movement or Actions are not stored for later turns. Attack Action The Attack Action makes one attack unless a feature such as Extra Attack says otherwise. Grapple and Shove are full Actions and do not replace one attack within Extra Attack. Player Weapon Requirement. A player character must be wielding an approved class weapon to take the normal Attack Action. Unarmed Attacks and Improvised Weapons are not player combat options unless a later explicit feature creates a specific exception. Opportunity Attacks. Opportunity Attacks remain part of the core combat rules. When a hostile creature you can perceive voluntarily leaves your melee reach, you may use your Reaction to make one melee attack against it, resolving the attack before it leaves that reach. Forced movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Universal Actions Dash. Gain additional movement equal to your current Speed for the turn. Difficult Terrain and other movement costs still apply. While flying, Dash adds horizontal movement but does not grant an additional altitude-layer change. Disengage. Until the end of your turn, your movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks. Dodge. Until the start of your next turn, attacks against you have Disadvantage if you can perceive the attacker, and you have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws. Dodge ends if you become Incapacitated or your Speed becomes 0. Hide. You must have meaningful concealment or another circumstance that allows hiding. Make Dexterity (Stealth) against Passive Perception or active Perception as appropriate. You cannot Hide while clearly seen. Hidden is not Invisible. Making an attack reveals your position after that attack resolves. Search. Deliberately search using a GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation). Use Object. Use this Action for substantial manipulation beyond the one free simple object interaction. A specific item’s activation rule controls when it states another cost. Ready A creature can prepare one Action for a perceivable trigger. When the trigger occurs, the creature may use its Reaction to perform the readied Action. Ready does not store ordinary movement, but Dash can be readied as the Action. Readied attacks retain all weapon properties. A readied spell must still meet implement and targeting requirements when released. Losing a mandatory implement before release prevents release. Concentration begins when the spell actually resolves. Ready never bypasses aerial restrictions, range, or other universal rules. Simultaneous Effects Effects resolve one at a time. The active creature orders its own simultaneous effects; the GM orders GM-controlled simultaneous effects. For opposing same-time effects, resolve the active creature first, then use Initiative if needed. Damage resolves before state changes caused by that damage. Start-

text: Territorial Familiarity. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Backgrounds All nine player Backgrounds, their skill choices, roleplaying guidance, Languages, and Territorial Familiarity. Source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page is a player-facing reference extracted from the handbook rather than a replacement ruleset. Background Rules Soldier Scholar Acolyte Noble Outlander Underworld Artisan Merchant Entertainer Languages Background Rules Skill Selection: Choose exactly 2 Background Skills from the six options listed for your Background. Duplicate selections are prohibited. A Skill selected as a Class Skill cannot also be selected as a Background Skill. The four selected Class and Background Skill Proficiencies must therefore be four different Skills. Background Choose 2 Skills Soldier Athletics, Intimidation, Perception, Survival, Medicine, Religion Scholar Arcana, History, Investigation, Religion, Medicine, Perception Acolyte History, Insight, Medicine, Religion, Athletics, Survival Noble History, Insight, Persuasion, Performance, Investigation, Sleight of Hand Outlander Athletics, Nature, Perception, Survival, Persuasion, Stealth Underworld Deception, Insight, Sleight of Hand, Stealth, Investigation, Persuasion Artisan Investigation, Perception, Sleight of Hand, History, Arcana, Persuasion Merchant Insight, Investigation, Persuasion, History, Stealth, Athletics Entertainer Acrobatics, Deception, Performance, Persuasion, Nature, Animal Handling A relevant Background may establish that you have the experience necessary to attempt obscure or specialized knowledge. It does not automatically grant Advantage, Expertise, a numerical bonus, or guaranteed success. Understanding Your Background Your Class describes what your character has learned to do as an adventuring Daeva. Your Background describes the life, training, profession, upbringing, or experiences that helped shape who they were before the campaign began. Faction tells you where you belong, Background helps explain where you came from, and Class describes how you operate as an adventurer. A Background does not determine your morality, personality, beliefs, faction loyalty, or future choices. Two characters with the same Background may have completely different lives and goals. Mechanically, use the Background table above exactly as written: choose two skills from your Background’s listed skill pool. The entries below add roleplaying context and do not grant additional rules benefits. Soldier What Is a Soldier?. A Soldier has meaningful experience with organized military service: troops, guards, scouts, officers, fortress personnel, or other disciplined fighting forces. Life and Origins. Military life may have included patrols, garrison duty, campaigns, escort work, reconnaissance, fortification defense, or service under a commander. That service may have occurred before or after ascension. Motivations and Outlook. Duty, loyalty, comradeship, ambition, patriotism, protection, regret, or the memory of fallen companions may still shape the character. A Soldier may respect military order, resent it, or be deciding what is truly worth fighting for. Playing a Soldier. Decide what kind of service shaped you, who you served beside, and what relationship you now have with authority and your former comrades. Being a Soldier does not require obedience or a martial Class. Scholar What Is a Scholar?. A Scholar has devoted part of their life to seeking, preserving, interpreting, or teaching knowledge. Scholars include researchers, historians, scribes, teachers, philosophers, archivists, investigators, and field specialists. Life and Origins. Study may have taken place under a teacher, within an archive or institution, or independently. Subjects can include history, geography, creatures, Aether, ruins, cultures, warfare, or any other serious field of inquiry. Motivations and Outlook. A Scholar may adventure to recover lost knowledge, investigate mysteries, study ruins or creatures directly, protect important discoveries, or prevent dangerous knowledge from being misused. Playing a Scholar. Choose the subject that fascinates you and decide whether you are an academic, a practical field researcher, or something between. Being scholarly does not require being socially awkward or confined to books. Acolyte What Is an Acolyte?. An Acolyte has meaningful experience with religious or spiritual service, sacred traditions, temples, ceremonies, or communities of worship. Life and Origins. The character may have been raised around a temple, studied under a religious teacher, volunteered in a sacred institution, maintained holy places, assisted ceremonies, or found faith after a life-changing event. Motivations and Outlook. Faith, service, protection, reform, doubt, duty, spiritual curiosity, or concern for a community may lead an Acolyte into adventure. An Acolyte can be devout, questio

WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Exploration & Interaction Vision, stealth, traps, locks, theft, hazards, social rules, chases, and loot. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Vision, Stealth, Traps, Locks & Theft Vision and Light Cover, Line of Sight & Line of Effect Stealth and Infiltration Traps and Non-Aether Hazards Locks Theft and Pickpocket Social Interaction, Information & Captivity Vision, Stealth, Traps, Locks & Theft Vision and Light Light states are Bright Light, Dim Light, and Darkness. Obscuration states are Lightly Obscured and Heavily Obscured. Dim Light lightly obscures; Darkness heavily obscures a creature that cannot otherwise see through it. Daeva Darkvision treats Darkness within 60 feet as Dim Light, not Bright Light. A recommended ordinary light source has a stated Bright radius plus an equal additional Dim radius unless its own text says otherwise. Bright light does not universally prohibit Stealth. Obscurity and Invisibility do not automatically make a creature Hidden. Cover, Line of Sight & Line of Effect No Cover. No defensive benefit from Cover. Half Cover. A creature or object behind meaningful partial obstruction gains +2 AC and +2 to Dexterity saving throws against effects originating from the covered direction. Intervening creatures can provide Half Cover when they materially obstruct the line. Full Cover. Full Cover blocks the relevant Line of Effect and prevents direct targeting through that obstruction unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Three-Quarters Cover does not exist in Wings of Atreia. Cover does not stack; use the best applicable Cover. Altitude neither inherently grants nor ignores Cover. Line of Sight and Line of Effect are distinct. Line of Sight determines whether you can see a target or point. Line of Effect determines whether an attack, spell, or effect can physically reach it. Heavy obscurement is not Cover by itself. Stealth and Infiltration Use scene states Undetected, Suspicious, and Alerted; these are not Conditions. Stealth must exceed Passive Perception; ties favor the observer. An active Search uses the GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation), against the relevant DC or opposing Stealth; ties favor the Searcher where opposed. Do not reroll Stealth every 5 feet; roll again only when circumstances materially change. For group Stealth, at least half the group must succeed. A failed check may create Suspicion rather than immediate full alarm when appropriate. Distractions create an opportunity to Hide rather than automatic success. Disguises are primarily social. Invisibility is not the same as Hidden. Wings do not automatically prevent Stealth. Traps and Non-Aether Hazards Describe a hazard with Trigger, Detection, Avoid/Disable method, Save/Check, Effect, and Reset/Duration. Hazards may be obvious, concealed, or hidden. Detection normally uses Passive Perception, active Perception, or Investigation. Disable methods depend on the mechanism and can use Sleight of Hand, Investigation, Athletics, or another appropriate Skill. There is no mandatory Thieves’ Tools system. Failure triggers the hazard only when the hazard says so. Damage and Conditions use existing universal rules. Forced movement is horizontal unless the hazard explicitly creates vertical displacement. Hazards normally resolve when triggered rather than taking their own Initiative turns. Repeat attempts require changed circumstances. Locks Mechanical Lock DC Simple 10 Standard 12 Secure 15 High Security 18 Exceptional 20+ The correct key opens a normal lock without a check. Mechanical locks generally use Dexterity (Sleight of Hand). Unusual mechanisms can use Intelligence (Investigation). Forcing uses Strength (Athletics); destroying a lock or door uses normal object/destruction adjudication. Failure does not automatically break or trigger a lock unless its design says so. Aether locks use Aether Interaction. If a task is impossible, do not assign an absurd DC—state that it cannot be done by that method. Theft and Pickpocket A theft attempt requires a plausible opportunity. Taking an accessible small item uses Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) against Passive Perception and must exceed it. If the target is actively watching, oppose with active Perception; ties favor the observer. Secured items can require a different approach. Failure may create suspicion or alarm. Success means the theft was unnoticed at that moment; later discovery remains possible. Distraction creates opportunity rather than automatic success. Help can grant +2 when genuinely meaningful. Worn armor, shields, Wings, wielded weapons, and equipped mandatory implements cannot simply be pickpocketed. Repeated attempts require changed circumstances. Social Interaction, Information & Cap

text: Tradition & Outlook. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Bastion Pilot • Aether Core • Heat • Adaptive Weapons Combat Aethertech “Steel, meet face. Face, meet steel.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. On this page Overview Chassis Core Mechanics Action Reference Specializations Progression Examples ↑ Top The Aethertech fights from one piloted Large Bastion platform. The pilot and Bastion are one character’s action economy, not two independent turns. The class alternates between integrated Bastion armaments, Aether Core expenditures, controlled Heat accumulation, venting, repairs, and system integration. The Bastion is a separate physical HP pool that enemies can damage without directly healing or harming the pilot unless an effect specifically targets the pilot. Class Identity Aethertechs are technist warriors who channel Aether through a Bastion: a magical-mechanical combat platform that transforms how the Daeva occupies the battlefield. The class combines personal skill, engineered systems, heavy protection, and controlled bursts of power. Aether Core and Heat represent the constant balance between available energy and the strain created by pushing the Bastion harder. Tradition & Outlook Aethertech is a comparatively modern Daeva discipline born from the recovery, study, and weaponization of advanced magical technology. The wider Aion tradition connects the class to Daeva analysis of Danuar technology and the lessons surrounding Hyperion; Wings of Atreia preserves that technological identity while its own campaign chronology and mechanics remain authoritative. Aethertechs often value ingenuity, technical discipline, experimentation, and the belief that knowledge taken from dangerous enemies can be turned toward Atreia’s defense. Appearance & Adventuring An Aethertech is visually defined by the Bastion and the contrast between a Daeva operator and an imposing Aether-powered war platform. Outside it, the Aethertech remains a trained combatant using the class’s approved weapons and equipment. Aethertechs adventure to recover technology, test designs under real conditions, oppose Balaur war machines, protect expeditions with a durable mobile platform, or prove that engineering can stand beside sword and spell as a heroic discipline. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Ability Intelligence Secondary Ability Constitution Hit Die d8 Saving Throws Intelligence, Constitution Armor Chain Armor Skills Choose 2 from 6: Arcana, Athletics, Investigation, Perception, Sleight of Hand, Survival Weapons Shortswords, Maces, Hammers Signature Resources Aether Core and Heat Signature Mechanic Piloted Bastion Bastion Size Large Class Save DC 8 + PB + INT modifier Extra Attack Level 5; two Bastion weapon attacks only Spellcasting None Bastion Targeting and Chassis The pilot and Bastion have separate HP and temporary HP. Repairs restore Bastion HP and are not healing. While occupied, ordinary physical attacks targeting the Aethertech generally strike the Bastion first. Mental, emotional, biological, and similar effects target the pilot when appropriate. One area effect normally does not double-hit both pilot and Bastion. Bastion physical STR/DEX/CON saves use PB + INT modifier. Mental saves use the pilot’s relevant save. When the Bastion reaches 0 HP it is Disabled. The pilot is ejected to the nearest legal space, takes 1d6 Force damage, and does not provoke Opportunity Attacks from the ejection. A disabled Bastion retains its current Core and Heat; a fresh chassis does not replace it. A Short Rest repairs a Disabled or damaged Bastion by half its maximum HP. A Long Rest repairs the Bastion to its maximum HP. These restorations are repairs, not healing. Once the Bastion has at least 1 HP, it is operational. Entering or re-entering a deployed Bastion uses an Action when otherwise legal. A defeated or voluntarily replaced Bastion never functions as a companion or second PC. Contesting STR checks with the Bastion e.g Grapple, pushing, pulling, except for skill or ability effects, will have the PC use this formula: 1d20+8+INT modifier+PB considering that a Bastion is a Large entity. Target must contest with their choice of Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics). Level Band Bastion AC Bastion Maximum HP 1–4 11 + PB 8 + (5 × Aethertech level) + INT 5–10 12 + PB 8 + (5 × level) + INT 11–17 13 + PB 12 + (6 × level) + INT 18–20 13 + PB 16 + (7 × level) + INT Whenever a chassis improvement raises maximum HP, increase current Bastion HP by the same amount; this is a maximum-HP adjustment rather than healing. Bastion Weapon Synchronization While piloting a Bastion, designate one eligible carried weapon with which you are proficient as your Synchronized Weapon. A Bastion weapon attack roll is 1d20 + PB + INT modifier + the Synchronized Weapon's current equipment-quality bonu

WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Melee Striker • Sneak Attack • Rune Marks • Execution Assassin “You'll know I'm there when you're dead.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Sneak Attack and Rune Marks Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Assassin is a precision melee striker that builds target-bound Rune Marks, converts them into burst damage or execution riders, and uses Shadow Step to remain difficult to pin down. Unlike a conventional Extra Attack martial, its Level 5 Assassination Sequence is a conditional follow-up attack tied to a successful Sneak Attack. Class Identity Assassins are precision predators who win through positioning, timing, concealment, and carefully prepared execution. Their art is not simply “attacking from stealth.” An Assassin studies a target, creates the right opening, carves Rune Marks, and converts preparation into a sudden lethal advantage. Their greatest strength is the ability to decide where and when a close-range confrontation becomes dangerous. Tradition & Outlook The Assassin tradition descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines and is practiced by infiltrators, covert operatives, hunters of dangerous individuals, intelligence agents, and Daevas who favor certainty over spectacle. Assassins often prize patience, awareness, self-control, and economy of motion. Their motives vary widely: service to a faction, revenge, professional duty, protection through preemptive action, or the pursuit of perfect technique. Appearance & Adventuring Assassins favor equipment that permits mobility and unobstructed movement, with Shortswords and Daggers forming the class’s approved weapon identity in Wings of Atreia. Their appearance may be subdued or ceremonial, but practical Assassins avoid anything that compromises movement or control. They adventure when a threat must be found before it strikes, a route must be infiltrated, an enemy leader must be neutralized, or a mystery demands someone comfortable operating unseen. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Ability Dexterity Secondary Ability Constitution Hit Die d8 Saving Throws Dexterity, Intelligence Armor Leather Armor Weapons Shortswords, Daggers Skills Choose 2 from 6: Acrobatics, Deception, Investigation, Perception, Sleight of Hand, Stealth Class Save DC 8 + PB + DEX modifier Signature Resource Rune Marks placed on enemies Signature Mechanics Sneak Attack, Rune Carving, Rune Burst, Shadow Step Extra Attack No standard Extra Attack; Assassination Sequence at Level 5 Spellcasting None Core Engine — Sneak Attack and Rune Marks Sneak Attack applies once on each of your own turns when an eligible finesse melee weapon attack has Advantage, or when another qualifying enemy is adjacent to the target and you do not have Disadvantage. Sneak Attack damage scales from 1d6 at Level 1 to 10d6 at Level 19. Levels Sneak Attack Rune Die Marked Targets 1–2 1d6 d4 1 3–4 2d6 d4 1 5–6 3d6 d6 1 7–8 4d6 d6 1 9–10 5d6 d6 2 11–12 6d6 d8 2 13–14 7d6 d8 2 15–16 8d6 d8 2 17–18 9d6 d10 3 19–20 10d6 d10 3 A creature can carry up to 3 of your Rune Marks. Rune Carving: once on your turn, a qualifying melee hit that actually deals Sneak Attack places 1 Rune Mark after that hit resolves. Alternatively, hitting the same creature with two different melee attacks during your turn can place 1 Rune Mark after the second hit. Normal attack-based Rune placement is limited to 1 Mark per turn unless a feature explicitly increases it. Newly created Rune Marks cannot be consumed by the same hit that created them. If you exceed your current marked-target limit, choose one previously marked creature and remove all of your Marks from it. Marks disappear when consumed, when the marked creature is defeated, or when the encounter ends. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Resource Form Rune Marks are target-bound counters, not a generic personal pool. A creature carries your Marks until they are consumed or removed. Maximum Up to 3 Rune Marks per creature. Marked-target capacity is 1 creature through Level 8, 2 from Levels 9–16, and 3 from Level 17 onward. How You Place Marks Once on your turn, a qualifying melee hit that actually deals Sneak Attack places 1 Mark after the hit resolves. Alternatively, two different melee hits against the same creature during your turn can place 1 Mark after the second hit. Placement Limits Normal attack-based placement is limited to 1 Mark per turn unless an explicit feature increases it. A newly created Mark cannot be consumed by the hit that created it. View Chanter Spell List → Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Cadence Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Spell List Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Rhythm Sequence Specialization Reassignment The Chanter wins by alternating weapon attacks, spells, and active Mantra management. Cadence is earned by changing categories rather than repeating one action, then spent on damage, protection, healing, and tactical movement. It is a secondary healer and hybrid support, not a replacement for the Cleric or a dedicated martial striker. Class Identity Chanters are martial support specialists who combine staff technique, enchantment, restorative magic, and Mantras into a continuous rhythm of battle. Rather than solving every problem through one large spell, a Chanter improves the party’s performance over time and responds to changing pressure with Cadence. Their presence is felt in how effectively the entire group moves, strikes, and recovers together. Tradition & Outlook The Chanter tradition grows from Atreia’s priestly disciplines but emphasizes disciplined body, voice, repetition, and the shaping of Aether through words and practiced forms. Chanters are often teachers, battle companions, spiritual guides, martial ascetics, or morale-keepers. They tend to value harmony between individual excellence and collective strength: the ideal Chanter does not merely stand beside allies but helps those allies become more capable. Appearance & Adventuring Chanters are strongly associated with Staff and Quarterstaff techniques in Wings of Atreia. Their clothing and armor tend to allow movement while retaining the ceremonial or disciplined character of a priestly warrior. They adventure to guide companions, strengthen military or exploratory groups, carry teachings into dangerous places, preserve morale during long campaigns, or prove that disciplined cooperation can overcome enemies stronger than any one Daeva. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Ability Intelligence Secondary Ability Charisma Hit Die d8 Saving Throws Constitution, Intelligence Armor Chain Armor Weapons Staff, Quarterstaff Skills Choose 2 from 6: History, Insight, Medicine, Performance, Persuasion, Religion Spellcasting Ability INT Mantra Ability CHA Signature Resource Cadence Spell Advancements +1 each level after 1; 19 total Maximum Spell Level 7 Extra Attack Level 5; two attacks only Core Engine — Cadence Cadence is a genuine-combat resource. It begins at 0 when combat starts, resets to 0 when combat ends, and artificial initiative cannot create or restore it. Maximum Cadence is 3 at Levels 1–4, 4 at 5–8, 5 at 9–12, 6 at 13–16, and 7 at 17–20. Category Qualifying Event Martial You hit a hostile creature with a weapon attack. Spell A Chanter spell meaningfully affects a creature by hit, damage, failed save, actual healing, meaningful prevention, or another significant effect. Chant You activate, replace, or deliberately invoke a Mantra/Chant and it meaningfully changes at least one creature. Passive maintenance never qualifies. Your previous qualifying category is always the most recent successful qualifying category, whether or not that event generated Cadence. When you successfully complete a qualifying event whose category differs from your previous successful qualifying category, gain 1 Cadence, subject to the normal generation limit. Your first successful qualifying event in a combat establishes your previous category; it does not generate Cadence by itself. Normal Cadence generation is limited to 1 per turn unless a feature explicitly grants more. Secondary Chanter riders do not recursively generate Cadence, Resonant Network triggers, Mantra Weaving, or other support sequences unless explicit. Maximum 3 at Levels 1–4; 4 at 5–8; 5 at 9–12; 6 at 13–16; 7 at 17–20. Qualifying Categories Martial: a weapon attack hits a hostile. Spell: a Chanter spell meaningfully affects a creature. How You Gain It When a successful qualifying event uses a category different from your previous successful qualifying category, gain 1 Cadence. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Primary Healer • Divine Grace • Protection • Purification Cleric “Protect me and you shall never fall.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Spellcasting Reference: Cleric has a dedicated spell-list page for quick browsing. View Cleric Spell List → Class Identity Class Chassis Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Spell List Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Support Sequence Tradition & Outlook Specialization Reassignment The Cleric is Wings of Atreia’s primary restorative spellcaster. It is deliberately more durable than the d6 full casters and is rewarded for meaningful intervention: healing an ally in real danger, actually preventing damage, or removing a significant hostile effect. Divine Grace then converts that successful support into more emergency power. Class Identity Clerics are Atreia’s foremost restorative and protective spellcasters. Their calling is not limited to healing wounds after the fact: they preserve the party through recovery, cleansing, protection, and timely intervention while retaining the ability to fight when necessary. Divine Grace represents the reserve of sacred and restorative power through which a Cleric answers moments of genuine need. Tradition & Outlook The Cleric tradition grows from Atreia’s priestly disciplines and is associated with healers, battlefield ministers, temple servants, protectors of communities, and Daevas who understand survival as a collective responsibility. Clerics often value service, perseverance, mercy, duty, or faith, but they need not share one personality or theology. A militant Cleric and a gentle healer may practice the same class through very different convictions. Appearance & Adventuring Clerics commonly combine durable armor with practical healing or ritual equipment. In Wings of Atreia they may use Maces, Hammers, Staffs, Quarterstaffs, and shields from Round Shields to Medium Shields according to their approved access. They adventure to protect lives, confront corruption or supernatural danger, recover sacred knowledge, serve a cause, or ensure that an expedition can survive places where retreat and ordinary medicine are not enough. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Ability Wisdom Secondary Ability Constitution Hit Die d8; additionally +2 maximum HP per Cleric level Saving Throws Wisdom, Constitution Armor Chain Armor Weapons Mace, Hammer, Staff, Quarterstaff, Round Shield, Medium Shield Skills Choose 2 from 6: History, Insight, Medicine, Nature, Perception, Religion Spellcasting Ability WIS Spell Save DC 8 + PB + WIS modifier Spell Attack PB + WIS modifier Signature Resource Divine Grace Spell Advancements +2 each level after 1; 38 total Maximum Spell Level 9 Extra Attack None Meaningful Support and Divine Grace Maximum Divine Grace equals PB + WIS modifier, minimum 2. Long Rest restores all; Short Rest restores PB. Once per round, when you Meaningfully Support yourself or an ally with a Cleric spell or feature, regain 1 Grace. Your normal once-per-round generation becomes available again at the start of your turn, allowing an off-turn protection to qualify without double-dipping around initiative boundaries. Meaningful Support means one of the following actually occurs: restore HP while the creature was below half maximum HP; prevent or reduce damage by at least PB; or suppress/remove a mechanically significant hostile condition or effect. Healing a full-HP creature, preventing 0 damage, refreshing temporary HP without increasing it, cosmetic effects, or intentionally manufactured harmless damage do not qualify. Self-support must satisfy the same standard. Temporary HP are not healing and cannot restore a creature from 0 HP. Passive aura bonuses and passive AC do not generate Divine Grace unless a feature explicitly says so. A secondary Cleric rider created by another Cleric feature does not recursively trigger Twin Devotion, Sacred Intervention, Graceful Channeling, Empowered Restoration, or another support sequence unless explicit. Only one Cleric rolled-healing class rider normally modifies the same individual healing instance, except Graceful Restoration may coexist with one specialization rolled-healing rider. Flat Cleric save penalties do not stack; use the largest. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Starting State Divine Grace is a rest-based reserve. It does not automatically reset to 0 when combat starts or ends; later features can establish a minimum starting amount. Maximum PB + WIS modifier, minimum 2. Rest Recovery Long Rest restores all Divine Grace. Short Rest restores Grace equal to PB, up to maximum. How You Gain It Once per round, regain 1 Grace when a Cleric spell or feature Meaningfull

Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Tempo, Firearms, and Reload Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Tradition & Outlook Specialization Reassignment The Gunslinger is a mobile firearm martial whose power comes from maintaining Tempo through successful firearm play. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Fire. Move. Reload. Keep the rhythm alive long enough to turn Tempo into control, defense, and lethal pressure. Class Identity Gunslingers are technist marksmen who turn Aether-assisted firearms into speed, precision, and controlled ranged pressure. Pistols support rapid, mobile sequences through Quick Shot and Akimbo, while Muskets provide deliberate two-handed fire that concentrates Tempo into stronger individual hits through Deliberate Shot. Tempo represents the Gunslinger’s ability to build combat rhythm through successful action rather than treating every shot as an isolated event. Tradition & Outlook Gunslingers belong to Atreia’s newer technological traditions. The wider Aion tradition describes early firearm research being dismissed as technist tinkering until battlefield success forced major institutions to recognize the discipline. Wings of Atreia keeps that identity of innovation earning legitimacy through results while using Pistols and Muskets as the class’s only firearm categories. Gunslingers often value nerve, technical familiarity, accuracy, independence, and adaptability. Appearance & Adventuring Gunslingers favor mobile equipment, ammunition management, firearm maintenance, and a practical awareness of range and firing position. Their weapons can make them look strikingly modern beside older martial traditions, but their discipline remains Aetheric and distinctly Atreian. They adventure to test new techniques, serve as ranged specialists, hunt dangerous targets, protect expeditions from positions others cannot exploit, or demonstrate that innovation has earned its place in the war for Atreia. Either way, you'll only die tired.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Focus Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Ranger is a nonmagical ranged hunter that controls enemy movement with persistent battlefield traps, spends Focus on precision or evasive shots, and is rewarded for exploiting targets that walk into prepared terrain. Its sustained damage comes from two ranged attacks, not from spellcasting or a third standard attack. Class Identity Rangers are mobile ranged specialists who control distance through marksmanship, movement, traps, and battlefield awareness. They are most effective when they can read terrain before committing, choose favorable lines of attack, and punish enemies that approach carelessly. Focus represents the Ranger’s ability to convert patience and perception into precise action. Tradition & Outlook The Ranger tradition also descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines, but where Assassins close with a chosen target, Rangers cultivate distance, fieldcraft, and control of the approach. Rangers are common among scouts, hunters, pathfinders, border wardens, reconnaissance troops, and independent Daevas accustomed to surviving beyond secure settlements. They tend to value preparedness, observation, mobility, and freedom of movement. Appearance & Adventuring Rangers usually wear mobile armor and carry bows, ammunition, traps, and field equipment suited to extended movement. Their gear often reflects the terrain in which they learned their craft. Rangers adventure to explore dangerous regions, hunt monsters or enemy operatives, guide expeditions, secure routes, protect remote communities, or prove that no battlefield is truly open ground when preparation and range are on their side. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Full Caster • Song Roles • Refrains • Resonance Songweaver “Here's a note you won't forget.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Spellcasting Reference: Songweaver has a dedicated spell-list page for quick browsing. View Songweaver Spell List → Class Identity Class Chassis Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Spell List Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Performance Sequence Tradition & Outlook Specialization Reassignment The Songweaver changes battlefield purpose from moment to moment. Every Songweaver spell belongs to Harmony, Guard, Dissonance, or Requiem. Successful performances create short-lived Refrains, changing Song Roles builds Resonance, and Resonance is spent to amplify, sustain, counter, or conduct the performance. Class Identity Songweavers shape Aether through music, using performance as destructive spellcraft, support, control, and restoration. Their strength lies in versatility: the same class can pressure an enemy, sustain an ally, or shift the emotional and tactical rhythm of an encounter. Resonance represents the accumulating harmony between performance, spellcraft, and the unfolding battle. Tradition & Outlook The Songweaver tradition is rooted in Atreia’s Muses and in remembrance of Siel. The wider Aion tradition describes Muses who continued their studies after the Cataclysm and eventually joined music with Aether in service to their people; their battlefield contribution led to recognition as an established Daeva class. Songweavers may therefore approach performance as remembrance, artistry, scholarship, service, or a declaration that beauty still has power in a broken world. Appearance & Adventuring Songweavers use Lutes and Lyres as their approved implements, often making instrument, costume, gesture, and magical display part of a single visible identity. Their appearance can range from formal performer to traveling battle-musician without changing class mechanics. They adventure to preserve stories, honor Siel, inspire allies, master Aetheric music, carry culture into war-torn regions, or use beauty and sound as weapons against forces that would reduce Atreia to silence. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Ability Charisma Secondary Ability Intelligence Hit Die d6 Saving Throws Charisma, Dexterity Armor Cloth Focus Lute, Lyre, or suitable magical instrument Skills Choose 2 from 6: Arcana, Deception, Insight, Performance, Persuasion, Religion Spellcasting Ability CHA Technical Refrain Ability INT Signature Resource Resonance Spell Advancements +2 each level after 1; 38 total Maximum Spell Level 9 Extra Attack None Song Roles and Resonance Song Role Primary Function Harmony Healing and positive support Guard Protection and defensive enhancement Dissonance Debuffs and control Requiem Offensive magical pressure Track the most recent Song Role of a Songweaver spell that successfully affected at least one creature, whether or not that casting generated Resonance. Resonance is genuine-combat only: it begins at 0, resets to 0 at combat end, and artificial initiative cannot generate it. Maximum Resonance is 3 at Levels 1–4, 4 at 5–8, 5 at 9–12, 6 at 13–16, and 7 at 17–20. After a Songweaver spell resolves, if that casting satisfies at least one of the generation conditions below, gain 1 Resonance, subject to the normal per-turn limit. The first successful Song Role in a combat establishes role history for Contrasting Verse; it cannot contrast with a role that does not yet exist. Harmonic Support: a single Songweaver spell meaningfully benefits two or more creatures. Dissonant Performance: a single Songweaver spell meaningfully affects two or more hostile creatures. Contrasting Verse: you successfully cast a Songweaver spell whose Song Role differs from your previous successful Song Role. Each generation condition triggers at most once per casting. Normal generation is capped at 1 Resonance per turn unless a feature explicitly increases it. A Refrain, Chorus Echo, Resonance rider, specialization rider, or other secondary Songweaver effect cannot recursively generate Resonance, create/trigger another Refrain, or activate another Songweaver rider unless explicit. Maximum 3 at Levels 1–4; 4 at 5–8; 5 at 9–12; 6 at 13–16; 7 at 17–20. View Sorcerer Spell List → Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Aether Focus Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Spell List Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Spellcasting Example Specialization Reassignment The Sorcerer is the raw magical-damage benchmark. It casts through Fire, Ice, Lightning, and Wind spell chains, then spends Aether Focus only when a particular spell needs more damage, area, control pressure, or reliability. Aether Focus enhances spells; it is never the fuel required to cast ordinary Sorcerer spells. Class Identity Sorcerers are masters of direct Aetheric spellcraft, combining destructive magic with the ability to control the shape and tempo of a fight. They can punish clustered enemies, deny movement or action, and unleash powerful spells when an opening appears. Aether Focus represents the concentration and arcane discipline required to turn immense magical potential into reliable battlefield power. Tradition & Outlook The Sorcerer tradition grows from Atreia’s mage disciplines and is associated with formal magical study, experimentation, academies, battlefield arcanists, and Daevas fascinated by the structure of Aether itself. Sorcerers commonly value knowledge, precision, preparation, and intellectual mastery, although their personalities range from scholarly restraint to spectacular confidence. For many, magic is both a weapon and a language through which Atreia can be understood. Appearance & Adventuring Sorcerers favor cloth armor and magical implements such as Orbs and Spellbooks under the Wings of Atreia equipment rules. Their appearance may reflect academic, military, ceremonial, or highly individual magical traditions. They adventure to recover lost knowledge, study Aetheric phenomena, test magical theories, defend their people with overwhelming spellcraft, or confront powers that ordinary weapons cannot adequately answer. A Long Rest restores all expended Aether Focus. A Short Rest restores Aether Focus equal to PB, up to your maximum. The resource is an enhancement reserve: casting an ordinary Sorcerer spell never requires Aether Focus unless a spell or class feature explicitly says otherwise. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Starting State Aether Focus is a rest-based enhancement reserve and does not reset merely because combat begins or ends. After a Long Rest it is normally full. Maximum PB + INT modifier, minimum 2. Aether Sage and the Level 20 capstone can explicitly increase this maximum. Rest Recovery Long Rest restores all expended Aether Focus. Short Rest restores Focus equal to PB, up to maximum; Aether Sage can improve this recovery. Base Generation The base Sorcerer does not generate Aether Focus from ordinary spell hits or damage. Combat refunds exist only where a class or specialization feature explicitly grants them. How You Spend It Intensify 1 Focus; Widen 1 Focus; Potent Control 1 Focus; other Sorcerer features spend Aether Focus only when their text states a cost. Ordinary spellcasting costs no Focus. Refunds / Discounts Aether Sage and later features may discount a shaping cost or refund Focus after a qualifying shaped spell. A refund is not a second casting or a new spell trigger. Persistence Unused Aether Focus persists between encounters until spent or restored. Important Distinction Aether Focus is a Sorcerer class resource. It is not environmental Aether, Refined Aether, an Aether State, or a universal damage type. Your spirit is with you.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Spellcasting Reference: Spiritmaster has a dedicated spell-list page for quick browsing. View Spiritmaster Spell List → Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Summon Spirit Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Spell List Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequence Specialization Reassignment The Spiritmaster is a two-body tactical caster. One active elemental spirit shares the Spiritmaster’s turn and action economy; together they equal one complete player character. The class establishes two battlefield positions, casts through the spirit, and earns Spirit Bond only through meaningful master-spirit coordination. Class Identity Spiritmasters are binders and commanders of elemental spirits who fight as a partnership rather than as a solitary caster. Their strength comes from coordinating their own spellcraft with a Greater Spirit, applying pressure, disruption, and control across more than one position on the battlefield. Spirit Bond represents the relationship and command structure that makes this divided presence function as one class. Tradition & Outlook The Spiritmaster tradition develops from Atreia’s mage disciplines but turns outward toward spirits, elemental forces, and the difficult art of directing entities shaped by Aether. Spiritmasters are often patient observers, researchers, summoners, or specialists in threats that cannot be understood through ordinary physical study. Their beliefs about spirits differ: some emphasize command, others partnership, responsibility, curiosity, or respect for elemental power. Appearance & Adventuring Spiritmasters use cloth armor and magical implements, while the visible presence of a summoned spirit often defines their silhouette more strongly than clothing does. Their equipment may include ritual, scholarly, or elemental motifs without creating additional mechanics. They adventure to understand unusual spirits, recover lost summoning knowledge, counter supernatural threats, serve as versatile magical operatives, or deepen the bond between Daeva and elemental ally. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Ability Intelligence Secondary Ability Charisma Hit Die d6 Saving Throws Wisdom, Charisma Armor Cloth Implements Spellbook, Magical Orb Skills Choose 2 from 6: Arcana, Deception, Insight, Intimidation, Nature, Religion Spellcasting Ability INT Spell Save DC 8 + PB + INT modifier Spell Attack PB + INT modifier Signature Resource Spirit Bond Spell Advancements +2 every level after 1; 38 total Maximum Spell Level 9 Extra Attack None Core Engine — Summon Spirit You know all four fundamental spirits—Fire, Water, Earth, and Wind—and choose among them tactically. Only one Spiritmaster spirit may normally be active. Summoning uses an Action and places the spirit in a visible unoccupied space within 15 feet. A defeated spirit disperses into Aether, makes no death saves, and cannot be resummoned until the start of your next turn. Outside combat a newly summoned spirit appears at full HP; voluntary replacement during combat preserves the dismissed spirit’s current HP percentage rather than healing by switching forms. It moves normally during your turn without consuming your action. Normally you spend your Bonus Action to command its basic Spirit Action. If not commanded, it may move, Dodge, or remain in place. A spirit normally makes only one basic Spirit Attack per turn unless a feature explicitly allows otherwise. Spirit attacks are class features, not spells. A character may have only one Active Profession at a time. The only Profession ranks are Apprentice and Master. There is no Profession XP, no intermediate rank, and no separate recipe, formula-book, manual, or recipe-learning subsystem. Earning a rank automatically grants the standard functions assigned to that rank. Rule Profession Ruling Starting Rank None. Backgrounds, including Artisan, grant no Profession rank. Active Limit One Active Profession at a time. Changing Profession Only when the character gains a character level. Inactive Profession Retains earned rank, paid entry fee, and completed Training Progress, but cannot be used or advanced. Reactivation Restores the highest earned rank and retained Training Progress; an already-paid rank entry fee is not paid again. The trainee and trainer cannot adventure, undertake missions, perform adventuring travel, conduct other downtime work, perform Profession production, or complete other substantive activities that day. Training Days need not be consecutive. An interrupted day grants no Training Progress, but previously completed Training Days remain. A character cannot train themselves. One qualified trainer may instruct up to four trainees of the same rank category during one Training Day. When a PC provides training, that PC receives the one-time entry fee: 100 Kinah per Apprentice trainee or 500 Kinah per Master trainee. NPC or institutional fees go to that provider. Tradition & Outlook The Ranger tradition also descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines, but where Assassins close with a chosen target, Rangers cultivate distance, fieldcraft, and control of the approach. Rangers are common among scouts, hunters, pathfinders, border wardens, reconnaissance troops, and independent Daevas accustomed to surviving beyond secure settlements. They tend to value preparedness, observation, mobility, and freedom of movement. Appearance & Adventuring Rangers usually wear mobile armor and carry bows, ammunition, traps, and field equipment suited to extended movement. Their gear often reflects the terrain in which they learned their craft. Rangers adventure to explore dangerous regions, hunt monsters or enemy operatives, guide expeditions, secure routes, protect remote communities, or prove that no battlefield is truly open ground when preparation and range are on their side. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Exploration & Interaction Vision, stealth, traps, locks, theft, hazards, social rules, chases, and loot. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Vision, Stealth, Traps, Locks & Theft Vision and Light Cover, Line of Sight & Line of Effect Stealth and Infiltration Traps and Non-Aether Hazards Locks Theft and Pickpocket Social Interaction, Information & Captivity Vision, Stealth, Traps, Locks & Theft Vision and Light Light states are Bright Light, Dim Light, and Darkness. Obscuration states are Lightly Obscured and Heavily Obscured. Dim Light lightly obscures; Darkness heavily obscures a creature that cannot otherwise see through it. Daeva Darkvision treats Darkness within 60 feet as Dim Light, not Bright Light. A recommended ordinary light source has a stated Bright radius plus an equal additional Dim radius unless its own text says otherwise. Bright light does not universally prohibit Stealth. Obscurity and Invisibility do not automatically make a creature Hidden. Cover, Line of Sight & Line of Effect No Cover. No defensive benefit from Cover. Half Cover. A creature or object behind meaningful partial obstruction gains +2 AC and +2 to Dexterity saving throws against effects originating from the covered direction. Intervening creatures can provide Half Cover when they materially obstruct the line. Full Cover. Full Cover blocks the relevant Line of Effect and prevents direct targeting through that obstruction unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Three-Quarters Cover does not exist in Wings of Atreia. Cover does not stack; use the best applicable Cover. Altitude neither inherently grants nor ignores Cover. Line of Sight and Line of Effect are distinct. Line of Sight determines whether you can see a target or point. Line of Effect determines whether an attack, spell, or effect can physically reach it. Heavy obscurement is not Cover by itself. Stealth and Infiltration Use scene states Undetected, Suspicious, and Alerted; these are not Conditions. Stealth must exceed Passive Perception; ties favor the observer. An active Search uses the GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation), against the relevant DC or opposing Stealth; ties favor the Searcher where opposed. Do not reroll Stealth every 5 feet; roll again only when circumstances materially change. For group Stealth, at least half the group must succeed. A failed check may create Suspicion rather than immediate full alarm when appropriate. Distractions create an opportunity to Hide rather than automatic success. Disguises are primarily social. Invisibility is not the same as Hidden. Wings do not automatically prevent Stealth. Traps and Non-Aether Hazards Describe a hazard with Trigger, Detection, Avoid/Disable method, Save/Check, Effect, and Reset/Duration. Hazards may be obvious, concealed, or hidden. Detection normally uses Passive Perception, active Perception, or Investigation. Disable methods depend on the mechanism and can use Sleight of Hand, Investigation, Athletics, or another appropriate Skill. There is no mandatory Thieves’ Tools system. Failure triggers the hazard only when the hazard says so. Damage and Conditions use existing universal rules. Forced movement is horizontal unless the hazard explicitly creates vertical displacement. Hazards normally resolve when triggered rather than taking their own Initiative turns. Repeat attempts require changed circumstances. Locks Mechanical Lock DC Simple 10 Standard 12 Secure 15 High Security 18 Exceptional 20+ The correct key opens a normal lock without a check. Mechanical locks generally use Dexterity (Sleight of Hand). Unusual mechanisms can use Intelligence (Investigation). Forcing uses Strength (Athletics); destroying a lock or door uses normal object/destruction adjudication. Failure does not automatically break or trigger a lock unless its design says so. Aether locks use Aether Interaction. If a task is impossible, do not assign an absurd DC—state that it cannot be done by that method. Theft and Pickpocket A theft attempt requires a plausible opportunity. Taking an accessible small item uses Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) against Passive Perception and must exceed it. If the target is actively watching, oppose with active Perception; ties favor the observer. Secured items can require a different approach. Failure may create suspicion or alarm. Success means the theft was unnoticed at that moment; later discovery remains possible. Distraction creates opportunity rather than automatic success. Help can grant +2 when genuinely meaningful. Worn armor, shields, Wings, wielded weapons, and equipped mandatory implements cannot simply be pickpocketed. Repeated attempts require changed circumstances. Social Interaction, Informati

WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Combat Turn structure, actions, movement, attacks, damage, conditions, death, rests, and survival. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative Round and Turn Action Economy Attack Action Universal Actions Ready Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative, rounds, and combat-only resources are used only for genuine combat or another situation where structured turn order is necessary. Characters cannot manufacture artificial combat to farm cooldowns, resources, or timing triggers. Initiative Initiative = 1d20 + Dexterity modifier. Do not add PB unless an explicit feature says so. Alert adds +2 Initiative. There is no Surprise Round and Surprise does not grant Advantage on Initiative. When one side genuinely catches another side unaware, the GM may, at discretion, allow one appropriate pre-Initiative attack roll against the target's normal defense before Initiative is rolled. This is not an extra round, is not automatic, and does not create a general Surprise action economy. After that resolution, roll Initiative normally. Round and Turn One combat round represents approximately six seconds in the game world. Each participant normally takes one turn in Initiative order. All turns in the round abstract actions occurring within the same six-second span; do not add each turn as another six seconds. Action Economy Action. One per turn. Movement. Up to the creature’s available movement, subject to terrain and conditions. Bonus Action. Up to one, but only when a feature grants something that uses a Bonus Action. Reaction. Normally one per round, refreshing at the start of the creature’s turn unless an explicit class rule says otherwise. Object interaction. One free simple object interaction per turn. There is no universal Action-to-Bonus-Action or Bonus-Action-to-Action conversion. Unused movement or Actions are not stored for later turns. Attack Action The Attack Action makes one attack unless a feature such as Extra Attack says otherwise. Grapple and Shove are full Actions and do not replace one attack within Extra Attack. Player Weapon Requirement. A player character must be wielding an approved class weapon to take the normal Attack Action. Unarmed Attacks and Improvised Weapons are not player combat options unless a later explicit feature creates a specific exception. Opportunity Attacks. Opportunity Attacks remain part of the core combat rules. When a hostile creature you can perceive voluntarily leaves your melee reach, you may use your Reaction to make one melee attack against it, resolving the attack before it leaves that reach. Forced movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Universal Actions Dash. Gain additional movement equal to your current Speed for the turn. Difficult Terrain and other movement costs still apply. While flying, Dash adds horizontal movement but does not grant an additional altitude-layer change. Disengage. Until the end of your turn, your movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks. Dodge. Until the start of your next turn, attacks against you have Disadvantage if you can perceive the attacker, and you have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws. Dodge ends if you become Incapacitated or your Speed becomes 0. Hide. You must have meaningful concealment or another circumstance that allows hiding. Make Dexterity (Stealth) against Passive Perception or active Perception as appropriate. You cannot Hide while clearly seen. Hidden is not Invisible. Making an attack reveals your position after that attack resolves. Search. Deliberately search using a GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation). Use Object. Use this Action for substantial manipulation beyond the one free simple object interaction. A specific item’s activation rule controls when it states another cost. Ready A creature can prepare one Action for a perceivable trigger. When the trigger occurs, the creature may use its Reaction to perform the readied Action. Ready does not store ordinary movement, but Dash can be readied as the Action. Readied attacks retain all weapon properties. A readied spell must still meet implement and targeting requirements when released. Losing a mandatory implement before release prevents release. Concentration begins when the spell actually resolves. Ready never bypasses aerial restrictions, range, or other universal rules. Simultaneous Effects Effects resolve one at a time. The active creature orders its own simultaneous effects; the GM orders GM-controlled simultaneous effects. For opposing same-time effects, resolve the active creature first, then use Initiative if needed. Damage resolves before state changes caused by that da
