WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Glossary & Core Terms A player-facing A–Z reference for the vocabulary used throughout Wings of Atreia, with direct links to the full rules and lore pages. How to use this page: definitions here are quick-reference summaries. Follow the “Read more” link whenever you need the complete rule, class text, or world context. A B C D E F G I K L M P R S U W 46 terms A Action Your main turn action. Many attacks, spells, class features, and other options specify that they use your Action. Read more: Combat → Advantage / Disadvantage Roll two d20s and use the higher result for Advantage or the lower result for Disadvantage. Read more: Core Resolution → Aether The supernatural power that underlies Daeva abilities, spellcasting, flight, and many extraordinary phenomena in Atreia. Read more: Aether & Spellcasting → Aether Enhancement The higher equipment-quality path beyond Profession +2. Aether upgrades are level-gated and handled separately from ordinary Profession work. Read more: Equipment → Ascension The transformation by which a mortal becomes a Daeva and receives Wings. WoA begins with this event in Session 0. Read more: Character Creation → At-Will A spell or ability frequency that may be used whenever its normal action and other requirements are met. Read more: Aether & Spellcasting → B Background A character-creation choice representing experience and identity before or around Ascension; it provides its defined skills and related benefits. Read more: Backgrounds → Bonus Action A secondary turn action available only when a feature, spell, or rule explicitly gives an option that uses it. Read more: Combat → C Character Manager The official WoA character-management method for creation records, advancement, current resources, equipment, spells, and other tracked character data. Read more: Character Creation → Class Your Daeva’s primary mechanical path. WoA uses eleven classes and does not use multiclassing. Read more: Classes → Class Resource A class-specific pool, charge, stance, meter, or other tracked mechanic defined by that class. Read more: Quick Reference → Class Save DC Normally 8 + Proficiency Bonus + the class ability identified by your class, unless a rule states otherwise. Read more: Core Resolution → Concentration A spell/effect limit: only one Concentration effect can be maintained at a time, and Incapacitated ends it. WoA does not use Concentration saving throws. Read more: Aether & Spellcasting → Condition A named rules state such as Poisoned or Incapacitated that changes what a creature can do or how rolls affect it. Read more: Combat → Cooldown A spell or ability frequency that becomes unavailable after use until its stated cooldown is satisfied; WoA also uses the universal out-of-combat cooldown rule where applicable. Read more: Aether & Spellcasting → D Daeva An Ascended immortal warrior of Atreia. Player characters in Wings of Atreia are Daevas. Read more: Character Creation → Daeva Points (DP) A resource unlocked at Level 10 and earned through participation in genuine combat victories. DP powers Ultimate Abilities and persists through rests. Read more: Daeva Points & Ultimates → E Empyrean Boon A powerful universal character option gained at Level 19 according to the advancement rules. Read more: Feats & Empyrean Boons → Empyrean Lord One of the great Daeva Lords whose authority and legacy shape Elyos and Asmodian civilization, together with the two historic Tower Guardians. Read more: World → F Faction Your character’s allegiance as Elyos or Asmodian. Faction affects culture, homeland, and campaign relationships rather than class statistics. Read more: Character Creation → Feat A universal character option chosen at designated advancement points instead of an Ability Score Improvement where the rules allow it. Read more: Feats & Empyrean Boons → Flight Slot A tracked unit of a Daeva’s flight capacity. The number of Flight Slots increases with character level. Read more: Flight → G Genuine Combat A real encounter using initiative and combat timing. Artificial encounters cannot be used to farm resources such as Daeva Points. Read more: Combat → I Implement A spellcasting equipment category that can follow the established quality and enhancement progression. Read more: Equipment → K Kinah The standard currency used for purchases, profession training, supplies, and other economic transactions. Read more: Professions & Economy → L Legendary Equipment Story-driven top-tier equipment above the Aether enhancement tiers. Legendary items are not ordinary Profession products. Read more: Equipment → Long Rest An 8-hour recovery period. What it restores depends on the specific class, spell, feature, or rule. Read more: Combat → Lord Action The dedicated off-turn action framework used by Empyrean Lords and Dragon Lords. Read more: Combat → M Milestone Advancement WoA’s advancement method. Characters gain levels through campaign m

text: Understanding Your Background. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Backgrounds All nine player Backgrounds, their skill choices, roleplaying guidance, Languages, and Territorial Familiarity. Source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page is a player-facing reference extracted from the handbook rather than a replacement ruleset. Background Rules Soldier Scholar Acolyte Noble Outlander Underworld Artisan Merchant Entertainer Languages Background Rules Skill Selection: Choose exactly 2 Background Skills from the six options listed for your Background. Duplicate selections are prohibited. A Skill selected as a Class Skill cannot also be selected as a Background Skill. The four selected Class and Background Skill Proficiencies must therefore be four different Skills. Background Choose 2 Skills Soldier Athletics, Intimidation, Perception, Survival, Medicine, Religion Scholar Arcana, History, Investigation, Religion, Medicine, Perception Acolyte History, Insight, Medicine, Religion, Athletics, Survival Noble History, Insight, Persuasion, Performance, Investigation, Sleight of Hand Outlander Athletics, Nature, Perception, Survival, Persuasion, Stealth Underworld Deception, Insight, Sleight of Hand, Stealth, Investigation, Persuasion Artisan Investigation, Perception, Sleight of Hand, History, Arcana, Persuasion Merchant Insight, Investigation, Persuasion, History, Stealth, Athletics Entertainer Acrobatics, Deception, Performance, Persuasion, Nature, Animal Handling A relevant Background may establish that you have the experience necessary to attempt obscure or specialized knowledge. It does not automatically grant Advantage, Expertise, a numerical bonus, or guaranteed success. Understanding Your Background Your Class describes what your character has learned to do as an adventuring Daeva. Your Background describes the life, training, profession, upbringing, or experiences that helped shape who they were before the campaign began. Faction tells you where you belong, Background helps explain where you came from, and Class describes how you operate as an adventurer. A Background does not determine your morality, personality, beliefs, faction loyalty, or future choices. Two characters with the same Background may have completely different lives and goals. Mechanically, use the Background table above exactly as written: choose two skills from your Background’s listed skill pool. The entries below add roleplaying context and do not grant additional rules benefits. Soldier What Is a Soldier?. A Soldier has meaningful experience with organized military service: troops, guards, scouts, officers, fortress personnel, or other disciplined fighting forces. Life and Origins. Military life may have included patrols, garrison duty, campaigns, escort work, reconnaissance, fortification defense, or service under a commander. That service may have occurred before or after ascension. Motivations and Outlook. Duty, loyalty, comradeship, ambition, patriotism, protection, regret, or the memory of fallen companions may still shape the character. A Soldier may respect military order, resent it, or be deciding what is truly worth fighting for. Playing a Soldier. Decide what kind of service shaped you, who you served beside, and what relationship you now have with authority and your former comrades. Being a Soldier does not require obedience or a martial Class. Scholar What Is a Scholar?. A Scholar has devoted part of their life to seeking, preserving, interpreting, or teaching knowledge. Scholars include researchers, historians, scribes, teachers, philosophers, archivists, investigators, and field specialists. Life and Origins. Study may have taken place under a teacher, within an archive or institution, or independently. Subjects can include history, geography, creatures, Aether, ruins, cultures, warfare, or any other serious field of inquiry. Motivations and Outlook. A Scholar may adventure to recover lost knowledge, investigate mysteries, study ruins or creatures directly, protect important discoveries, or prevent dangerous knowledge from being misused. Playing a Scholar. Choose the subject that fascinates you and decide whether you are an academic, a practical field researcher, or something between. Being scholarly does not require being socially awkward or confined to books. Acolyte What Is an Acolyte?. An Acolyte has meaningful experience with religious or spiritual service, sacred traditions, temples, ceremonies, or communities of worship. Life and Origins. The character may have been raised around a temple, studied under a religious teacher, volunteered in a sacred institution, maintained holy places, assisted ceremonies, or found faith after a life-changing event. Motivations and Outlook. Faith, service, protection, reform, doubt, duty, spiritual curiosity, or concern for a community may lead an Acolyte into adventure. An Acolyte can be devout, q

text: Understanding Your Background. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Character Creation Create your Daeva from faction and class through abilities, Background, starting equipment, skills, and proficiencies. Character-management workflow on this page is synchronized to Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.13 — CHARACTER_MANAGER_SYNC . The full current rules remain authoritative if any website summary differs. Character Creation Step by Step Universal Daeva Traits Starting Equipment & Kinah Ability Scores Abilities and the 18 Skills Backgrounds and Proficiencies Understanding Your Background Character Creation Step by Step 1. Choose Elyos or Asmodian. 2. Choose one of the 11 classes. 3. Assign 16, 14, 14, 12, 10, 8 among STR, DEX, CON, INT, WIS and CHA. 4. Choose one Background. 5. Enter class saving throws, armor, shield and weapon access in the Character Manager. 6. Choose exactly 2 Class Skills from the six Skill options listed for your Class and exactly 2 Background Skills from the six Skill options listed for your Background. Duplicate selections are prohibited. A Skill selected as a Class Skill cannot also be selected as a Background Skill; the four selected Skill Proficiencies must therefore be four different Skills. 7. Calculate HP, AC, Initiative, class Save DC, Speed, Passive Perception, and Passive Investigation. 8. Enter starting Common equipment, Common Wings and starting Kinah in the Character Manager. 9. Choose name, appearance, wing appearance, personality, history, relationships and motivation. Character Manager. The Wings of Atreia Character Manager is the official character record for creation, live play, and advancement. Enter your character choices and starting values there as you complete the steps above. The Character Manager tracks the character’s current state; the current Player Handbook and Core Rulebook remain authoritative if a displayed value and the governing rule ever differ. Universal Daeva Traits Trait Rule Creature Type Humanoid (Daeva) Size Medium Walking Speed 30 ft Darkvision 60 ft Ageless Living beings who do not age normally. Manifest Wings Every Daeva has functional Common Wings. Aether-Dependent Flight Flight depends on local Aether conditions. Aetheric Reconstitution A Daeva who truly dies may reform through a functioning attuned Obelisk under the reconstitution rules. Starting Equipment & Kinah Every character begins with one fixed base class weapon or implement, one armor set, Common Wings, and starting Kinah. No character automatically receives potions, ammunition bundles, upgraded equipment, extra adventuring gear, or a shield unless a class feature or other explicit rule grants it. Starting Kinah = 500 Kinah + 250 Kinah for each character level above 1. A Level 1 character starts with 500 Kinah; a Level 20 character starts with 5,250 Kinah. Class Fixed Base Weapon / Implement Armor Gladiator Longsword Plate Templar Longsword Plate Assassin Dagger Leather Ranger Longbow Leather Sorcerer Magical Orb Cloth Spiritmaster Spellbook Cloth Cleric Mace Chain Chanter Staff Chain Aethertech Shortsword Chain Gunslinger Pistol Leather Songweaver Lyre Cloth Ability Scores Score Modifier 1 -5 2–3 -4 4–5 -3 6–7 -2 8–9 -1 10–11 +0 12–13 +1 14–15 +2 16–17 +3 18–19 +4 20 +5 Starting Rule. Use the fixed array 16, 14, 14, 12, 10, 8. No rolling and no point buy. Faction, Background and universal Daeva traits grant no starting Ability Score increases. Abilities and the 18 Skills A skill is a trained way of applying an ability. The GM chooses the ability that best fits the approach; the familiar ability below is the normal pairing. These are player-use explanations, not new automatic bonuses. Skill Usual Ability What It Lets You Attempt Acrobatics DEX Balance, controlled movement, tumbling, landing and physically awkward agility. Animal Handling WIS Calm, understand, direct or manage ordinary trainable creatures. Arcana INT Magic, Aether theory, magical phenomena, spell structures and intellectual Aether analysis. Athletics STR Climb, jump, swim, grapple-related exertion and other raw physical effort. Deception CHA Mislead, bluff, conceal intent, maintain a false story or impersonate. History INT Recall public history, cultures, institutions, conflicts and notable people or places. Insight WIS Read motives, sincerity, emotional state and social intent; not mind reading. Source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page is a player-facing reference extracted from the handbook rather than a replacement ruleset. Background Rules Soldier Scholar Acolyte Noble Outlander Underworld Artisan Merchant Entertainer Languages Background Rules Skill Selection: Choose exactly 2 Background Skills from the six options listed for your Background. Duplicate selections are prohibited. A Skill selected as a Class Skill cannot also be selected as a Background Skill. The four selected Class and Background Skill Proficiencies must therefore be four different Skills. Background Choose 2 Skills Soldier Athletics, Intimidation, Perception, Survival, Medicine, Religion Scholar Arcana, History, Investigation, Religion, Medicine, Perception Acolyte History, Insight, Medicine, Religion, Athletics, Survival Noble History, Insight, Persuasion, Performance, Investigation, Sleight of Hand Outlander Athletics, Nature, Perception, Survival, Persuasion, Stealth Underworld Deception, Insight, Sleight of Hand, Stealth, Investigation, Persuasion Artisan Investigation, Perception, Sleight of Hand, History, Arcana, Persuasion Merchant Insight, Investigation, Persuasion, History, Stealth, Athletics Entertainer Acrobatics, Deception, Performance, Persuasion, Nature, Animal Handling A relevant Background may establish that you have the experience necessary to attempt obscure or specialized knowledge. It does not automatically grant Advantage, Expertise, a numerical bonus, or guaranteed success. Understanding Your Background Your Class describes what your character has learned to do as an adventuring Daeva. Your Background describes the life, training, profession, upbringing, or experiences that helped shape who they were before the campaign began. Faction tells you where you belong, Background helps explain where you came from, and Class describes how you operate as an adventurer. A Background does not determine your morality, personality, beliefs, faction loyalty, or future choices. Two characters with the same Background may have completely different lives and goals. Mechanically, use the Background table above exactly as written: choose two skills from your Background’s listed skill pool. The entries below add roleplaying context and do not grant additional rules benefits. Soldier What Is a Soldier?. A Soldier has meaningful experience with organized military service: troops, guards, scouts, officers, fortress personnel, or other disciplined fighting forces. Life and Origins. Military life may have included patrols, garrison duty, campaigns, escort work, reconnaissance, fortification defense, or service under a commander. That service may have occurred before or after ascension. Motivations and Outlook. Duty, loyalty, comradeship, ambition, patriotism, protection, regret, or the memory of fallen companions may still shape the character. A Soldier may respect military order, resent it, or be deciding what is truly worth fighting for. Playing a Soldier. Decide what kind of service shaped you, who you served beside, and what relationship you now have with authority and your former comrades. Being a Soldier does not require obedience or a martial Class. Scholar What Is a Scholar?. A Scholar has devoted part of their life to seeking, preserving, interpreting, or teaching knowledge. Scholars include researchers, historians, scribes, teachers, philosophers, archivists, investigators, and field specialists. Life and Origins. Study may have taken place under a teacher, within an archive or institution, or independently. Subjects can include history, geography, creatures, Aether, ruins, cultures, warfare, or any other serious field of inquiry. Motivations and Outlook. A Scholar may adventure to recover lost knowledge, investigate mysteries, study ruins or creatures directly, protect important discoveries, or prevent dangerous knowledge from being misused. Playing a Scholar. Choose the subject that fascinates you and decide whether you are an academic, a practical field researcher, or something between. Being scholarly does not require being socially awkward or confined to books. Acolyte What Is an Acolyte?. An Acolyte has meaningful experience with religious or spiritual service, sacred traditions, temples, ceremonies, or communities of worship. Life and Origins. The character may have been raised around a temple, studied under a religious teacher, volunteered in a sacred institution, maintained holy places, assisted ceremonies, or found faith after a life-changing event. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Legions & Complete Abyss Warfront System Player-created Legions plus the complete player-operable Warfront rules, unit catalogue, War Asset costs, Fortress procedures, and Open Abyss procedures. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Core Rulebook v4.2 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026 , synchronized with Player Handbook v3.10 . This page exposes the complete player-operable Warfront subsystem. Explicitly GM-facing enemy statblocks, hidden force composition, and closed GM-only resolution tables remain off the public player site. Legions Warfront Overview War Assets Unit Statistics Battle Exchange Unit Catalogue Unit Costs PC Participation Fortress Wars Open Abyss Reinforcements Quick Reference PLAYER-CREATED LEGIONS A player-created Legion is a lightweight organization for shared identity, missions, resources, and cross-faction cooperation when the campaign permits it. Legion membership does not create a new character progression track or grant automatic combat bonuses. When a Legion Can Be Founded Campaign Gate. The Campaign Director or controlling GM must explicitly declare Legion Founding available. Reaching Level 11 by itself does not unlock the system. Founding Player. One Founding Player must be Level 11 or higher. That character becomes the initial Legion Leader. Other members. Every other founding or joining member must be Level 3 or higher before joining and must already have reached their Specialization or Archetype choice where applicable. A Level 1-2 character cannot join early. Membership has no maximum size. There is no minimum number of additional founders; a qualifying Founding Player may establish the Legion alone if all other founding requirements are satisfied. Elyos and Asmodians may belong to the same Legion once the required campaign state is active. Every member retains their original faction identity and its normal consequences. Founding Fund and Treasury Founding requires 5,000 Kinah deposited into the new Legion Treasury. Eligible founding members may contribute toward the total. Before establishment, the Founding Fund cannot be withdrawn. If founding is abandoned, each contributor receives their contribution back. Once established, the 5,000 Kinah remains usable Treasury money. Any Legion member may deposit Kinah. Only the Legion Leader may withdraw Kinah or authorize spending. Legion missions may reward participating members, the Treasury, or both as determined by the GM. There is no passive Legion income, automatic salary, interest, business-profit engine, or mandatory recurring membership dues. Leadership and Membership The only default roles are Legion Leader and Legion Member. The Legion Leader admits and removes members, controls permissions for Legion assets, may transfer leadership, and may formally dissolve the Legion. Leadership may be transferred to any existing legal Legion member. The new Leader does not need to be Level 11; Level 11 is a founding requirement only. Member Benefits Members may display the Legion name, colors, crest, and insignia. Ordinary Legion identification occupies no Inventory Slot. Members may accept Legion missions and may use resources, facilities, contacts, and support the Legion actually possesses when the Legion Leader permits it. Where the campaign's cross-faction arrangements recognize the Legion, its insignia provides a legitimate reason for Elyos and Asmodian members to operate together. It does not grant diplomatic immunity or unrestricted access. Legion membership grants no automatic Hit, AC, damage, HP, saving throw, skill, Advantage, Spell DC, DP, class-resource, equipment-quality, or personal Inventory bonus. Legion Storage and Headquarters An established Legion has one secure shared Storage location with a capacity of 100 Inventory Slots. Normal Inventory Slot and stacking rules apply; Kinah remains in the Treasury and uses no Storage Slots. Any Legion member may deposit eligible items. Only the Legion Leader may withdraw items or authorize another member to retrieve them. Legion Storage is stationary and cannot be accessed remotely. It never increases a member's personal Inventory capacity in the field. A Legion may designate one legitimate location as its Headquarters. The Headquarters is simply its meeting place and Storage location; it grants no automatic bonuses and has no upgrade track. Lightweight Rule. There is no Legion XP, Legion Level, officer hierarchy, skill tree, research tree, reputation meter, headquarters progression, or other default Legion management subsystem. Abyss Warfront System Warfronts resolve formation-scale warfare separately from ordinary character-scale combat. They are used for Fortress Wars and Open Abyss Battles. Strategic travel and marching between major engagements are handled narratively, off-table, or during downtime. Shared Warfront Command The player side uses one shared strat

WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Combat Turn structure, actions, movement, attacks, damage, conditions, death, rests, and survival. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative Round and Turn Action Economy Attack Action Universal Actions Ready Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative, rounds, and combat-only resources are used only for genuine combat or another situation where structured turn order is necessary. Characters cannot manufacture artificial combat to farm cooldowns, resources, or timing triggers. Initiative Initiative = 1d20 + Dexterity modifier. Do not add PB unless an explicit feature says so. Alert adds +2 Initiative. There is no Surprise Round and Surprise does not grant Advantage on Initiative. When one side genuinely catches another side unaware, the GM may, at discretion, allow one appropriate pre-Initiative attack roll against the target's normal defense before Initiative is rolled. This is not an extra round, is not automatic, and does not create a general Surprise action economy. After that resolution, roll Initiative normally. Round and Turn One combat round represents approximately six seconds in the game world. Each participant normally takes one turn in Initiative order. All turns in the round abstract actions occurring within the same six-second span; do not add each turn as another six seconds. Action Economy Action. One per turn. Movement. Up to the creature’s available movement, subject to terrain and conditions. Bonus Action. Up to one, but only when a feature grants something that uses a Bonus Action. Reaction. Normally one per round, refreshing at the start of the creature’s turn unless an explicit class rule says otherwise. Object interaction. One free simple object interaction per turn. There is no universal Action-to-Bonus-Action or Bonus-Action-to-Action conversion. Unused movement or Actions are not stored for later turns. Attack Action The Attack Action makes one attack unless a feature such as Extra Attack says otherwise. Grapple and Shove are full Actions and do not replace one attack within Extra Attack. Player Weapon Requirement. A player character must be wielding an approved class weapon to take the normal Attack Action. Unarmed Attacks and Improvised Weapons are not player combat options unless a later explicit feature creates a specific exception. Opportunity Attacks. Opportunity Attacks remain part of the core combat rules. When a hostile creature you can perceive voluntarily leaves your melee reach, you may use your Reaction to make one melee attack against it, resolving the attack before it leaves that reach. Forced movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Universal Actions Dash. Gain additional movement equal to your current Speed for the turn. Difficult Terrain and other movement costs still apply. While flying, Dash adds horizontal movement but does not grant an additional altitude-layer change. Disengage. Until the end of your turn, your movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks. Dodge. Until the start of your next turn, attacks against you have Disadvantage if you can perceive the attacker, and you have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws. Dodge ends if you become Incapacitated or your Speed becomes 0. Hide. You must have meaningful concealment or another circumstance that allows hiding. Make Dexterity (Stealth) against Passive Perception or active Perception as appropriate. You cannot Hide while clearly seen. Hidden is not Invisible. Making an attack reveals your position after that attack resolves. Search. Deliberately search using a GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation). Use Object. Use this Action for substantial manipulation beyond the one free simple object interaction. A specific item’s activation rule controls when it states another cost. Ready A creature can prepare one Action for a perceivable trigger. When the trigger occurs, the creature may use its Reaction to perform the readied Action. Ready does not store ordinary movement, but Dash can be readied as the Action. Readied attacks retain all weapon properties. A readied spell must still meet implement and targeting requirements when released. Losing a mandatory implement before release prevents release. Concentration begins when the spell actually resolves. Ready never bypasses aerial restrictions, range, or other universal rules. Simultaneous Effects Effects resolve one at a time. The active creature orders its own simultaneous effects; the GM orders GM-controlled simultaneous effects. For opposing same-time effects, resolve the active creature first, then use Initiative if needed. Damage resolves before state changes caused by that damage. S

Advancement is milestone-only. Level 20 is the maximum normal level. There is no automatic post-Level-20 progression, recurring ASIs, additional class levels or recurring Boons. What to Do Every Time You Level Up • Read the full class-level entry and every specialization feature gained at that level. • Increase maximum HP using the class's fixed HP gain, CON modifier and class durability rules. • Update PB only if the universal table changes it. • Update class resource caps, dice, ranges, trap limits, spirit/Bastion chassis or other scaling. • Make an ASI/Feat choice if the level grants one. • Apply Spell Advancements if your class grants them, using the spell advancement rules. • Update Flight Slots, Exploration Flight and Inventory Slots. • Recalculate class Save DC, spell attack, AC, passive values and PB/ability-dependent features. • If you are changing your Active Profession, make that change now; Active Profession changes are allowed only when you gain a character level. Character Manager. Apply level-up choices and resulting character-state changes in the Wings of Atreia Character Manager after resolving the governing class and advancement rules. The rules determine what changes; the Character Manager records and tracks the resulting character state. ASI / Feat Choices Whenever your class grants a Feat / Ability Score Improvement, choose one: +2 to one Ability Score; +1 to two different Ability Scores; or one eligible Universal Feat. An Ability Score normally cannot exceed 20 through an ASI. Level Choice 4 ASI or Universal Feat 8 ASI or Universal Feat 12 ASI or Universal Feat 16 ASI or Universal Feat 19 Empyrean Boon; not a normal ASI Universal Feats — Full Player Explanations Feat Prerequisite Exact Benefit Player Use Alert None +2 Initiative. You cannot be Surprised while conscious. Acting early and staying ready. Skilled None Gain proficiency in two Skills. Duplicate proficiency must be replaced with another choice. Broader exploration/social competence. Expertise Proficient in chosen Skill Double PB contribution for one proficient Skill. Doubling effects do not stack. One signature highly reliable skill. Keen Senses None +2 passive Perception and passive Investigation. Active checks unchanged. Notice threats and clues passively. Mobile None Walking Speed +10 ft. Dash ignores extra cost of Difficult Terrain for that turn. Does not increase Flight. Ground repositioning. Sure-Footed None Advantage on checks/saves specifically to resist being knocked Prone by terrain, hazards or forced movement. Defensive stability. Weapon Specialist Access/proficiency with chosen weapon Choose one weapon. Once per turn before an attack roll with it, you may gain +2 to that attack roll. Reliability on one key weapon hit. Tough None HP maximum increases by 2 × character level when selected, then +2 each later level. Durability. Resilient Level 8 Choose a saving throw you lack proficiency in; gain proficiency. Patch a defensive weakness. Aerial Endurance Level 16 +2 maximum Flight Slot. Longer aerial combat. Controlled Descent None Successful DC 12 DEX Emergency Landing save causes 0 falling damage instead of half. Safer forced landing. Master Glider None Exploration Glide ratio improves 3:1 → 4:1. 1-hour cooldown remains. Exploration mobility. Aerial Conditioning None First grounded Flight Slot recovery

text: Universal Gunslinger Safeguards. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Tempo • Firearm Rhythm • Reload Mastery • Mobile Precision Gunslinger “A bullet sounds the same to everybody.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Tempo, Firearms, and Reload Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Tradition & Outlook Specialization Reassignment The Gunslinger is a mobile firearm martial whose power comes from maintaining Tempo through successful firearm play. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Fire. Move. Reload. Keep the rhythm alive long enough to turn Tempo into control, defense, and lethal pressure. Class Identity Gunslingers are technist marksmen who turn Aether-assisted firearms into speed, precision, and controlled ranged pressure. Pistols support rapid, mobile sequences through Quick Shot and Akimbo, while Muskets provide deliberate two-handed fire that concentrates Tempo into stronger individual hits through Deliberate Shot. Tempo represents the Gunslinger’s ability to build combat rhythm through successful action rather than treating every shot as an isolated event. Tradition & Outlook Gunslingers belong to Atreia’s newer technological traditions. The wider Aion tradition describes early firearm research being dismissed as technist tinkering until battlefield success forced major institutions to recognize the discipline. Wings of Atreia keeps that identity of innovation earning legitimacy through results while using Pistols and Muskets as the class’s only firearm categories. Gunslingers often value nerve, technical familiarity, accuracy, independence, and adaptability. Appearance & Adventuring Gunslingers favor mobile equipment, ammunition management, firearm maintenance, and a practical awareness of range and firing position. Their weapons can make them look strikingly modern beside older martial traditions, but their discipline remains Aetheric and distinctly Atreian. They adventure to test new techniques, serve as ranged specialists, hunt dangerous targets, protect expeditions from positions others cannot exploit, or demonstrate that innovation has earned its place in the war for Atreia. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Role Ranged weapon damage Secondary Role Mobility, precision, disruption Primary Ability DEX Secondary Ability INT Hit Die d8 Saving Throws DEX, INT Armor Leather Skills Choose 2 from 6: Acrobatics, Deception, Investigation, Perception, Sleight of Hand, Survival Weapons Pistols, Muskets Signature Resource Tempo Signature Mechanic Firearm sequencing and reload rhythm Core Engine — Tempo, Firearms, and Reload The Gunslinger is a mobile firearm martial whose power comes from maintaining Tempo through successful firearm play. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols Ranged Gunslinger One-handed Weapon Attack. Range 30/90 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d8 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. A Gunslinger can wield two Pistols, but doing so does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols are compatible with Quick Shot and Akimbo. Muskets Ranged Gunslinger Two-handed Weapon Attack. Range 60/180 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d12 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. Ammunition capacity is fixed at 2. Muskets cannot use Quick Shot or Akimbo. Gunslinger ammunition-restoration features can restore Musket shots normally, but a Musket can never hold more than 2 shots. Standard one-handed firearm capacity increases do not apply to Muskets. Reload Every firearm attack consumes one shot. A firearm with no shots remaining is Empty and cannot make firearm attacks until at least one shot is restored. Normal Bonus Action Reload: an Empty firearm is restored to its full Reload capacity. Ammunition restoration is not the Reload action unless a feature explicitly says so. Ammunition-restoration features can restore shots to either Pistols or Muskets up to that firearm's maximum capacity. A Musket's maximum capacity remains 2. Switching between carried one-handed Gunslinger firearms as part of a firearm attack requires no separate object interaction. Standard one-handed firearm capacity progression: Ammo Capacity 4 at Levels 1-4, Ammo Capacity 5 at 5-8, Ammo Capacity 6 at 9-14, and Ammo Capacity 7 at 15-20. Increasing capacity does not automatically reload an Empty firearm. Tempo Tempo is a genuine-combat resource representing firing rhythm, accuracy, and momentum. It begins at 0, resets to 0 when combat ends, and artificial initiative cannot generate it. Maximum Tempo: Levels 1-4 = 3; 5-8 = 4; 9-12 = 5; 13-16 = 6; 17-20 = 7. Clean Hit: after

text: Universal Model. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Aether & Spellcasting Aether environment and interaction, universal spellcasting, and Spell Advancement. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Aether Environment, Interaction & Gathering Aether Interaction Aether Sources Refined Aether Gathering Aether Hazards Universal Spellcasting Universal Model Spell Acquisition Aether Environment, Interaction & Gathering Aether Interaction Aether Interaction uses Intelligence (Arcana) for intellectual analysis and Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) for physical manipulation. Typical DC guidance is 10, 12, 15, 18, or 20+ according to complexity and danger. Aether Sources Nodes, Currents, Fissures, and other environmental Aether phenomena can provide opportunities, hazards, travel effects, or Refined Aether. Their exact scene behavior is defined by the source. Refined Aether Gathering Gathering Refined Aether uses Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) against the source DC. Aether Level DC Yield Range Default Yield 1 8 2–6 4 2 10 6–12 9 3 12 12–24 18 4 15 24–40 32 5 18 40–60 50 The GM identifies a valid source and its Aether Level. Only the interacting character rolls. Apply normal modifiers and Help only if actually meaningful. On success, gain a yield within the listed range based on source richness; if no special richness is established, use the Default Yield. A successful gathering normally exhausts that source. Multiple deposits exist only when the GM explicitly establishes them. Failure gives no Refined Aether and does not automatically exhaust the source, but a new attempt requires a meaningful change in circumstances. Another party member does not automatically create a fresh attempt. Normal gathering is not performed during active combat unless gathering itself is an explicit encounter objective. Already-refined Aether recovered from caches or stores is ordinary loot and requires no gathering check. Aether Hazards Aether Hazards use the universal sequence Trigger → Save → DC → Effect → Duration. Standard severity bands are Minor DC 10–11, Moderate DC 12–14, Severe DC 15–17, and Extreme DC 18–20+. The four approved hazard families are Aether Storm, Aether Surge, Aether Eruption, and Unstable Zone. Each specific hazard defines its actual Trigger, Save, Effect, and Duration. Dangerous Aether changes are normally telegraphed in advance unless the hazard is specifically concealed. Strategic Refined Aether uses not defined in this handbook are deferred unless a future subsystem explicitly establishes them. Vehicle-related Refined Aether rules remain deferred with vehicle rules, and the current Abyss Warfront system uses no universal Refined Aether conversion for Fortress power. Universal Spellcasting Universal Model WoA has no spell slots and no cantrip category. Each spell is individually At-Will, Cooldown-based, Short-Rest limited, or Long-Rest limited. Class resources may modify spells but are not universal casting costs. Spell Acquisition Spells are class-granted abilities. They cannot be bought, sold, looted, copied from spellbooks or scrolls, learned from vendors, or acquired by commerce or exploration. A spell becomes available only when the character reaches its Unlock Level and, when applicable, satisfies the immediately preceding spell in its linear prerequisite chain. Unlocking a later spell never removes the earlier spell. Newly unlocked spells begin at Spell Level 1 unless explicitly stated otherwise. Spell Advancement — Final Rule. A class grants Spell Advancements according to its finalized progression. One Spell Advancement raises one eligible unlocked spell by 1 Spell Level, subject to that class’s Maximum Spell Level and listed prerequisites. Unspent Spell Advancements may be banked indefinitely, but banked or newly earned Spell Advancements may be spent only when the character gains a level; they cannot normally be spent during an adventure, between encounters, or during a rest. A character cannot spend more Spell Advancements than they have earned. Spell Retraining. There is no universal spell retraining. Once a Spell Advancement is spent, it is permanent unless a specific class feature, explicit story effect, or GM-approved exceptional circumstance directly permits reassignment. Casting Frequency and Action Economy At-Will spells may be cast whenever action economy permits. Cooldown X spells become available at the start of the caster’s Xth turn after the casting turn. Round-based cooldowns advance only during genuine combat; artificial Initiative cannot refresh, farm, or manipulate cooldowns or class resources. Outside genuine combat, a Cooldown spell becomes available again 1 minute after use unless the spell states a longer restriction. Short-Rest and Long-Rest spells regain uses after the named rest. Casting Time is binding. C

text: Universal Unit Catalogue. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Legions & Complete Abyss Warfront System Player-created Legions plus the complete player-operable Warfront rules, unit catalogue, War Asset costs, Fortress procedures, and Open Abyss procedures. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Core Rulebook v4.2 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026 , synchronized with Player Handbook v3.10 . This page exposes the complete player-operable Warfront subsystem. Explicitly GM-facing enemy statblocks, hidden force composition, and closed GM-only resolution tables remain off the public player site. Legions Warfront Overview War Assets Unit Statistics Battle Exchange Unit Catalogue Unit Costs PC Participation Fortress Wars Open Abyss Reinforcements Quick Reference PLAYER-CREATED LEGIONS A player-created Legion is a lightweight organization for shared identity, missions, resources, and cross-faction cooperation when the campaign permits it. Legion membership does not create a new character progression track or grant automatic combat bonuses. When a Legion Can Be Founded Campaign Gate. The Campaign Director or controlling GM must explicitly declare Legion Founding available. Reaching Level 11 by itself does not unlock the system. Founding Player. One Founding Player must be Level 11 or higher. That character becomes the initial Legion Leader. Other members. Every other founding or joining member must be Level 3 or higher before joining and must already have reached their Specialization or Archetype choice where applicable. A Level 1-2 character cannot join early. Membership has no maximum size. There is no minimum number of additional founders; a qualifying Founding Player may establish the Legion alone if all other founding requirements are satisfied. Elyos and Asmodians may belong to the same Legion once the required campaign state is active. Every member retains their original faction identity and its normal consequences. Founding Fund and Treasury Founding requires 5,000 Kinah deposited into the new Legion Treasury. Eligible founding members may contribute toward the total. Before establishment, the Founding Fund cannot be withdrawn. If founding is abandoned, each contributor receives their contribution back. Once established, the 5,000 Kinah remains usable Treasury money. Any Legion member may deposit Kinah. Only the Legion Leader may withdraw Kinah or authorize spending. Legion missions may reward participating members, the Treasury, or both as determined by the GM. There is no passive Legion income, automatic salary, interest, business-profit engine, or mandatory recurring membership dues. Leadership and Membership The only default roles are Legion Leader and Legion Member. The Legion Leader admits and removes members, controls permissions for Legion assets, may transfer leadership, and may formally dissolve the Legion. Leadership may be transferred to any existing legal Legion member. The new Leader does not need to be Level 11; Level 11 is a founding requirement only. Member Benefits Members may display the Legion name, colors, crest, and insignia. Ordinary Legion identification occupies no Inventory Slot. Members may accept Legion missions and may use resources, facilities, contacts, and support the Legion actually possesses when the Legion Leader permits it. Where the campaign's cross-faction arrangements recognize the Legion, its insignia provides a legitimate reason for Elyos and Asmodian members to operate together. It does not grant diplomatic immunity or unrestricted access. Legion membership grants no automatic Hit, AC, damage, HP, saving throw, skill, Advantage, Spell DC, DP, class-resource, equipment-quality, or personal Inventory bonus. Legion Storage and Headquarters An established Legion has one secure shared Storage location with a capacity of 100 Inventory Slots. Normal Inventory Slot and stacking rules apply; Kinah remains in the Treasury and uses no Storage Slots. Any Legion member may deposit eligible items. Only the Legion Leader may withdraw items or authorize another member to retrieve them. Legion Storage is stationary and cannot be accessed remotely. It never increases a member's personal Inventory capacity in the field. A Legion may designate one legitimate location as its Headquarters. The Headquarters is simply its meeting place and Storage location; it grants no automatic bonuses and has no upgrade track. Lightweight Rule. There is no Legion XP, Legion Level, officer hierarchy, skill tree, research tree, reputation meter, headquarters progression, or other default Legion management subsystem. Abyss Warfront System Warfronts resolve formation-scale warfare separately from ordinary character-scale combat. They are used for Fortress Wars and Open Abyss Battles. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Sneak Attack and Rune Marks Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Assassin is a precision melee striker that builds target-bound Rune Marks, converts them into burst damage or execution riders, and uses Shadow Step to remain difficult to pin down. Unlike a conventional Extra Attack martial, its Level 5 Assassination Sequence is a conditional follow-up attack tied to a successful Sneak Attack. Class Identity Assassins are precision predators who win through positioning, timing, concealment, and carefully prepared execution. Their art is not simply “attacking from stealth.” An Assassin studies a target, creates the right opening, carves Rune Marks, and converts preparation into a sudden lethal advantage. Their greatest strength is the ability to decide where and when a close-range confrontation becomes dangerous. Tradition & Outlook The Assassin tradition descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines and is practiced by infiltrators, covert operatives, hunters of dangerous individuals, intelligence agents, and Daevas who favor certainty over spectacle. Assassins often prize patience, awareness, self-control, and economy of motion. Their motives vary widely: service to a faction, revenge, professional duty, protection through preemptive action, or the pursuit of perfect technique. Appearance & Adventuring Assassins favor equipment that permits mobility and unobstructed movement, with Shortswords and Daggers forming the class’s approved weapon identity in Wings of Atreia. Their appearance may be subdued or ceremonial, but practical Assassins avoid anything that compromises movement or control. They adventure when a threat must be found before it strikes, a route must be infiltrated, an enemy leader must be neutralized, or a mystery demands someone comfortable operating unseen. Sneak Attack damage scales from 1d6 at Level 1 to 10d6 at Level 19. A character may have only one Active Profession at a time. The only Profession ranks are Apprentice and Master. There is no Profession XP, no intermediate rank, and no separate recipe, formula-book, manual, or recipe-learning subsystem. Earning a rank automatically grants the standard functions assigned to that rank. Rule Profession Ruling Starting Rank None. Backgrounds, including Artisan, grant no Profession rank. Inactive Profession Retains earned rank, paid entry fee, and completed Training Progress, but cannot be used or advanced. The trainee and trainer cannot adventure, undertake missions, perform adventuring travel, conduct other downtime work, perform Profession production, or complete other substantive activities that day. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Exploration & Interaction Vision, stealth, traps, locks, theft, hazards, social rules, chases, and loot. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Vision, Stealth, Traps, Locks & Theft Vision and Light Cover, Line of Sight & Line of Effect Stealth and Infiltration Traps and Non-Aether Hazards Locks Theft and Pickpocket Social Interaction, Information & Captivity Vision, Stealth, Traps, Locks & Theft Vision and Light Light states are Bright Light, Dim Light, and Darkness. Obscuration states are Lightly Obscured and Heavily Obscured. Dim Light lightly obscures; Darkness heavily obscures a creature that cannot otherwise see through it. Daeva Darkvision treats Darkness within 60 feet as Dim Light, not Bright Light. A recommended ordinary light source has a stated Bright radius plus an equal additional Dim radius unless its own text says otherwise. Bright light does not universally prohibit Stealth. Obscurity and Invisibility do not automatically make a creature Hidden. Cover, Line of Sight & Line of Effect No Cover. No defensive benefit from Cover. Half Cover. A creature or object behind meaningful partial obstruction gains +2 AC and +2 to Dexterity saving throws against effects originating from the covered direction. Intervening creatures can provide Half Cover when they materially obstruct the line. Full Cover. Full Cover blocks the relevant Line of Effect and prevents direct targeting through that obstruction unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Three-Quarters Cover does not exist in Wings of Atreia. Cover does not stack; use the best applicable Cover. Altitude neither inherently grants nor ignores Cover. Line of Sight and Line of Effect are distinct. Line of Sight determines whether you can see a target or point. Line of Effect determines whether an attack, spell, or effect can physically reach it. Heavy obscurement is not Cover by itself. Stealth and Infiltration Use scene states Undetected, Suspicious, and Alerted; these are not Conditions. Stealth must exceed Passive Perception; ties favor the observer. An active Search uses the GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation), against the relevant DC or opposing Stealth; ties favor the Searcher where opposed. Do not reroll Stealth every 5 feet; roll again only when circumstances materially change. For group Stealth, at least half the group must succeed. A failed check may create Suspicion rather than immediate full alarm when appropriate. Distractions create an opportunity to Hide rather than automatic success. Disguises are primarily social. Invisibility is not the same as Hidden. Wings do not automatically prevent Stealth. Traps and Non-Aether Hazards Describe a hazard with Trigger, Detection, Avoid/Disable method, Save/Check, Effect, and Reset/Duration. Hazards may be obvious, concealed, or hidden. Detection normally uses Passive Perception, active Perception, or Investigation. Disable methods depend on the mechanism and can use Sleight of Hand, Investigation, Athletics, or another appropriate Skill. There is no mandatory Thieves’ Tools system. Failure triggers the hazard only when the hazard says so. Damage and Conditions use existing universal rules. Forced movement is horizontal unless the hazard explicitly creates vertical displacement. Hazards normally resolve when triggered rather than taking their own Initiative turns. Repeat attempts require changed circumstances. Locks Mechanical Lock DC Simple 10 Standard 12 Secure 15 High Security 18 Exceptional 20+ The correct key opens a normal lock without a check. Mechanical locks generally use Dexterity (Sleight of Hand). Unusual mechanisms can use Intelligence (Investigation). Forcing uses Strength (Athletics); destroying a lock or door uses normal object/destruction adjudication. Failure does not automatically break or trigger a lock unless its design says so. Aether locks use Aether Interaction. If a task is impossible, do not assign an absurd DC—state that it cannot be done by that method. Theft and Pickpocket A theft attempt requires a plausible opportunity. Taking an accessible small item uses Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) against Passive Perception and must exceed it. If the target is actively watching, oppose with active Perception; ties favor the observer. Secured items can require a different approach. Failure may create suspicion or alarm. Success means the theft was unnoticed at that moment; later discovery remains possible. Distraction creates opportunity rather than automatic success. Help can grant +2 when genuinely meaningful. Worn armor, shields, Wings, wielded weapons, and equipped mandatory implements cannot simply be pickpocketed. Repeated attempts require changed circumstances. text: W. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Glossary & Core Terms A player-facing A–Z reference for the vocabulary used throughout Wings of Atreia, with direct links to the full rules and lore pages. How to use this page: definitions here are quick-reference summaries. Follow the “Read more” link whenever you need the complete rule, class text, or world context. A B C D E F G I K L M P R S U W 46 terms A Action Your main turn action. Many attacks, spells, class features, and other options specify that they use your Action. Read more: Combat → Advantage / Disadvantage Roll two d20s and use the higher result for Advantage or the lower result for Disadvantage. Read more: Core Resolution → Aether The supernatural power that underlies Daeva abilities, spellcasting, flight, and many extraordinary phenomena in Atreia. Read more: Aether & Spellcasting → Aether Enhancement The higher equipment-quality path beyond Profession +2. Aether upgrades are level-gated and handled separately from ordinary Profession work. Read more: Equipment → Ascension The transformation by which a mortal becomes a Daeva and receives Wings. WoA begins with this event in Session 0. Read more: Character Creation → At-Will A spell or ability frequency that may be used whenever its normal action and other requirements are met. Read more: Aether & Spellcasting → B Background A character-creation choice representing experience and identity before or around Ascension; it provides its defined skills and related benefits. Read more: Backgrounds → Bonus Action A secondary turn action available only when a feature, spell, or rule explicitly gives an option that uses it. Read more: Combat → C Character Manager The official WoA character-management method for creation records, advancement, current resources, equipment, spells, and other tracked character data. Read more: Character Creation → Class Your Daeva’s primary mechanical path. WoA uses eleven classes and does not use multiclassing. Read more: Classes → Class Resource A class-specific pool, charge, stance, meter, or other tracked mechanic defined by that class. Read more: Quick Reference → Class Save DC Normally 8 + Proficiency Bonus + the class ability identified by your class, unless a rule states otherwise. Read more: Core Resolution → Concentration A spell/effect limit: only one Concentration effect can be maintained at a time, and Incapacitated ends it. WoA does not use Concentration saving throws. Read more: Aether & Spellcasting → Condition A named rules state such as Poisoned or Incapacitated that changes what a creature can do or how rolls affect it. Read more: Combat → Cooldown A spell or ability frequency that becomes unavailable after use until its stated cooldown is satisfied; WoA also uses the universal out-of-combat cooldown rule where applicable. Read more: Aether & Spellcasting → D Daeva An Ascended immortal warrior of Atreia. Player characters in Wings of Atreia are Daevas. Read more: Character Creation → Daeva Points (DP) A resource unlocked at Level 10 and earned through participation in genuine combat victories. DP powers Ultimate Abilities and persists through rests. Read more: Daeva Points & Ultimates → E Empyrean Boon A powerful universal character option gained at Level 19 according to the advancement rules. Read more: Feats & Empyrean Boons → Empyrean Lord One of the great Daeva Lords whose authority and legacy shape Elyos and Asmodian civilization, together with the two historic Tower Guardians. Read more: World → F Faction Your character’s allegiance as Elyos or Asmodian. Faction affects culture, homeland, and campaign relationships rather than class statistics. Read more: Character Creation → Feat A universal character option chosen at designated advancement points instead of an Ability Score Improvement where the rules allow it. Read more: Feats & Empyrean Boons → Flight Slot A tracked unit of a Daeva’s flight capacity. The number of Flight Slots increases with character level. Read more: Flight → G Genuine Combat A real encounter using initiative and combat timing. Artificial encounters cannot be used to farm resources such as Daeva Points. Read more: Combat → I Implement A spellcasting equipment category that can follow the established quality and enhancement progression. Read more: Equipment → K Kinah The standard currency used for purchases, profession training, supplies, and other economic transactions. Read more: Professions & Economy → L Legendary Equipment Story-driven top-tier equipment above the Aether enhancement tiers. Legendary items are not ordinary Profession products. Read more: Equipment → Long Rest An 8-hour recovery period. What it restores depends on the specific class, spell, feature, or rule. Read more: Combat → Lord Action The dedicated off-turn action framework used by Empyrean Lords and Dragon Lords. Read more: Combat → M Milestone Advancement WoA’s advancement method. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Core Rulebook v4.2 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026 , synchronized with Player Handbook v3.10 . This page exposes the complete player-operable Warfront subsystem. Explicitly GM-facing enemy statblocks, hidden force composition, and closed GM-only resolution tables remain off the public player site. Legions Warfront Overview War Assets Unit Statistics Battle Exchange Unit Catalogue Unit Costs PC Participation Fortress Wars Open Abyss Reinforcements Quick Reference PLAYER-CREATED LEGIONS A player-created Legion is a lightweight organization for shared identity, missions, resources, and cross-faction cooperation when the campaign permits it. Legion membership does not create a new character progression track or grant automatic combat bonuses. When a Legion Can Be Founded Campaign Gate. The Campaign Director or controlling GM must explicitly declare Legion Founding available. Reaching Level 11 by itself does not unlock the system. Founding Player. One Founding Player must be Level 11 or higher. That character becomes the initial Legion Leader. Other members. Every other founding or joining member must be Level 3 or higher before joining and must already have reached their Specialization or Archetype choice where applicable. A Level 1-2 character cannot join early. Membership has no maximum size. There is no minimum number of additional founders; a qualifying Founding Player may establish the Legion alone if all other founding requirements are satisfied. Elyos and Asmodians may belong to the same Legion once the required campaign state is active. Every member retains their original faction identity and its normal consequences. Founding Fund and Treasury Founding requires 5,000 Kinah deposited into the new Legion Treasury. Eligible founding members may contribute toward the total. Before establishment, the Founding Fund cannot be withdrawn. If founding is abandoned, each contributor receives their contribution back. Once established, the 5,000 Kinah remains usable Treasury money. Any Legion member may deposit Kinah. Only the Legion Leader may withdraw Kinah or authorize spending. Legion missions may reward participating members, the Treasury, or both as determined by the GM. There is no passive Legion income, automatic salary, interest, business-profit engine, or mandatory recurring membership dues. Leadership and Membership The only default roles are Legion Leader and Legion Member. The Legion Leader admits and removes members, controls permissions for Legion assets, may transfer leadership, and may formally dissolve the Legion. Leadership may be transferred to any existing legal Legion member. The new Leader does not need to be Level 11; Level 11 is a founding requirement only. Member Benefits Members may display the Legion name, colors, crest, and insignia. Ordinary Legion identification occupies no Inventory Slot. Members may accept Legion missions and may use resources, facilities, contacts, and support the Legion actually possesses when the Legion Leader permits it. Where the campaign's cross-faction arrangements recognize the Legion, its insignia provides a legitimate reason for Elyos and Asmodian members to operate together. It does not grant diplomatic immunity or unrestricted access. Legion membership grants no automatic Hit, AC, damage, HP, saving throw, skill, Advantage, Spell DC, DP, class-resource, equipment-quality, or personal Inventory bonus. Legion Storage and Headquarters An established Legion has one secure shared Storage location with a capacity of 100 Inventory Slots. Normal Inventory Slot and stacking rules apply; Kinah remains in the Treasury and uses no Storage Slots. Any Legion member may deposit eligible items. Only the Legion Leader may withdraw items or authorize another member to retrieve them. Legion Storage is stationary and cannot be accessed remotely. It never increases a member's personal Inventory capacity in the field. A Legion may designate one legitimate location as its Headquarters. The Headquarters is simply its meeting place and Storage location; it grants no automatic bonuses and has no upgrade track. Lightweight Rule. There is no Legion XP, Legion Level, officer hierarchy, skill tree, research tree, reputation meter, headquarters progression, or other default Legion management subsystem. Abyss Warfront System Warfronts resolve formation-scale warfare separately from ordinary character-scale combat. They are used for Fortress Wars and Open Abyss Battles. Strategic travel and marching between major engagements are handled narratively, off-table, or during downtime. Shared Warfront Command The player side uses one shared strat

text: Watchful Hunter. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Ranged Striker • Focus • Traps • Tactical Repositioning Ranger “Chase me or run away. Either way, you'll only die tired.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.14 — Mechanics Sync, 15 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Focus Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Ranger is a nonmagical ranged hunter that controls enemy movement with persistent battlefield traps, spends Focus on precision or evasive shots, and is rewarded for exploiting targets that walk into prepared terrain. Its sustained damage comes from two ranged attacks, not from spellcasting or a third standard attack. Class Identity Rangers are mobile ranged specialists who control distance through marksmanship, movement, traps, and battlefield awareness. They are most effective when they can read terrain before committing, choose favorable lines of attack, and punish enemies that approach carelessly. Focus represents the Ranger’s ability to convert patience and perception into precise action. Tradition & Outlook The Ranger tradition also descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines, but where Assassins close with a chosen target, Rangers cultivate distance, fieldcraft, and control of the approach. Rangers are common among scouts, hunters, pathfinders, border wardens, reconnaissance troops, and independent Daevas accustomed to surviving beyond secure settlements. They tend to value preparedness, observation, mobility, and freedom of movement. Appearance & Adventuring Rangers usually wear mobile armor and carry bows, ammunition, traps, and field equipment suited to extended movement. Their gear often reflects the terrain in which they learned their craft. Rangers adventure to explore dangerous regions, hunt monsters or enemy operatives, guide expeditions, secure routes, protect remote communities, or prove that no battlefield is truly open ground when preparation and range are on their side. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Ability Dexterity Secondary Ability Wisdom Hit Die d10 Saving Throws Dexterity, Strength Armor Leather Armor Weapons Longbows, Shortbows, Crossbows Skills Choose 2 from 6: Animal Handling, Athletics, Investigation, Nature, Perception, Survival Class Save DC 8 + PB + WIS modifier Signature Resource Focus Signature Mechanic Ranger Traps Extra Attack Level 5; two attacks only Spellcasting None Core Engine — Focus Maximum Focus equals your PB + WIS modifier, minimum 2. A Long Rest restores all expended Focus. A Short Rest restores Focus equal to PB, up to your maximum. Focus is a tactical reserve rather than ammunition or a tax on ordinary ranged attacks; Ranger Traps normally cost no Focus. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Starting State Focus is a rest-based reserve and does not reset merely because combat begins or ends. After a Long Rest it is normally full. Maximum PB + WIS modifier, minimum 2. Rest Recovery Long Rest restores all expended Focus. Short Rest restores Focus equal to PB, up to your maximum. Combat Recovery Hunter’s Rhythm and certain later Ranger/specialization features can regain Focus during genuine combat when their tactical conditions are actually satisfied. How You Spend It Precision Shot 1 Focus; Pinning Shot 1 Focus; Evasive Step 1 Focus; Deadeye Perfect Shot 1 Focus. Other Ranger features spend Focus only when their text states a cost. Refunds / Recovery A combat refund or recovery is not a new attack, trap trigger, or separate technique. It simply restores Focus up to your maximum. Persistence Unused Focus persists between encounters until spent or restored; there is no automatic combat-end reset. Does Not Generate Standing still and firing, harmless staged interactions, or ordinary trap placement do not create Focus unless an explicit recovery feature is actually triggered. Each attack expends 1 shot. Normal Bonus Action Reload restores to 2 shots. Cannot use Quick Shot or Akimbo. Gunslinger ammunition-restoration features can restore Musket shots normally, but never above 2. Standard one-handed firearm capacity increases do not apply. Ranged Weapon Range. The first listed range is the weapon’s Normal Range and the second is its Maximum Range. A target within the weapon’s Normal Range is attacked normally unless another modifier applies. A target beyond Normal Range but within Maximum Range can still be targeted, but the ranged weapon attack is made with Disadvantage. A target beyond Maximum Range cannot be hit and the attack automatically misses. If the target is within 5 feet of the attacker, the ranged weapon attack is made with Disadvantage regardless of which listed range applies. Multiple sources of Disadvantage do not stack. Straight-Line Fire Crossbows, Pistols, and Muskets use Straight-Line. If an allied creature intersects the line between shooter and target, the nearest such ally makes DC 15 Dexterity. On success, the shot proceeds. On failure, the ally is hit and takes normal damage; the original target is not hit. The intercepted hit cannot inherit a Natural-20 critical result rolled against the original target. Resolve multiple possible interceptors nearest first. The same rule applies in 3D aerial lines. Ammunition All fired ammunition is lost. Fired Arrows, Bolts, Pistol Bullets, and Musket Bullets are never recovered. A character may have only one Active Profession at a time. The only Profession ranks are Apprentice and Master. There is no Profession XP, no intermediate rank, and no separate recipe, formula-book, manual, or recipe-learning subsystem. Earning a rank automatically grants the standard functions assigned to that rank. Rule Profession Ruling Starting Rank None. Backgrounds, including Artisan, grant no Profession rank. Active Limit One Active Profession at a time. Changing Profession Only when the character gains a character level. The trainee and trainer cannot adventure, undertake missions, perform adventuring travel, conduct other downtime work, perform Profession production, or complete other substantive activities that day. Training Days need not be consecutive. An interrupted day grants no Training Progress, but previously completed Training Days remain. A character cannot train themselves. One qualified trainer may instruct up to four trainees of the same rank category during one Training Day. text: WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About 28 September 2026 Website Rules Reference v1.0.0 Established Website as Mechanical Authority The GitHub website is now the overall authoritative mechanical reference for Wings of Atreia. Books and the Character Manager follow the mechanics established on the website. Established Synchronization Workflow Mechanics changes begin on the website, followed by review and synchronization of affected books and Character Manager behavior. Non-mechanical website changes do not automatically require downstream updates. Added Version Record Website Rules Reference v1.0.0 is effective 28 September 2026 and is recorded in the repository as the baseline for this authority model. Living Player Reference Website Changelog A concise record of player-facing website improvements, clarifications, and reference-tool updates. The GitHub website is the authoritative mechanical reference beginning with Website Rules Reference v1.0.0. This changelog describes the website reference experience . A website usability change does not itself create or alter a game rule. 20 September 2026 Rules & Character Progression Synchronization Updated HP Progression The player-facing reference now reflects the approved Level 1 and Level 2–20 fixed HP progression, including Hit Die Base values and the separation between level-up HP and Short Rest Hit Dice healing. Updated Class References All 11 class pages were synchronized to Player Handbook v3.16, including the revised Templar and Cleric HP chassis. Updated Publication Status The website status page now tracks Player Handbook v3.16, Core Rulebook v4.9, Game Master’s Guide v1.24, and FAQ v2.9. 14 September 2026 Player Reference Upgrade Added At-table Reference Tools Favorites, Recently Viewed pages, and a global Quick Reference drawer are now available throughout the site and are stored locally on the player’s device. Added Mobile & Sharing Tools Improved mobile navigation, page sharing, direct section-link copying, reading progress, and a Back-to-Top control were added for long reference pages. Added Offline Awareness The header now shows a compact rules/offline status badge. The site can alert players when a newer offline reference has been downloaded and is ready to reload. Improved Accessibility Keyboard skip navigation, stronger visible focus treatment, larger touch targets, reduced-motion support, and higher-contrast preferences were added. Added Installable Full Offline Reference The player-facing site can be installed as a PWA and prepares the complete listed reference bundle for offline use, with a visible Ready status when caching completes. Improved Search Search is site-wide, category-aware, supports partial matching, highlights matching text, and includes keyboard result navigation. Added Rules Compendium & Expanded Glossary Fast rule lookup, A–Z glossary navigation, and cross-links were added for in-session reference. Improved Spell & Class Browsing The spell library gained multi-filter browsing and full effect-text search. Class pages gained sticky on-page navigation and direct spell-list links where applicable. Added New Player, Faction & World Navigation A guided Start Here journey, expanded faction guidance, interactive Gazetteer, expanded region entries, campaign-start context, and player-safe Lord references were added. Added Publication Status A dedicated Rules & Publication Status page now identifies the current reference baseline and the standing synchronization workflow. text: When a Legion Can Be Founded. WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Player Rules Legions & Complete Abyss Warfront System Player-created Legions plus the complete player-operable Warfront rules, unit catalogue, War Asset costs, Fortress procedures, and Open Abyss procedures. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Core Rulebook v4.2 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026 , synchronized with Player Handbook v3.10 . This page exposes the complete player-operable Warfront subsystem. Explicitly GM-facing enemy statblocks, hidden force composition, and closed GM-only resolution tables remain off the public player site. Legions Warfront Overview War Assets Unit Statistics Battle Exchange Unit Catalogue Unit Costs PC Participation Fortress Wars Open Abyss Reinforcements Quick Reference PLAYER-CREATED LEGIONS A player-created Legion is a lightweight organization for shared identity, missions, resources, and cross-faction cooperation when the campaign permits it. Legion membership does not create a new character progression track or grant automatic combat bonuses. When a Legion Can Be Founded Campaign Gate. The Campaign Director or controlling GM must explicitly declare Legion Founding available. Reaching Level 11 by itself does not unlock the system. Founding Player. One Founding Player must be Level 11 or higher. That character becomes the initial Legion Leader. Other members. Every other founding or joining member must be Level 3 or higher before joining and must already have reached their Specialization or Archetype choice where applicable. A Level 1-2 character cannot join early. Membership has no maximum size. There is no minimum number of additional founders; a qualifying Founding Player may establish the Legion alone if all other founding requirements are satisfied. Elyos and Asmodians may belong to the same Legion once the required campaign state is active. Every member retains their original faction identity and its normal consequences. Founding Fund and Treasury Founding requires 5,000 Kinah deposited into the new Legion Treasury. Eligible founding members may contribute toward the total. Before establishment, the Founding Fund cannot be withdrawn. If founding is abandoned, each contributor receives their contribution back. Once established, the 5,000 Kinah remains usable Treasury money. Any Legion member may deposit Kinah. Only the Legion Leader may withdraw Kinah or authorize spending. Legion missions may reward participating members, the Treasury, or both as determined by the GM. There is no passive Legion income, automatic salary, interest, business-profit engine, or mandatory recurring membership dues. Leadership and Membership The only default roles are Legion Leader and Legion Member. The Legion Leader admits and removes members, controls permissions for Legion assets, may transfer leadership, and may formally dissolve the Legion. Leadership may be transferred to any existing legal Legion member. The new Leader does not need to be Level 11; Level 11 is a founding requirement only. Member Benefits Members may display the Legion name, colors, crest, and insignia. Ordinary Legion identification occupies no Inventory Slot. Members may accept Legion missions and may use resources, facilities, contacts, and support the Legion actually possesses when the Legion Leader permits it. Where the campaign's cross-faction arrangements recognize the Legion, its insignia provides a legitimate reason for Elyos and Asmodian members to operate together. It does not grant diplomatic immunity or unrestricted access. Legion membership grants no automatic Hit, AC, damage, HP, saving throw, skill, Advantage, Spell DC, DP, class-resource, equipment-quality, or personal Inventory bonus. Legion Storage and Headquarters An established Legion has one secure shared Storage location with a capacity of 100 Inventory Slots. Normal Inventory Slot and stacking rules apply; Kinah remains in the Treasury and uses no Storage Slots. Any Legion member may deposit eligible items. Only the Legion Leader may withdraw items or authorize another member to retrieve them. Legion Storage is stationary and cannot be accessed remotely. It never increases a member's personal Inventory capacity in the field. A Legion may designate one legitimate location as its Headquarters. The Headquarters is simply its meeting place and Storage location; it grants no automatic bonuses and has no upgrade track. Lightweight Rule. There is no Legion XP, Legion Level, officer hierarchy, skill tree, research tree, reputation meter, headquarters progression, or other default Legion management subsystem. The first listed range is the weapon’s Normal Range and the second is its Maximum Range. A target within the weapon’s Normal Range is attacked normally unless another modifier applies. A target beyond Normal Range but within Maximum Range can still be targeted, but the ranged weapon attack is made with Disadvantage. A target beyond Maximum Range cannot be hit and the attack automatically misses.
