On success, the shot proceeds. On failure, the ally is hit and takes normal damage; the original target is not hit. The intercepted hit cannot inherit a Natural-20 critical result rolled against the original target. Resolve multiple possible interceptors nearest first. The same rule applies in 3D aerial lines. title: Wings of Atreia Character Manager — Getting Started
desc: Wings of Atreia reference: Wings of Atreia Character Manager — Getting Started.
text: ← Back to Wings of Atreia Wings of Atreia Character Manager — Getting Started A step-by-step guide for Game Masters and players. No screenshots are required: follow the labels and controls shown in the Character Manager. Quick Start For Game Masters For Players Returning Players Troubleshooting Quick Start Important: a new player does not create a normal public account. The Game Master creates a private Player Access Code first. Correct order GM signs in with the GM access code GM opens GM Player Access GM uses Generate Player Code GM privately gives the code to the player Player enters the code on the Character Manager login screen Player chooses New Character The new character is saved under that player's access For Game Masters 1. Sign in as the GM Open the Wings of Atreia Character Manager. On the opening screen, find the field asking for a Wings of Atreia access code . Enter your current GM access code. Use the sign-in/continue control directly below the access-code field. After GM access is accepted, the GM controls will become available. Keep the GM access code private. Do not give the GM code to players. 2. Create access for a new player In the GM controls, locate GM Player Access . Open that section. Use Generate Player Code . The Character Manager will create a private player code in the format used by the app. Copy that player's code carefully. Send the code privately to the correct player. Give each player their own Player Access Code. Do not reuse one player's code for another player. 3. Tell the player how to enter Give the player only these two things: the normal Character Manager link; and their private Player Access Code. Tell the player to open the Character Manager, enter their code in the Wings of Atreia access code field, then continue. If this is their first time using that code, they can choose New Character and create their character. 4. Existing characters and assignments GM Player Access can also be used when the GM needs to manage which existing characters are available to a player. Before creating a replacement character because something appears missing, verify the player's access assignment first. 5. Multiple characters A player may own multiple Wings of Atreia characters, but only one character is played by that player in a session. When a player creates another character while signed in under their own Player Access Code, the newly created character is automatically associated with that player access. For Players 1. Get your Player Access Code Before you create a character, your Game Master must give you a private Player Access Code. You should receive: the Character Manager link; and your personal Player Access Code. If you have not received a Player Access Code, contact your GM before trying to create a character. 2. Sign in Open the Character Manager link from your GM. Find the field labeled for the Wings of Atreia access code . Enter your Player Access Code exactly as your GM provided it. Use the sign-in/continue control directly below the field. When the code is accepted, your player area will open. 3. Create your first character If you have no character yet, choose New Character . Complete each part of character creation shown by the Character Manager. Choose your faction: Elyos or Asmodian. Choose one of the available classes. Complete the remaining required character details and choices. Review the character before saving. Save the character and wait for the Character Manager to confirm the save. The Character Manager is the official player character record and management tool. Current Wings of Atreia rules remain authoritative if a display summary ever conflicts with the books. 4. Keep your access code private Your Player Access Code is used to reach your characters. Do not post it publicly. Do not give it to another player. Do not use another player's code. If you think someone else obtained it, contact your GM. Returning Players Open the Character Manager. Enter the same Player Access Code issued by your GM. Continue past the access screen. Your authorized character list will appear. Select the character you want to use. Open/load the character. Use the Character Manager normally during play. If a character you already created is missing, do not immediately make a duplicate. Contact your GM so the player access assignment can be checked first. During play Keep live character information current, including where applicable: Current and Temporary HP Flight Slots class resources Daeva Points equipment and inventory changes consumables and ammunition conditions and other live-play state spell, feature, Specialization, and Profession information Troubleshooting My Player Access Code does not work Check that you entered the code exactly as provided. Remove accidental spaces before or after the code. Make sure you are using the current Character Manager link. If it still fails, contact your GM. I signed in, but I see no characters If this is your first time, choose New Character . If you previously had a character, contact your GM before creating another one. The Character Manager looks outdated Refresh the page first. On Windows, use Ctrl + F5 for a full browser refresh if the older interface is still being shown. The app says offline data is not ready Open the Character Manager while connected to the internet and allow the required application files to finish loading. Once the app reports that its offline data is ready, cached parts of the Character Manager can be used according to the app's offline capabilities. I lost my Player Access Code Contact your Game Master. Do not create a second player identity simply because you cannot find the original code. The GM should check your existing player access first. GM: a player cannot see an existing character Open GM Player Access and verify the player's character assignment before creating or authorizing a replacement. Remember: GM creates the Player Access Code first. Player signs in with that code. Player then creates or opens their authorized character. ← Back to Wings of Atreia ↑ Back to top Wings of Atreia Character Manager — Player & GM Getting Started Guide

title: World of Atreia | Wings of Atreia
desc: Player-safe guide to the regions of Elysea, Asmodae, Reshanta, and the known Balaurea frontier.
text: WINGS OF ATREIA Home Rules Classes Spells World Character Companion About Setting Reference World of Atreia A spoiler-safe guide to the shattered world, its major realms, and the regions Daevas may know in the Present Age. Choose Your Faction Compare Elyos and Asmodians, their homelands, traditions, and what faction means for your Daeva. Interactive Gazetteer Filter and search every currently named WoA region by realm, terrain, landmark, or identity. History of Atreia From ancient Atreia to the opening age of the Abyss War. Current Campaign Start Where player characters enter the Present Age and the Abyss War. Twelve Empyrean Lords The Daeva Lords who shaped Elyos and Asmodian civilization. Six Dragon Lords The supreme Balaur powers whose influence hangs over the war. Elysea Sanctum, Oriel, Poeta, Verteron, Eltnen, Heiron, Theobomos, and Iluma. Asmodae Pandaemonium, Pernon, Ishalgen, Altgard, Morheim, Beluslan, Brusthonin, and Norsvold. Reshanta / The Abyss Lower Abyss, Upper Abyss, and the Core / Eye of Reshanta. Balaurea Inggison, Gelkmaros, Silentera Canyon, and the largely unknown greater frontier. Before You Explore the World Atreia was not always divided. Discover how the rise of the Balaur, the Millennium War, the Cataclysm, and the opening of the Abyss shaped the age in which your Daeva begins their story. Read the History of Atreia → Explore by Faction or Region Elyos or Asmodian? Compare the two playable factions as cultures and homelands rather than as mechanical races. Learn what each side knows, values, and inherits at the start of the Abyss War. Compare the Factions → Interactive Gazetteer Browse the named regions of Elysea, Asmodae, Reshanta, and the known Balaurean frontier with realm filters and instant region search. Open the Gazetteer → Current Campaign Start: The Present Age The default Wings of Atreia campaign begins circa 1,000 AC, during the long Abyss War. Player characters begin as newly Ascended Daevas who have only recently received their Wings and entered an immortal life of service, discovery, and conflict. Elyos and Asmodians remain bitter rivals, with Terminon and Primum serving as their enduring footholds in Reshanta, while the Balaur stand as a powerful third force rather than a distant legend. Beyond the familiar realms, the known Balaurean frontier has opened through Inggison, Gelkmaros, and Silentera Canyon, but Greater Balaurea remains largely unknown. Your Daeva begins with a faction, a homeland, and reasons to distrust the opposing side, but the world does not promise that every enemy will remain simple. Early adventures can place Elyos and Asmodians against the same Balaur threat, and circumstances may force rivals to decide whether survival matters more than inherited hatred. Lepharist revolutionaries are active in this age and may become part of the characters’ first encounters with the wider conflict, but their deeper motives are something players discover through play. The starting world is therefore a snapshot, not a fixed future: fortresses can change hands, alliances can form or collapse, and the actions of player characters can become part of Atreia’s history. The Twelve Empyrean Lords The Empyrean Lords are extraordinary Daevas elevated into Lordhood whose names stand at the heart of Atreia’s history. After the Cataclysm, the surviving rulers became associated with the Seraphim tradition of Elysea and the Shedim tradition of Asmodae, while the two Tower Guardians remain central to the story of the world’s division. To player characters, these Lords are not merely distant mythology: their institutions, teachings, military orders, laws, temples, and legacies shape the societies in which Daevas live. Seraphim Lords of Elysea Ariel — Lady of Light Kaisinel — Lord of Illusion Nezekan — Lord of Justice Vaizel — Lord of Freedom Yustiel — Lady of Life These Lords stand among the highest powers recognized in Elyos civilization. Their influence reaches player characters through Sanctum, Elyos institutions, military service, cultural traditions, and the expectations placed upon Daevas. A player may serve organizations shaped by a Lord’s legacy, receive missions from authorities acting in a Lord’s name, or eventually become important enough for the concerns of the Lords themselves to matter. Shedim Lords of Asmodae Azphel — Lord of Shadow Lumiel — Lady of Wisdom Marchutan — Lord of Fate Triniel — Lady of Death Zikel — Lord of Destruction These Lords stand among the highest powers recognized in Asmodian civilization. Their influence is felt through Pandaemonium, Archon service, Asmodian institutions, cultural traditions, and the hard-won identity of Asmodae. Player characters may encounter their authority through commanders, temples, missions, judgments, and eventually events important enough to draw the attention of the Lords themselves. The Tower Guardians Israphel — Lord of Space Siel — Lady of Time Israphel and Siel are remembered as the two Guardians of the Tower of Eternity and are counted among the Twelve Empyrean Lords of Atreia’s great history. Their roles are different from those of the post-Cataclysm faction rulers: they belong to the story of the Tower, the Cataclysm, and the sacrifice that shaped the divided world. For beginning players, their importance is primarily historical, and deeper truths concerning their legacy are meant to be discovered through the campaign rather than explained in advance. The Six Dragon Lords The Dragon Lords are the supreme powers of the Balaur and represent threats on a scale far beyond ordinary soldiers or monsters. Their names are known through history, warfare, rumor, and the devastation associated with Balaur dominion. Player characters are far more likely to encounter their armies, agents, fortresses, schemes, and consequences before ever standing before a Dragon Lord directly. Fregion — Dragon Lord of Fire Fregion is remembered as the first Dragon Lord and the beginning of the transformation that produced the Balaur order. To players, his name represents the oldest and greatest shadow behind Balaur power. Any direct involvement with Fregion belongs to the highest scale of Daeva conflict rather than ordinary adventuring. Meslamtaeda — Dragon Lord of Rage and Destruction Meslamtaeda embodies overwhelming destructive power among the Dragon Lords. Players should understand his influence through the fear, devastation, and military consequences associated with forces acting beneath such a ruler. Confronting power of this magnitude is not the same as facing a conventional battlefield commander. Ereshkigal — Dragon Lord of Ice and Justice Ereshkigal is one of the great Balaur powers whose name is bound to the long struggle surrounding the Abyss. For players, she represents a strategic power capable of shaping entire theaters of war rather than merely individual encounters. Her deeper circumstances in the Present Age are intentionally left for discovery during play. Beritra — Dragon Lord of Darkness Beritra is a Dragon Lord whose power extends through Balaur forces, plans, and conflicts reaching beyond any single region. Player characters may experience that influence through enemies and events long before understanding the full design behind them. His true objectives and present movements are matters for the campaign to reveal. Tiamat — Dragon Lord of Earth and Death Tiamat commands power associated with conquest, warfare, and Balaur dominion. To beginning Daevas, her name belongs to the class of enemies capable of moving armies and changing the fate of territories. What she seeks in the Present Age—and how her struggles with other Balaur powers affect Atreia—should emerge through play. Apsu — Dragon Lord of Wind Apsu is counted among the Six Dragon Lords and remains part of the history and power structure players inherit at the start of the campaign. Public knowledge does not provide beginning characters with a complete account of his present circumstances. His deeper role is therefore deliberately left unexplained here so that the campaign can reveal it at the proper time. What the Lords mean to your character: Empyrean Lords can stand behind the institutions, duties, beliefs, and authorities that shape a Daeva’s life, while Dragon Lords define the scale of the Balaur threat looming over both factions. Neither group should be reduced to a list of quest-givers or boss fights. As the campaign grows, the players’ relationship to these powers can change from distant history and military consequence to direct choices capable of affecting Atreia itself. Elysea Elysea forms the southern half of shattered Atreia and is the homeland of the Elyos. Its regions range from fertile countryside and monumental cities to arid badlands, mountain forests, devastated islands, and places where ancient history remains close to the surface. Sanctum Sanctum is the monumental floating capital of Elysea, suspended above Oriel and visible as one of the great symbols of Elyos civilization. Its luminous plazas, temples, government halls, Legion offices, archives, and scholarly institutions make it a center of civic life as much as military power. The city was raised during the long southern reconstruction after the Cataclysm rather than surviving unchanged from ancient Atreia. Public ceremony, learning, art, diplomacy, and service all contribute to the capital’s cultivated identity. For Elyos Daevas, Sanctum is where victories become policy, discoveries enter archives, and service to Elysea can draw the attention of powerful institutions. Most civic areas are orderly and accessible, while military compounds, temple spaces, and restricted records remain controlled. Adventures here tend toward investigation, diplomacy, political consequences, research, or threats hidden beneath the security of the capital. Sanctum represents what Elyos society believes it rebuilt from the ruin of the old world. Oriel Oriel is the cultivated residential sanctuary directly beneath Sanctum on the same greater floating geography, not a distant island of its own. Gardens, estates, homes, workshops, and carefully maintained public spaces give it a gentler character than the monumental capital overhead. It reflects the domestic side of Elyos civilization: households, artistry, hospitality, and the patient work of maintaining a beautiful place to live. Its closeness to Sanctum ties everyday life directly to the political and religious heart of Elysea. Daevas who come to Oriel encounter the lives that continue beyond military service—families, artisans, residents, visitors, and generations shaped by an immortal society. The region can host social stories, community problems, personal obligations, celebrations, quiet investigations, and consequences that feel very different from fortress warfare. Its tranquility should not make it meaningless; Oriel helps show players what Elyos characters are actually protecting. Looking upward toward Sanctum also reinforces the intimate relationship between capital and home. Poeta Poeta is a fertile rural region of Elysea, defined by broad plains, farms, forests, and clear lakes. Akarios Village stands among a landscape that includes Cliona Lake, Daminu Forest, Kabarah Strip Mine, and Timolia Mine. Compared with the grandeur of Sanctum, Poeta feels close to the land and to the ordinary rhythms of food, work, family, and local community. Its pastoral appearance makes it one of the clearest expressions of the hospitable southern environment. For many Elyos, Poeta represents homeland in its most immediate form: fields worth tending, communities worth defending, and wilderness that still holds mysteries of its own. Daevas may be called to protect travelers, investigate trouble around mines and forests, assist isolated settlements, or deal with dangers that ordinary residents cannot face alone. The region works especially well for adventures where local stakes matter before the campaign expands into larger wars. Poeta
